Strong candidates will have experience holding that balance, not letting empathy become avoidance, and not letting collections pressure override service quality.

What JMC Brings to the Role

John M. Corcoran & Company has operated in New England real estate since 1951, and the organization carries institutional knowledge that shows up in how properties are managed day to day. The team culture skews collaborative, and the company has a track record of long-tenured employees, which tends to reflect well on how internal processes are structured and supported.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • At least 6 months of experience in office administration, collections, finance, or property management
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience expected
  • Multifamily property management background preferred
  • Strong organizational and communication skills across written and verbal formats

Pay range is $23.00 to $33.35 per hour. For candidates looking to build a career in property management operations, collections experience is a direct path toward leasing management, assistant property manager, and eventually property manager roles, since delinquency oversight is one of the clearest windows into how a property's finances actually function.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Arbors at Turnberry
job.description:
A prospect calls at 9:05 on a Tuesday morning. They want to see a two-bedroom today. You pull up availability, check the unit's condition, schedule the tour, and log the guest card before you've finished your coffee. That's the pace at Arbors at Turnberry.

The Role

Arbors at Turnberry is a 367-unit community in Pickerington, OH, managed by Ackermann Group, a Midwest developer and operator with a track record going back to 1938. This is a full-time leasing position: Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, plus rotating Saturdays from 9am to 4pm.

Day to day, you're the first voice prospects hear and the first face they see. You convert inquiries into tours, tours into signed leases, and new residents into long-term ones. You handle the full leasing cycle: guest card entry, follow-up, lease prep, and move-in documentation. You also walk units and common areas regularly, tidying what you can and flagging what maintenance needs to handle.

You'll keep up with the local rental market well enough to speak to it during tours. You'll respond to resident questions and route anything complex to the right person. You'll participate in after-hours resident events on occasion and support outreach efforts when needed. The CRM and property management software (Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe are the preferred platforms here) are tools you'll use daily, not occasionally.

Ackermann offers hourly pay plus commission on new and renewed leases, health benefits, a 401k with company match, paid time off including your birthday, an employee rent discount, and career development support.

What They're Looking For

  • Prior customer service experience, required
  • Leasing or sales background, strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe, or similar CRM tools, preferred
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable working as part of a small site team
  • High school diploma or equivalent

What separates strong candidates here is follow-through. Leasing at a 367-unit community means managing a real volume of prospects at different stages. The people who perform well track their pipeline carefully, follow up without being prompted, and close tours without high-pressure tactics. If your background is in retail or hospitality sales and you're transitioning into property management, that experience translates well to this kind of role.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance teams run lean, and when a property has real volume, a single Maintenance Supervisor can't cover everything alone. BAM Companies, a Des Moines-area operator founded in 2010, is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Supervisor to carry real weight on the maintenance side at one of their West Des Moines communities.

What the Work Looks Like

This role splits time between hands-on repairs and light supervisory support. Day to day, you're turning units, working through work orders, and handling the mechanical systems that keep a property running: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, drywall. You'll also take part in preventive maintenance inspections and help document what gets done.

On the administrative side, you'll work directly with the Maintenance Supervisor on scheduling, parts ordering, and unit walks. That coordination piece matters. Knowing where the team is on make-readies, which units are punched, and what's still outstanding keeps the operation from falling behind.

After-hours coverage is part of the job. The team rotates on-call, and snow removal is an all-hands responsibility in winter. If that kind of shared accountability doesn't appeal to you, this role isn't the right fit.

Pay runs $22 to $25 per hour depending on experience.

What BAM Needs From You

  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and drywall
  • Previous maintenance experience in residential or related settings
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and handle physical, hands-on work throughout the day
  • EPA Type 2 Certification is a plus but not required to apply

Strong candidates at this level tend to be the ones who already troubleshoot independently before escalating. If you can walk a unit, spot what needs to happen, and execute without waiting to be told, you'll move faster in this role and likely move up faster too. The assistant supervisor seat is a common stepping stone to leading a maintenance team on your own property.

BAM offers PTO after 90 days, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus rent discounts at their properties for employees who want to live on-site.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front of Bozzuto's leasing funnel at their Oakland community. Your core job is converting prospect interest into signed leases. That starts with lead follow-up: responding quickly, giving people genuinely useful information about the unit, the building, and the neighborhood, and booking tours. From there, you're running those tours in a way that feels personal, not scripted. The goal is a lease, and your ability to read a prospect and tailor the conversation is what separates a tour that closes from one that doesn't.

Beyond the one-on-one work, you'll manage the community's social media presence on platforms like Facebook and Instagram. This means creating content that builds awareness and keeps the brand visible to people who are still early in their apartment search. It's a real part of the job, not an afterthought.

The schedule runs three weekends per month, with two weekdays off in exchange. That's the nature of residential leasing: prospects tour when they're not at work, and your availability needs to match theirs.

What You Bring

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You can adjust your tone for a text follow-up, a phone call, and an in-person tour without losing the thread.
  • Sales instincts. You know how to move a conversation forward without being pushy.
  • Comfort with social media content creation, specifically Facebook and Instagram.
  • Proficiency with software, apps, and property management platforms. You pick up new tools quickly.
  • A professional presentation and genuine interest in helping people find a home that works for them.

Context Worth Knowing

Leasing Consultant roles at well-run operators like Bozzuto tend to be a solid entry point into broader property management careers. Strong performers here often move into Senior Leasing, Leasing Manager, or Assistant Community Manager roles within two to three years. The skills you build, reading traffic patterns, tightening your follow-up cadence, understanding what drives lease conversion, carry directly into those next roles.

The Oakland market runs competitive. Renters have options, and they're researching before they ever call. What separates strong candidates here is the ability to provide information that's specific and useful before the tour even happens. Generic follow-up gets ignored. The consultants who close consistently are the ones who make the prospect feel like the decision is easy before they walk through the door.

Base salary runs $50,000 to $54,000, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician - The Colony, TX
job.description:
This role runs on physical stamina, route discipline, and consistent customer-facing professionalism. If those three things come naturally to you, the work itself is straightforward and predictable.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Each shift, you'll cover a set route through a multifamily community in The Colony, TX, collecting bagged waste from resident doorsteps and transferring it to carts and then to onsite compactors or containers. The route includes stairs, parking lots, pool areas, dog waste stations, and mail kiosks. You'll clear debris, clean spills around doorsteps and compactor zones, and keep common areas presentable throughout your time on property.

You'll also monitor for improper or prohibited waste and handle it according to company protocol. Every shift gets logged through a mobile app, including start and end times and photos where required. This documentation piece matters: Cortland tracks route completion and productivity, so staying organized during your shift is part of doing the job well.

Residents and staff will see you regularly. A professional, courteous interaction goes a long way in this role. You're the most visible person on property during your shift.

Skills This Role Relies On

  • Physical endurance: walking long distances, climbing stairs, and lifting up to 50 lbs repeatedly
  • Route efficiency: completing collection rounds on schedule without cutting corners on cleanliness or safety
  • EPA and OSHA awareness: understanding what waste handling protocols apply and following them consistently
  • Basic tech comfort: logging shift data and photos through a smartphone app (Android or iOS required)
  • Customer service instincts: handling resident interactions calmly and professionally
  • A valid Class E driver's license for local driving as needed

A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred. At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role gives you a realistic baseline for what this work involves. Bilingual ability is a plus given the resident mix at most Texas communities.

Working at Cortland

Cortland ranks among the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the country and manages its properties with in-house operations, which means decisions get made closer to the property level. For a technician role, that typically translates to clearer expectations, consistent processes, and a management team that's accessible rather than distant.

One honest note about this type of role: you'll work outdoors in Texas heat, handle waste that smells, and maintain a pleasant attitude while doing it. Candidates who last in valet trash positions treat the route like a craft, take pride in how a property looks after their shift, and don't need external motivation to stay on pace. That consistency is what separates people who do well here from those who don't.

job.title: Administrative Assistant
job.description:
The lobby at a busy third-party management corporate office moves fast. A courier drops off a package, two calls come in at once, and someone from the executive team needs a report reformatted before the 10 a.m. meeting. That's a Tuesday morning here.

The Role

Asset Living, one of the larger third-party management firms in the country with a portfolio spanning multifamily, student housing, affordable housing, and build-to-rent, is hiring an Administrative Assistant for its corporate office in Houston. This is a front-desk-anchored position. You're the first voice callers hear and the first face visitors see, which means you set the tone for how the company presents itself day to day.

The work is varied and moves quickly. You'll manage incoming calls, route messages, greet visitors, handle mail and package logistics (UPS, FedEx, and the like), and keep fax and filing systems in order. Beyond that, you'll take on word processing, spreadsheet work, report formatting, and presentations as requested. The ability to manage several things at once without letting anything slip is genuinely important here, not a line buried in a job description.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Solid basic computer skills, including word processing, spreadsheets, and database entry
  • Comfort with office software and the ability to learn company-specific platforms
  • Clear, professional communication, both written and verbal
  • Strong organizational habits and follow-through on tasks without being reminded

No travel is required. This is an onsite position.

One thing worth knowing: corporate office admin roles at large third-party management firms tend to expose you to a lot of the business quickly. You'll field calls from site teams, vendors, and ownership groups. You'll see how a company that manages thousands of units across multiple asset classes actually operates at the home office level. For someone who wants to grow into property operations, asset management coordination, or corporate support roles, there are worse places to start building that fluency.

Asset Living holds an AMO designation through IREM and has consistently ranked among the NMHC top 50. The company has grown significantly over the past decade, and the Houston corporate office reflects that scale.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Olympus Alameda
job.description:
It's Tuesday morning, and three work orders from the night before are already in the queue. One resident lost heat, another has a leaking faucet under the kitchen sink, and a dryer in unit 214 stopped spinning. By noon, all three are closed out. That rhythm, varied, physical, and genuinely useful, is what defines a day in this role.

What This Role Covers

Olympus Property is bringing on a full-time Maintenance Technician for Olympus Alameda in Albuquerque. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with availability for emergency calls as needed. You'll work alongside the Lead Maintenance Tech and the broader service team to keep apartment homes and common areas in good working order.

The work spans a wide range of trades. On any given week, you might be handling HVAC preventative maintenance, cleaning coils and swapping filters, then shifting to minor plumbing repairs, fixture replacements, or appliance work on refrigerators, washers, dryers, and stoves. Electrical fixture and switch repairs, lock changes, door hardware, painting, carpentry, and pool and grounds upkeep all fall within scope. Service requests are tracked through software, so comfort with basic digital tools matters. You'll also help keep the maintenance shop organized and inventory accounted for.

This is a property that takes make-ready quality seriously. Residents notice when things are done right the first time, and so does the team.

What You'll Need

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • CPO (Certified Pool Operator) certification (required)
  • Comfort working across trades: plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting
  • Ability to respond to emergency maintenance requests outside regular hours

Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three consecutive years, 2023, 2024, and 2025. That recognition tends to reflect something real about how companies treat the people doing hands-on work. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, educational assistance with tuition reimbursement, and monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility. Pay is experience-based.

From a career standpoint, a role like this builds the kind of cross-trade fluency that opens doors. Technicians who develop strong HVAC diagnostics alongside solid plumbing and electrical skills tend to move into Lead Tech positions faster than those who specialize narrowly. From Lead Tech, the natural next step is Service Manager, a role that adds team oversight, capex planning, and vendor coordination to the skill set. If you're two or three years into maintenance work and want a company where that path is clearly defined, this is worth a close look.

job.title: Services Coordinator I (Chestnut Square Senior)
job.description:
Affordable housing communities serving seniors carry a layer of complexity that standard property management roles don't. Residents may be navigating health challenges, language barriers, financial instability, or social isolation, and the property staff who show up daily are often their most consistent point of contact. The Services Coordinator role at MidPen's Chestnut Square Senior community in Livermore exists to fill that gap: organized programming, genuine outreach, and the kind of steady follow-through that helps residents stay housed and connected.

This is a ground-level human services role attached to an affordable housing property. You're not a case manager, but you'll do crisis intervention for low-to-moderate situations and make sure mandated reporting procedures are followed when needed. You're not a social worker by license, but you'll work alongside community agencies and monitor how partner services are actually landing with residents. The work is relational and administrative in equal measure.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

On a typical day you might run a health or wellness workshop in the morning, spend part of the afternoon doing door-to-door outreach to residents who haven't engaged with a program yet, then close out by entering data into Salesforce and drafting a report for an external agency partner. You'll coordinate food distribution, support financial literacy programming, and help new residents find their footing in the community. Some evenings run until 7:00 PM, and the schedule is Monday through Friday with at least one evening shift per week built in. If you've worked in after-school programs or senior services, that rhythm will feel familiar.

Communication is a real part of the job. The resident population at a senior affordable community often includes people whose primary language isn't English, and you'll use translation tools and services regularly. Bilingual skills are a plus and may be required depending on the specific population at Chestnut Square. The posting is honest that this varies by property.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of experience working with older adults, youth, or diverse adult populations in a service, classroom, or community setting
  • High school diploma or GED required; progress toward an associate's or bachelor's degree is preferred
  • Comfortable with the Microsoft Office suite, Outlook, Teams, and ideally Salesforce for tracking and reporting
  • Strong organizational habits, because documentation and timely reporting are non-negotiable parts of the role
  • Calm judgment in moments of resident crisis, and the discretion to know when to escalate

What separates strong candidates here is experience with populations that don't always self-advocate or walk through an open door. Residents who most need services are often the hardest to reach. If you've done outreach work before, especially door-to-door or phone-based engagement, that skill transfers directly. The ability to build trust slowly and consistently matters more than any single credential.

Pay ranges from $24.62 to $27.70 per hour based on experience. MidPen offers a full benefits package including health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, and an employee education reimbursement program, among others.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set, and this role at Hawthorne Residential Partners' Trilliam community in Clanton, Alabama puts that skill set to daily use. You'll draw on sales technique, relationship management, and clear communication from the moment a prospect calls or walks in, and you'll build sharper versions of those skills with every lease you close and every resident interaction you handle well.

Skills This Role Requires on Day One

Confidence in front of people is the baseline. You're conducting apartment tours, fielding phone and email inquiries, and converting traffic into signed leases. That means you need to read what a prospect actually wants, match the community's value to their specific situation, and follow up without being pushy. Customer service experience translates directly here. Sales experience translates even more directly. Neither is formally required, but the role moves fast enough that coachability matters just as much as raw experience.

Accuracy matters too. Processing leasing applications, running verifications, and completing move-in paperwork correctly isn't just administrative work. Errors at that stage create problems that ripple through the lease term. Attention to detail is a real requirement, not a box to check.

Skills This Role Actively Develops

Leasing consultants who pay attention build a working knowledge of occupancy strategy, renewal rate management, and how concessions affect the property's overall performance. You won't own those decisions at this level, but you'll be close enough to them to understand how your daily leasing activity connects to community-wide goals. That context accelerates your career.

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real structure, not just a talking point. The stated trajectory from leasing consultant to assistant community manager reflects how most strong leasing professionals move up inside a management company. The skills you develop here, specifically objection handling, CRM follow-up discipline, and resident relations, are the same skills that distinguish a capable assistant manager from one who struggles.

  • Lead-to-lease conversion through follow-up and relationship building
  • Resident event coordination and community engagement
  • Social media and local outreach to support property marketing
  • Monitoring competitor properties and local market activity
  • Maintaining a clean, professional leasing office and common areas

What Makes This Worth Considering

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off per week keeps the total at 40 hours. Resident events or community-specific needs may occasionally extend that, which is standard for leasing roles at engaged communities.

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, along with leasing incentive programs. For someone who closes consistently, the commission structure makes a real difference in take-home pay. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance.

A valid driver's license is required. A CALP designation is a plus. A high school diploma or GED is the minimum education requirement. Hawthorne is an equal opportunity employer.

job.title: Recertification Specialist
job.description:
Recertification work sits at one of the more technically demanding intersections in affordable housing administration. The paperwork has to be right, the timing has to be right, and the resident experience has to stay intact through all of it. This role at Metromark Apartments in Jamaica Plain puts you at that intersection, supporting the property management team on the full cycle of tenant recertification for an affordable housing community operated by John M. Corcoran and Company, a firm that has been active in New England real estate since 1951.

The day-to-day centers on scheduling and coordinating recertification interviews, keeping resident files current and compliant with both company standards and regulatory agency requirements, and supporting apartment inspections tied to the recertification process. You'll also assist with waitlist management and applicant processing, which means you'll see both ends of the occupancy picture: existing residents moving through annual recerts and prospective residents working through the intake pipeline. Beyond those core responsibilities, the role connects to general office operations, including rent collection, maintenance request processing, phone coverage, and occasional support for resident activities.

Part-time at 24 hours per week across three days, with flexibility on which days those are. That structure works well for someone who wants meaningful, substantive work without a full-time schedule, though the compliance nature of recertification means the work itself is rarely lightweight. Affordable housing recertification carries real regulatory weight. Errors in income verification, household composition, or file documentation can affect a property's standing with oversight agencies. Attention to detail here compounds directly into the property's compliance health.

What separates strong candidates in this kind of role is comfort sitting inside a process that is highly structured by external rules while still communicating warmly with residents who may find recertification confusing or stressful. The administrative skill set is table stakes. The candidates who thrive long-term are the ones who can explain a document checklist to a resident in plain language and then turn around and maintain airtight files for a regulatory audit.

From a career trajectory standpoint, recertification experience is a genuine differentiator in affordable housing property management. It's one of the few administrative roles that builds direct fluency in compliance frameworks like HUD, LIHTC, or Section 8, depending on the property's funding structure. That knowledge transfers cleanly into leasing compliance roles, assistant property manager positions at affordable communities, and eventually site management or portfolio compliance roles. JMC's tenure history suggests real internal mobility for people who perform well and want to grow.

What You'll Bring

  • At least two years in an administrative role, ideally in property management or a regulated industry
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work clearly with residents, staff, and regulatory contacts
  • Organizational discipline to manage multiple resident files simultaneously while keeping everything current and accurate
  • Solid computer skills across standard office software
  • Familiarity with affordable housing regulations is a real advantage, though not a hard requirement

The pay range runs from $25.75 to $31.00 per hour, and the position includes a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus paid time off, holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
A resident puts in a service ticket at 8 a.m. for a broken furnace. By noon, your tech has resolved it, closed the ticket, and you've already followed up with the resident directly. That's the standard you set at Timber Hollow Apartments in Fairfield, Ohio.

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor to lead the maintenance operation at this community. The role covers the full scope: hands-on repairs, team leadership, make-ready management, and keeping the property running safely and cleanly day to day.

What the Job Covers

You'll lead a team of maintenance techs and community care associates. That means hiring, scheduling, training, and holding people accountable to consistent standards. You'll manage the turn process closely, coordinating make-ready timelines so vacant units get back online fast and new residents can move in on time.

On the technical side, you'll troubleshoot and repair HVAC systems, handle electrical and plumbing issues, and manage appliance repairs. You'll also oversee grounds upkeep and general building cleanliness, enforce 24/7 emergency coverage through monthly staffing schedules, and make sure all work follows applicable building codes and safety standards.

Resident service is central to this role. Timely follow-through on service tickets matters here. Residents notice when things get fixed quickly and when they don't.

What You Need

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Solid HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Valid driver's license
  • CPO certification (a plus)
  • Demonstrated experience leading a maintenance team
  • Attention to detail on punch lists and turn timelines

The strongest candidates in this role tend to be the ones who can move between managing people and doing hands-on technical work without losing quality on either end. If you're used to delegating everything or fixing everything yourself, this role will push you to do both well at the same time.

Cottonwood offers competitive pay with a bonus structure, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within 30 days, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance techs at a luxury community earn their pay in the details. A scuff on a freshly painted wall before move-in, a pool chemical reading that's two points off, an HVAC unit that starts cycling too long on a Florida afternoon. This role at Waypoint Management Services in Daytona Beach demands the kind of attention that keeps a high-end property running the way residents expect it to.

The Work Itself

Your day centers on keeping the property in condition. That means diagnosing and repairing plumbing, HVAC, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. It means completing make-readies that are actually ready, walking units with a critical eye before a new resident signs off on their keys. You'll coordinate with contractors on punch list items, run preventive maintenance on HVAC equipment on a scheduled basis, and keep pool chemical logs current. Priority work orders carry a 24-hour resolution standard, and you'll carry on-call availability to back that up. Grounds upkeep, trash compactor maintenance, gate and security equipment checks: all of it falls within your scope.

EPA Section 608 Type I and II certification is required coming in. A CPO is a plus and makes practical sense given the pool responsibilities in a Florida climate. OSHA standards aren't background knowledge here; you apply them daily.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Hands-on experience across multiple trade areas: plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, general repairs
  • EPA 608 Type I and II certification (required)
  • Comfort working from a scheduled PM calendar, not just reactive work orders
  • A service orientation that holds up under pressure from residents who expect fast, professional responses
  • On-call availability and the reliability to follow through on it
  • High school diploma or equivalent, plus relevant field experience or technical training

Working at Waypoint

Waypoint operates a growing portfolio, and this is a luxury community where the bar for presentation and response time is genuinely higher than at a Class B or C asset. The company offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, 401k with matching, an employee referral program, and an onsite housing discount. Bonus and incentive opportunities are part of the package as well.

One practical note for anyone considering this role: Florida's heat load means HVAC preventive maintenance isn't a once-a-year checkbox. Units that aren't properly serviced fail during peak summer demand, which drives up emergency calls and resident complaints. Techs who stay ahead of the PM schedule make a measurable difference in how the property performs operationally and how residents experience it. That's the kind of contribution Waypoint is looking for here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (268) Aubrey, TX
job.description:
Maintenance technicians carry the physical plant of a property on their backs. Leasing fills units, management sets policy, but the tech keeps the asset running. At a vertically integrated owner-operator like Berkshire Residential, that role carries real weight because the same team that manages the property also owns it. There's no third-party management buffer. When something breaks at Villages 3Eighty in Aubrey, TX, it matters directly to the balance sheet.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a general maintenance technician position covering the full range of day-to-day needs at a residential community. You'll handle service requests across appliances, plumbing, electrical, and carpentry. Curb appeal and unit condition fall in your lane too, which means keeping an eye on the property the same way a good tech always does: not waiting to be told something looks off. Inventory control, equipment upkeep, and key security are part of the routine. You'll work alongside the on-site management team and be expected to hold community standards without needing someone to spell them out every time.

Berkshire is a self-managing owner, so the maintenance team here reports into a structure that actually cares about preservation and NOI, not just getting tickets closed. That can be a better environment to work in. It can also mean higher expectations.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on residential maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with basic computer use and written communication in English
  • Steady, dependable presence. Residents notice inconsistency fast.

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who take pride in a tight make-ready, catch a punch list item before a manager does, and treat a resident's service request like it actually matters. That instinct either exists or it doesn't. A year of experience is the floor here, but attitude carries more weight than most postings admit.

Berkshire lists benefits including three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, health insurance, and personal development planning. For a technician role, that's a competitive package worth factoring into your read of the opportunity.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultants carry more of the operation than the title suggests. At a well-run community, they're touching traffic, applications, renewals, move-ins, move-outs, delinquency follow-up, and make-ready walks all in the same week. Weinstein Properties, a Richmond-based owner-operator with a multi-state portfolio spanning Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, is adding a Leasing Consultant at their Bexley community in Mt. Juliet, TN.

The Day-to-Day

The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, Saturdays 9 to 5 on a team rotation, Sundays closed. Pay is $21 per hour with quarterly bonuses. Worth noting: this is not commission-based, which tends to produce a different kind of leasing culture, one where the team isn't competing for every lead and resident service gets treated as part of the job, not a distraction from it.

On any given day, you'll work internet leads and phone calls, schedule tours, process applications, and put together lease paperwork through move-in. On the resident side, that means renewals, notices to vacate, early terminations, pet addenda, transfers, account questions, and work order follow-up. You'll coordinate with maintenance to confirm apartments are ready, walk units to confirm punch list items are cleared, and handle move-out processing including security deposit dispositions. Rent posting and balance follow-up are also part of the role, as is occasional resident event planning.

That's a full-cycle leasing role. The administrative load is real, and attention to detail matters more here than a lot of postings let on.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

They're open to candidates coming from customer service, sales, or hospitality backgrounds, not just people with prior property management experience. Training is provided. That said, the candidates who tend to hit the ground running bring:

  • Strong administrative skills and genuine organizational follow-through
  • A high sense of urgency without burning out on the details
  • Articulate communication, especially in difficult or persuasive conversations
  • Self-motivation and a preference for staying busy
  • A warm, professional manner with both prospects and current residents

Weinstein promotes from within and has the portfolio to support that. A Leasing Consultant who performs well here has a clear path toward Assistant Manager and eventually Community Manager, particularly across a company that owns and manages its own assets rather than operating as a third-party manager. That structure means decisions get made closer to the property, which tends to matter when you're trying to build a career rather than just fill a role.

job.title: Services Coordinator I (Open Doors)
job.description:
Relationship skills drive this role more than anything else. The ability to knock on a stranger's door, introduce yourself, and leave that person feeling genuinely welcomed into their community is the core competency MidPen is hiring for at Open Doors in Los Gatos. Program coordination and documentation matter too, but they're in service of that human connection.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

On a typical day, you might run an after-school session for kids ages 5 to 12 in the morning, coordinate a health workshop for families in the afternoon, and follow up with a resident who flagged a financial hardship. Door-to-door outreach is a regular part of the week, especially when new residents move in and need to know what's available to them. You'll also handle documentation for both MidPen's internal systems and external agency partners, so accuracy in Salesforce and Microsoft Office Suite is genuinely part of the job, not an afterthought.

Crisis intervention comes up. The role involves low-to-moderate situations requiring sound judgment, discretion, and knowledge of mandated reporting procedures. You won't be doing this alone, but you do need to be comfortable assessing a situation and knowing when to escalate. Strong problem-solving instincts and a calm, steady approach matter here.

Collaboration with the property management team is built into the role. You'll share what you're hearing from residents, flag emerging needs, and help shape the property's service plan. That bridge between resident services and operations is something MidPen takes seriously across its portfolio of more than 130 communities.

Skills This Role Demands

  • Community outreach and relationship-building with diverse, multilingual populations
  • Program facilitation across age groups including youth, families, and older adults
  • Documentation and reporting for both internal compliance and external agency requirements
  • Comfort communicating across language barriers, using translation tools when needed (bilingual ability may be required depending on resident population)
  • Independent time management across multiple concurrent programs and priorities

The MidPen Context

MidPen has been developing and managing affordable housing in Northern California since 1970, and their resident services model reflects that depth of experience. Open Doors is a family property, which means your caseload will include children and youth programming alongside adult services like ESL support, financial literacy, and rental assistance. The $24.62 to $27.70 hourly range reflects an entry-level coordinator tier, and for someone building a career in community development or social services, this role offers real exposure to program implementation, cross-sector partnerships, and the operational side of affordable housing. Many coordinators who grow within MidPen move into senior coordinator or program manager roles as they build portfolio experience.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with one or more evenings extending to 7 PM. That's worth knowing before you apply. Evening hours are when many working families are actually available, so it's a feature of the work, not an edge case.

Minimum qualifications include a high school diploma or GED plus one year of relevant experience in community development, social services, youth programming, or related fields. Progress toward a two or four-year degree is preferred.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance supervision in multifamily housing sits at the intersection of physical asset management and team leadership. The person in this role carries responsibility for both the condition of the property and the performance of the people maintaining it. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, that dual accountability shows up every day at Avenues of West Ashley, a residential community in Charleston's West Ashley corridor.

What the Role Demands

Hawthorne requires at least three years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience or equivalent trade background in HVAC, plumbing, or electrical. Prior lead or supervisory experience is strongly preferred, and you'll need a valid driver's license and EPA certification coming in. CPO certification is highly preferred and may be required depending on state regulations. A high school diploma or GED rounds out the baseline.

Day to day, you'll lead and schedule your maintenance team, assign and track work orders, supervise vendor partners, and manage the budget and inventory for your department. Unit turns fall under your direct oversight: you'll coordinate make-ready schedules and personally inspect vacants before move-in to confirm cleanliness, function, and presentation. On the preventative side, you'll execute quarterly PM programs covering HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems. Capital improvement projects also land on your plate, from pulling bids to overseeing execution. On-call emergency rotation is part of the schedule, as is occasional support for resident events.

What the Role Builds

Supervisors who come from a strong trade background often develop their management craft in roles like this one. Running a team, managing vendor relationships, controlling departmental spend, and keeping occupancy-ready unit counts on track are skills that translate directly to Regional Maintenance Director paths and eventually Director of Facilities roles at the portfolio level. Hawthorne supports that trajectory through a formal Career Path Program, a dedicated Learning and Development team, and an education reimbursement program specifically aimed at maintenance skill growth.

Strong candidates in this role bring more than technical competence. The supervisors who perform best here are the ones who can hold their team accountable without micromanaging, read a punch list as both a quality control tool and a training opportunity, and communicate clearly with the property management team about timelines and budget. Technical problem-solving gets you in the door. Consistent follow-through and organized documentation keep the asset performing.

  • Minimum 3 years apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience
  • EPA certification required; CPO certification highly preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Prior supervisory or lead technician experience strongly preferred
  • High School diploma or GED equivalent

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance Technicians at Berkshire's Residence at Chris Wren carry the physical condition of the property on their shoulders. That means handling work orders across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry, keeping up with make-readies between turns, and making sure curb appeal doesn't slip. You'll also help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security, which sounds minor until something goes missing or breaks at the wrong moment.

Residents notice everything. A slow response on a leaking faucet or a unit that isn't punched out properly before move-in reflects on the whole community. This role requires someone who takes those details personally without being told to.

A realistic day includes a mix of scheduled work orders, a few surprises, and probably a conversation with a resident who's frustrated about something. The ability to stay even-keeled and professional through all three is what separates the people who last in this work from those who don't. After-hours calls happen. That's part of the job, and it's worth knowing that going in.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Comfort with basic computer use and related applications for work order management
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • The kind of attention to detail that catches a punch list item before a resident does

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions move through one organization rather than through a third-party management structure. For maintenance staff, that typically translates to clearer accountability and less friction when you need something approved or sourced. The company offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, insurance, and personal development plans. There's also a $1,000 sign-on bonus, paid out after 90 days.

Strong maintenance techs who build solid relationships with their service managers often move into lead technician or maintenance supervisor roles over time. If you're consistent, communicative, and technically sharp, that path is real here.

job.title: Evening Concierge (Mon - Fri, 3-11PM) - D.C.
job.description:
Bozzuto's residential portfolio in Washington, D.C. carries a particular standard. The company manages some of the more design-forward, amenity-rich communities in the region, and the front desk is where that standard either holds or slips. This Evening Concierge role, running Monday through Friday from 3 to 11 p.m., is the shift when residents actually come home. That distinction matters more than it sounds.

The 3-to-11 window is the most resident-facing part of any weekday. You're greeting people returning from long commutes, fielding package deliveries during the holiday crunch, and fielding requests that have stacked up since morning. The role asks for genuine hospitality instincts, the kind built through actual experience in hotels, travel, or retail service environments. Knowing a resident's name matters. Knowing their dog's name matters more. That level of personalization is what separates a concierge who logs entries from one who builds a community.

Beyond the desk, you'll coordinate resident events meant to create real engagement, manage reservations for shared spaces like club rooms and freight elevators, and keep package rooms organized well enough to handle high-volume periods without chaos. Social media presence is part of the job too, both generating interest in the community and encouraging satisfied residents to share their experiences publicly.

What the role asks for

  • At least two years in hospitality, hotel, retail, or a travel-related service environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, polished appearance, and comfort with software and apps
  • An instinct for anticipating what someone needs before they ask for it
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds (package volume gets real in December)

The salary range for this position is $48,000 to $51,000, with eligibility for additional bonus opportunities. Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One honest note for candidates considering this path: the evening concierge role at a well-run luxury community is a credible entry point into property management. People who develop genuine rapport with residents and demonstrate operational reliability often move into leasing or assistant community manager positions. The skills built here, resident relations, event execution, front-of-house operations, carry directly into those next steps.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician - Dallas, TX
job.description:
Valet trash is one of those amenity services that residents notice immediately when it's done poorly and rarely think about when it's done right. That invisibility is actually the standard. Cortland is hiring a Front Door Waste Technician to run that service at a multifamily community in Dallas, keeping common areas clean, routes completed on schedule, and the resident-facing experience consistent every day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is an outdoor, physical role with a defined route and a real finish line each shift. You'll collect waste bags from resident doorsteps, load them into leak-proof hampers and carts, transfer everything to the designated vehicle, and dispose of it into onsite compactors or containers. Beyond the primary route, you're also clearing debris from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and compactor zones. Sidewalks and doorsteps get cleaned as you go. You'll walk stairs, cover significant ground on foot, and lift up to 50 pounds regularly.

Each shift, you log start and end times, document your work through a mobile app, and flag any improper or prohibited waste. You're expected to follow EPA and OSHA safety protocols throughout. If a resident, staff member, or manager crosses your path, you represent Cortland in that interaction. The customer service piece isn't secondary here. It's part of the job description for a reason.

Dallas summers are real. You'll work through heat, humidity, and whatever weather shows up, and you'll encounter strong odors as a matter of course. That's worth saying plainly so there are no surprises.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Ability to read and follow written instructions and operate basic equipment
  • Valid Class E driver's license with the ability to drive locally
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan and email access for daily documentation
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs in varying outdoor conditions

Strong candidates in this role tend to be self-managed. The route is yours to own. A supervisor won't walk it with you every day, so people who take pride in finishing a job correctly without being watched are the ones who tend to stick and grow here. Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with genuine internal mobility, and maintenance-adjacent roles like this one have historically been a foot in the door for candidates who want to move into broader property operations over time.

job.title: Vice President, Affordable Housing
job.description:
A Monday morning call lands on your calendar: a LIHTC property in your portfolio just received notice of an upcoming NSPIRE inspection, recertifications are running behind, and the site manager needs coaching before the auditors arrive. That's the kind of moment this role is built for.

What This Role Actually Covers

As Vice President of Affordable Housing Operations at Asset Living, you're the offsite operational leader for a portfolio that spans LIHTC, HUD, and other affordable regulatory programs. That means you're accountable for the full picture at every site: people, leasing performance, financial health, maintenance standards, and regulatory compliance. You're not reviewing reports from a distance. You're diagnosing problems early, coaching site staff through them, and making sure ownership clients get accurate, timely information.

On the financial side, you'll build and defend annual operating budgets, monitor NOI trends, flag expense variances, and bring capital improvement recommendations forward at the right time. You'll also keep a close eye on rent collections, deposit reconciliation, and property closeouts. Asset Living operates as a third-party fee management firm, so your ability to communicate proactively with clients and translate operational data into clear recommendations matters as much as your internal execution.

Leasing and compliance here aren't separate tracks. You'll make sure site staff understand how to lease within affordable program requirements, and you'll work directly with the compliance team to keep certifications and recertifications on schedule. NSPIRE preparation is part of your administrative oversight as well.

The People Side of the Job

A significant part of your time goes toward your teams. You'll hire, train, coach, and when necessary, counsel and separate staff using consistent, well-documented processes. You'll coordinate with HR and senior leadership on performance issues and compensation reviews, approve timesheets, and actively work to build site cultures where people perform well and stay. Affordable housing communities often carry higher operational complexity than conventional properties, and the staff on the ground feel that weight daily. Your job is to make sure they're equipped to handle it.

  • Proven experience overseeing affordable housing portfolios with LIHTC and HUD programs
  • Strong grasp of compliance requirements including certifications, recertifications, and NSPIRE standards
  • Demonstrated ability to develop budgets, analyze financials, and drive NOI improvement
  • Experience managing and developing on-site teams across multiple locations
  • Effective communicator with ownership clients and internal leadership
  • Fair housing knowledge and consistent application of company policies

What separates strong candidates from average ones in a VP-level affordable housing role is usually this: the ability to hold compliance rigor and people leadership in equal regard at the same time. Properties that run well under regulatory scrutiny almost always have a VP who treats staff development as seriously as they treat file audits. If you've built that balance across a multi-site portfolio, this role will fit how you already work.

Asset Living is one of the larger third-party management firms in the country, ranked in the NMHC top 50 and recognized as an Accredited Management Organization through IREM. The Atlanta base puts you close to a significant concentration of affordable housing development activity in the Southeast, where LIHTC pipelines have remained active even as other housing sectors have slowed.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Avion
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month. Rent is coming in, the delinquency list needs to be reconciled, and a resident just stopped by the office with a complaint before you've had your coffee. That's a normal Tuesday as an Assistant Manager at Avion in Bozeman, MT.

The Role at Avion

Olympus Property, a three-time National Apartment Association Top Employer (2023, 2024, and 2025), is hiring an Assistant Manager for Avion. This is a full-cycle operations role. You'll handle rent collection and daily deposits, maintain accurate resident files, process move-out account statements, and step in for the Property Manager when needed. The financial side of the job is real: receipts deposited before bank close each day, collections monitored consistently, and any liability or legal issues escalated immediately to the appropriate parties.

The role also keeps you close to the leasing floor. You'll help show apartments, support resident retention efforts, and participate in community events. Before move-ins, you'll walk make-ready units to confirm they're turn-complete and ready for a new resident. You'll also stay current on the Bozeman submarket: new construction, hiring trends, nearby retail activity, anything that could affect occupancy or income at the property.

Olympus expects you to carry their core values into every interaction: customer care, teamwork, trust, family, and fun. That's not decorative language. It shows up in how the office runs, how your team treats residents, and how leadership treats you.

What You Bring

  • Onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Comfort with financial record-keeping, rent collection processes, and daily deposits
  • Experience with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite (strongly preferred)
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with flexibility for resident events and the first weekend of each month
  • Detail orientation and a systematic approach to managing both people and paperwork

Pay runs $23 to $25 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly renewal bonuses and quarterly incentives. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, sabbatical eligibility, and structured career pathing.

From a growth standpoint, the Assistant Manager seat is one of the most direct paths to a Property Manager role in multifamily. The skills you build here, specifically financial accountability, collections discipline, and the ability to cover full operations during a manager's absence, are exactly what regional teams look for when they're evaluating internal candidates for promotion. If you're a Leasing Consultant ready to move up, or an Assistant Manager looking to grow with a company that has formal career pathing built in, Avion is worth a close look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles exist because traffic doesn't convert itself. Someone has to answer the phone, walk the prospect, follow up, close the lease, and still have enough energy left to handle the renewal question from the resident in 204. At Weinstein Properties' Bexley 3Five community in South Austin, that person is you.

Weinstein is a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business and a portfolio of 60-plus communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity in this industry means they've figured out what works, and a big part of that is how they develop people. They're upfront that they hire for attitude and train for skill. Plenty of their strongest performers came in with zero leasing background.

What the Role Actually Looks Like

This is a front-line leasing position. You'll be the first voice a prospect hears and the first face they see when they walk in. Your days will include handling inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, inspecting units, following up on leads, and supporting current residents. There's administrative work woven in too: applications, documentation, the general operational rhythm of keeping a leasing office running. Expect to be on your feet. Expect variety. The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6 and Saturdays 9 to 5 on a rotation with the team. Sundays are closed.

Pay starts at $20 per hour and moves up with experience. Quarterly bonuses are part of the comp structure, along with a rent discount, health, dental and vision coverage, 401k with company match, paid holidays, and birthday time off. There's also a $500 sign-on bonus (details covered during the interview).

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Strong communication skills, in person and in writing
  • A genuine interest in helping people and solving problems
  • The ability to stay organized and positive when priorities shift mid-day
  • Team-first attitude: willing to pitch in beyond the job description
  • Goal orientation and the drive to grow within the company

Leasing experience is not required. What they're screening for is work ethic, warmth, and the kind of adaptability that holds up when a walk-in arrives five minutes before close.

One thing worth knowing about this trajectory: leasing consultant is one of the most common entry points into property management careers. People who excel here often move into assistant manager or property manager roles, sometimes within a year or two. Weinstein has clearly built that pipeline internally. If you're thinking about this as a long-term industry career rather than a short-term job, that context matters.

job.title: Central Leasing Administrator - any region
job.description:
Centralized leasing functions have become more common as operators look to consolidate traffic handling, reduce per-unit overhead, and keep occupancy steady across a portfolio without staffing every property at full strength. MG Properties, which has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over three decades, runs a Central Leasing team out of an approved property location. This role sits inside that structure.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this position is phone-based sales and lease administration. Prospects come in through the CRM and Elise AI, and your job is to screen those leads, qualify applicants thoroughly, and convert traffic into signed leases. Strong phone skills aren't a nice-to-have here; they're the primary tool. You'll maintain prospect lists, prepare lease files, process applications, and oversee lease signings for new residents. Monthly administrative tasks, move-in paperwork, and making sure files are organized and complete are also part of the rhythm.

Because this is a centralized role, you'll be handling inquiries across properties rather than walking one community. That means staying sharp on availability, qualification criteria, and fair housing compliance without a site manager standing nearby. You'll also route resident and vendor calls to the right departments, which requires knowing the operation well enough to triage quickly.

What Makes Someone Good at This

  • Genuine comfort on the phone, including with objections, difficult callers, and back-to-back volume
  • Accuracy with data entry and lease documentation. Errors in lease files create downstream problems at move-in and beyond
  • Familiarity with CRM platforms and the ability to pick up new software without extended hand-holding
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing, FCRA, and ADA requirements in a multifamily context
  • Ability to stay organized across multiple prospect pipelines at once

Candidates who come from on-site leasing backgrounds tend to ramp quickly here, since the fundamentals carry over. The adjustment is volume and pace rather than skill set. Centralized leasing roles also build a kind of portfolio-level awareness that's useful if you eventually move into a leasing manager, regional support, or training role.

Compensation runs $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience. The position is full-time, five days per week in office. MG Properties offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, and company profit sharing.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a leasing calendar that leaves almost no margin for error. Pre-leasing for the next academic year starts while current residents are still mid-lease, and by the time summer turn arrives, the property needs to flip hundreds of units in a matter of weeks. Every interaction between now and then either builds occupancy or chips away at it. That's the operational reality this role sits inside.

The Scion Group is hiring a Leasing Consultant (internally called an Experience Team Member) for Alight West Lafayette, a student housing community near Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana. The position spans leasing, marketing, customer experience, and day-to-day property administration. It's a genuinely cross-functional role at the front lines of the asset's performance.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your primary job is converting traffic into signed leases. That means community tours, follow-up communication, and staying sharp on objection handling. You'll feed feedback on sales barriers back to the management team, which matters because pricing and concession decisions get made partly on what leasing staff hear directly from prospects. You'll also assist with social media content and local marketing outreach, helping the property stay visible in a competitive college market where students are comparing multiple options online before they ever walk through the door.

On the administrative side, the role covers package management, office and amenity upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout duty on a rotating on-call basis. Turn periods are a specific availability requirement. If you haven't worked a student housing turn before, expect a compressed, high-volume push where make-readies need to happen fast and coordination between leasing, maintenance, and vendors is constant.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A customer-first approach with genuine comfort talking to a wide range of people
  • Flexibility to work daytime business hours, weekends, and participate in an after-hours on-call rotation
  • Availability during summer and turn periods, which are the highest-stakes weeks of the student housing calendar
  • Self-discipline and reliability without needing constant direction
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort with social media platforms

The strongest candidates in this type of role tend to be people who treat every prospect interaction like it affects occupancy, because it does. In student housing, word of mouth travels fast across campus. One bad tour experience gets shared; so does a great one. The leasing staff sets the tone for how the community is perceived before a student ever signs a lease.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. This is a full-time, non-exempt position based on-site at Alight West Lafayette.

job.title: Regional Leasing Consultant (Santa Clara)
job.description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group operates a sizable portfolio of communities across the Bay Area, and this Regional Leasing Consultant role sits at the intersection of sales, customer service, and day-to-day leasing operations. At properties with real traffic volume, the person in this seat shapes occupancy numbers more directly than most people outside the leasing office realize.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your days will shift between guiding prospects through the leasing experience, handling the administrative side of the role (market surveys, rental agreements, ad postings, neighborhood reports), and making sure current residents feel genuinely taken care of. The sales piece is real: you're converting future residents into signed leases, which means understanding the product, reading the prospect, and knowing when to move someone forward. The admin piece is also real, and it's where a lot of newer leasing consultants get surprised. Good lease files and accurate reporting aren't glamorous, but they matter to how a property runs.

Weekend availability is required. That's not a footnote. Bay Area apartment communities see their heaviest foot traffic on Saturdays and Sundays, and Prometheus schedules accordingly. Your days off will fall mid-week. If that works for your life, great. If it doesn't, this particular role won't be a fit.

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range runs $25.00 to $28.75, with a $200 per-lease incentive and a discretionary semi-annual bonus on top of that. Weekend shifts carry a premium. There are also additional bonus opportunities tied to referrals, renovations, and lease-up activity, which means a strong performer can meaningfully exceed base pay. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental (dependents included), 401(k) with employer match, tuition reimbursement, and tenure-based housing discounts, among others.

Who Does Well in This Role

  • Prior customer-facing experience in any industry, not necessarily property management
  • Comfortable with both the people side and the paperwork side of the job
  • Self-directed enough to manage a busy leasing floor without waiting to be told what to do next
  • Weekend availability that actually works with your schedule

For someone early in a property management career, this kind of role builds the foundation that makes everything else easier. Leasing consultants who get strong here tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles faster than people who come in from the back-office side. You learn traffic, you learn what drives a lease decision, and you learn the operational rhythm of a property all at once. That's a solid starting point.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Sugarmont Apartments sits in one of Salt Lake City's more active rental corridors, and the first impression a prospective resident gets often happens before they ever reach the leasing office. It happens in the parking lot, on the walkway, at the entrance. The Groundskeeper is the person who controls that impression every single day.

Cottonwood Residential is hiring for this role at Sugarmont, and the work is physical and concrete. You'll remove trash and litter from the grounds, sweep and pressure wash pathways and building exteriors, handle basic gardening and weeding, clean windows and common area furniture, and complete general maintenance tasks tied to the building and grounds. This is a role where the output is visible. You can look at what you did at the end of a shift and see it.

The physical demands are real and worth understanding before you apply. You'll be on your feet for most of the day, navigating elevation changes, climbing stairs and ladders, lifting up to 50 pounds, and getting into tight or awkward spaces to do the job right. On-call availability during nights and weekends is also part of the commitment.

What this role requires is reliability, attention to detail at a grounds level, and the physical stamina to work through a full shift outdoors in Utah's climate, which ranges from summer heat to winter cold. What it builds is equally practical: a working understanding of how a well-maintained property functions, familiarity with the maintenance cycle, and the kind of professional reputation that comes from showing up consistently and doing visible work well.

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking about long-term growth in property management: groundskeeping is one of the clearest entry points into maintenance technician roles. The people who advance fastest are those who treat the grounds not as isolated tasks but as part of the overall make-ready and presentation cycle for the community. That mindset, connecting curb appeal to occupancy, is something experienced maintenance supervisors and property managers notice.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Ability to read, write, and speak English well enough to process company paperwork and follow safety procedures
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs and sustain extended periods of walking, standing, stooping, kneeling, and climbing
  • Availability for on-call shifts including nights, weekends, and company events
  • Willingness to work across varied terrain and access confined or elevated areas safely

Cottonwood offers health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within the first 30 days, a 401k and HSA with company match, 10.5 paid holidays, and three weeks of paid time off available in the first year.

job.title: $1,500 Sign-On Bonus - Multisite Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a multisite role, which means your day doesn't start and end at one address. BAM Companies is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor to cover multiple properties across Indianapolis, keeping systems operational, teams productive, and residents from filing work orders twice. You'll own HVAC, plumbing, and electrical across your assigned portfolio while keeping an eye on curb appeal, common areas, and the general condition that determines whether a property holds its Class standing or quietly starts to slip.

Preventative maintenance scheduling is a real part of this job, not just a line in a posting. You'll be the person who catches the water heater before it fails in January, not after. Beyond the wrench work, you're leading and developing a team: setting standards, providing hands-on training, and doing the kind of coaching that keeps turnover on your crew from becoming someone else's make-ready backlog. Budget awareness matters here too. Managing supply purchases and keeping operations cost-effective is part of the supervisor title, not optional.

The $1,500 sign-on bonus and free rent benefit (housing discount at a BAM property) are part of the compensation package, with hourly pay ranging from $25 to $30 depending on experience.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on property maintenance experience; supervisory background is a plus
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license and a reliable vehicle for multisite travel
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • Clear communication skills, written and verbal, for coordinating with team members and property management staff

A Note on Multisite Work

Multisite maintenance roles sort candidates pretty quickly. Technicians who thrive in single-property environments sometimes struggle once the portfolio expands, because prioritization becomes the real skill. You're triaging across addresses, coordinating techs who aren't always in the same place you are, and making judgment calls about what gets done today versus what goes on the schedule. Strong candidates here tend to be people who already think in systems: they document, they delegate with clear expectations, and they don't let deferred items pile up until they become a capital problem. If you've supervised a team before, even informally, that experience will matter more than most of the technical credentials on the list.

BAM Companies was founded in 2010 and operates with an internally recognized culture they take seriously. The PTO package includes 14.5 paid holidays plus accrued PTO after 90 days, alongside medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - Brookland
job.description:
Bozzuto's maintenance teams carry real responsibility. This isn't just work order management. It's asset stewardship, resident trust, and team leadership wrapped into one physical, demanding, relationship-driven role. At Brookland in Washington, DC, the Assistant Maintenance Manager position sits at that intersection every single day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll spend your days moving between hands-on repairs and team oversight, sometimes within the same hour. A resident's HVAC ticket needs attention, a make-ready needs a punch list walk, and a vendor needs direction on a preventative maintenance item. You're not managing from a distance. You're in the work, modeling the standard you expect from the people around you.

The technical scope covers HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, along with basic carpentry, drywall, and painting. Exposure to more complex mechanical systems like boilers, chillers, or central plant equipment is a genuine advantage here. The turn and make-ready process will be part of your regular rhythm, and the attention you bring to unit readiness directly affects how quickly apartments lease and how new residents experience their first days in the community.

Preventative maintenance isn't a checkbox exercise at Bozzuto. It's how the building holds its value. You'll also handle grounds maintenance, snow removal, and general upkeep, and you'll participate in the emergency on-call rotation. Weekends are part of this role.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Five or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification
  • Solid working knowledge of OSHA, risk management, and MSDS standards
  • Supervisory experience, or a clear track record of leading others informally
  • Comfort with technology platforms, work order systems, and basic Microsoft Office tools
  • Physical capability to handle the demands of the role, including lifting up to 50 pounds frequently, climbing ladders, and working in variable weather

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is attitude toward accountability. The people who thrive here take ownership of the building the way a builder would. They notice things before residents do, close out tickets completely, and follow up without being prompted. If your instinct is to fix the root cause rather than patch the symptom, that mindset translates well.

Team Fit and What Bozzuto Offers

Bozzuto's culture leans toward care, for residents, for colleagues, and for the physical spaces people call home. That shows up in how maintenance teams are expected to communicate with residents, not just fix things and leave. Clear communication and a professional presence matter here as much as technical skill.

This position comes with a salary range of $70,000 to $75,000, plus bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. Career-wise, Assistant Maintenance Manager roles at companies like Bozzuto typically feed into Maintenance Manager and eventually Director of Facilities tracks, particularly for candidates who develop both their technical depth and their ability to coach a team.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician - Austin, TX
job.description:
Cortland runs one of the top multifamily portfolios in the country, and the physical condition of a community shows up in every resident satisfaction score, every renewal decision, and ultimately in NOI. The Front Door Waste Technician role in Austin is part of that equation. Valet trash is a resident-facing amenity, and when it runs well, it's invisible. When it doesn't, leasing traffic notices and renewals suffer. This position keeps that from happening.

The core work is straightforward: each evening you walk assigned routes through the community, collecting bagged waste from resident doorsteps, transferring it to leak-proof carts and then to onsite compactors or containers.
