Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own properties, which means you're working in-house rather than in a third-party management structure. That distinction matters: your decisions affect assets the company has a long-term stake in, and there's generally more consistency in how policies get applied. Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and health insurance benefits.

If you've been doing collections or AR work in a scattered, under-resourced environment, this is a role with real structure behind it and a portfolio large enough to keep the work substantive.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
The Role in Context

Bozzuto operates some of the most design-forward multifamily communities in the country, and in a market like Seattle, that means you're likely working in a mid-rise or high-rise building with complex mechanical systems: central plant, boilers, chillers, and the kind of infrastructure that demands real technical fluency. The Assistant Maintenance Manager role sits between hands-on trade work and team leadership, which makes it one of the more skill-compounding positions in residential property management.

What This Role Actually Involves

Day to day, you're doing two things at once: resolving maintenance issues (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances) and keeping the make-ready process moving so turns are completed on time and new residents can take occupancy without delays. Those two tracks pull in different directions when a unit is down, a service ticket is aging, and a vendor is late. Managing that tension is where the real work happens.

Beyond reactive work, you'll own preventative maintenance programs, which is where asset preservation actually lives. PM schedules catch problems before they become capital expenditures, and a manager who understands that connection tends to earn a lot of trust from ownership and leadership quickly. You'll also handle grounds upkeep, safety compliance, OSHA standards, and participate in an on-call emergency rotation on weekends.

Bozzuto's culture leans heavily on accountability and presentation. A sharp appearance and clear written communication aren't filler requirements here. Residents in Class A communities have high expectations, and your team's follow-through on service tickets directly affects satisfaction scores and renewals.

What You Bring

  • At least 5 years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Solid knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair, plus basic carpentry, drywall, and paint skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems (central plant, split systems, boilers, chillers) is a strong differentiator
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Supervisory experience and the ability to motivate a crew, not just direct one
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to handle up to 50 pounds of force frequently, climb ladders, and work in variable outdoor conditions
  • Availability for emergency on-call and weekend rotations

Where This Role Leads

The Assistant Maintenance Manager title is a genuine career inflection point. People who do this job well, specifically those who can run a clean punch list, build a reliable on-call team, and speak fluently about capex risk and preventative maintenance, move into Maintenance Manager and then Director of Facilities roles with relative speed at operators like Bozzuto. The skills you build here around systems thinking, team accountability, and resident-facing communication transfer directly into senior operations roles. The salary range for this position is $62,000 to $67,000, with bonus eligibility, plus a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Bilingual Leasing Hub Associate - Dallas, TX
job.description:
Centralized leasing hubs have become a meaningful operational shift in multifamily management. Rather than placing leasing consultants at individual communities, companies like Cortland route prospect traffic through a dedicated team that handles volume across an entire portfolio. This role sits inside that model, and understanding that context matters before you apply.

This is not a community-based position. You won't be walking prospects through a model unit or staffing a leasing office. Instead, you'll work from a hub environment, handling inbound and outbound contact across Cortland's Dallas-area communities, converting leads into scheduled tours for onsite teams. On a typical day, that means working a queue of 40 to 50 leads sourced through RealPage, responding across phone, email, and text, and keeping communication warm enough that prospects stay engaged until they sit down with a community team. The goal is appointments, and the metric is consistent.

What This Role Actually Requires

Two or more years of customer service experience, ideally with a sales component, is the baseline. You need genuine comfort with high-contact outbound work, because the volume here is real and the pace reflects it. Written communication matters as much as verbal skill since a significant portion of lead nurturing happens over email and text. Proficiency in OneSite is listed as a requirement; familiarity with L2L is a plus. Bilingual fluency, English plus one additional language, is a stated qualification, and given Dallas's resident demographics, Spanish fluency carries practical weight in this market.

What This Role Builds

Hub leasing develops a specific kind of skill that's harder to build in a single-site role: the ability to pitch multiple communities fluently, reading what a prospect values and pivoting your positioning accordingly. You'll develop deep familiarity with Cortland's portfolio, pricing structure, and community-level amenities across locations, rather than one property's features. That cross-portfolio fluency is genuinely transferable. Associates who perform well here often move into senior leasing roles, community management tracks, or training and development positions within larger operators.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is less about charm and more about discipline. The pipeline doesn't manage itself. Candidates who thrive tend to treat each lead as a fresh opportunity regardless of where they are in the day, maintain consistent follow-up cadence, and know how to match a prospect's needs to a specific community rather than pitching generically. If you've worked in a call center, inside sales, or a high-traffic leasing environment and you've built habits around lead tracking and follow-through, that background translates directly here.

job.title: Community Manager-Fountain Wood
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning. A vendor is late on a turn, your leasing team has three tours back-to-back, and a resident just escalated a noise complaint that's been sitting in the queue since Friday. That's the job. Cortland is hiring a Community Manager for Fountain Wood in Euless, TX, and they need someone who handles all of it without losing composure.

What the Role Actually Involves

You're responsible for the full operation of a multimillion-dollar multifamily community. That means owning NOI, managing a leasing team, keeping occupancy and revenue targets on track, and making sure the physical asset stays in shape. You'll review financial performance regularly, manage budgets and expense control, and use community metrics to make real decisions, not just report numbers upward.

On the leasing side, you set goals, coach the team on conversion and follow-up, and partner with marketing on campaigns and social media. You're not just monitoring traffic; you're actively shaping how prospects experience the community from first contact through move-in.

Operations include vendor management, contract oversight, property inspections, and compliance with Fair Housing, OSHA, and company policy. You handle escalated resident concerns directly and make sure the team resolves issues with urgency and professionalism.

Cortland operates with centralized support teams, so you'll work closely with corporate partners and a center of excellence. That means strong stakeholder communication matters as much as onsite execution.

What Cortland Is Looking for

  • At least two years of measurable sales leadership in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment (multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, timeshare, or similar)
  • Demonstrated history of hitting and exceeding occupancy, revenue, and NOI targets
  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing onsite teams
  • Strong financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, and expense management
  • Proficiency with property management software, CRM tools, and Microsoft Office
  • Comfort using social media for community marketing and brand presence
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Professional presentation and the ability to represent a premium brand consistently

What separates a strong candidate from an average one here: Cortland's vertically integrated structure means you'll interact with in-house design, construction, and operations teams, not just third-party vendors. Managers who thrive here understand how to work within a larger institutional system while still driving results at the property level. If you've only operated in a smaller, independent ownership environment, expect a real adjustment period. If you've worked within a large portfolio operator before, that experience transfers directly.

This role is a logical stepping stone toward a regional or district-level position for someone who builds a strong NOI track record and demonstrates the ability to develop talent consistently. Cortland promotes internally and has the portfolio size to support that kind of growth.

job.title: Senior Property Manager
job.description:
Commercial property management at the senior level runs on a specific mix of skills: financial literacy, lease fluency, people management, and the judgment to know when a tenant complaint is routine and when it's a liability. This role at Lincoln Property Company in Newport Beach calls on all of them, simultaneously, across a portfolio that can include office, retail, and industrial assets.

The Skills This Role Demands Most

Budget work here goes beyond filling in a spreadsheet. You'll prepare annual operating and capital budgets, track variance against actuals, and deliver reports that give ownership a clear picture of asset performance. CAM reconciliations, OpEx recovery charges, and AR collection are all part of your regular cycle. Yardi or MRI experience helps considerably since the reporting cadence at a firm like LPC moves fast.

Lease administration is the other core competency. You'll coordinate with lease administrators and accounting on setups and changes, review final approvals, and maintain oversight of covenant and expiration tracking. If you've managed a portfolio where a missed lease clause created a financial or legal problem, you already understand why this matters. Reading a lease critically, not just administratively, separates strong candidates from average ones here.

On the people side, you're not just supervising a team. You're recruiting, coaching, writing performance reviews, cross-training staff, and setting the pace for how tenant onboarding and vendor management actually get done. The job title is Senior Property Manager, but a meaningful part of the work is team leadership.

Day-to-Day Reality

A typical week includes tenant walkthroughs, vendor bid reviews, property inspections, monthly report preparation, and fielding whatever comes up operationally across your assets. Vacant spaces need to stay tour-ready. Move-ins and move-outs need coordination with the tenant improvement side of the business. Emergency response planning isn't theoretical: you're responsible for having documented plans, supplies, and trained staff in place before something goes wrong.

You're also the primary point of contact for property owners. That means you're not just managing properties; you're managing relationships with clients who have real financial stakes in how you perform. The ability to communicate complex financial or operational topics clearly, without softening the hard news, matters as much as the technical skills.

After-hours availability is a genuine requirement here, not fine print. Emergency situations don't schedule themselves, and the role expects you to respond when they happen.

What Lincoln Property Company Brings to This Role

Lincoln Property Company is one of the larger third-party management firms operating nationally, which means the systems, reporting standards, and compliance expectations are well-defined. For a senior manager, that's a double-edged reality: there's infrastructure and support, but there's also accountability to client and company standards that aren't negotiable. If you've worked in smaller operations where you built process from scratch, the structure here will feel different. If you've worked in institutional or fee management environments before, you'll recognize the expectations.

  • Bachelor's degree preferred; 5 to 8 years of commercial property management experience required
  • Active real estate license required where mandated; CPM or RPA designation (or active candidacy) preferred
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; familiarity with Yardi, MRI, and Kardin preferred
  • Working knowledge of leases, contracts, financial instruments, and construction
  • Ability to travel daily between assigned properties

job.title: Regional Manager, Affordable Housing
job.description:
Affordable housing portfolios demand a different operating discipline than conventional multifamily. Compliance calendars, regulatory agency relationships, LIHTC certification timelines, and HUD reporting layers sit on top of the same NOI pressure every regional manager faces. Asset Living, a nationally recognized third-party management firm with an NMHC top 50 ranking and AMO accreditation, is adding a Regional Manager to oversee an affordable housing portfolio spanning communities in Issaquah, Puyallup, Tacoma, and Vancouver, Washington.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope regional position. You own financial performance, personnel, leasing, maintenance oversight, and compliance across your portfolio. On the affordable side, that means keeping LIHTC application and annual recertification processes on track, conducting file reviews, managing regulatory agency interactions, and ensuring Section 8 and Equal Housing Opportunity procedures are followed without gaps. Semi-annual physical inspections are part of the calendar, not an exception to it.

Financially, you're building yearly operating budgets, tracking NOI performance against those budgets, writing monthly variance explanations when income or expense lines drift, and flagging capex needs before they become deferred maintenance problems. You'll review and approve vendor invoices, monitor large project contracts, and make sure property closeout and ownership reporting hit deadlines accurately.

On the people side, you screen, hire, coach, and when necessary, counsel out underperforming site staff. You approve timesheets, process salary increase requests, and coordinate with HR on documentation. Your community managers need a regional who gives them clear direction and consistent standards, not one who shows up only when something breaks.

Leasing responsibility includes developing annual marketing plans, evaluating staff closing rates and follow-up procedures, and building resident retention programs that reduce turnover. In affordable housing, concessions are limited by program rules, so your leasing strategy relies more on traffic quality, application processing speed, and occupancy management than on pricing flexibility.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Direct experience with LIHTC compliance, including file audits and recertification cycles
  • Familiarity with Section 8 / HCV program requirements and regulatory reporting
  • Proven track record managing on-site teams across multiple properties simultaneously
  • Ability to read a T-12, build an operating budget, and explain variances in writing to ownership
  • Working knowledge of fair housing law with the discipline to keep site staff consistently compliant
  • Experience conducting or overseeing physical inspections with an eye toward both compliance and capex planning

The candidates who stand out in affordable housing regional roles aren't just strong operators. They understand that a failed file review or a missed recertification deadline can trigger regulatory consequences that no amount of good occupancy numbers can offset. The compliance layer here is real, and it runs parallel to every financial and leasing metric you're also accountable for. If you've managed that dual responsibility before, this role will feel familiar.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospect walks in on a Saturday morning, third community they've toured this week, arms crossed. Your job is to turn that skepticism into a signed lease before the weekend's over.

Weinstein Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for Bexley Round Rock in Round Rock, TX. Weinstein is a family-owned company, now 70+ years in, with over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. They run their own properties, which means decisions get made close to the ground and training is taken seriously.

What This Role Actually Involves

You're the first contact most prospective residents have with the community. That means handling inbound inquiries, conducting tours, following up on leads, and walking prospects through the application process. You'll also maintain relationships with current residents, handle day-to-day administrative tasks at the leasing office, and help inspect units as part of the make-ready and move-in process. Expect to be on your feet most of the day, not at a desk.

Schedule is weekdays 9 to 6, Saturdays 9 to 5 on a rotating basis with the team, Sundays off. Starting pay is $20/hour, increasing with experience, plus quarterly bonuses. Occasional availability outside standard hours may be needed for resident events or weather-related situations.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

Prior leasing experience is not required. Weinstein trains from scratch and says so directly. What they're screening for instead:

  • Strong verbal and written communication, including genuine listening skills
  • A customer-first approach, especially when situations get difficult
  • Ability to manage competing priorities without losing composure
  • Team orientation, willingness to cover tasks outside your defined role
  • Goal-oriented mindset and basic organizational discipline

If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role where you had to close a sale or resolve a complaint under pressure, that background translates well here.

One honest note on the role: leasing is sales. Occupancy goals are real, and your results will be visible. The consultants who advance at Weinstein aren't just personable, they follow up consistently, track their traffic, and take ownership of their conversion numbers. Many of Weinstein's current property managers and regional staff started in leasing, so the path upward exists if you're willing to perform.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The academic calendar dictates everything: traffic spikes in fall, Turn is a genuine operational event (not just a busy week), and your residents are often signing their first-ever lease. If you understand that rhythm and actually enjoy working with that population, this role at Redpoint Knoxville fits.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

The Experience Team Member position at Scion draws on a specific combination of abilities. Sales and relationship-building sit at the center. You'll conduct community tours, field objections, and feed intel back to management on what's slowing conversions. That's a real leasing function, not just showing units and hoping for the best.

Equally important is communication across channels. Social media engagement, direct outreach, event promotion, and in-person interaction with a diverse resident population are all part of the day. You're not just staffing a front desk. You're functioning as a local face of the brand, and that extends to how you carry yourself off-site as well.

On the administrative side, expect package management, maintenance request coordination, office and amenity upkeep, and after-hours lockout coverage on rotation. None of that is glamorous. It's the operational connective tissue that keeps a student property running between the bigger leasing moments.

What the Role Actually Demands

Availability matters here in ways it doesn't at conventional properties. Summer is not a slow season in student housing. Turn, the period when hundreds of residents vacate and re-occupy within days, requires all hands and a tolerance for controlled chaos. Holidays and weekends are part of the rotation. If your schedule can't flex around the academic calendar, this will be a frustrating fit.

Beyond availability, the candidates who do well in this role tend to share a few traits:

  • Genuine comfort working with 18 to 22-year-olds, including the calls at inconvenient hours
  • Ability to shift between sales mode and administrative tasks without losing momentum
  • Enough self-discipline to stay organized during the chaotic pre-Turn and lease-up stretches
  • Honest interest in local marketing, not just executing what management hands down

Why Scion and Why This Property

Scion operates at scale in purpose-built student housing, which means their systems, training, and leasing processes are more developed than what you'd find at a smaller operator running a few converted properties near a campus. For someone early in a property management career, that infrastructure matters. The skills you build here, particularly around lease-up pacing, traffic conversion, and resident experience programming, transfer cleanly into conventional multifamily or into a senior leasing role at another student housing operator.

Redpoint Knoxville serves the University of Tennessee market, which runs a predictable but demanding leasing cycle. This is not a slow property. If you want volume, variety, and a role that won't look the same week to week, that's what student housing delivers.

job.title: Maintenance Lead (Foon Lok East)
job.description:
Foon Lok East is part of MidPen Housing's portfolio of more than 130 affordable communities across Northern California, home to roughly 20,000 residents including working families, seniors, and people with special needs. The Maintenance Lead here isn't just fixing things. They're running the day-to-day physical operation of the property, and the quality of that work shows up directly in resident experience, inspection outcomes, and long-term asset condition.

Reporting to the Community Manager, you'll own maintenance operations end to end. That means scheduling and supervising your crew, managing vendor bids and contractor oversight, and staying on top of the full range of trades work: electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, appliance repair, flooring, locks, and more. Unit turns are a core part of the rhythm here. Every make-ready has to hit a standard that supports both resident satisfaction and regulatory compliance, and you'll be responsible for keeping that process tight. Annual inspections (REAC, TCAC, MOR) are a real part of affordable housing maintenance management, and comfort with those compliance frameworks matters.

Preventive maintenance programs, common area upkeep, inventory control, parts procurement, and emergency on-call rotations all fall within scope. You're not just responding to work orders. You're building a system that keeps the property safe and functional before things break down.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of hands-on trade depth and genuine supervisory experience. Five years of broad maintenance work is the baseline. Three years managing a crew is the other piece. The candidates who thrive understand that coaching a junior tech through a repair correctly is as important as completing the repair itself. On the compliance side, familiarity with affordable housing inspection regimes gives you a real advantage. REAC and TCAC inspections have specific requirements that differ from conventional property audits, and being caught flat-footed on either can have real consequences for the property's standing.

MidPen offers company-provided on-site housing as part of the compensation package for this position, which is worth factoring in given Oakland's cost of living. Pay runs $27.00 to $30.38 per hour based on experience, with a full benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, 403(b) retirement, paid parental leave, and education reimbursement.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma and five years of broad maintenance experience across trades (plumbing, carpentry, painting, flooring, electrical, irrigation), or equivalent combination
  • Minimum three years of supervisory experience managing maintenance staff and overseeing apartment turnovers
  • Knowledge of affordable housing inspection standards: REAC, TCAC, and MOR
  • Experience managing vendors, reviewing bids, and coordinating contractor work
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and basic property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to perform physically demanding work across varying weather conditions
  • Alignment with MidPen's mission serving low-income and special needs residents

MidPen has held Great Place to Work certification in 2025, which reflects something real about how they operate. For a maintenance professional who wants stable, mission-driven work with genuine leadership responsibility, this role offers the kind of scope that builds a long-term career in affordable housing operations.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Arroyo Green, Firehouse Square)
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles at affordable housing nonprofits carry a different weight than comparable positions at market-rate properties. The residents here, working families, seniors, and people with special needs, depend on functional, safe housing in ways that make a slow work order or a deferred repair genuinely consequential. MidPen Housing has operated in Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 130 properties across 12 counties. This opening covers two Redwood City communities: Arroyo Green and Firehouse Square.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll report to the Community Manager and handle the kind of multi-trade workload that keeps affordable communities running day to day. That means plumbing repairs on water and sewage systems, electrical work on appliances, fixtures, switches, and circuits, and carpentry across both structural framing and finish work. Unit turns are a core part of the job. You'll take vacant units through the full make-ready process, painting, flooring, fixture and appliance installation, getting them back to move-in condition within MidPen's established timeframes.

Beyond the unit-level work, you'll maintain landscaping and irrigation systems, keep common areas clean, well-lit, and secure, and run preventive maintenance schedules with accurate work order documentation. You'll also coordinate with outside contractors, helping with bid coordination, scheduling, and monitoring completion.

One part of this role that distinguishes it from a straight technician position: you'll coach and provide oversight to Maintenance Groundskeeper staff. That's a real supervisory responsibility, not just informal mentorship. Strong candidates will have experience giving direction to others and some patience for developing less experienced team members.

The on-call rotation is worth understanding clearly. You'll cover 24/7 emergency maintenance for seven consecutive days at a time, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. That's a real commitment and one of the honest challenges of any on-call maintenance role in residential property management.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED with at least three years of maintenance experience, ideally in property management
  • Solid plumbing knowledge and hands-on electrical repair experience (appliances, circuits, fixtures)
  • Rough and finish carpentry skills for both structural and cosmetic repairs
  • Landscape and irrigation maintenance experience
  • Basic OSHA safety knowledge
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic computer documentation
  • Valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and work in all weather conditions
  • Experience coaching or training others is a genuine plus here, not just a checkbox

Compensation and Context

The pay range is $25.00 to $28.13 per hour, based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options for childcare, medical, and commuter expenses, an employee education reimbursement program, EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

Technicians who build a track record in affordable housing nonprofits often move into Lead Maintenance or Maintenance Supervisor roles as portfolios grow. MidPen's scale across Northern California means those advancement paths exist internally. The skills you develop here, multi-trade repairs, contractor coordination, team oversight, transfer cleanly to any residential maintenance career, market-rate or affordable.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Carson & Raleigh)
job.description:
Skills This Role Lives On

This position runs on three things: people skills, sales instincts, and attention to detail. You'll spend your days converting prospects into residents, keeping current residents happy, and handling the administrative work that keeps a leasing office running. If you're strong in one area but not the others, this role will feel uneven. The best candidates bring all three.

Prometheus calls this role a Neighbor Ambassador rather than a Leasing Consultant, and the distinction matters. The expectation isn't just to close leases. It's to build genuine rapport with prospects from the first inquiry through move-in, and to stay present for residents long after the lease is signed.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

On the sales side, you'll guide prospects through tours, follow up on leads, and work to convert traffic into signed leases. Prometheus uses its own leasing framework, so you'll learn their process rather than improvise. Leasing contests and per-lease incentives are built into the comp structure, so your effort shows up directly in your paycheck.

On the administrative side, expect to handle rental agreements, market surveys, occupancy reporting, and apartment advertising. It's not glamorous, but it's where you build the operational foundation that makes every other part of this job work. Errors here cost time and sometimes money, so accuracy matters.

On the customer service side, you're the face of the property for people who live there. Complaints, requests, day-to-day friction: you handle it or route it. Residents notice when someone follows through, and they notice when someone doesn't.

One honest note on scheduling: weekends are required. The Portland communities are busiest Saturday and Sunday, so your regular days off fall on weekdays. If a Monday-to-Friday schedule is a firm need, this isn't the right fit.

What Makes This Role at Prometheus Different

Prometheus is a privately held company with over 13,000 units across the Bay Area, Portland, and Seattle. They've operated since 1965 and build for the long term, which means you're not working for a company that's flipping assets or cutting corners on reinvestment. The Portland portfolio sits within a larger vertically integrated operation that includes acquisitions, development, and value-add renovations. That's meaningful for someone early in a property management career: you're not siloed, and there are real paths to grow.

For entry-level candidates, this role is a solid starting point. Leasing Consultants who develop strong closing skills and operational habits often move into Assistant Manager or Property Manager roles within a few years. Prometheus's size means those opportunities exist internally rather than requiring a job change to find them.

  • Hourly pay: $21.00 to $24.25, plus a $200 per-lease incentive
  • Semi-annual discretionary bonus
  • Weekend shift premium pay
  • Additional bonuses for referrals, training, lease-up, and renovation projects
  • 100% company-paid medical, vision, and dental (including eligible dependents)
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Tenure-based housing discounts
  • Tuition reimbursement and educational assistance
  • Your birthday is a paid holiday

This position covers two Portland communities: Carson and Raleigh. Prior property management experience isn't required. Customer service or sales background from any industry is relevant here.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Role in Context

The Assistant Community Manager position exists because running an apartment community is genuinely a two-person job at the leadership level. Occupancy, delinquency, leasing traffic, resident relations, and daily operations don't pause when the Community Manager is out, in a meeting, or handling a vendor escalation. Hawthorne Residential Partners, a top-50 multifamily operator with a strong Southeast footprint, is staffing this role at Encore at Heritage in Wake Forest, NC. It's not an administrative support role. It's a developmental leadership seat with real financial accountability from day one.

Wake Forest sits in one of the faster-growing suburban corridors outside Raleigh, which means resident turnover expectations, renewal pressure, and leasing traffic all carry real weight here. The person in this role will feel that directly.

What the Job Actually Involves

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, work leads, and shepherd prospects through the full leasing process, including applications and move-in documentation. Renewals are part of your performance picture, not an afterthought. You'll also own the community's social media presence, which in 2025 is less about creative content and more about consistent visibility that supports traffic goals.

The financial side is where this role separates itself from a pure leasing position. You'll handle rent collection, payment posting, ledger audits, and delinquency follow-up, including the less pleasant work of coordinating eviction procedures when residents reach that point. Weekly delinquency calls are part of the rhythm here. You'll also contribute to financial reporting that goes up to regional leadership, so comfort reading and interpreting basic reports matters.

When the Community Manager is unavailable, you run the operation. That includes keeping the team focused and maintaining service continuity. It's not a fill-in role; it's expected accountability.

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays, 10 to 4, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager role is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus, not a requirement
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

Compensation includes an hourly base plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with company match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and telehealth access. Hawthorne also offers a formal Career Path Program, and this role has a clear line to Community Manager for people who want it.

What separates strong candidates here: It's not leasing instinct alone. The ACMs who move up fastest are the ones who get comfortable with the financial side early. Reading a ledger, catching a misapplied payment, understanding where delinquency is trending before it becomes a regional conversation. Those habits, built at this level, are exactly what prepares someone to run their own community.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 8:45 on a Tuesday and you're reviewing yesterday's delinquency report before the office opens, flagging two accounts that need notices before end of day, checking a vendor invoice that doesn't match the approved scope, and skimming an online review that went up overnight. The leasing team arrives at nine. You've already been at work for twenty minutes.

The Role at Hawthorne Northwest

Hawthorne Residential Partners operates as one of the larger Southeast-rooted multifamily management companies in the country, and this Community Manager position sits at the center of day-to-day operations for their Greensboro property on Brigham Road. You own the full picture: financial performance, occupancy, team development, resident experience, and vendor oversight. That's not a partial list. This is a genuine general manager role, not a glorified leasing position with a fancier title.

On the financial side, you'll manage budgets, oversee rent collection, handle deposit accounting, and track delinquency. You'll work primarily in Yardi and Knock. Pricing strategy and renewals fall to you as well, and you'll be accountable to occupancy goals in the same breath as NOI targets. Operationally, you'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders and preventative care, manage vendor relationships, and conduct regular property inspections to keep curb appeal and unit quality where they need to be.

The team leadership component here is real. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly team meetings, and handle performance conversations when they're needed. Hawthorne has a defined internal career path program, which means your team members will be looking to you not just for direction but for genuine mentorship. That's a responsibility worth taking seriously.

Resident-facing, you'll handle escalated concerns, manage the community's online reputation, plan resident events, and support leasing by conducting tours and guiding prospects through the process when traffic demands it.

What This Role Requires

  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Proficiency with Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate or property management license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license required

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to hold the total at 40 hours. Resident events and community needs can pull you outside those hours occasionally. That's the reality of site-level management.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role from average ones: the ability to read a T-12 and connect what it's telling you to what's actually happening on-site. Financial literacy at the community level isn't just about running reports. It's about knowing when your concessions are eating into NOI or when a maintenance cost spike is signaling a capital expense conversation with ownership. That judgment comes with experience, and Hawthorne will expect you to show it.

job.title: Market Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at Kimball Court in Woburn, a suburban Boston market where JMC manages a portfolio of well-maintained residential communities. The day-to-day here is genuinely varied. You'll work through a queue of resident service requests covering appliance repairs, smoke detector installations, door hardware, tile, handrails, and light fixtures. You'll also handle the cosmetic side of unit upkeep: painting, screen replacements, and window work that keeps the property looking sharp between turns and throughout tenancy.

Beyond the routine work order flow, you'll coordinate with outside contractors and vendors, track your own paperwork and invoices, and stay ready for emergency calls. Flood response and back-to-back move-ins are specifically called out, which tells you this team moves fast when vacancy demands it. Make-ready quality matters here, and your ability to complete a punch list cleanly and quickly will show up directly in how the property performs.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:30 to 5:00, with an on-call rotation. That rotation is worth understanding before you apply: it means occasional evenings or weekends when something urgent comes up. It's not constant, but it's real.

What You Bring

  • At least six months of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of basic electrical and mechanical systems
  • Comfort identifying safety hazards and acting on them without waiting to be told
  • Ability to manage your own work order documentation and vendor invoices
  • Specialized trade background in plumbing, HVAC, electrical, or roofing is a genuine advantage

The candidate who stands out here isn't necessarily the one with the longest resume. It's the person who takes pride in the finished product, communicates clearly with residents under pressure, and doesn't need to be reminded to close the loop on a work order. JMC has been operating since 1951 and retains a lot of long-tenured staff. That sticks out because it usually reflects a management culture that actually supports its maintenance team rather than burning through them.

Compensation and Context

The pay range runs from $26.75 to $32.00 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match.

For someone early in a maintenance career, this kind of general maintenance role at a well-run residential property builds a wide foundation. Technicians who develop strong diagnostic skills and vendor management experience here often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within a few years. The exposure to multiple trade categories, especially if you add HVAC or plumbing certifications along the way, makes that path fairly direct in the New England multifamily market.

job.title: Maintenance Technician 2
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles get underestimated as career starting points, but they're actually where some of the most transferable skills in property management get built. The Technician 2 designation at Ackermann Group is explicit about this: it's a training-oriented position designed to deepen your proficiency across the full range of residential maintenance trades, not just hand you a work order queue and leave you to figure it out.

Ackermann has been operating in the Midwest since 1938, which means their systems, their expectations, and their culture have had decades to mature. For a technician early in their career, that kind of institutional depth matters. You're not joining a startup trying to figure out its maintenance protocols. You're joining an organization with established processes around make-readies, preventative maintenance, and inventory management, and you're being brought in to learn those processes correctly.

Day to day, the work covers the full spectrum of what keeps a residential community running. Make-ready turns, intermediate plumbing and electrical, appliance repair, HVAC basics, painting, grounds upkeep, pool chemistry where applicable, and participation in the move-in and move-out inspection process. Snow removal and after-hours emergency on-call are part of the rotation as well. That's the honest version of the role. It's physical, it's varied, and the on-call component is real.

What separates candidates who grow quickly in this kind of role from those who plateau is usually diagnostic thinking. Anyone can follow a checklist. Technicians who advance to Lead or Maintenance Supervisor are the ones who start to understand why a unit keeps having the same plumbing issue, or how to sequence a make-ready so the paint doesn't get scuffed during the final punch. Ackermann's explicit mention of career coaching and development suggests they're paying attention to that ceiling and trying to raise it.

What They're Looking For

  • At least one year of general maintenance experience across multiple trade areas
  • EPA Type I and II, CAMT, or CPO certifications are a plus but not required
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Strong attention to detail and a collaborative, team-oriented approach
  • Availability for a Monday through Friday schedule with rotating emergency on-call

Columbus is a market worth noting here. It's been one of the more active apartment markets in Ohio, with consistent population growth driving steady demand across garden-style and mid-rise communities. Ackermann's footprint in the region means there's genuine room to grow within the company rather than having to change employers to move up. For a technician who builds real competency in HVAC, electrical, and the make-ready process, the path toward Maintenance Supervisor or even Facilities Manager at a larger asset becomes a realistic medium-term goal, not a distant one.

job.title: Property Manager (Aldon at Keys Crossing Apartments)
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on three things working together: operational discipline, financial literacy, and the kind of interpersonal skill that keeps residents renewing and prospects converting. If you're someone who reads a T-12 as comfortably as you coach a leasing associate through a difficult conversation with a resident, this role fits that profile. Van Metre is looking for a Property Manager to run Aldon at Keys Crossing Apartments, a 241-unit community in Greenville, SC, reporting to a Regional Manager and leading a small on-site team of two.

The financial side here is real and recurring. You'll own the annual budget process, prepare quarterly forecasts, monitor income and expenses against targets, and keep a close eye on delinquency and accounts receivable for both current and former residents. Concession strategy, pricing adjustments, and contract negotiation for maintenance bids all fall within your scope. This isn't a role where someone else handles the numbers and you handle people. Both land on your desk.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Much of your week will move between people and paperwork. Daily or weekly touchpoints with your leasing and maintenance team members keep operations aligned and surface problems before they compound. You'll walk units, review make-ready standards, conduct market-ready inspections, and stay on top of the punch list to make sure the physical asset reflects Van Metre's standards. On the leasing side, you'll track traffic, follow up on leads, monitor lease renewals, and pull together sales administrative reports for your Regional Manager.

When things get difficult, including the eviction process when it becomes necessary, you're the one who sees it through. Deposit accounting on move-outs, fair housing compliance, and Landlord Tenant Law in South Carolina all require your attention. It's not glamorous work, but it's the kind of consistent execution that protects NOI and keeps the property running cleanly.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with occasional weekend coverage when the property needs it.

What Strong Candidates Bring

Prior property management experience is required. Yardi experience is a plus. But beyond credentials, the candidates who thrive in roles like this tend to share a few traits worth naming honestly:

  • They coach their team without micromanaging, because a two-person team needs autonomy to function
  • They stay organized under competing priorities without losing the human side of resident interactions
  • They hold themselves accountable to budget targets the same way they hold their team to leasing goals
  • They communicate clearly in writing, not just in person, because reports and documentation matter here

Van Metre has been operating since 1955 and brings a long track record in residential development and management. For a property manager, that means working within established standards and processes while still owning the day-to-day decisions that shape resident experience and property performance. The compensation range is $70,000 to $75,000 annually, with quarterly bonus potential, leasing and renewal commissions, and a benefits package that includes generous PTO, wellness reimbursement, tuition assistance, and a matched 401(k).

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs, you'll carry the full weight of keeping a residential community functional and livable. That means diagnosing and repairing plumbing, electrical, and carpentry issues across units and common areas, completing make-readies between turns, and responding to after-hours emergency calls on rotation with the support of a Service Manager. The on-call component is real and worth acknowledging upfront: this role asks you to be available when residents need help most, and that's not a footnote.

Day to day, you'll move between punch list items on vacant units, resident work orders, and preventive tasks on building systems. HVAC troubleshooting will come up regularly, so candidates who've worked through refrigerant issues, thermostat failures, or seasonal system startups will have an immediate advantage. EPA Type II or Universal certification and a CPO certification both signal that you've worked at this level before, though neither is a hard requirement to apply.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience with plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry repairs in a residential setting
  • Solid HVAC troubleshooting background, enough to diagnose before escalating
  • A valid driver's license and the physical ability to lift up to 50 lbs, climb ladders and stairs, and work in confined or difficult-to-access spaces
  • Availability for standard community hours including evenings and weekends, plus on-call rotation
  • English fluency sufficient to read work orders, communicate with residents, and interpret safety documentation
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (preferred, not required)
  • CPO certification (preferred, not required)

The Craft This Role Builds

A maintenance technician position in a professionally managed apartment community teaches you something that solo trade work rarely does: how to prioritize competing demands across a live property while keeping resident satisfaction intact. You'll get faster at reading a unit's condition on entry, estimating scope accurately, and sequencing repairs so turns don't drag. Those skills transfer directly if you want to grow into a lead tech or Service Manager role. Cottonwood Residential operates at a scale where internal advancement is a real path, and technicians who show diagnostic depth and accountability tend to move up.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just trade knowledge. It's the ability to communicate clearly with a frustrated resident, close out a work order completely the first time, and treat every make-ready like the next person moving in is already watching. That combination of technical competence and resident-facing professionalism is what Cottonwood is actually evaluating.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance
job.description:
Maintenance technicians in value-add multifamily operations carry a wider scope than the job title suggests. When a company manages a concentrated portfolio of older residential properties, the technician isn't just fixing what breaks. They're the person who keeps occupancy defensible, turns units on schedule, and catches deferred issues before they become capital problems. That's the kind of role Birgo is filling in Cleveland.

Birgo manages a four-property portfolio split between Shaker Heights and Edgewater, and they're adding one Maintenance Technician to the team covering all four sites. Both neighborhoods feature older housing stock, which means you'll encounter the full range of building systems rather than the narrow scope you'd find in a newer Class A community. Boiler experience carries real weight here. If you've worked in older multifamily or similar building types, you already know that heating systems in this part of Ohio aren't a seasonal afterthought.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of the role covers the usual multifamily maintenance mix: turns and make-readies, drywall, painting, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and HVAC repairs, plus a preventative maintenance program that runs alongside the reactive work. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That rotation is worth understanding before you apply. It's a standard part of this work, but it does mean some nights and weekends will pull you in when things go sideways. The tradeoff is a predictable weekday schedule most of the time.

Pay lands between $23 and $26 per hour, paid weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life coverage with an employer contribution, paid time off, holidays, sick time, a 401(k) match, professional development reimbursement, and discounted rent at Birgo properties. You'll need a valid driver's license and your own insured transportation to move between sites. Physical requirements include lifting up to 50 pounds, working in confined spaces, and safe use of power tools and ladders.

Where This Role Can Take You

For a technician who wants to grow, a multi-site role like this builds something specific: diagnostic range. When you're responsible for four properties instead of one, you see more failure modes, more system types, and more variation in how buildings age. That breadth is exactly what separates a senior technician or a future maintenance supervisor from someone who's spent years in a single building doing the same dozen repairs.

The strongest candidates for this kind of role tend to have a few things in common. They're comfortable prioritizing on the fly when multiple work orders compete for the same afternoon. They know the difference between a repair that can wait for a parts order and one that needs a workaround today. And they document their work clearly enough that the next person on-call isn't starting from scratch. That last habit, more than any single trade skill, is what tends to accelerate a maintenance career in multifamily.

  • Multi-trade experience across plumbing, electrical, drywall, and HVAC
  • Boiler system familiarity (particularly relevant for this portfolio)
  • Valid driver's license and personal insured transportation
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds, use power tools safely, and work in confined spaces
  • Eligible to work in the United States

Birgo describes itself as mission-driven and places real emphasis on professional development, team culture, and staff wellbeing. If you want a maintenance role where the work is varied, the portfolio keeps you sharp, and the company has actual infrastructure for growth, this is worth a serious look.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is where most successful property management careers begin, and for good reason. The skills you build here, reading prospects, managing objections, understanding what drives a lease decision, compound directly into roles like Leasing Manager, Assistant Property Manager, and eventually Property Manager. Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Palm Bay, FL community, and the structure of this role is set up to accelerate that trajectory.

The day-to-day centers on converting traffic into leases. You'll handle inbound inquiries across phone, email, and walk-ins, conduct community tours, and guide prospects through the full leasing process: qualification, application review, lease prep, proration calculations, and move-in coordination. That last part matters more than most postings acknowledge. Understanding how rent calculations and prorations work gives you a financial fluency that separates consultants who stay at the front desk from those who move into operations.

What the Role Actually Requires

Beyond the standard sales energy, this position asks you to manage the leasing office as a functioning operation. Records stay current, prospect traffic gets logged, lease files get organized for manager approval, and the model unit stays tour-ready. Waitlist management and renewal outreach are also part of the mix, which means you're not just chasing new leases. You're helping protect occupancy from both ends. Familiarity with Yardi is a plus, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish is preferred, which reflects the Palm Bay market's demographics and gives Spanish-speaking prospects a meaningfully better experience.

Fair Housing compliance isn't a checkbox here. You'll be expected to apply it fluently across every interaction, from how you describe availability to how you document application decisions. Candidates who already understand why Fair Housing rules exist, not just what they say, will move faster in this environment.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive base wage with monthly leasing and renewal bonuses
  • Leaser of the Month monetary reward
  • Employee Housing Discount Program
  • 120 hours PTO in year one, with progressive increases
  • Two floating days annually
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage subsidized and active on day one
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Commuter benefits, employee referral program, and professional development training

Weekend rotation is part of the schedule. That's standard for leasing roles, and it's worth naming honestly. Leasing volume on weekends tends to be high, and if you're newer to the field, those shifts often produce the most reps in the shortest time. Two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience is preferred. A valid driver's license is required.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just closing ability. It's follow-through. Prospects who don't hear back within a few hours often lease elsewhere. Consultants who build a reliable follow-up rhythm and treat every inquiry as a relationship rather than a transaction tend to post the best conversion numbers and the strongest renewal rates when they eventually move into broader leasing or management responsibilities.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 223 - Conroe, TX
job.description:
Berkshire Jones Forest is a Berkshire Residential-managed community in Conroe, Texas, and this Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of keeping it running well. Conroe has seen steady population growth as residents move north out of the Houston metro, which means newer lease-ups and communities in the area carry real expectations for physical upkeep and resident experience. A property that looks sharp and turns units quickly holds an edge in that market.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of hands-on maintenance work: appliance repairs, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll support management in holding the property to community and corporate standards, keep the shop organized, manage inventory, and make sure key security stays tight. Curb appeal is taken seriously, and part of this role is being the set of eyes that catches what needs attention before residents do.

What separates a strong candidate in this role from an average one isn't just technical range. It's the combination of solid diagnostic instincts and genuine follow-through on resident interactions. Make-ready quality matters here. A unit that comes back clean and fully punched out on schedule keeps occupancy steady and avoids concessions. Technicians who treat the punch list as a checklist to rush through tend to generate callbacks; technicians who treat it as a standard to hit tend to build trust with the site team quickly.

What Berkshire is looking for

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with computers and related software for work orders or communication
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A self-directed approach to physical property inspections and curb appeal standards

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, so there's no third-party management layer between the site team and decision-makers. That structure tends to mean faster approvals on repairs and a more direct connection between the work you do and how the asset performs. For a technician who wants to grow toward a lead or service manager role, that kind of visibility matters.

Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and health insurance coverage. Berkshire has a stated commitment to equal opportunity employment across all protected classes.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 229, Aubrey - Dallas area
job.description:
Park 3Eighty in Aubrey sits in one of the fastest-growing corridors north of Dallas, where occupancy pressure is real and resident expectations run high. Berkshire Residential Investments is hiring a Maintenance Technician to keep this community performing at the physical level that supports everything else: retention, NOI, and the kind of curb appeal that converts traffic into leases.

The day-to-day reality of this role is broad. You're not a specialist sitting in one trade. You're handling appliance repairs in the morning, a plumbing call by midday, and a punch list walk on a make-ready unit before the afternoon's done. Curb appeal isn't just a checkbox here. It's a direct input to how the property presents to prospects and how residents feel about renewing. When the physical condition slips, delinquency and turnover tend to follow. You keep that chain from starting.

Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, which means decisions move faster and accountability sits closer to the property level. You'll work directly alongside site management, not through layers of third-party approvals. That structure gives a good tech real visibility into how their work connects to the community's broader performance.

What Berkshire is looking for

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a multifamily or similar residential setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with computer-based work order systems and basic digital tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A genuine attention to physical detail, from unit interiors to common areas and grounds

What separates strong candidates here isn't just trade knowledge. It's the combination of technical range and resident-facing composure. A tech who can diagnose a plumbing issue quickly and then explain the timeline clearly to a resident without creating friction is the one who actually moves the needle on satisfaction scores. Berkshire's culture rewards that kind of dual competency.

On the career side, maintenance technicians who build out their trade depth and develop a track record on well-run assets often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles. Berkshire's portfolio gives that path real options.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development plans, a 25% rent discount, and a benefits package. They're an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace across all protected characteristics.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Mid-rise and high-rise apartment communities in the greater Seattle area carry mechanical complexity that garden-style properties simply don't. Central plant systems, boilers, and sophisticated HVAC infrastructure mean that keeping a building performing at a high level requires someone who thinks like a technician and leads like a manager. This role exists at that intersection.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Mountlake Terrace community, and the scope here goes well beyond turning units and handling service requests. This is a hands-on leadership position where you'll work alongside the maintenance team, set the standard for workmanship, and carry real responsibility for the long-term condition of the asset.

What This Role Actually Covers

Day-to-day, you're splitting your time between direct technical work and team oversight. You'll diagnose and repair across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, while also managing the make-ready process to keep turns moving on schedule so leasing has inventory to work with. Preventative maintenance programs fall under your watch, and executing those consistently is what separates a building that holds its value from one that doesn't.

You'll also carry after-hours responsibility through an on-call rotation and weekend availability. That's a real part of the job, not a footnote. Emergency calls for a community with complex mechanical systems can range from a boiler issue in January to a plumbing failure mid-week. Candidates who've handled that kind of unpredictability in a residential setting will have an easier adjustment.

Additional responsibilities include:

  • Responding to resident service tickets with timely follow-through and documented completion
  • Maintaining compliance with applicable building codes, OSHA standards, and safety protocols
  • Overseeing grounds upkeep, snow removal, and common area cleanliness
  • Keeping all building systems running at peak efficiency

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

Five or more years working in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance is the baseline. HVAC, EPA, or NAPE certification is expected. Supervisory experience is preferred, and given the leadership component of this role, candidates who've coached less experienced technicians or overseen a crew will have a clear advantage over those with deep technical skills but no management exposure.

Familiarity with complex mechanical systems, including split systems, central plant, chillers, and boilers, is a genuine differentiator here. Many applicants will have solid apartment maintenance backgrounds. The ones who stand out will also understand how those larger systems behave, how to troubleshoot them, and how to build a PM schedule around them.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with property management software, apps, and the Microsoft Office suite
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting capability
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather conditions
  • A detail-oriented, safety-first approach to every task

The salary range for this position is $62,400 to $66,560, with additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Lease Administrator
job.description:
Lease administration is detail work at its core. If you thrive on accuracy, catch errors others miss, and find satisfaction in keeping complex records clean and current, this role at Lincoln Property Company in Nashville puts those skills to daily use. It's not a glamorous position, but for someone who genuinely enjoys the data and documentation side of commercial real estate, it's substantive and stable work.

Where Your Skills Actually Get Used

The majority of your time goes toward lease abstracts and database integrity. You'll prepare and edit abstracts, verify data pulled from paper and electronic sources, and make sure lease files meet institutional-quality standards. That last phrase matters here. Lincoln manages commercial portfolios on behalf of institutional clients, which means the accuracy bar is high and the paper trail has to be clean. A miskeyed commencement date or a missed amendment can create real downstream problems for accounting and legal teams.

You'll also handle monthly production and tracking reports, maintain a daily lease document tracker, and process client-specific reporting. The work requires you to read and interpret actual legal documents, including lease agreements, amendments, subordination agreements, and title commitments. You don't need to be an attorney, but you need to be comfortable with legal language and know when something looks off.

This is a fully in-office role in Nashville. No hybrid, no remote option. Standard business hours, desk-based work, with occasional cross-functional communication with property managers, accounting personnel, area managers, clients, and outside legal counsel.

What the Role Requires

  • High school diploma or GED required; associate degree or higher preferred
  • At least two years of database administration or commercial real estate experience
  • Experience with Yardi, MRI, or Visual Lease is a real advantage
  • Strong Excel and Word skills, plus comfort learning new lease administration software
  • Ability to read and interpret lease documents and legal agreements
  • Property management or real estate accounting background preferred
  • Solid math comprehension for tracking and reporting functions
  • Background check required prior to start

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The difference between someone who does this job adequately and someone who does it well usually comes down to two things: proofing instincts and communication. You're going to be the person catching data discrepancies before they reach a client report. That requires a genuine habit of double-checking your own work, not just a line on a resume about attention to detail. The communication piece matters too because you'll interact across disciplines, including legal counsel and clients, not just internal staff. Being clear and professional in writing without over-explaining is a real skill in this context.

Lincoln's commercial portfolio spans more than 680 million square feet across multiple asset types and geographies. Working inside that infrastructure gives you exposure to how institutional-grade lease administration actually functions at scale, which is a meaningful credential if you're building a career in commercial real estate operations or real estate accounting.

job.title: Centralized Collections Associate
job.description:
Collections work in property management doesn't always get framed as a career builder, but it should. The Centralized Collections Associate role at Asset Living sits at the intersection of financial operations, resident relations, and legal compliance. For someone who's spent time on-site as a leasing agent or assistant manager, this position takes what you already know about ledgers, delinquency, and resident communication and puts it to work at scale across a student housing portfolio, all without the commute.

Asset Living is one of the larger third-party management companies in the country, ranked in the NMHC top 50 and operating across multifamily, student housing, build-to-rent, affordable, and active adult assets. The centralized collections function is remote, meaning you're not tied to a single property. You're managing accounts receivable across multiple sites, which means you'll develop a sharper eye for ledger discrepancies, a faster hand with move-out reconciliations, and a more systematic approach to the eviction process than most site-level roles ever require.

Student housing adds its own complexity here. Guarantor relationships are common, lease timelines are compressed around academic calendars, and the delinquency window before turnover is short. If you've worked student housing before, you know the pace. If you haven't, this role will teach you quickly, and that knowledge transfers cleanly to conventional multifamily, affordable, and build-to-rent portfolios later in your career.

Day to day, you're monitoring accounts across assigned properties, posting payments and charges accurately, issuing notices, coordinating with legal teams on filings, and keeping records audit-ready through monthly close. You're also the point of contact for residents and guarantors navigating balances and payment plans, which means you need to hold a firm line on policy while communicating with real empathy. That balance is harder than it sounds, and people who do it well tend to move into property manager or regional roles faster than peers who only have leasing or maintenance coordination experience.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just the ability to work independently (though that matters in a fully remote role). It's ledger fluency. Candidates who can read an account, spot a misapplied payment, and trace a discrepancy back to its source before it becomes a reporting problem are the ones who add the most value in centralized operations.

What the role requires

  • At least one year of site-level property management experience, leasing or assistant/community manager level; student housing background is a strong plus
  • Working knowledge of general ledger functions and account reconciliation
  • Familiarity with county and state eviction procedures and Fair Housing compliance
  • Comfort with property management software and the ability to manage tasks independently in a remote setting
  • High school diploma required; a bachelor's degree is preferred

No travel is required. This is a fully remote position with Asset Living's centralized operations team.

job.title: Business Manager - Preserve at Henderson Beach
job.description:
Destin's residential market sits in one of Florida's most competitive coastal corridors, where Class A communities compete hard on lifestyle, amenity quality, and resident experience. The Business Manager role at Preserve at Henderson Beach puts you at the center of all of it: financials, people, physical asset, and culture. That's a lot of plates to keep spinning, and that's exactly why this role builds the kind of operator that regional and VP-level leadership is made of.

Olympus Property, a three-time National Apartment Association Top Employer (2023, 2024, and 2025), is looking for a proven multifamily property manager to lead this community. The title says Business Manager, but the scope is full asset leadership. You'll own the financial performance, which means tracking NOI, managing occupancy and delinquency, building annual business plans, and running budget projections in close collaboration with your Regional Manager and Regional VP. You'll also lead the on-site team, covering both office and maintenance staff, with real responsibility for training, counseling, and performance development.

On any given day, you might be reviewing a T-12 in the morning, walking a make-ready punch list before noon, negotiating a vendor contract after lunch, and hosting a resident event in the evening. That variety is genuinely what this role demands. Olympus is transparent about the expectation for schedule flexibility, including after-hours coverage for events and emergencies, which is honest and worth factoring in.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just experience with the operational checklist. It's the ability to hold a luxury resident experience standard while simultaneously running a tight financial operation. Coastal Class A communities carry real expectations around amenity presentation, unit condition, and service responsiveness. Managers who treat those as competing priorities tend to struggle. The ones who thrive understand that a market-ready asset and a satisfied resident base are the same goal approached from different angles.

RealPage, Knock, and Onesite experience will help you hit the ground running, as Olympus prefers candidates already comfortable in that software environment. Minimum two years of multifamily property management experience is required, with luxury background preferred.

What Olympus is looking for

  • At least two years of direct property management experience in multifamily, with Class A exposure strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, read financials, and drive NOI performance
  • Experience supervising both office and maintenance teams
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite platforms
  • Full-time availability Monday through Friday, with flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergencies

The compensation structure includes monthly commissions alongside quarterly and annual bonuses, which means your financial upside is tied directly to how the asset performs. Olympus also offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Career pathing and leadership conferences round out an employer that's clearly invested in retention and internal promotion, which matters if your goal is to move into a regional or multi-site role over time. This kind of full-scope property management seat is often the last stop before that transition happens.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Olympus at Three Springs
job.description:
Maintenance technician roles at apartment communities tend to attract two types of candidates: those who can fix things, and those who can fix things while keeping residents satisfied, tracking their work in software, and jumping on an emergency at 9 PM without too much grumbling. Olympus Property is clearly looking for the second type.

Olympus at Three Springs is a residential community in Durango, CO, and this full-time technician position sits within the service team reporting up through a Lead Maintenance Technician. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability built in. That's a relatively standard structure for a managed apartment community, and it means your weeks have shape to them, even if the occasional off-hours call does not.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're moving through a work order queue that covers the usual range: plumbing repairs, appliance troubleshooting, electrical fixture swaps, lock changes, HVAC filter replacements, and coil cleaning. You'll handle minor to moderate plumbing and electrical, which in practice means sink and toilet fixture replacements, switch and outlet repairs, and knowing when something needs to escalate.
