That's a real asset if you're someone who performs well within structure and appreciates direct communication from leadership. It also means expectations are high and visible. If you prefer to operate independently with minimal oversight, this probably isn't the right fit.

What You Bring

  • Prior property management experience, with Class A multifamily background preferred
  • Proven ability to lead and develop an on-site team, including delegation and mentorship
  • Comfort managing competing priorities: leasing, operations, resident relations, and reporting all run simultaneously
  • Strong communication skills and a sense of urgency that comes naturally, not just when someone's watching
  • A solutions-focused mindset. Escalations land on your desk because you're expected to resolve them, not just pass them along

Where This Role Fits in a PM Career

Managing a 342-unit Class A community with a team of seven is genuinely substantial experience. You're building fluency in all the metrics that matter at the portfolio level: occupancy trends, NOI contribution, traffic conversion, renewal rates, and capex coordination. Property Managers who perform well at this scale typically move into Regional Manager or District Manager roles, and the operational discipline you develop working under a structured, corporate-supported model translates directly into managing multiple assets or stepping into a portfolio oversight position.

Austin's multifamily market has been through significant lease-up activity and rent correction over the past few years, with new supply continuing to test occupancy and concessions strategies across the metro. Managing a stabilized asset in that environment, and keeping performance metrics sharp while the broader market fluctuates, is exactly the kind of experience that compounds over time. Weinstein's 70-year track record as a family-owned operator also means you're learning from an organization that has navigated multiple market cycles, which carries real value when you're eventually making decisions at a higher level.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Brix 325 Apartments
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles at well-run apartment companies aren't just about showing units. They're the front line for occupancy, resident experience, and the first impression a community makes. At Brix 325 Apartments in Santa Rosa, MG Properties is looking for someone who can handle that responsibility well.

What the Job Actually Involves

Day to day, you're greeting prospects, qualifying applicants, preparing leases, and making sure new residents get through move-in without friction. That means staying in sync with the maintenance team on make-ready status and keeping rental files current and accurate. You'll also handle the resident-facing side of things: fielding maintenance concerns, addressing complaints professionally, and following up on rent collection. Monthly administrative tasks round out the workload.

The property is Brix 325, a community in Santa Rosa, CA. MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They're an owner-operator, not a third-party manager, which tends to mean more consistency in how properties are run and more internal resources behind the team.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred, not required)
  • Solid sales instincts and genuine customer service skills
  • Attention to detail in data entry and file management
  • Professional communication with both prospects and current residents
  • Comfort working as part of a team in a leasing office environment

Compensation and Growth

The pay range is $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly and quarterly bonuses and company profit sharing. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. That's a solid package for a leasing role.

MG Properties promotes from within. Leasing Consultant is a real starting point here, not a dead end. Strong performers in this role typically move into Assistant Manager positions, where the focus shifts toward financials, delinquency management, and broader property operations. If you want to build a career in property management rather than just fill a leasing seat, the path exists.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one in this role: the ability to convert traffic into leases while keeping existing residents satisfied. Those two things pull in different directions sometimes. The people who do it well stay organized, communicate clearly, and don't let the admin side slip when traffic picks up.

job.title: Maintenance Technician I (Villages)
job.description:
A Maintenance Role With Real Roots

Prometheus Real Estate Group has been operating apartments in the Bay Area since 1965, and as the largest privately held apartment owner in the region, they've had a long time to figure out what good maintenance actually looks like. This Maintenance Technician I position, based at a community in Cupertino, sits at the center of that daily experience. You're not just fixing things. You're the person residents actually see and interact with, often on some of their more stressful days.

The work covers the full range of general maintenance: service requests, apartment turns, appliance repairs, basic plumbing and electrical, carpentry, and painting. If something breaks in a unit, you're the first line of response. When a unit turns, you're moving through the make-ready process to get it rent-ready on time. Prometheus uses "Neighbors" to refer to residents, which tells you something about the culture they're trying to build. The expectation isn't just technical competence. It's showing up with some genuine care for the people who live there.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

On a typical day, you might start with a handful of open service requests, work through a punch list on a recently vacated unit, and field a couple of walk-in concerns from residents along the way. The work shifts quickly. A plumbing call can push your turn schedule back, and you'll need to communicate that clearly to the leasing team and your supervisor. Most of the work happens outdoors or in units rather than in a shop, so you're moving around the property constantly. On-call rotation is part of the role, so after-hours availability matters.

The best technicians in roles like this tend to combine solid trade knowledge with the kind of communication skills that keep residents from escalating. You don't have to be a licensed contractor, but two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience is the baseline. Basic computer proficiency helps, since most work orders run through a digital system. Physical demands are real: lifting up to 50 lbs., climbing, extended time on your feet, and working in varying outdoor conditions.

Compensation, Benefits, and Where This Can Go

The hourly range runs from $26.25 to $30.25, with standby and on-call premium pay added on top. There's a semi-annual discretionary bonus, plus additional incentives tied to referrals, training, renovations, and lease-ups. Benefits are unusually strong for this level: Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums for employees and eligible dependents, with affordable buy-up options available. The 401(k) includes employer matching, and there's tenure-based housing discounts and tuition reimbursement for those who want to build toward something longer term.

For technicians who want to grow, Prometheus operates a vertically integrated platform with value-add renovation work in-house. That creates a real path from general maintenance into renovation-focused roles, lead tech positions, or eventually service manager responsibilities. The company's size in the Bay Area means internal mobility is a genuine option, not just a recruiting line.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum two years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Proficiency across basic appliance, plumbing, electrical, and carpentry repairs
  • Comfort with basic computer tools for work order management
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and perform physical tasks throughout the shift

Prometheus holds B Corporation certification, which reflects a stated commitment to operating as a responsible business. Whether that resonates with you personally or not, it tends to attract people who take their work and their community seriously. If that's the environment where you do your best work, this one's worth a closer look.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance at a well-run mid-rise or high-rise isn't just fixing things. It's protecting an asset, keeping residents from churning, and making sure the team around you stays sharp enough to handle what shows up next. Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager at their Alexandria, VA community to do exactly that work, in a supporting leadership role that sits between hands-on trade work and full property oversight.

What This Role Actually Involves

You'll carry a real technical load here. HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair are daily territory. So is managing the make-ready process, which means tracking turns from vacant to rent-ready with the kind of attention to punch list detail that keeps lease-up timelines honest. Preventative maintenance programs, grounds upkeep, snow removal, and general building cleanliness all fall under your watch. The community runs better because you're keeping score on all of it.

Leadership is also part of the job from day one. You're expected to set standards and model them, not just assign work. That means timeliness on resident service tickets, follow-through on safety codes, and running an operation that stays OSHA-compliant and accident-free. Bozzuto properties carry a reputation for presentation and resident experience, and the maintenance team is a large part of how that reputation holds up.

This role includes weekend availability and participation in the emergency on-call rotation. That's worth stating plainly. After-hours calls happen, and the expectation is that you respond. If that's a dealbreaker, it's better to know upfront.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • At least 5 years of experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC certification, EPA certification, and/or NAPE certification
  • Solid working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems (central plant, boilers, chillers, split systems) is a plus
  • Understanding of OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS
  • Supervisory experience, or a demonstrated readiness to lead a team
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb stairs, use ladders, and work in variable weather

The salary range for this position is $61,000 to $67,000, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

Strong candidates in this role tend to be the ones who treat the building like they own it. Knowing where the shut-offs are, catching deferred maintenance before it becomes an emergency, flagging a failing unit component during a routine walk rather than waiting for a resident to call. That proactive mindset is what separates a good technician from someone ready for a management track.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Portofino Place
job.description:
A prospective resident tours the model at 10 a.m., follows up with three questions by noon, and signs a lease by Friday. That's the cycle this role runs on, and it runs fast. At Cortland Portofino Place in West Palm Beach, the Community Relations Manager sits at the intersection of leasing performance and daily operations, which means the job is genuinely two things at once.

What the Role Actually Involves

On the operations side, you'll support the Community Manager in keeping the property running to brand standard. That includes conducting inspections of vacant units, make-ready apartments, and model homes, as well as handling move-in and move-out walkthroughs. You'll monitor curb appeal, flag maintenance needs, track policy compliance, and manage vendor relationships to keep projects on schedule. Fair Housing and OSHA compliance aren't afterthoughts here. They're part of the daily rhythm.

On the leasing side, you own your pipeline. That means prompt follow-up, consultative conversations with prospective residents, accurate CRM records, and consistent attention to conversion metrics. Cortland tracks KPIs closely, so if numbers like conversion rate and lead-to-lease velocity aren't already part of how you think about your work, they will be here. You'll also manage the community's social media presence and plan resident events designed to build retention, not just fill a calendar.

Resident experience runs through both sides of the role. When a current resident has a complex concern, you handle it with urgency and professionalism. When a prospect has objections, you work through them honestly rather than deflecting. The concierge-level standard Cortland expects is consistent, not situational.

What Cortland Is Looking for

  • At least two years of measurable sales success in a high-velocity, short-cycle environment. Multifamily is the clearest fit, but hospitality, luxury retail, timeshare, or premium automotive backgrounds also translate well.
  • A demonstrated track record of meeting or exceeding quotas, not just holding the role where quotas existed.
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM systems, and Microsoft Office. Social media proficiency matters too, since you'll be contributing to the community's digital presence directly.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to handle difficult conversations without losing composure.
  • High school diploma required. A bachelor's degree is preferred but not mandatory if your track record speaks clearly.

One honest note about the role: the blend of leasing and operations means your attention is split on most days. You might be reviewing a punch list on a make-ready in the morning and closing a lease in the afternoon. Candidates who've only done one or the other sometimes underestimate how much discipline it takes to do both well simultaneously. The people who thrive here tend to be highly organized, genuinely comfortable with accountability metrics, and willing to pick up whatever the day requires without waiting to be asked.

Cortland is a vertically integrated multifamily owner and operator, founded in 2005 and currently ranked among the top ten multifamily owners in the U.S. The in-house design, construction, and management structure means decisions move faster than they do at a third-party management shop, and the resources behind the brand are real. This position is based at Portofino Place in West Palm Beach, Florida.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Regional Manager roles in third-party management carry a different weight than in-house equivalents. You're accountable to ownership groups who expect NOI performance and accurate reporting, while also directing on-site teams who look to you for operational clarity. At Asset Living, one of the larger fee management operators in the country with a portfolio spanning multifamily, single-family rentals, build-to-rent, affordable, and student housing, that dual accountability is the baseline expectation, not an occasional demand.

What You'll Actually Do

This is an offsite leadership role covering a portfolio of communities in the Reno market. Your week won't look the same twice. One day you're reviewing monthly financials, identifying expense line items running over budget, and writing evaluations for ownership. The next you're on-site doing a property inspection, walking punch list items with a maintenance lead, or working through a performance issue with a Community Manager. You'll build annual operating budgets, develop marketing strategies to move occupancy or support rent growth, and monitor delinquency and collections across your sites. Vendor contracts, capital improvement planning, and emergency response coordination are all in scope.

Personnel management takes up more time than most people expect at this level. Screening and hiring site staff, coaching underperformers, documenting counseling statements, approving timesheets, submitting salary recommendations through proper channels: it's consistent, detailed work. If you've managed Community Managers before, you know that the quality of your coaching directly affects everything from leasing conversion to resident retention to maintenance turnaround times.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience overseeing a portfolio of multifamily properties as a Regional or similar offsite role
  • Solid financial acumen: budget development, T-12 analysis, NOI management, and monthly variance reporting
  • Experience with leasing strategy, marketing plans, and occupancy management across multiple sites simultaneously
  • Familiarity with fair housing compliance and company liability standards in an operational context
  • The ability to hold people accountable clearly and consistently, and to document performance issues correctly when termination becomes necessary
  • Comfort working in a third-party management environment where ownership relationships and reporting accuracy carry direct business consequences

A Realistic Look at the Role

Reno's multifamily market has seen real supply pressure in recent years as growth from California migration pushed occupancy up and then new deliveries started catching up. A Regional here needs to read shifting traffic patterns quickly and adjust leasing strategy or concessions before occupancy slides. That kind of market awareness, not just internal reporting, separates strong candidates from average ones at this level.

The honest part: after-hours emergencies happen, difficult ownership conversations happen, and there will be sites where the team needs significant development before performance stabilizes. This role suits someone who doesn't need the work to be easy to find it worthwhile. Asset Living operates across a wide range of asset classes, which means Regional Managers here often build cross-sector experience that transfers well into VP-level roles or portfolio director positions over time.

job.title: Regional Operations Specialist
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on analytical thinking, organized communication, and the ability to hold multiple moving pieces without dropping any of them. The Regional Operations Specialist at Asset Living works directly with senior-level regional managers, handling the kind of behind-the-scenes work that keeps a third-party management portfolio functioning at scale. If you're comfortable pulling financial data, spotting trends in a T-12, and then turning that analysis into a clean client-facing report, you'll recognize what this job actually is: a connective role between field operations and executive decision-making.

Asset Living manages a broad mix of property types, including multifamily, single-family rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing. That breadth means the work here isn't narrowly defined. One week you might be pulling rent comparables and summarizing market trends. The next, you're coordinating travel logistics, fielding resident calls that escalate to the corporate level, or preparing materials for a client performance review. The variety is real, and so is the expectation that you can context-switch without losing accuracy.

What the Work Actually Involves

On the financial side, you'll collect and review historical income and expense data across properties in the assigned portfolio. Understanding how to read that information, and how to present it clearly to clients and managers who need to act on it, is central to the job. Weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting cycles create steady deadlines, and the expectation is that those reports are accurate and on time, not approximately right and eventually submitted.

The market research component involves gathering and analyzing rent comparables and market trends using both internal tools and third-party sources. Experience with property management platforms like MRI or One-Site is helpful here, though not required. Strong Excel skills matter more than any single software platform.

  • Administrative support for senior regional managers
  • Historical income and expense analysis across portfolio properties
  • Client communication and property performance reporting
  • Market research including rent comps and trend analysis
  • Internal project coordination and preparation of supporting materials
  • Resident call handling at the corporate level
  • Travel and logistics coordination as needed

Travel is estimated at around 10% annually, mostly for property visits or internal meetings. It's not a road-warrior role, but you will get out to properties periodically, which helps ground the data work in real context.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The honest challenge in a role like this is that the work is detail-heavy and deadline-driven, and the consequences of errors show up in client reports and management decisions. Candidates who do well here tend to have a genuine tolerance for repetitive accuracy work alongside the more variable project and research tasks. A background in finance, real estate, or economics helps, but what matters most is whether you can move between a messy data request and a client communication without needing someone to reset your priorities for you.

Asset Living is an AMO-accredited, NMHC top-50 firm with a portfolio that spans multiple housing verticals. For someone early in a property management or real estate career, the exposure here to third-party fee management operations, client reporting, and multi-asset portfolio analysis builds transferable skills that carry into asset management, regional manager, or analyst roles down the line. The Des Moines office puts you inside a growing regional operation, not a peripheral one.

job.title: Floating Maintenance Technician - The Brodie
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer recognition three years running (2023, 2024, and 2025), which tells you something about how they treat the people doing the actual work. This Floating Maintenance Technician role is based at The Brodie in Austin and sits right at the intersection of resident satisfaction and property performance. It's a hands-on position where your day is shaped by what the community needs, not a rigid script.

The core of this role is general service work: plumbing repairs, appliance troubleshooting, HVAC maintenance, electrical fixture replacements, lock changes, painting, carpentry. You'll work through resident requests, handle preventative maintenance on HVAC units (filter changes, coil cleaning), and keep the shop organized and inventory tracked. You'll coordinate daily priorities with the Lead Maintenance Technician, which means communication matters as much as technical skill. You're not just fixing things in isolation. You're part of a service team that the office staff depends on to keep residents happy and occupied units in good condition.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with some flexibility built in and the expectation that you're available for emergency calls when they come up. That's a real part of the job, and it's worth being honest about. After-hours emergencies aren't constant, but they happen, and being genuinely okay with that is part of being a good fit here.

Olympus is looking for someone with at least two years of residential, apartment, or commercial maintenance experience. EPA or HVAC certification is a plus, and solid HVAC knowledge is expected regardless of whether the paperwork is in hand.

What makes someone stand out here

The candidates who thrive in floating or generalist maintenance roles aren't necessarily the ones with the most specialized certifications. They're the ones who communicate well with residents during a service visit, who notice a potential issue while fixing the reported one, and who hand off information clearly to the next shift or the lead tech. Austin's rental market runs competitive, and at a property like The Brodie, resident retention often comes down to how quickly and professionally maintenance issues get resolved. That's where this role carries real weight.

  • Minimum 2 years of apartment, residential, or commercial maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; EPA/HVAC certification preferred
  • Comfortable with plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting
  • Able to work a consistent Monday through Friday schedule and respond to emergencies as needed
  • Proficient or willing to learn maintenance tracking software

Starting pay is $27 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and even a sabbatical program. It's a solid total package for a technician who wants stability and room to grow.

job.title: Field Support Supervisor - Multifamily Regional Maintenance
job.description:
Regional maintenance support roles like this one sit at the intersection of field operations and asset management. You're not running a single property's shop. You're the technical backbone across a portfolio, the person onsite teams call when something is outside their wheelhouse or when a capital project needs a second set of experienced eyes before the check gets written.

What This Role Actually Covers

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned operator with more than 70 years in the business, self-managing communities across Virginia, the Carolinas, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. This position supports their DFW-area communities as part of the company's Asset Management and Support team. The work is varied by design. On any given week you might be walking a property to assess water intrusion issues, reviewing contractor proposals for scope and cost reasonableness, or helping facilitate a handoff from the Construction Group to the onsite team with proper documentation and knowledge transfer. That last piece is more important than it sounds. Transitions between construction and property-level oversight are where things fall through the cracks, and this role exists partly to prevent that.

Day-to-day, you'll work alongside property managers and maintenance supervisors to prioritize needs, define work scope, vet vendors, and see projects through to completion. You'll also actively recruit quality contractors to bid work, which matters more than people realize. A thin bidder pool leads to inflated proposals and rushed decisions. Part of the value you bring is knowing who the good operators are in the market and getting them to the table.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • At least 3 years in a multifamily regional support capacity
  • 5 or more years in multifamily maintenance overall
  • EPA certification at Type I and II or Universal level
  • Hands-on capex experience: exterior building repairs, water intrusion remediation, erosion issues, blueprint reading, and writing work requirements
  • Comfort with vendor management and proposal review
  • Valid driver's license (this is a field role, not a desk role)

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who tend to struggle in regional support roles are the ones who were excellent hands-on maintenance supervisors but haven't made the shift to advising others rather than doing the work themselves. The technical knowledge is necessary, but so is the ability to evaluate someone else's approach, give clear guidance without taking over, and document findings in a way that's actually useful to the next person who reads it. If you've spent time writing scopes of work, managing bid processes, and coordinating construction-to-operations transitions, that experience will matter more than almost anything else here.

Weinstein offers competitive compensation, benefits, and a 401(k). For someone looking to grow within a stable, privately held operator that has stayed the course for seven decades, there's real runway here on the asset management side of the business.

job.title: Dual-Site Leasing Consultant - Tivalli Apartments/Newberry Square Apartments
job.description:
Leasing is often described as a sales job, and it is. But the consultants who thrive long-term in property management understand that it's equally a relationship and operations role. This dual-site position at MG Properties, covering Tivalli Apartments and Newberry Square Apartments in Lynnwood, WA, gives you a chance to develop all three skill sets at once.

Working across two communities sharpens something that single-site roles rarely do: adaptability. Each property has its own rhythm, its own resident profile, and its own occupancy story. You'll learn to read traffic patterns across both communities, adjust your pitch based on what each property needs in a given week, and coordinate move-ins with maintenance teams at two different locations. That coordination piece matters more than most job postings acknowledge. A smooth move-in depends on a punched unit, accurate lease paperwork, and a resident who feels genuinely welcomed. When those three things come together consistently, it shows in retention numbers.

The day-to-day work includes greeting and qualifying prospective residents, preparing and executing leases, keeping rental files current and accurate, and handling resident concerns with professionalism. You'll also support monthly administrative tasks and help ensure the property's records stay organized. MG Properties uses a leasing software system, so accurate data entry is part of the job, not an afterthought.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one isn't just sales confidence. It's the ability to manage competing priorities without letting either property feel like the afterthought. Prospective residents at Tivalli don't know you were just at Newberry Square, and they shouldn't have to. Consistency of service across both sites is the real skill this role develops.

What You'll Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Genuine sales ability paired with customer service instincts
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry
  • Professional communication with both prospective and current residents
  • The organizational discipline to manage files and paperwork across two sites

MG Properties has operated across the Western United States for over 30 years, with a track record in acquisition, development, rehabilitation, and management. They promote from within, which means this role can be a real starting point. Leasing consultants who build strong occupancy records and demonstrate operational reliability tend to move into assistant manager roles. From there, the path to property manager becomes much shorter than most people expect when they're first starting out.

Compensation ranges from $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and rental discounts.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a calendar that doesn't care about your weekends. The annual turn at a collegiate property is unlike anything in conventional multifamily. You've got a hard move-out date, a hard move-in date, and every unit on the property cycling simultaneously. The General Manager at View on 10th owns that process from planning through punch list, and that context shapes everything about this role.

View on 10th is a Scion-managed student community in Waco, TX, serving the Baylor University market. Scion operates at scale in the purpose-built student housing sector, and this GM position sits at the center of property operations: financial performance, staff leadership, facilities oversight, leasing velocity, and resident experience all report up through this role.

Day to day, that means working closely with an Assistant General Manager and Facilities Supervisor to keep the asset running cleanly between turns, while simultaneously planning for the next one. During peak leasing season you're monitoring traffic and concessions. During turn, you're pulling move-out inspections, walking vendor service progress, managing Turnable boards, and yes, occasionally moving furniture. The role doesn't ask you to manage from a distance.

On the financial side, this position carries real budget accountability. You're preparing annual and capex budgets, managing variance reporting, handling invoice entry and payroll, and working to protect NOI through both expense discipline and revenue performance. Gain to lease, leasing velocity, and market rate achievement are all KPIs this role owns. Scion uses Vena for budgeting and Entrata as the PMS, so comfort with those platforms matters. Experience with the broader tech stack, including Qualtrics, Greenhouse, Lattice, and ClickUp, is a plus.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just operational competence. Student housing GMs who thrive long-term tend to be genuinely calm under the particular chaos of move-in weekend, skilled at building seasonal staff quickly, and honest with themselves about delinquency trends before they become a problem. The resident base is young, the expectations are high, and reputation management on public platforms carries real weight in lease-up velocity the following year.

What Scion is Looking For

  • Minimum 3 years managing a residential community with a team of 3 or more direct reports
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata experience preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, vendor relationships, and financial reporting
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across staff, residents, and ownership-side stakeholders
  • Comfort with conflict resolution, both with residents and within a team
  • Eligibility to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

This role includes standard business hours with the honest caveat that student housing has its own rhythm. Peak periods, emergencies, and on-call responsibilities come with the territory. The position is exempt and includes health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, PTO, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. The job is on-site at the Waco property.

job.title: Dual-Site Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a dual-site role covering both Lark West Lafayette Apartments and Lark West Lafayette Townhomes, which means you're managing operational continuity across two distinct asset types simultaneously. On any given day, you might be reviewing delinquency reports to keep month-end below 2%, coordinating vendor walkthroughs on one property while a work order backlog builds on the other, or stepping into the General Manager seat when they're out. The role sits between pure execution and junior leadership. You own enough to matter, but you're still learning the full P&L picture.

Financially, you'll help prepare month-end reports, reconcile accounts receivable, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, and enforce late fee and NSF collection policies. Operationally, you'll run monthly property walks, respond to escalated resident concerns, manage utility billing and resident accounts, and track KPIs like leasing velocity, concessions, and gain-to-lease. The Customer and Sales Experience Manager owns the leasing strategy, but you're a close partner on execution and reporting.

The annual turn is where this role gets genuinely demanding. Student housing turns are compressed, high-volume, and unforgiving on timing. You'll work inside Turnable to track the electronic turn board, conduct move-out inspections, process damage charges, handle disputes, and provide hands-on help during peak weeks. That includes moving furniture, assisting with punch list items, and managing the sheer volume of resident trash that comes with a full-building turnover. This isn't a role that watches from a clipboard.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of on-site experience in property management or residential living communities
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata experience strongly preferred
  • Strong written communication skills, given the volume of resident notices, review responses, and escalation handling
  • Comfort managing multiple priorities across two sites without letting either one slip
  • Familiarity with or willingness to learn platforms including Greenhouse, Lattice, Turnable, Qualtrics, ClickUp, and Microsoft Office
  • A genuine customer-service orientation, not just a talking point. Resident escalations land on your desk and you're expected to resolve them
  • Discretion with confidential resident and employee information

The Bigger Picture

Student housing operates on a fundamentally different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Occupancy targets are built around academic calendars, not rolling 12-month absorption. Traffic and leasing velocity spike hard in fall and spring, then quiet down. Turns happen in a matter of weeks rather than staggered throughout the year. If you've worked conventional multifamily and are transitioning into student, that compressed turn window is the biggest operational adjustment you'll face.

What separates a strong candidate here isn't just systems knowledge or leasing experience. It's the ability to hold accountability across two properties, keep delinquency controlled, stay composed during turn chaos, and build enough trust with the GM to step in confidently when needed. Assistant General Managers who perform well in student housing at this level typically progress to General Manager roles managing a single asset's full operations, with ownership of budgets, staffing, and NOI outcomes. This role builds the foundation for that transition.

Scion is a student housing operator with properties across multiple markets. The West Lafayette location puts you in a Purdue University market, which carries consistent demand but also a concentrated leasing season tied tightly to the academic year. If you want a role where the metrics are clear and the pace is real, this one delivers both.

job.title: Leasing and Experience Manager (Villages)
job.description:
Most apartment companies treat the leasing-to-management pipeline as a straight ladder: leasing agent, assistant manager, community manager. Prometheus built something a little different. The Leasing and Experience Manager role at their Cupertino community sits at the intersection of sales leadership, resident relations, and daily operations, which means the skills you build here compound in ways a conventional assistant manager title doesn't fully capture.

Prometheus is the largest privately held apartment owner in the Bay Area, with a portfolio of over 13,000 homes across Silicon Valley, Portland, and Seattle. They operate vertically integrated, keeping acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and property management all in-house. That structure matters for your career because it means internal mobility is real, not a talking point.

What This Role Actually Covers

The scope here is broader than a typical assistant manager position. On any given weekend (and weekends are a core part of the schedule, with weekday days off in exchange), you might be coaching a leasing agent through a close, reviewing pricing and concessions to protect occupancy, following up on a resident concern to make sure it was actually resolved, and planning a community event. That blend of supervisory, sales, and relationship work is the point. You're not siloed into one function.

On the operations side, you'll work with resident profiles, delinquency, and occupancy reporting. You'll help shape leasing strategy by developing a working knowledge of local market conditions, which in Cupertino means understanding a high-demand, supply-constrained submarket where residents expect a premium experience. You'll also contribute to marketing programs designed to maximize traffic and rental activity.

  • At least two years of leasing experience required
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; high school diploma or GED required
  • Strong background in customer service, sales, or marketing environments
  • Comfortable supervising a team, setting goals, and developing leasing staff
  • Weekend availability is a consistent part of the schedule

Compensation and What Builds Over Time

Base pay runs from $33.25 to $38.00 per hour, with a $200 incentive per lease, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and weekend shift premium pay layered on top. Additional bonuses apply for referrals, training coaching, renovations, lease-up assignments, and leasing contests. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for you and eligible dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, tenure-based housing discounts, and twelve paid holidays including your birthday.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds the exact muscle memory that community manager positions require: comfort with pricing decisions, the ability to lead a team without micromanaging, and the judgment to handle resident escalations before they become real problems. Candidates who do well here typically have strong instincts about when to close a conversation and when to keep listening. That's harder to teach than leasing mechanics, and it's what separates good performance from a promotion track.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position lives at the intersection of people skills and financial accountability. You'll spend real time on leasing conversations, resident de-escalation, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up, often in the same afternoon. The ability to shift between a warm, consultative tone with a prospective resident and a clear-headed, detail-focused mindset when reconciling payment postings is genuinely what separates people who thrive here from those who struggle.

Hawthorne Residential Partners is a top-50 multifamily operator with deep roots in the Southeast, and their Orange City community reflects that regional culture: relationship-driven, service-oriented, and expectation-conscious. This isn't a background-role position. The Assistant Community Manager is visible to residents, to the team, and to regional leadership every week.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Leasing is a meaningful part of the job. You'll conduct tours, respond to incoming leads, guide applicants through the leasing process, and make sure renewals and documentation are completed accurately and on time. Occupancy goals are real here, and your leasing performance contributes directly to hitting them. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which means thinking about how to authentically represent resident life and community events, not just posting filler content.

On the financial side, you'll handle rent collection, check scanning, payment posting, and weekly delinquency calls. Ledger reviews are part of your regular rhythm, and you'll coordinate eviction procedures when other options are exhausted. If numbers make you nervous, this role will push you to get comfortable with them fast. That's not a warning, it's an honest description of the work.

When the Community Manager is out, you step up. You keep the team focused, maintain momentum, and handle whatever the day brings. That kind of coverage responsibility is what makes this role a genuine developmental opportunity rather than just a support position.

Strong candidates typically have at least two years of property management experience and some prior time in an assistant manager capacity. A valid driver's license is required. A CALP credential is a plus but not a requirement.

What's Distinctive About This Role at Hawthorne

Hawthorne runs a structured Career Path Program, and the Assistant Community Manager role is explicitly positioned as a stepping stone to Community Manager. That's not just recruiting language. Their Learning and Development team is actively involved in employee progression, which matters if you're looking for a company that will invest in where you're going, not just where you are now.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off each week to keep the total at 40 hours. Some evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events. It's a real retail-style schedule, which is standard for leasing offices, and worth factoring into your decision.

If you're someone who genuinely enjoys working with people, can hold yourself accountable to financial metrics, and want a clear path toward running your own community, this role is worth a close look.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Assistant Community Manager role sits right at the intersection of leasing, operations, and finance. At a well-run property, this person is the engine behind day-to-day continuity. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a top-50 multifamily operator with deep Southeast roots, this position at Hawthorne at Southside in Asheville carries real responsibility across all three areas.

What This Role Actually Covers

On the leasing side, you'll handle tours, follow up on leads, guide prospects through applications, and work renewals. Occupancy doesn't manage itself, and this position owns a meaningful piece of that outcome. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which at most properties now means consistent content tied to resident events and community engagement rather than a few posts a month.

The financial side is where a lot of ACMs either prove themselves or struggle. You'll post payments, run ledger reviews, monitor delinquency, make weekly follow-up calls, and coordinate eviction procedures when it gets to that point. Hawthorne expects you to read the financials and act on them, not just pass paperwork up the chain. If you've never done ledger audits or tracked delinquency through to legal, that's a skill set you'll build quickly here.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the site. That's not a footnote in the job description. It means you need to be comfortable setting the tone for the team and handling whatever comes through the door.

What Separates Strong Candidates from Average Ones

Two years of property management experience is preferred, and at least six months at the ACM level. The CALP designation is a plus but not required. What actually separates a strong candidate here isn't the credential. It's whether you can hold a delinquency conversation with a resident in the morning, pivot to a tour in the afternoon, and close a renewal before the office shuts down. That range of gear-shifting is the job.

Asheville's rental market has tightened and loosened in cycles, and Class A communities there compete on experience as much as price. Strong retention instincts matter. Concessions are easy to offer; keeping a resident because you actually resolved their concern is harder and worth more to the NOI.

Compensation and Career Path

The role pays hourly and includes monthly leasing and renewal commissions plus quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program, and the ACM-to-Community Manager track is real. If you're looking to get to the CM seat, this is a legitimate step. The company's Learning and Development team is structured to support that progression, not just mention it in a job posting.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of ACM experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP accreditation a plus
  • Weekend availability required on a rotating basis

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Evening and weekend availability may come up around resident events.

job.title: Market Maintenance Manager IV
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday and two units need to turn by Friday, a vendor didn't show up for a scheduled inspection, and there's already a work order in from the weekend on-call. That's not a bad week at Washington Mill 240. That's just Tuesday.

What This Role Actually Involves

John M. Corcoran and Company is hiring a Maintenance Manager for Washington Mill 240, a residential community in Lawrence, MA. JMC has been operating in New England since 1951, and the maintenance team here reflects that same expectation of steady, accountable work. This isn't a hands-off supervisory role. You'll be in the middle of daily operations: reviewing work orders, walking units, managing your crew, and keeping the property physically sound and resident-ready.

Day to day, you'll oversee all maintenance operations including preventive maintenance scheduling, unit turnovers, inspections, and vendor coordination. You'll supervise maintenance technicians, janitorial staff, and grounds personnel, which means you're accountable for the quality and pace of their output, not just your own. Budget adherence matters here. You'll track supplies, manage purchase orders, and work within set cost parameters. When units turn, you'll coordinate closely with the management team to make sure make-ready timelines stay on track and units are move-in ready when they need to be.

The on-call rotation is real. After-hours emergencies happen, and this role participates in that coverage. If that's a dealbreaker, it's worth knowing upfront. If you've already been doing on-call in a maintenance role, it won't be a surprise.

What JMC Is Looking For

  • A high school diploma or equivalent; experience counts alongside credentials here
  • At least three years of hands-on trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and general building systems
  • Demonstrated ability to lead a team, not just work alongside one
  • Strong organizational habits and clear communication with both staff and residents
  • Comfort following safety procedures and company policy consistently

The pay range for this position runs from $47.50 to $54.00 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with company match. The standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with on-call rotation included.

What separates strong candidates here isn't technical knowledge alone. It's the ability to hold a crew accountable without micromanaging, keep turns moving without cutting corners on quality, and stay organized when three things break at once. JMC has retained team members for decades, which suggests the culture rewards people who show up consistently and take the work seriously. If you're coming from a similar supervisory maintenance role and want a company with real institutional stability, this is worth a close look.

job.title: Seasonal Grounds Person
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This seasonal role at Quincy Commons puts you on the ground floor of what keeps a residential community looking sharp through the busiest months of the year. Five mornings a week, you're out early handling the work that sets the tone for every resident's day: mowing and trimming lawns, pruning plantings, pulling trash, clearing pet waste stations, and keeping the common areas clean and presentable. When something on the exterior needs attention, whether that's a fence repair, touch-up painting, or a minor installation, you'll assist with that too. You'll also keep an eye out for safety hazards and coordinate with vendors when a task falls outside your scope.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., giving you 25 hours per week with some flexibility built in. This is a summer position, but the work is real and the expectations are professional.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience with landscaping and grounds maintenance
  • Comfort operating standard landscaping equipment safely
  • The ability to work independently and stay on task without constant supervision
  • Clear communication, especially when flagging hazards or coordinating with a team
  • A strong work ethic and attention to detail in how a property looks and feels

Why This Role Is Worth Taking Seriously

Curb appeal isn't cosmetic in property management. It directly affects how prospective residents perceive a community during tours, how current residents feel about where they live, and how ownership views the site's presentation. A grounds person who operates with consistency and care is genuinely valuable to the maintenance team, not just seasonal filler.

John M. Corcoran and Company has operated in New England since 1951 and carries a reputation built on long-term relationships with both residents and staff. That kind of organizational culture tends to notice people who show up and do the work well. For someone building experience in property maintenance, this is the kind of employer where a seasonal role can turn into something more, if that's a direction you want to explore.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one isn't just knowing how to run a mower. It's showing up consistently, keeping the property's standards in mind throughout a shift, and communicating proactively when something looks off. Those habits are exactly what property management teams remember when full-time positions open up. Pay for this role runs between $16.00 and $18.75 per hour depending on experience.

job.title: Community Manager - The Fort Apartments
job.description:
The Fort Apartments is a 224-unit community in Indianapolis, and Ackermann Group has been operating in the Midwest since 1938. That's not a startup with a ping-pong table. It's a company that has survived multiple real estate cycles by doing the fundamentals well, and they're looking for a Community Manager who can do the same.

This is a full-scope site leadership role. You're running the property: financial performance, occupancy, team management, capex coordination, turns, and resident relations. You'll work directly with a Maintenance Supervisor on the operational side, which means punch lists, preventative maintenance schedules, and service request completion all fall within your purview. On the leasing side, you'll collaborate with your Regional Manager and corporate recruiting to staff the team, set performance goals, and keep traffic converting. You're the decision-maker on-site when residents or prospects have concerns, and you're accountable to the budget.

Ackermann uses Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe CRM, EliseAI, and AIRM. If you've worked with that stack before, you'll get up to speed quickly. If you haven't, it's learnable, but you need to be genuinely comfortable pulling reports and reading what they're telling you. Financial literacy here isn't optional. You'll be expected to understand your NOI drivers, manage delinquency, and have an honest read on where your T-3 and T-12 are heading.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this role: EliseAI is an AI-powered leasing assistant, and its presence in the tech stack signals that Ackermann is moving toward automated lead response and follow-up. Strong candidates will know how to work alongside that kind of tool rather than around it. The managers who struggle are the ones who treat it as a threat to their leasing team instead of a filter that hands them warmer, more qualified conversations.

What They're Looking For

  • At least two years of residential property management experience, or comparable leadership and operations background
  • Demonstrated ability to hit financial targets at the community level
  • Comfortable with property management software, specifically the Yardi ecosystem
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • CAM certification preferred; bachelor's degree preferred but not required
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, plus at least one Saturday per month

Ackermann offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid time off including your birthday, an employee rent discount across their portfolio, quarterly bonuses, and lease commission. Career development is listed as a priority, which at a company with this tenure tends to mean something. Indianapolis is a market where a well-run Class B garden-style community can perform consistently, and 224 units is a size where a manager can actually know their property without drowning in it. That's not a small thing.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Saturday morning, the leasing office opens in ten minutes, and there are already two walk-ins waiting by the door. That's the job in a nutshell. If you thrive in that moment rather than dread it, read on.

Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their community in St. Augustine, FL. This is a front-line sales and service role, and it carries real weight. Traffic converts to leases, leases drive occupancy, and occupancy drives NOI. The person sitting across from a prospect during a tour is the one who makes or breaks that outcome.

What the Role Covers

Day-to-day, you're owning the full leasing cycle: fielding inquiries by phone and email, scheduling and conducting tours, overcoming objections, and closing. You'll prep and process applications, handle prorations and rent calculations at move-in, and keep lease files organized and audit-ready. Renewals are part of your scope too, not just new leases. Waypoint also expects you to contribute to outreach and referral efforts to keep traffic coming in, not just work the leads that land in your lap.

The model unit and leasing office are your responsibility to keep tour-ready. That's a small thing that matters a lot. First impressions close leases or kill them.

  • Conduct tours, follow-ups, and prospect communication across all channels
  • Qualify applicants and prepare files for manager review and approval
  • Manage lease preparation, move-in paperwork, and financial communications
  • Maintain accurate records in the property management system (Yardi experience is a plus)
  • Support occupancy goals through new leases, renewals, and waitlist management
  • Apply Fair Housing regulations and company leasing policies consistently
  • Weekend rotation required

What Waypoint Is Looking For

Two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience is preferred. More important than the resume line is whether you can read a prospect, adjust your pitch, and close without being pushy about it. Bilingual English/Spanish is preferred given the regional market, and it's genuinely useful in St. Augustine, not just a checkbox. A valid driver's license is required.

Fair Housing knowledge matters here. If you don't have formal training, be ready to get it quickly.

Waypoint offers monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a Leaser of the Month monetary reward, an employee housing discount, 120 hours of PTO in year one, two floating days, medical/dental/vision coverage starting day one, 401k with company match, and commuter and referral benefits.

One honest note on where strong candidates separate themselves in this role: it's follow-up. The tour is easy. The conversion happens in the days after, in how consistently and personally you stay in contact with a prospect who's still shopping. The consultants who build a pipeline rather than just react to walk-ins are the ones who hit their numbers and move up. Leasing Consultant is a common entry point into Assistant Manager and eventually Property Manager roles, and Waypoint's recognition programs suggest they're paying attention to who performs.

job.title: Full-Time Concierge (Mon-Fri 4pm-12am)
job.description:
The evening shift at a Class A community runs on a different rhythm than the daytime. Traffic slows, but the stakes don't. Residents returning from work, guests arriving for visits, deliveries piling up, a maintenance issue that nobody caught during the day walk. The concierge on the 4pm to midnight shift is often the last line of quality control before the building goes quiet, and that requires a specific kind of person.

Comstock is hiring a full-time evening concierge for their Rockville, MD community, Monday through Friday. The role centers on front-of-house presence: greeting residents and guests, managing access control so only authorized individuals enter, handling incoming calls, and coordinating reservations for amenity spaces, loading elevators, and the loading dock. You'll also complete building walks each shift, flagging maintenance items, straightening common areas, and keeping the reception desk organized and professional. The work is active, not sedentary, and it asks you to hold a lot of moving pieces simultaneously.

What this role requires is a foundation in high-end customer service, at least a year of concierge or comparable hospitality experience, and the communication skills to handle both a polite resident inquiry and a frustrated complaint without losing composure. Proficiency in Outlook, Word, and Excel matters for day-to-day coordination tasks. What it builds is something harder to teach: the ability to read a space, anticipate needs before they become requests, and represent a property's brand through every interaction, including the routine ones at 10pm when nobody's watching.

The strongest candidates in this type of role aren't just friendly. They're observant. They notice the chair that's slightly out of place, the guest who's been waiting a few minutes too long, the call that needs to go to maintenance rather than management. That attention to detail, combined with genuine accountability, is what separates a good concierge from one residents actually trust and remember.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum one year of concierge or high-end customer service experience preferred
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when needed
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Self-directed, accountable, and comfortable working independently during evening hours

Comstock offers a competitive salary in the $18 to $22 per hour range for this position, along with a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, housing discount, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, parental leave, and annual professional development funds. The company also offers advancement opportunities across its growing portfolio, which makes this a reasonable entry point for someone looking to build a longer career in residential property management.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is where a property's financial story begins. Every tour, every follow-up call, every application processed ties directly to occupancy and NOI. The Leasing Consultant role at Berkshire Residential Investments exists at that front line, and it demands more craft than it often gets credit for.

Berkshire owns and manages its own assets, which means you're not working for a third-party fee management shop where decisions happen somewhere else. You're embedded in the operation, which gives leasing work here a different kind of weight. Your closing ratio, your tour presentation, your resident communications all feed the same asset your company holds on its books.

What This Role Actually Requires

Berkshire sets a clear performance baseline: a closing ratio of at least 20%. That number matters because it gives you something concrete to measure yourself against. Strong leasing consultants know their traffic sources, track their own conversion week to week, and adjust their pitch based on what prospects actually object to, not just what they hope they'll hear.

Beyond the sales function, the role carries real administrative responsibility. Keeping the leasing office and tour routes in sharp condition, maintaining accurate records, and communicating clearly in writing are not secondary tasks. They're the scaffolding that makes the sales work credible. Residents and prospects notice when the details are off.

You'll also be expected to stay current on local market conditions, which means knowing competitor concessions, understanding where your property sits in the market tier, and bringing useful intelligence to your property manager rather than waiting to be briefed.

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience (property management background helpful but not required)
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to adapt as platforms change
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A genuine interest in helping people find a home, not just closing a transaction

What This Role Builds

A leasing consultant position done well is one of the most transferable foundations in property management. You develop market awareness, sales discipline, resident relations skills, and administrative fluency at the same time. Those are exactly the competencies that property managers and assistant managers lean on every day. Consultants who take the closing ratio seriously, who study their traffic patterns, and who treat the move-in experience as carefully as the initial tour tend to move into assistant management roles faster than those who treat leasing as a purely social job.

Berkshire offers personal development plans alongside its benefits package, which signals that internal growth is an actual priority rather than a talking point. If you're early in your property management career and want a role where performance is visible and progression is real, this is a reasonable place to build that foundation.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor, 300-500 Units - 212
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance supervision at a 300 to 500 unit community is a coordination job as much as a technical one. You need solid hands-on knowledge, yes, but the bigger daily demand is organizing people, time, and resources so the work actually gets done right. At Berkshire at The Rim, you're running a service team, managing the shop, keeping inventory stocked, and making sure your crew has what they need before they show up at a resident's door. Your technical background earns you credibility with the team. Your organizational skills are what keep the property running.

Scheduling is a real skill here. Balancing make-ready turns, preventive maintenance, and unplanned service requests without letting anything fall through takes practice. You'll also need to stay familiar with the property budget and contribute to long-range capital planning conversations. That means understanding the difference between a repair that buys another year and one that signals a capex line item is overdue.

What You're Actually Responsible For

You manage the performance of your service team. That includes coaching, setting individual goals, and modeling the standard you expect. You support the Property Manager in holding the community to company policies and making sure safety protocols aren't optional. Route inspections and model units fall under your watch. If a prospective resident walks a unit today, it needs to reflect the quality your team is capable of.

  • At least 2 years of experience managing maintenance operations at a residential community
  • At least 1 year of direct team leadership
  • Comfort with technology and property management software
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage inventory, supplies, equipment, and key security

One honest note: this is a role where after-hours calls happen. Equipment doesn't fail on a schedule, and residents notice when something's wrong at 9pm. If you've led a maintenance team before, that's not a surprise. If it would be, it's worth knowing upfront.

What's Different About Doing This Here

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions move differently than they do at a third-party management shop. You're not waiting on an owner who has never seen the property to approve a repair. The people setting policy are the same ones invested in the outcome. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that matters. It tends to mean less friction when you need something done correctly rather than cheaply.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones isn't just technical range. It's whether you actually enjoy developing the people on your team. A supervisor who fixes everything themselves keeps the work moving short-term but builds a team that doesn't grow. Berkshire is looking for someone who coaches, delegates with accountability, and takes some satisfaction in watching a newer tech handle something they couldn't six months ago. That's the job within the job.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Strong communication skills, financial awareness, and the ability to shift between leasing and leadership without losing momentum are what this role runs on. The Assistant General Manager position at Bozzuto's Boston community sits at the intersection of all three, and candidates who've only done one or two of those things well will feel the gap quickly.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're covering the full range of on-site operations when the General Manager is present, and running point when they're not. That means conducting tours that convert, managing rent collection, posting receipts, and keeping delinquency tight. It also means walking the property with a critical eye, making sure the exterior and common areas hold up to a high standard, and stepping in to coach team members when the situation calls for it.

The financial side of this role is real. You'll work toward occupancy and retention goals with an understanding of how leasing activity connects to NOI. You're not just showing apartments. You're building a case for why someone should sign and stay, and then doing the follow-through that keeps them there.

Weekend availability is part of the job structure, roughly one to two weekends per month, with weekday time off in exchange. That's worth knowing upfront.

Skills This Role Puts to Work

  • Leasing and sales: conducting personalized tours, converting traffic to signed leases
  • Delinquency management: rent collection, posting receipts, tracking accounts receivable
  • Team leadership: covering GM responsibilities, mentoring staff, setting the behavioral standard
  • Resident relations: handling issues with genuine care, not just scripted responses
  • Social media: creating and posting content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook
  • Software proficiency: Yardi preferred, comfort with property management platforms generally

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Boston's rental market is competitive, and residents at a Bozzuto community expect a certain level of attentiveness. The candidates who do well in this AGM role aren't just organized or friendly. They're the ones who notice when something's off before a resident has to say anything, who can close a lease without it feeling transactional, and who understand that delinquency follow-up and a warm resident event can both happen in the same afternoon. Experience with Yardi and a background in property management, hospitality, or retail all translate well here. A four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience is expected.

Compensation for this role falls between $68,000 and $72,000 annually, with bonus eligibility, medical, dental and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates across design, construction, and property management, and the maintenance team is what keeps the resident experience from falling apart at the seams. This Assistant Maintenance Manager role sits at Lakewood, WA and reports into the building's maintenance leadership. You're not just fixing things. You're running a program.

Day to day, that means closing out service tickets with the kind of follow-through residents actually notice, keeping the make-ready process moving so units turn on time and leasing has inventory to work with, and executing preventative maintenance before small issues become capital problems. You'll work across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair while also keeping an eye on the bigger mechanical systems: central plant, boilers, split systems. The building's overall condition reflects directly on your work.

There's a supervisory component here too. You're expected to lead by example and hold the team to a standard, not just complete tasks yourself. That means coaching habits around safety, cleanliness, and code compliance, not just correcting mistakes after the fact. OSHA awareness and a working knowledge of MSDS aren't checkbox items at Bozzuto. They're part of how the operation runs daily.

On-call rotation and weekend availability are part of the job. Emergency response at a residential property isn't predictable, and candidates who've done this work before already know that.

What this role calls for

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities maintenance, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Hands-on proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Exposure to complex mechanical systems (boilers, chillers, central plant) is a plus
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, even informal, preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, use ladders, and work in varying outdoor conditions

The pay range is $28 to $32 per hour, with bonus eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: the ability to think like an owner. Technicians fix what's broken. The best assistant maintenance managers catch what's about to break, document it, and build a case for the repair before it becomes an emergency or a capex line item. If you read a property's mechanical systems the way some people read weather patterns, that instinct matters here.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Belmar
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on two skill sets that don't always coexist comfortably: sales discipline and operational follow-through. At Cortland Belmar in Lakewood, CO, the Community Relations Manager closes leases, manages a pipeline, and hits conversion KPIs. Then, in the same shift, that person is doing move-in walkthroughs, flagging make-ready punch list items, and keeping vendor relationships on track. If you're strongest at one and weak at the other, the job will show it quickly.

The sales side is consultative. You're working prospects through a short cycle, updating CRM records after every interaction, and following up with enough consistency to move people from interest to signed lease. Cortland positions its communities as premium product, so the conversation isn't just about square footage. You're presenting a living experience and handling objections without flinching. A background in multifamily leasing, hospitality, or any high-contact sales environment where you had real quotas and real accountability translates well here.

What the Operational Side Actually Looks Like

Alongside the leasing work, you'll support the Community Manager in keeping daily operations compliant and consistent. That means regular inspections of vacant units, model homes, and common areas. It means catching curb appeal issues before they become a brand problem. It means knowing your Fair Housing guidelines cold, because this role touches resident interactions at every stage of the leasing process.

You'll also manage the community's social media presence and plan resident events. Those responsibilities sound lighter on paper than they are in practice. Resident engagement programming takes real coordination, and social content that doesn't feel generic requires actual effort and consistency.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is simple: the ability to shift modes without losing momentum. Closing a lease and then immediately walking a vacant unit to flag a maintenance issue before a scheduled showing requires mental flexibility. People who treat the operational tasks as secondary to leasing tend to struggle. Both sides of this job feed occupancy and NOI.

What's Distinctive About This Role at Cortland

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator, which means design, construction, and management all sit under one roof. For the onsite team, that typically means better resources for capital improvements and less friction when escalating maintenance or property condition issues. It also means the brand standards are specific and consistently enforced. You're expected to show up to every resident interaction with the same level of polish the physical product projects.

  • 2 or more years of measurable sales success with real quotas, ideally in multifamily, hospitality, or a comparable premium service environment
  • Comfort with CRM systems, property management software, and Microsoft Office
  • Experience managing social media for a brand or community, not just personal use
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to de-escalate difficult resident situations professionally
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

This role is a legitimate stepping stone toward a Community Manager position. You're operating as a support partner to management now, but the combination of leasing performance, operational exposure, and resident relations experience builds exactly the profile that moves into full site leadership.

job.title: Regional Leasing Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a remote role with real reach.
