A Business Manager who loves the numbers but struggles to motivate a team will hit a ceiling quickly. So will one who builds great resident relationships but loses track of budget variances. At a luxury community like Cielo, both matter constantly, and the Regional team will expect you to be fluent in both. The pay range is $75,000 to $80,000 base, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonuses on top of that.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Every apartment community makes its first impression before a prospective resident ever steps inside a unit. The condition of the grounds, the cleanliness of the breezeways, the state of the pet waste stations , these details shape how people feel about a place before they've spoken to a single leasing agent. The Groundskeeper role exists because that first impression requires real, consistent, daily effort from someone who actually cares about it.

Weinstein Properties has operated for more than 70 years as a family-owned company, managing over 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. They're not a faceless REIT. They take a hands-on approach to operations, and that philosophy extends to how they invest in their on-site teams. This opening is at Bexley 3Five, a community in South Austin.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Honest answer: this job has some unglamorous parts. Picking up pet waste, trashing out vacant apartments, cleaning up after other people , those tasks are daily and recurring. If you need variety to stay motivated, you'll want to think carefully. But if you're someone who takes satisfaction in leaving a space noticeably better than you found it, that repetition becomes its own rhythm.

Beyond the daily rounds, you'll operate equipment including backpack blowers and power washers, handle light planting and weeding, assist with make-ready support when the maintenance team needs an extra set of hands, and occasionally take on light painting or housekeeping tasks. You'll work Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, outdoors year-round. Austin summers are genuinely hot, and this role requires working through that, along with cold snaps, rain, and humidity. Physical stamina matters here: expect prolonged walking and standing, frequent lifting up to 50 pounds, and a lot of bending and stooping.

Who Fits Well Here

The traits Weinstein calls out are worth taking seriously. Reliability isn't a soft quality in this role , if the grounds don't get walked in the morning, nobody else covers it. Self-motivation matters because you'll often be working independently without someone checking in. And a collaborative spirit helps too, because you'll be part of a broader on-site team that includes maintenance techs and leasing staff, all of whom are easier to work with when the person keeping the community presentable communicates well and pitches in without being asked.

  • Reliable and punctual , consistent attendance is foundational to this role
  • Comfortable with physically demanding, outdoor work in all weather
  • Self-directed enough to manage daily tasks without close supervision
  • Willing to take on varied work including light maintenance support
  • Open to learning and growing toward a maintenance technician role over time

The pay starts at $19/hour with quarterly bonuses, and there's a stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing (your recruiter can walk through the specifics). Benefits include rent discount, health, dental and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, and birthday time off.

One thing worth noting for anyone thinking longer term: Groundskeeper roles at companies that promote from within, as Weinstein explicitly does, are a real entry point into maintenance tech work. You're building familiarity with the physical plant of a property, earning trust with a team, and developing habits that translate directly into a more technical role. It's not a guaranteed path, but it's a genuine one.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Every morning at Bexley at Anderson Mill, the property's first impression gets set before most residents leave for work. As a Groundskeeper, that first impression is yours to own. You'll walk the community daily, picking up trash and pet waste, clearing debris, and keeping the common areas looking sharp. Blowing off walkways, pressure washing surfaces, pulling weeds, touching up landscaping, helping trash out a vacant unit before a make-ready gets started. These are the rhythms of the role, and they repeat. That's not a warning so much as a reality check: if you take genuine satisfaction in maintaining a standard rather than just completing a checklist, this kind of work is actually fulfilling.

You'll also support the maintenance team when needed, whether that means light painting, housekeeping tasks in common areas, or pitching in on jobs that don't fit neatly into one category. The leasing team notices when the property looks good. Residents notice. Prospective renters notice. Your work shows up in occupancy and in how people feel about where they live.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with no on-call rotation. The starting pay is $19 per hour, and there's a quarterly bonus structure plus a stay-on bonus after 90 days for employees in good standing.

What You Bring

  • Reliability, plain and simple. You show up on time, consistently.
  • A self-starter approach. You don't need someone to find you the next task.
  • Physical readiness for an outdoor, active role year-round in Central Texas heat, cold, and everything in between, including lifting up to 50 pounds regularly.
  • Comfort operating equipment like backpack blowers, power washers, and golf carts.
  • A thick skin for the less glamorous parts: pet waste stations, unit cleanouts, repetitive daily rounds.
  • A good attitude toward the maintenance and leasing teams you'll work alongside.

The Bigger Picture

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company that's been operating apartment communities for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 properties across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. They're not a REIT or a private equity shop trying to squeeze margin. That hands-on ownership culture tends to mean more direct feedback, more visibility, and honestly, more accountability too. It's a workplace where people know your name.

One thing worth knowing: Weinstein explicitly promotes from within, and Groundskeeper roles here have historically been a starting point for people who want to grow into maintenance technician positions. If you've ever been curious about HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work but don't have formal experience yet, this is a realistic path into that world. Not guaranteed, but genuinely available to people who show up and learn. That's a real differentiator compared to companies that post groundskeeper roles with no upward visibility attached.

job.title: General Manager - Gresham, OR
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-scope General Manager role at a residential apartment community in Gresham, OR. You're not inheriting a finished product and coasting. You're building and leading the on-site team, owning the budget top to bottom, and driving the operational metrics that keep NOI healthy. That means you're accountable for occupancy, delinquency, renewals, and every line item between gross potential rent and net income. Marketing the property, managing turns, approving make-ready costs, and keeping traffic converting to signed leases all fall on your desk.

Day to day, you're splitting time between people management and operational oversight. In the morning that might mean reviewing a delinquency report and coordinating with your team on notices. By afternoon you're approving a vendor invoice, reviewing a lease application, or working through a budget variance with your regional. The role demands someone who can read a T-12, spot where the property is bleeding, and actually fix it.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. This isn't a startup operation. There's infrastructure behind you, including company profit sharing that connects your site's performance directly to your compensation.

What You Bring

  • Recent hands-on experience managing a multifamily apartment community (not just assistant-level exposure)
  • Supervisory experience: you've hired, trained, and managed on-site staff
  • Demonstrated budget management skills: you can build, read, and defend a property budget
  • Sales and marketing fluency: traffic generation, closing ratios, concession strategy
  • Yardi experience is preferred, not optional in spirit
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance

The Operational Reality

General Managers at this level typically sit at the intersection of people leadership and financial accountability in a way that Assistant Managers and Leasing Consultants simply don't. If you perform here, the career path typically opens toward Regional Manager or Director of Operations roles, especially within a company that promotes from within and has a growing Western U.S. portfolio.

The Gresham submarket sits east of Portland, a Class B and C heavy corridor where operational discipline matters more than luxury amenity packages. Residents are price-sensitive. Delinquency management, retention strategy, and controlled turn costs tend to separate the strong GMs from the average ones here more than flashy marketing ever will. If you've kept occupancy above 95% and held delinquency under 2% at a comparable community, that track record will carry serious weight in this search.

Compensation ranges from $85,000 to $95,000 annually depending on experience, with monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses layered on top. The full benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, profit sharing, and rental discounts.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Gresham, OR
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three prospects are lined up to tour a two-bedroom. You've already qualified two of them by phone, pulled their files, and coordinated with maintenance to make sure the unit is show-ready. That's the rhythm of leasing.

The Role

MG Properties is hiring a Leasing Consultant for an apartment community in Gresham, OR. With more than 30 years operating across the Western U.S., MG Properties manages a portfolio built on acquisition, development, and rehabilitation. This isn't a passive administrative role. You're the front line of occupancy, and the metrics reflect it directly.

Day to day, you're converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting and qualifying applicants, preparing lease documents, and walking new residents through a smooth move-in by staying in close contact with the maintenance team. When a unit turns, you're part of the chain that gets it leased back up quickly. You'll also keep rental files current and accurate, enter data into property management software, and help close out monthly administrative tasks so the property's paperwork stays clean.

Resident relations are part of the job too. When a resident has a maintenance concern or a billing question, you handle it professionally and follow through. Delinquency doesn't fix itself, and neither does a frustrated resident who never heard back. Consistent communication keeps renewals strong and occupancy stable.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Genuine sales ability, not just friendliness. You close.
  • Comfort with leasing software and accurate data entry habits
  • Professional communication with both prospects and current residents
  • A team-oriented mindset. Leasing doesn't happen in a silo.

The candidates who stand out in leasing roles aren't just personable. They track their own numbers. They know their closing ratio, they notice when traffic is up but applications are lagging, and they adjust their pitch accordingly. If you've ever looked at a T-3 occupancy trend and thought about what it means for your month, you're already thinking like the right person for this role.

Compensation runs $20 to $22 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and a rental discount program.

This role is a real launching pad within MG Properties. The company promotes from within, and leasing is where most property management careers begin. Strong performers here typically move into assistant manager roles, where NOI accountability and full-site operations come into focus.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing leasing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The academic calendar drives everything: fall turn periods compress a staggering volume of move-ins into a matter of days, summer is peak leasing season rather than a slow stretch, and your residents are 18 to 22 years old with parents often involved in the decision. If you've worked conventional residential leasing and want to try student housing, that context matters before you apply.

What the Role Actually Covers

The Scion Group calls this position an Experience Team Member, and the title reflects the scope honestly. You're not just pulling traffic and closing leases. The role blends leasing, light marketing, customer service, and property administration into one position. On a given day you might be running a community tour for a prospective resident and their parents in the morning, logging and distributing packages in the afternoon, following up on open maintenance requests before close, and jumping on an after-hours lockout call that evening. The on-call rotation is real. It's listed in the requirements, not buried in fine print.

On the sales side, you'll give tours of the community and amenities, work through objections with prospects, and contribute ideas on local marketing and outreach. Scion operates in collegiate markets, so building relationships with campus organizations, local businesses, and student groups is part of the outreach picture. You'll also help manage the community's social media presence and assist in planning resident engagement events.

Property administration is a consistent part of the workload too: keeping the office and common areas clean and organized, scheduling maintenance follow-ups, and handling general operational tasks that keep the property running smoothly day to day.

What the Job Requires

  • Genuine comfort working with a diverse, mostly college-age population and their families
  • Strong verbal communication and the ability to read a room during a tour or a tense conversation
  • Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and during turn periods when the schedule gets demanding
  • Reliability and self-direction. Managers can't babysit a leasing floor
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (Scion does not sponsor visas)

Where This Role Can Take You

For someone early in a property management career, a student housing leasing role builds a specific and transferable skill set. Turn coordination alone teaches you more about logistics and resident communication than months of conventional leasing. The sales, marketing, and administrative blend here also maps well onto an Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager path, either within student housing or at a conventional Class A or B property. Scion operates communities across multiple university markets, so internal movement is a realistic option for strong performers. The work isn't always easy, but the foundation it builds is solid.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Running a multifamily community at the manager level means wearing several hats at once: financial steward, team coach, leasing driver, and resident advocate. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the top 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country and a company with deep Southeast roots, the Community Manager role at Landmark Apartments in Murfreesboro, TN carries all of that weight and then some.

What This Role Actually Demands

The financial side of this position is real and consequential. You'll own the community's budget, monitor delinquency, oversee deposit accounting, and produce reporting through Yardi. That means reading a T-12 with fluency, not just skimming it. You'll set and adjust pricing strategy to protect occupancy, manage concessions carefully, and partner with ownership on performance expectations. Compliance with fair housing standards and company policy runs underneath all of it.

On the operational side, you'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders and preventative care, manage vendor relationships, and conduct regular property inspections to keep curb appeal and common areas sharp. The leasing function doesn't disappear at this level either. You'll guide your team through traffic, renewals, and lead response, and you'll step in on tours yourself when the situation calls for it.

Team leadership here is hands-on. You'll hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff, run weekly alignment meetings, and handle the harder conversations that come with accountability. Escalated resident concerns land on your desk, and how you resolve them shapes the community's reputation, including what shows up in online reviews.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • At least two years of property management experience, ideally progressing through Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager roles
  • Six months of direct community manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and Knock, preferred
  • A valid driver's license; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent required

What This Role Builds

Strong candidates for this position already understand delinquency tracking and can read a financial report without hand-holding. What the role builds is something harder to teach: the ability to hold a team accountable while keeping morale intact, to make pricing calls under pressure, and to translate ownership expectations into day-to-day operational decisions. Managers who develop those instincts here tend to move into regional oversight, and Hawthorne's internal career path program is structured to support exactly that progression.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off each week keeps the schedule at 40 hours, though resident events and community needs will occasionally require flexibility beyond those hours. Compensation includes a base salary along with monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners runs one of the more intentional cultures in Southeast multifamily, and the Leasing Consultant role at their 1287 Shoals community in Athens reflects that. This isn't a post-and-pray leasing job where you sit behind a desk waiting for walk-ins. The expectation is that you're the first and most lasting impression a prospect has of the property, and you carry that responsibility through every tour, every follow-up call, and every renewal conversation.

Athens is a college town with a rental market that moves in cycles tied closely to the academic calendar. That means traffic can spike hard at certain points in the year, and the ability to work a lead list with genuine follow-through, not just reactive inbox management, separates consultants who hit their occupancy targets from those who don't. Strong leasing consultants here understand that a prospect who toured on a Saturday and went quiet isn't a dead lead. They know how to re-engage without being pushy.

Day to day, you'll handle inbound inquiries across phone, email, and web, conduct personalized tours, process applications and move-in paperwork, and contribute to resident events and community programming. You'll also spend time on market surveys and social media outreach to keep the property visible and competitive. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the hours at 40. Some evening availability may come up for resident events.

What Hawthorne Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP certification is a plus
  • Genuine comfort communicating in person, by phone, and in writing
  • Ability to handle objections and guide prospects toward a decision without pressure tactics

On the compensation side, the hourly rate is supplemented by monthly leasing and renewal commissions, which means your effort has a direct line to your paycheck. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental and adoption leave options.

Hawthorne also runs a formal career path program, and this role has a clear next step: Assistant Community Manager. If you want to move toward property operations and eventually run a community, this is a reasonable place to start building that foundation. The leasing role gives you early exposure to occupancy metrics, resident retention, and the administrative side of property management, all of which matter when you step into a management track.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultant roles at established New England operators tend to be high-touch, relationship-driven positions. At Babcock Towers, a John M. Corcoran property in Boston, that holds true. JMC has been in the business since 1951, and the company still runs with the kind of hands-on culture where a leasing consultant's work is visible and valued.

What the Job Looks Like

Most of your week centers on converting traffic into signed leases. You'll show apartments, walk prospective residents through pricing and lease terms, and process applications. When someone decides to move in, you build the lease package and manage the move-in process so it goes smoothly from start to finish.

You're also responsible for keeping the property's occupancy pipeline active. That means setting your own sales goals and working toward them through online advertising, social media, and local networking. This isn't a role where marketing gets handed off to someone else. You own it at the property level.

Beyond leasing, you'll stay in contact with current residents throughout their tenancy and conduct property inspections to keep curb appeal sharp. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 9 AM to 5 PM.

What JMC Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with computers and standard leasing software
  • Organized, with solid time management habits
  • A genuine, positive presence with prospective and current residents

No prior leasing experience is required. JMC states openly that they want someone eager to learn the business, which means this role is a real entry point, not just a title for someone who already has three years of experience.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range runs from $24 to $27.50 per hour, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match.

One thing worth noting for candidates new to leasing: this role builds a skill set that transfers directly into assistant manager and property manager positions. The combination of sales, lease administration, resident relations, and basic marketing exposure is exactly what operators look for when promoting from within. JMC has a track record of long-tenured employees, which suggests those paths are real here, not just recruiting language.

job.title: Market Maintenance Manager II
job.description:
Maintenance Manager roles at residential communities tend to attract two kinds of candidates: those who want to stay hands-on forever, and those who see the position as a platform. At John M. Corcoran & Company, the structure genuinely supports the second group. JMC has been operating in New England since 1951, and the kind of institutional knowledge that accumulates over that span shapes how their maintenance teams are built and how they're led.

This opening is for a Market Maintenance Manager II based at Union 346 I & II in Somerville, a market where multifamily demand runs high and residents expect responsive, professional service. You'd be responsible for the full physical operation of the community: daily work orders, unit turns and make-readies, preventive maintenance scheduling, inspections, vendor coordination, and budget adherence on supplies and equipment. You'd also supervise maintenance, janitorial, and grounds staff, which means your day includes as much people management as it does building systems.

The on-call rotation is real, and worth naming plainly. After-hours emergencies are part of the job, and candidates who thrive here tend to be the ones who've already made peace with that reality. The upside is that participating in an on-call structure at a company like JMC builds the kind of operational judgment that's hard to learn any other way. When you're the person who responds, troubleshoots, and resolves, you develop a systems fluency that translates directly to Regional Facilities Director and Director of Maintenance roles down the line.

What separates strong candidates here

Technical range matters, but it's not the whole picture. JMC is looking for someone who can keep accurate records, track purchase orders, and communicate clearly with the management team so that unit availability is never a mystery. In a community where occupancy and turn timelines affect NOI, a Maintenance Manager who treats documentation as a core function, not an afterthought, is genuinely more valuable than one who's simply a skilled tradesperson. If you've ever had a leasing team thank you for a punch list that was actually complete, you already understand the dynamic.

  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience considered
  • At least 3 years in trade or general building maintenance
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and building systems
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise a team and manage vendor relationships
  • Comfort with safety procedures, compliance expectations, and budget guidelines

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with on-call rotation included. Compensation is competitive and includes a $2,500 sign-on bonus, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with company match.

For someone who wants to grow in property maintenance leadership, a company with JMC's tenure and portfolio depth in New England is a credible next step. The skills you build managing a community of this profile compound quickly, especially when you're working inside an organization that has promoted from within for decades.

job.title: Senior Property Manager
job.description:
Managing two properties simultaneously in the same submarket is a specific kind of challenge. You're not just running operations at one address. You're splitting attention between two communities, two teams, and two sets of resident expectations, while keeping both assets performing. That's the scope Cottonwood Residential is hiring for in Millcreek, where their Cottonwood Highland and Richmond Apartments need a Senior Property Manager who can hold both communities to a high standard without letting either one drift.

What This Role Requires

Cottonwood wants at least three years of property management experience in the seat, not adjacent to it. You'll need a genuine command of leasing and sales fundamentals, because occupancy doesn't maintain itself, and a Senior PM at a company this size is expected to coach the leasing team, not just monitor their numbers. Fair Housing fluency is expected. Experience with Entrata is a plus, and candidates coming from a REIT background will find the financial reporting expectations familiar. NALP credential holders are preferred, though not required.

The day-to-day scope covers full property operations: budget development, cost control, revenue programs, vendor relationships, maintenance coordination, and team leadership. You're the person who builds the annual operating budget and defends it, who spots a delinquency trend before it compounds, and who keeps the office and maintenance sides of the operation working as one unit rather than two separate departments that occasionally talk.

What This Role Builds

Running a two-property portfolio under one manager sharpens a specific skill set that single-site roles don't. You'll develop stronger prioritization instincts, because not every punch list item or leasing problem can get your attention at the same moment. You'll also build comfort with comparative analysis: how does occupancy at one community track against the other, where are concessions being used and why, and what's driving traffic differences between two properties that share a zip code. These are the analytical habits that translate directly into regional or multi-site director roles.

Cottonwood's early adoption of Self-Guided Tours is worth noting here. It means their leasing model leans on technology and resident-facing systems more than many conventional operators. A strong candidate in this role won't just tolerate that model. They'll find ways to improve it at the property level, whether that's tightening the follow-up process after a self-guided visit or identifying friction points in the prospect experience that the technology alone can't solve.

Who Fits This Role

  • Three or more years managing a property or portfolio, with real budget accountability
  • Demonstrated leasing and sales ability, with experience coaching a team
  • REIT or institutional management background preferred
  • Entrata experience helpful but not required
  • NALP credential preferred
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing law

Cottonwood offers a quarterly bonus structure alongside base pay, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within the first 30 days, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays. For a Senior PM ready to operate with real ownership over two communities, this is a well-supported role with a company that has shown a willingness to do things differently.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians are the operational backbone of any apartment community. When a resident can't get hot water at 7 a.m. or a unit needs to turn fast between leases, this is the role that either holds the property together or lets it slip. Waypoint Management Services is adding a Maintenance Technician to their team in Gainesville, FL, at what the posting describes as a high-end luxury community.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope maintenance role, not a single-trade position. Day to day, you'll work through service requests, handle make-readies, complete punch lists before move-ins, and run preventive maintenance on HVAC systems and other community equipment. You'll also manage pool chemistry, keep the trash compactor operating, and make sure gated access and security equipment stay functional. When something breaks on a plumbing line or a structural component needs attention, that's yours too.

The on-call rotation is real. Priority work orders carry a 24-hour resolution expectation, and some of those will come outside business hours. That's the honest part of this job that doesn't always make it into postings. If you're someone who resents the phone ringing on a weekend, this role will wear on you. If you take satisfaction in solving problems fast and keeping residents from sitting in a bad situation, it's actually one of the more rewarding parts of the work.

OSHA compliance isn't optional here. Waypoint expects you to stay current on safety standards and operate within those guidelines consistently.

What You'll Need

  • EPA Section 608 certification (Types I and II), required before starting
  • Hands-on experience repairing building systems and equipment across multiple trade areas
  • Comfort working on HVAC, plumbing, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Familiarity with service supplies, materials, and equipment selection
  • Availability for on-call rotation
  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant trade experience counts
  • CPO certification is a plus, especially given the pool service responsibilities

Customer interaction is part of this job at a luxury community. Residents expect a higher standard of communication and follow-through than you'd find at a Class C property. That means showing up on time, explaining what you did, and leaving the unit cleaner than you found it. Technical skill gets you in the door; how you handle residents determines whether you stay and grow.

Compensation and Benefits

Pay runs between $23 and $25 per hour. Benefits start on day one and include medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with a 401k with matching. There's an onsite housing discount available, plus bonus and incentive opportunities, an employee referral program, and an employee recognition program.

For technicians looking ahead, this type of full-scope role at a luxury property builds the kind of track record that leads to Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor positions. Managing make-ready schedules, coordinating with contractors, and keeping a high-end asset running well are exactly the skills that property management companies look for when they're filling those next-level seats.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Summer Intern)
job.description:
Leasing internships in property management can feel like busywork at some companies. At Berkshire Residential Investments, this summer role at Ellington Metro West is structured around real leasing activity: showing units, closing prospects, and learning what actually moves occupancy. If you want to spend a summer doing something that translates directly to a career in multifamily, this is a better starting point than most.

What You'll Actually Do

Your days will center on leasing traffic. You'll take prospects through tour routes and model units, which means keeping those spaces in show-ready condition before every appointment. That's not a small thing. A scuffed baseboard or a light bulb out during a tour costs a lease. You'll handle follow-up communications, work toward a closing ratio of at least 20%, and help maintain the kind of leasing office atmosphere that makes people feel comfortable enough to sign. You'll also track local market conditions and bring ideas to the property manager on marketing and resident satisfaction. This isn't a shadow-and-observe internship.

On the administrative side, expect detail work: accurate records, professional written communications to current and prospective residents, and attention to the small things that add up to a well-run office. Multifamily leasing involves more paperwork than most people expect coming in.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience in any field where closing or persuading mattered
  • Comfort adapting to new software and technology platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • The kind of energy that makes a leasing office feel alive without being exhausting to work around

Why This Internship Is Worth Considering

Leasing consultant experience is the most direct path into multifamily property management. Consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, understand what objections kill deals, and build relationships with residents often move into assistant manager roles within a year or two of full-time work. The skills here, closing, market awareness, administrative discipline, transfer cleanly to any Class A, B, or C community. Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party management firm, which means the culture and standards tend to be more consistent across sites. That's a better training environment for someone just starting out.

If you're considering a career in real estate, investment, or property operations, a summer spent actually leasing apartments gives you something concrete to point to. That matters more than most internships do.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager - $2,500 Sign- On Bonus
job.description:
Maintenance work at the assistant manager level is where technical fluency meets supervisory credibility. You can't lead a team through a demanding turn season or a complex boiler issue unless you've earned the trust that comes from actually knowing the trades. This role at Bozzuto's Cambridge property draws on both sides of that equation every day.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work

Five or more years in the trades gives you a foundation, but this position asks you to apply that knowledge across a wider surface area than most field technician roles. HVAC diagnosis, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair are the core technical competencies you'll use regularly. Beyond that, exposure to complex mechanical systems like central plant, chillers, and boilers is genuinely valued here. Cambridge's older and mid-rise residential stock tends to run more mechanically complex than garden-style product, so that systems knowledge compounds quickly in this market.

On the supervisory side, the skills that matter most are consistency and follow-through. Residents notice when service requests close on time and when they don't. You'll be the person who sets the standard for how tickets get completed, how punch lists get closed after a turn, and how the team approaches preventative maintenance as a discipline rather than an afterthought. Leadership aptitude and some prior supervisory experience are preferred, and for good reason: the jump from skilled technician to someone who can also motivate a crew is where a lot of candidates stall.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A significant portion of your week will involve the make-ready process. Coordinating apartment turns so units are rent-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy and the ability to convert leasing traffic into signed leases. That connection between maintenance execution and leasing performance is something strong candidates understand intuitively. You'll also run a preventative maintenance program, manage grounds and common area upkeep, and participate in the emergency on-call rotation. Weekend availability is part of the role.

Safety compliance is woven into all of it. OSHA standards, MSDS knowledge, and adherence to applicable building codes aren't box-checking exercises here. They're the foundation of running an accident-free operation, which is both a liability matter and a point of professional pride.

Where This Role Leads

Assistant Maintenance Manager is a natural stepping stone toward a Building Maintenance Manager or Regional Maintenance Director role, particularly within a company like Bozzuto that manages a substantial portfolio across multiple markets. The skills you build here, specifically the ability to balance hands-on technical work with team leadership and asset preservation thinking, transfer directly to those higher-level roles. Certifications like EPA 608 and HVAC credentials carry weight at every level of that progression.

  • 5+ years in trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA and MSDS standards
  • Supervisory experience preferred
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems (boilers, chillers, central plant)
  • Availability for on-call rotation and weekend work
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently and work in varying weather

The base salary for this position is $70,000, with additional bonus opportunities and a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Most Assistant Property Manager roles sit at the intersection of leasing and operations, and that's exactly where this one lives. At a Bozzuto community in San Francisco, you're not shadowing the Property Manager. You're carrying real responsibility across rent collection, delinquency management, tours, team coaching, and brand presentation. When the PM steps out, you step up.

What This Role Actually Requires

The financial side of this job is concrete. You'll manage delinquency, track rent collection, and develop familiarity with P&L and budget reporting. Yardi proficiency is preferred, and if you've worked in it before, you'll move faster. The leasing side is equally active. You'll conduct personalized community tours, handle objections, and close new leases while building the kind of resident loyalty that reduces turnover and holds occupancy. Weekend availability is part of the job structure: one to two weekends per month, with compensating weekdays off.

Beyond the numbers and the leasing desk, you're also a visible leader on site. That means coaching and mentoring team members, holding the community's interior and exterior to a high standard, and maintaining the professional presence that a Bozzuto property carries in the market. Social media content creation is part of the mix too. Platforms like Instagram and Facebook are active tools for community marketing, not afterthoughts.

  • At least two years of experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • A four-year degree or equivalent hands-on experience
  • Demonstrated comfort with revenue, P&L, and budget exposure
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Sales instincts and the ability to convert traffic into signed leases
  • Competency with industry software, with Yardi as the preferred platform

What This Role Builds

The APM seat is where Property Managers are made. You'll develop the financial fluency to read a T-12, understand NOI drivers, and explain delinquency trends to ownership. You'll practice the leadership habits that translate directly into running your own property. The coaching and mentoring responsibilities here aren't ceremonial. They're real reps at developing people, which is one of the hardest skills to build in this industry and one of the most valuable once you have it.

San Francisco adds its own layer of complexity. The market demands strong leasing skills because concessions and competition are real factors, and residents in this market tend to be discerning. The ability to create a genuinely memorable tour experience and follow through on every resident interaction carries more weight here than it might in a softer market. Candidates who come in with both hospitality instincts and financial literacy tend to separate themselves quickly in this environment.

The salary range for this position is $64,500 to $75,000, with additional bonus opportunities available. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Centralized Painter - Atlanta, GA
job.description:
Cortland runs a large multifamily portfolio across Atlanta, and keeping units turning quickly is central to how they operate. This painter role sits inside their Integrated Facilities Management team, which means you're not attached to a single property. You move across the portfolio, hitting wherever the turn volume demands it.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical day starts with knowing whether you're doing a full repaint or working through a couple of touch-up units. One full repaint or two touch-ups is the baseline daily expectation, so you need to be efficient without cutting corners on finish quality. That means strong spray skills, clean prep work, and the ability to match textures on drywall patches so the finished product doesn't look like a patchwork of repairs. You'll handle surface prep, priming, and finish coats for interiors, with some exterior work as needed.

Because you're centralized, you'll drive between properties regularly. You need a valid license, appropriate insurance, and the kind of self-direction that lets you show up somewhere, assess what's needed, do the work well, and move on. You'll log your work, materials used, and any follow-up items in a CMMS platform, and communicate clearly with service managers and occasionally residents when your work overlaps with occupied spaces.

The paint shop itself is your responsibility to maintain. Tools clean, spray equipment serviced, materials stocked, space organized. That discipline matters more in a centralized role because you're the consistent presence across multiple sites.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of interior residential painting experience; custom home background is a bonus
  • Proficiency with brush, roller, and spray application, including spray prep and equipment maintenance
  • Ability to do small drywall repairs and texture matching (larger repairs a plus)
  • Working knowledge of OSHA requirements, MSDS handling, and elevated-work safety procedures
  • Comfort working at heights using ladders, lifts, or scaffolding
  • Valid driver's license and required vehicle insurance for travel between properties
  • Familiarity with CMMS software, or genuine willingness to learn it
  • Availability for all shifts including weekends during peak turn periods

How This Role Works in Practice

What separates a strong candidate here from someone who just meets the qualifications on paper is production discipline. Cortland tracks turn timelines carefully, and a centralized painter who consistently delivers clean, durable finishes on schedule makes a real difference to occupancy outcomes across the portfolio. If you've worked in environments where quality and speed had to coexist, and where you were accountable for your own output without a supervisor watching every step, that experience translates directly here.

The centralized model also means you're less isolated than a single-property maintenance painter. You'll interact with multiple service teams, which can be genuinely energizing if you like variety. It also means you need to be adaptable, because priorities shift based on where turn volume spikes. Cortland is a vertically integrated operation with in-house construction and design, so there's real infrastructure behind this role, from material sourcing to process standards.

job.title: Community Manager-Cortland Manassas
job.description:
Community Manager roles at large, vertically integrated operators like Cortland carry more weight than the title suggests. You're not just keeping the lights on. You're running a multimillion-dollar asset, managing a team, hitting NOI targets, and fielding escalated resident concerns all in the same week. That's the job, and Cortland's Manassas community needs someone who can handle all of it without needing hand-holding.

What This Role Actually Involves

Day-to-day, you're the person everyone looks to. Your leasing team needs coaching on conversion rates and follow-up discipline. Your service team needs a manager who stays on top of inspections and vendor accountability. Corporate partners need someone who can speak to the T-12, explain delinquency trends, and defend budget decisions with actual data. None of that is glamorous. It's just the work.

On the financial side, you own the NOI. That means managing expenses without letting the asset slip, reviewing community metrics regularly, and knowing when to push concessions and when to hold the line on pricing. You'll work alongside Cortland's centralized support teams, which gives you more resources than a typical fee management setup, but you still need to drive results on your end.

Resident experience at a Cortland property runs at a premium standard. That means handling escalated concerns professionally and quickly, not passing them off. It also means your team's day-to-day interactions set the tone for retention. High turnover in residents almost always traces back to how they were treated during a problem, not whether the problem happened at all.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years of sales leadership in a high-volume, short-cycle environment. Multifamily is the obvious fit, but hospitality, luxury retail, or premium automotive backgrounds have translated well into this type of role.
  • A track record of hitting occupancy and revenue targets, not just participating in the process.
  • Experience coaching a team, not just managing one. There's a difference, and Cortland pays attention to it.
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM tools, and data analysis. You don't need to be a spreadsheet expert, but you do need to make decisions from numbers, not instinct alone.
  • High school diploma required. A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience is preferred.
  • Fair Housing knowledge and general compliance awareness. This is non-negotiable at any well-run community.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The managers who do well in roles like this aren't the ones who are great at one thing. They're the ones who can shift from reviewing budget variance in the morning to handling a difficult lease renewal conversation in the afternoon, then closing out the day coaching a leasing consultant on their follow-up process. The range is real, and it's constant.

Cortland's vertical integration, meaning in-house design, construction, and operations, gives their community managers more internal support than you'd find at many third-party management firms. That's worth something. But it also means you're held to a higher standard of execution, because the resources are there. Candidates who thrive here tend to welcome accountability rather than avoid it, and they see the support structure as an advantage rather than oversight.

If you've been running a Class A or Class B community and you're ready for a role with more visibility, more ownership, and a clear path toward senior operations or regional leadership, this is the kind of position that builds that resume.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Lincoln Property Company runs one of the larger third-party commercial management platforms in the country, and a role like this one sits at the center of how that platform actually performs. You're the operator of record: the person whose name is on the monthly reports, whose calls the tenants return, and whose read on the asset shapes what ownership decides next.

What This Role Actually Manages

This position carries full operational and financial accountability for a commercial portfolio that may include office, industrial, and retail properties in the Riverdale, MD area. Day-to-day, that means owning the P&L narrative. You're preparing monthly variance reports and annual operating budgets, tracking CAM and OpX recovery charges, and reporting AR status to clients with concrete recommendations rather than just numbers on a page. Lease administration runs through you: setups, changes, expirations, covenant tracking. If a lease clause affects NOI three years from now, you're the one flagging it today.

On the operations side, you're directing a team rather than doing everything yourself. That includes setting work schedules, cross-training staff, running performance reviews, and hiring when the team needs depth. Vendor procurement is a real part of this job: detailed bid analysis, contract compliance, and quality control on service delivery. Property inspections happen at least monthly, vacant spaces stay tour-ready, and emergency response plans stay current and tested.

Tenant relationship management is where retention either holds or slips. You'll coordinate move-ins and move-outs, resolve building issues before they become complaints, and run a tenant care program designed to keep renewals on the table. In commercial management, losing a tenant to a competitor because of deferred maintenance or slow communication is a direct hit to NOI that's hard to recover from mid-lease cycle.

What the Role Requires

  • 3 to 5 years of commercial property management experience, with office, retail, or industrial exposure strongly preferred
  • Bachelor's degree preferred; equivalent experience considered
  • Real estate license where required by Maryland regulation
  • CPM or RPA designation (or active candidacy) preferred
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills; Yardi, MRI, or Kardin experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate financial complexity for ownership audiences
  • Availability for after-hours response and emergency situations as client needs require

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The operators who do well in third-party commercial management can hold two things at once: the granular detail of a lease abstract and the big-picture view of what that lease means for asset value and client objectives. If you can walk a space, write a punch list, and then sit down and explain a budget variance to an owner in the same afternoon without losing a beat on either, that's the profile Lincoln is looking for. The entrepreneurial mindset the posting mentions isn't filler. Fee management environments reward people who treat the asset like it's their own capital at risk, because the client relationship depends on exactly that.

Career path from here typically runs toward portfolio director, regional manager, or asset management roles depending on whether your strengths pull more toward operations depth or client relationship development. Both tracks are viable from a seat like this one.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
Regional Manager roles at third-party management firms operate differently than in-house positions. You're accountable to ownership groups who expect accurate reporting and strong NOI, while simultaneously managing on-site teams who need coaching, direction, and someone to escalate to. At Asset Living, one of the larger third-party operators in the country with a portfolio that spans multifamily, affordable housing, student housing, and build-to-rent, that dual accountability is the job.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This role covers the full operational picture across a portfolio of communities in the Indianapolis market. On the financial side, you're developing annual budgets, monitoring income and expense variances each month, and pushing toward the highest achievable NOI through a mix of cost discipline and leasing strategy. You'll review capex proposals, track large vendor contracts, and make sure ownership reports go out accurately and on time. That last part matters more than it sounds. Ownership reports that are late or wrong erode trust fast in fee management relationships.

Personnel management takes up a real portion of your week. You'll screen and hire community managers, coach underperformers, document issues properly, and coordinate with HR when terminations are necessary. You'll approve timesheets, process salary increase requests, and keep your teams aligned with company policy. The expectation is consistency. Inconsistent handling of performance issues creates legal exposure and team dysfunction, and this role carries responsibility for avoiding both.

On the leasing side, you're developing annual marketing plans, reviewing traffic and occupancy trends, identifying where rent growth is possible and where concessions may be necessary, and making sure on-site staff are converting leads effectively. You'll also handle resident relations escalations and help build retention programs that reduce turnover costs.

Maintenance oversight is part of the role too. Regular property inspections, monitoring make-ready timelines, reviewing service request completion rates, and managing vendor relationships all fall under your scope. When a property emergency happens after hours, you're part of the response chain.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

The candidates who stand out in regional roles at third-party firms are the ones who can read a T-12 and identify where a property is bleeding margin, then walk the property the same afternoon and spot deferred maintenance or a leasing team that's lost its energy. That combination of financial fluency and operational groundedness is harder to find than either skill alone.

  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of multifamily communities as a regional or area manager
  • Comfort with budget development, variance reporting, and NOI analysis
  • Experience hiring, coaching, and when needed, terminating on-site staff
  • Familiarity with fair housing regulations and risk management practices
  • Strong written communication skills for ownership reporting and internal documentation
  • Ability to manage vendor contracts and oversee capital improvement projects

The Honest Part

Third-party management means your portfolio can include properties at different stages, different ownership expectations, and different physical conditions. Some sites will be well-capitalized and well-staffed. Others will be understaffed, underfunded, or in the middle of a difficult lease-up. You'll need to triage your time and energy across all of them. If you're someone who needs uniform conditions to perform well, this structure will be frustrating. If you're someone who adapts quickly and finds the variation interesting, it tends to be genuinely engaging work. Asset Living's scale, with NMHC top 50 recognition and AMO accreditation through IREM, means there are resources and systems behind you, but the regional manager role still requires someone who can operate with real independence.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Olympus Falcon Landing
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set, not just a personality type. The best consultants know how to read a prospect's hesitation, adjust their pitch mid-tour, and close without being pushy. They also know how to pivot from a lease signing to a maintenance call to a renewal conversation inside the same hour. If that kind of range sounds normal to you, this role at Olympus Falcon Landing in Katy, TX is worth a close look.

What This Role Actually Requires

The leasing consultant is the first real impression a prospect gets of the property, and the ongoing face residents see when something's wrong. That dual function demands more than a friendly attitude. You'll need genuine product knowledge: floor plan differences, unit locations, amenity details, pricing variations. Prospects ask detailed questions, and vague answers cost leases.

On the sales side, you'll work traffic from multiple channels, including locator referrals and walk-ins, and you'll be expected to hit monthly leasing goals. Commission and renewal bonuses are part of the compensation structure here, which means your income has real upside tied directly to your close rate. Base pay starts in the $18.50 to $19.25 per hour range, and the bonus structure adds meaningful earning potential on top of that.

Administratively, the job carries a full paperwork load: lease preparation, database entry, move-in coordination. None of that is glamorous, but it's where errors create real problems for residents and the team. Accuracy matters as much as salesmanship.

The Schedule Is Worth Understanding Before You Apply

This is a full-time, seven-day-operation role. Weekday hours run 9 AM to 6 PM, and both Saturday and Sunday are required. Monthly after-hours commitments exist for resident events, with dates and frequency that shift. If your availability doesn't accommodate weekends consistently, this role isn't the right fit. That's not a knock on the job. It's just the reality of leasing in residential multifamily.

Olympus lists bilingual ability as preferred, which reflects the Katy market. The Houston metro's west suburbs have a substantial Spanish-speaking population, and a bilingual consultant can connect with a wider prospect pool and handle resident concerns more effectively. It's a practical advantage, not a checkbox.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart Here

At least one year of apartment leasing experience is required. Beyond that baseline, the consultants who tend to thrive in roles like this are the ones who treat renewals as seriously as new leases. Occupancy is easier to maintain than to recover, and a consultant who builds genuine relationships with current residents directly supports renewal rates. That's a skill that compounds over time and one that property management companies notice when evaluating candidates for assistant manager tracks.

Olympus Property has been recognized as a top employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025), which reflects something real about how the company manages its teams. Culture claims are easy to make. That kind of repeat recognition from an industry body is harder to manufacture.

  • Minimum 1 year of apartment leasing experience required
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred
  • Full-time availability including weekends
  • Comfort with after-hours resident events on a monthly basis
  • Strong administrative accuracy alongside sales skills

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others.

job.title: Groundskeeper - Summer Temp Full Time
job.description:
Most summer jobs keep you cooped up inside. This one keeps you outside, moving, and part of something you can actually see at the end of each day. Weinstein Properties is hiring a full-time temporary Groundskeeper to cover two Austin-area communities: Bexley 3Five in South Austin and Bexley at Anderson Mill in Cedar Park. The assignment runs now through August, and it pays $19.50 an hour.

That rate is intentionally set $1.50 above the permanent starting wage to offset the lack of benefits. Weinstein also builds in three stay bonuses of $100 each, paid after 30, 60, and 90 days on the job. If you stick it out and perform well, there's a realistic shot at a permanent offer. That's not a throw-in line. Weinstein is a family-owned company that's been running apartment communities for over 70 years and actively promotes from within.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. No rotating weekends, no on-call shifts. For a grounds role, that's a reasonable structure.

Here's the honest version of what the work looks like day to day. You'll walk the property every morning picking up litter and pet waste before residents head out. You'll clean pet stations, handle trash-outs on vacant units, pull weeds, run a backpack blower, operate a power washer, and do whatever the grounds need to stay sharp. Some days you'll support the maintenance team with light painting or housekeeping tasks. It's repetitive in stretches, and in an Austin summer, it's hot. That's the job.

What separates the people who thrive in this role from those who don't is pretty simple: they don't wait to be told what to do next. A groundskeeper who notices a punch list item before the maintenance supervisor does, or who keeps the curb appeal tight without daily reminders, is the kind of person who ends up converting to a permanent spot. The ones who struggle tend to treat the repetitive tasks as beneath them. If you can find the rhythm in recurring work and take pride in a clean property, this fits.

For anyone considering a longer career in property management, grounds work is a legitimate entry point. You'll learn how a well-run community operates from the outside in, pick up basic maintenance skills, and build a track record that opens doors to maintenance tech roles down the line.

What the role requires

  • Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds or more regularly
  • Comfort operating equipment including backpack blowers, power washers, and golf carts
  • Prolonged walking, standing, bending, and stooping throughout the shift
  • Willingness to work outdoors through heat, humidity, and rain
  • Reliability and a self-starting work ethic

Weinstein Properties owns and manages more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Austin market is active, and these communities are maintained to a consistent standard. If you show up and do the work, this summer has a real path beyond August.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - 4400 Syracuse
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance supervision at a mid-size multifamily community runs on diagnostic thinking, trade breadth, and the ability to move between hands-on work and team coordination without losing momentum on either. At 4400 Syracuse Apartments in Denver, MG Properties is looking for a Maintenance Supervisor who can do both. You're not just executing repairs. You're triaging incoming service requests, assessing what your team can handle versus what needs outside coordination, and keeping the physical asset in the kind of condition that supports occupancy and resident retention.

Denver's multifamily market has seen sustained demand across its urban corridors, and properties along the I-25 spine have stayed competitive partly on the strength of their upkeep. A well-run maintenance operation directly supports a community's ability to hold occupancy and minimize costly turns. That connection between maintenance quality and NOI isn't abstract here. It shows up in resident renewals, in punch list efficiency on vacant units, and in how quickly a make-ready moves from notice-to-vacate to rent-ready.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you'll diagnose and perform routine repairs across all trade areas, or delegate them to your team and inspect the completed work. You'll manage the service request pipeline, schedule maintenance personnel in coordination with the property manager, and run regular safety meetings to keep your team sharp and compliant. Preventive maintenance tracking and accurate record-keeping for expenditures are part of the job. So is equipment maintenance oversight.

The qualification floor here reflects the scope: at least two years in a supervisory maintenance role and experience on properties of 150 units or more. Multi-trade competency is required. If you've only worked in one trade, this role will stretch you in ways you may not be ready for.

  • 2+ years of maintenance supervisor experience preferred
  • Experience managing maintenance at a community of 150+ units
  • Demonstrated competency across multiple trade areas
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required
  • Strong customer service orientation and team-first mindset

What MG Properties Offers and What Sets Them Apart

Compensation ranges from $36 to $38.35 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base pay. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, life insurance, FSA and dependent care spending accounts, paid sick time, holidays, personal days, and rental discounts. PTO accrues from day one.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of institutional continuity matters in maintenance leadership. It means you're working within established systems rather than building them from scratch, and that there's genuine organizational depth behind decisions about capital expenditures, vendor relationships, and team development. Strong candidates here tend to be supervisors who take preventive maintenance seriously rather than running purely reactive, and who treat accurate record-keeping as a professional standard rather than an afterthought. This position is anticipated to be filled in June 2026.

job.title: Part Time Resident Services Coordinator - San Diego
job.description:
Multifamily operators have learned that lease renewals and resident satisfaction don't happen by accident. They happen because someone is consistently showing up, communicating clearly, and making residents feel like the property actually cares about them. That's the gap this role fills.

MG Properties, a Western U.S. owner-operator with over three decades of apartment acquisition, development, and management behind them, is hiring a Part Time Resident Services Coordinator at Shift Apartments in San Diego. This isn't a traditional leasing role, though you'll assist with leasing when needed. The core of the job is communication and community: handling resident correspondence around lease questions and service requests, planning and running resident events, producing the monthly newsletter and events calendar, and keeping the overall resident experience feeling intentional rather than reactive.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

On a typical shift, you might start by working through the communication queue, responding to email inquiries, logging service requests, and following up on anything outstanding. From there, you could be finalizing details for an upcoming resident event, coordinating with vendors or staff, and checking that the amenity spaces are operating properly and policies are being followed. There's also a competitive awareness component: you'll stay current on what nearby communities are offering so the team can respond to market shifts. When leasing needs an extra hand, you step in.

It's a role with real variety, which means you need to be genuinely organized. Dropping the ball on event logistics or letting communication pile up affects residents directly, and residents notice.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • Strong written communicators who can shift tone between a friendly event announcement and a policy reminder without sounding robotic
  • People who take initiative on follow-through rather than waiting to be reminded
  • Customer service backgrounds that include handling complaints or escalations calmly
  • Basic computer proficiency and comfort with property management or communication platforms
  • Valid driver's license and flexibility for occasional travel off-site

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this specific role is the ability to build genuine rapport with residents over time. Anyone can answer an email. The people who thrive here are the ones residents actually recognize, trust, and come to with concerns before those concerns become problems. That kind of relationship doesn't come from a script; it comes from consistent, honest communication and follow-through.

This is a part-time position compensated at $23/hour, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing included. MG Properties also offers paid time off accrual and paid sick time for part-time team members, which is worth noting in a market where part-time benefits are often minimal.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A Leasing Role Built Around Relationships, Not Just Renewals

Student housing operates on a rhythm that's unlike any other segment of property management. Leases turn on an academic calendar, traffic spikes around housing fairs and move-in weekends, and your residents are navigating a major life transition while they're also deciding whether to re-sign. The Experience Team Member role at Lark Chapel Hill sits right at the center of that dynamic, and it requires someone who genuinely connects with people, not just someone who can recite floor plan pricing.

Scion has built its brand around the student living experience, and this position reflects that. It's part leasing consultant, part community ambassador, part administrative coordinator. On any given day, you might be giving a tour to a prospective resident and their parents in the morning, helping coordinate a resident engagement event in the afternoon, and fielding a package pickup or lockout call in the evening. The variety is real, and so is the pace.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your core focus is customer interaction: tours, follow-ups, fielding objections, and communicating what makes the community worth choosing. You'll also contribute to local marketing efforts and assist with social media content, which means you need to understand both the sales side and the storytelling side of leasing. Beyond the front-facing work, there's property administration involved: maintaining office organization, logging and retrieving packages, scheduling maintenance requests, and supporting the overall presentation of the clubhouse and common areas. Turn periods, which in student housing can mean hundreds of move-ins in a single week, are a critical part of the calendar, and availability during those stretches is a genuine requirement.

  • Conduct community and amenity tours for prospective residents
  • Support social media and resident engagement initiatives
  • Handle package management and general office upkeep
  • Follow up on maintenance requests and communicate status to residents
  • Participate in after-hours on-call rotation, including lockout assistance
  • Relay sales barriers and resident feedback to the management team

Who Tends to Thrive Here

The candidates who stand out in this role aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones who stay composed when three things need attention at once, who communicate clearly with an eighteen-year-old first-year student and their parent in the same conversation, and who take pride in how a space looks and feels. Reliability matters more than polish here. The on-call rotation and Turn availability requirements aren't optional, and the team depends on everyone pulling their weight during the high-demand stretches.

This kind of role also builds a strong foundation for growth in property management. Leasing consultants who develop a feel for traffic patterns, objection handling, and resident relations often move into assistant manager roles, and student housing specifically gives you exposure to lease-up pressure and high-volume operations that translate well across property types. Chapel Hill's market, anchored by UNC, keeps demand active and the leasing environment genuinely competitive, which means the skills you build here are real ones.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental and maternal leave, PTO, and learning reimbursement. A discretionary annual bonus is also part of the package. Work authorization is required; visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Experience Team Member role at The Magnolia at Auburn sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and resident relations. On any given day, you might be touring a prospective resident through the community, responding to a social media inquiry, logging packages, and following up on a maintenance request before your shift ends. That range isn't accidental. Scion builds this role to cover the full front-facing operation of a student housing community, which means you're rarely doing the same thing twice.

Touring is central. You'll walk prospects through amenities, handle objections in real time, and report sales barriers back to the management team so pricing strategy and messaging can adjust accordingly. You'll also support local marketing efforts, assist with resident engagement events, and help maintain the kind of community presence that keeps occupancy strong through the competitive student leasing cycle.

Property administration rounds out the role. Package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage are all part of the job. These aren't glamorous tasks, but they're where residents form their strongest impressions of a community's management.

What You Bring

  • Genuine comfort talking to a wide range of people, including prospective residents, parents, and current residents with complaints
  • Reliability during high-stakes periods: summer, holidays, and Turn (the concentrated move-in/move-out cycle that defines student housing operations)
  • Self-discipline to handle an on-call rotation without needing constant supervision
  • Flexibility when priorities shift mid-shift, because they will
  • Basic comfort with social media platforms used for community communication and marketing

What This Role Builds

Student housing leasing sharpens skills that transfer directly into conventional multifamily. You'll develop the ability to read traffic patterns, respond to seasonal leasing pressure, and communicate concessions and incentives clearly without overselling. The Turn period in student housing is one of the most operationally demanding experiences in residential property management. Executing it well, even in a supporting role, demonstrates a level of operational awareness that carries real weight on a resume.

Strong candidates here aren't necessarily the most extroverted people in the room. They're the ones who follow through consistently, stay professional when residents are frustrated, and treat the administrative side of the job with the same care they give the sales side. The two are inseparable in student housing, and the candidates who understand that early tend to advance quickly.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultants at garden-style communities in suburban markets like Hixson carry a specific kind of weight. Chattanooga's north shore corridor has seen steady residential growth, and properties in the Hixson submarket compete on experience as much as price. That means the person handling tours, follow-up calls, and move-in paperwork isn't just processing leads. They're often the deciding factor in whether a prospect signs or keeps shopping.

What the Role Actually Covers

Hawthorne Residential Partners calls this position a Leasing and Live It Specialist, which signals something about how the company thinks about front-line leasing. The work spans the full leasing cycle: greeting walk-ins, conducting personalized tours, working phone and email inquiries, completing applications and move-in paperwork accurately, and contributing to occupancy and renewal goals. You'll also support resident retention through event coordination and community engagement, help maintain a clean and welcoming office environment, and stay current on competing properties and local market conditions.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays from 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the total at 40 hours. Occasional evenings may come up around resident events, so some schedule flexibility is realistic to expect.

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience is preferred but not required. What actually separates people who thrive in this role from those who struggle is the combination of genuine follow-through and the ability to read a prospect's priorities quickly. A lot of applicants can give a decent tour.
