What separates strong candidates here isn't just technical range. It's the combination of trade competence with genuine comfort talking to residents. Maintenance supervisors at the community level are often the face of the property when something goes wrong. Residents remember how a repair interaction felt, not just whether it got done. If you can fix the problem and leave the resident feeling heard, you'll thrive in this kind of role. If you've been a strong tech who's ready to grow into leading others, this training structure is a real on-ramp, not just a title.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Weinstein Properties manages its communities in-house, which changes the day-to-day experience for maintenance staff in ways that matter. There's no third-party management layer between you and the decisions that affect your property. Standards are consistent, leadership is accessible, and when something needs to get done, the answer doesn't get lost in a chain of approvals. For a skilled technician who's tired of the disconnect that comes with fee management setups, that structure makes a real difference.

The opening at Bexley at Anderson Mill in the Cedar Park area is a full-time maintenance technician role built around someone with at least three years of apartment maintenance experience and a current EPA certification (Type II or Universal). The work spans the full range of residential maintenance: completing work orders in occupied units, supporting turns and make-readies, and handling HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry repairs. You'll also help maintain the community's grounds, amenities, and pool areas alongside the rest of the maintenance team.

The compensation starts at $22 per hour and moves up based on experience. On-call participation comes with a flat $150 weekly guarantee regardless of call volume, plus an additional $150 for holiday on-call shifts. Quarterly bonuses reach up to $980 tied to property and team performance. Benefits include rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, an Employee Assistance Program, and a referral program. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, with rotating emergency on-call coverage shared across the team.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just the EPA cert or the HVAC hours. It's the combination of technical range and resident-facing composure. Technicians who thrive in apartment maintenance understand that a work order is also a service interaction. The residents living in those units are your customers, and how you communicate while you're diagnosing a problem matters as much as how quickly you fix it. If you've developed that balance over your career, it tends to show up clearly during a walkthrough or a reference call.

From a career development standpoint, a role like this one builds the foundation for a lead technician or maintenance supervisor path. The skills that compound most over time: HVAC diagnostic depth, vendor coordination during turns, and the ability to prioritize a work order queue without letting anything age. Technicians who move into supervisory roles usually got there because they ran their properties like the performance of the asset was their responsibility, not just their manager's.

What You'll Need

  • Minimum three years of apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Certification, Type II or Universal
  • Hands-on HVAC troubleshooting and repair experience
  • Comfort with work order systems and basic computer and mobile device use
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round in Central Texas conditions
  • Reliable transportation and ability to pass a background check

job.title: Maintenance Technician- Scottsdale Horizon Apartments
job.description:
Multi-trade competency is the core skill set here. Not just the ability to fix things, but the ability to triage, prioritize, and close out work orders without constant hand-holding. At Scottsdale Horizon Apartments, MG Properties is looking for a Maintenance Technician who brings real hands-on experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and appliance repair. Two years minimum on a property of 200 units or larger is the baseline they're working from. That's not an arbitrary number. At that scale, you've seen enough volume to know how to work a board efficiently and keep turns from dragging.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Grounds and common area upkeep, service request completion, painting, and make-ready work are all part of the rotation. So is on-call coverage, which means you'll take emergency calls on your assigned nights and weekends. That's just the nature of residential maintenance. Anyone who's done it knows the on-call rotation is where you earn the trust of your team and your residents pretty quickly. Customer service isn't a soft skill here, it's operational. How you show up at a resident's door when their A/C goes out at 10 PM on a July evening in Scottsdale matters as much as whether you can fix it.

Speaking of Scottsdale in July: HVAC is not optional knowledge at this property. Arizona summers are unforgiving, and HVAC calls will dominate your board from late spring through early fall. If your A/C experience is thin, this role will expose that fast.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Genuine multi-trade experience, not familiarity with one or two disciplines and a learning attitude about the rest
  • Comfort managing a full work order board without losing track of priorities
  • The ability to communicate clearly with residents under pressure
  • Reliable transportation to get to the property and respond to on-call situations
  • Team orientation. Maintenance at a community this size is a team sport.

Working for MG Properties

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of track record in a regional operator usually means standardized processes, real support infrastructure, and a company that isn't figuring out property management as it goes. The compensation package includes monthly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, full medical, dental, and vision, and rental discounts. PTO, paid holidays, personal days, and sick time are also part of the package.

If you've got the trade skills and the temperament for residential maintenance work, this is a solid place to put them to use.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Where Sales, Relationship-Building, and Campus Life Overlap

Student housing leasing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Prospects are often first-time renters, their parents are frequently part of the conversation, and the leasing cycle compresses hard around academic calendars. At Redpoint Tempe, a Scion Group community serving the Arizona State University market, the Experience Team Member role sits at the center of all of it. This is a position built around interpersonal skill, and it calls on that skill constantly.

You'll conduct community and amenity tours, handle prospect follow-up, and execute sales and engagement initiatives set by the management team. Beyond the leasing floor, the role pulls in light marketing work: contributing ideas for local outreach, helping manage social media presence, and assisting with resident events. Property administration is part of the mix too. Package retrieval, office organization, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage all fall within scope. The range is real, and candidates who prefer narrow, task-specific work tend to find student housing ETM roles uncomfortable.

The Skills This Role Develops and Demands

Strong candidates bring communication skills that adapt quickly. You might be walking a high-energy sophomore through a floor plan, then shifting to a detailed phone call with a concerned parent, then following up with a prospect who raised objections during a tour earlier in the week. The ability to read a situation and adjust tone without losing momentum is the core competency here.

Reliability matters more than most postings acknowledge. Student housing turns are concentrated and intense. When the summer turn hits at a property like this, everyone is needed and tardiness or inconsistency creates real downstream problems for the operations team. Scion specifically requires availability during turn periods, summer, and holidays. That's not boilerplate. It reflects how student housing actually works.

  • Customer-facing communication with a diverse population of residents, prospects, and guarantors
  • Sales and objection handling at the leasing level
  • Social media and community engagement support
  • Package management, office maintenance, and general administrative support
  • After-hours on-call rotation for lockout assistance
  • Maintenance request tracking and follow-up coordination

What Makes This Role at Scion Worth Noting

Scion Group operates at scale in the student housing sector, which means the systems, training, and operational standards here are more developed than what you'd find at a smaller independent operator. For someone early in a property management career, that structure matters. The skills you build in a student housing ETM role, specifically high-volume prospect communication, creative marketing execution, and turn-cycle operations, transfer directly to conventional multifamily leasing roles and set a strong foundation for moving into assistant manager or leasing manager positions over time.

Tempe's rental market around ASU is genuinely competitive, with a steady supply of purpose-built student communities. That means leasing here isn't passive. Traffic needs to be converted with intention, and the feedback you provide to management about sales barriers and objections has real operational value. Candidates who treat that feedback loop seriously tend to stand out.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon and you're on the phone with a resident whose rent payment posted to the wrong ledger, while a prospect walks through the door for a scheduled tour. You wrap the call with a clear resolution, hand the prospect off smoothly, and get back to a delinquency follow-up list before the day closes. That's the rhythm of this role at Evolve Waterford in Leland, NC.

The Role at Evolve Waterford

Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the 50 largest multifamily management companies in the country and deeply rooted in the Southeast, is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for this Leland property. The position sits at the intersection of leasing, financial administration, and team leadership. You'll work alongside the Community Manager to keep occupancy strong, delinquency in check, and residents genuinely satisfied.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, respond to leads, guide prospects through applications, and work renewals to protect retention. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which at a property like this means showcasing resident events and keeping the community feel visible online. On the financial side, the job involves rent collection, payment posting, ledger audits, delinquency calls, and supporting eviction coordination when necessary. These aren't background tasks. They're a core part of what this role requires you to do well.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the office. That means maintaining team momentum, setting daily priorities, and fielding whatever comes through the door without letting things slide.

What This Role Requires

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus

Candidates who stand out in this role tend to be comfortable reading financial reports and acting on what they find, not just passing numbers up the chain. Delinquency management specifically rewards people who are organized, consistent, and direct without being combative. If you've worked at a property where rent collection was treated as a weekly discipline rather than a month-end scramble, that experience translates directly here.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off to maintain a 40-hour week. Some evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers a structured Career Path Program for employees working toward a Community Manager role.

job.title: Leasing Consultant Sales Intern (Nantucket Cove)
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work

Leasing is a sales role with a customer service wrapper, and this internship at Nantucket Cove makes that clear from day one. The skills you'll use most heavily are consultative selling, active listening, and persuasive communication. Every tour is a structured conversation: you're qualifying a prospect's needs, matching them to the right floor plan, and making the case for why this community fits their life. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or food service, you already know how to read people quickly and adjust your approach. That instinct transfers directly here.

You'll also work inside property management software to track leads and follow-ups, which means attention to detail and data discipline matter from the start. Inaccurate records create gaps in follow-up, and gaps in follow-up cost leases. That's a lesson experienced leasing professionals learn early, and you'll learn it here.

What You'll Do at Nantucket Cove

BAM Companies operates within a private equity real estate portfolio, so there's real business context behind the work. You'll be on the front line of occupancy, greeting prospects, running tours, and walking people through community amenities and available units. You'll support local marketing efforts and contribute to social media content designed to drive traffic to the property. On the administrative side, you'll keep lead records current and accurate, which feeds directly into the leasing team's ability to follow up effectively.

Resident relations are part of the role too. You'll assist with move-ins and move-outs and support community events, which means you're managing the experience of current residents while simultaneously selling to future ones. You'll also conduct competitor market surveys, which gives you exposure to how properties are priced and positioned relative to the local Champaign market. That kind of analysis is how leasing teams inform concessions strategy and occupancy goals.

Coordination with maintenance is part of the job as well. Making sure units are make-ready and meet BAM's standards before a showing isn't glamorous, but it's fundamental. A unit that isn't properly turned before a tour can lose a lease no matter how good the pitch is.

Skills This Role Builds

This is where the internship earns its value. Strong candidates will leave with a practical understanding of the leasing lifecycle, from first contact through move-in. They'll have used real property management software, run live market analysis, and contributed to a marketing strategy. Those are transferable skills that open doors to full-time leasing consultant roles, assistant manager positions, and eventually property management roles as a career path.

What separates interns who get the most from this experience: they treat every tour as a real sales conversation, not a task to complete. They follow up on leads without being reminded. They ask questions about NOI and occupancy when they have a chance. The candidates who do that tend to get noticed.

  • Currently pursuing a degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Real Estate, or a related field
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office; able to learn property management software quickly
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and accurate with data entry
  • Flexible availability to meet property scheduling needs
  • Prior customer-facing experience preferred (retail, hospitality, or similar)
  • Interest in real estate investment and property management is a genuine plus

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Saturday afternoon, traffic is picking up, and you've got two prospects waiting in the leasing office while a current resident stops by with a maintenance question. That's a normal hour at a busy lease-up. If you can hold all of that together and still close, this role is probably a fit.

The Position at Reveal Hackensack

Berkshire Residential Investments is hiring a Leasing Consultant at Reveal Hackensack, their property in northern New Jersey. Berkshire is an owner-operator, not a third-party management shop, which means decisions move faster and there's more direct accountability at the site level. The leasing consultant here carries real responsibility for converting traffic into signed leases and keeping the resident experience intact once they move in.

The day-to-day covers what you'd expect: touring prospects, maintaining model and tour route presentation, tracking local market conditions, and staying on top of resident communications. Berkshire holds their leasing staff to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is a reasonable benchmark and a clear signal that this isn't a purely administrative role. You're expected to sell.

Beyond the floor traffic, you'll contribute ideas to the property manager on marketing direction and resident satisfaction. That kind of input is taken seriously here. The office culture leans toward high energy and genuine hospitality, so if you're someone who goes flat after a long stretch of prospect calls, it's worth being honest with yourself about that.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of customer service experience that translates well to leasing, sales, or hospitality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including professional resident correspondence
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to adapt as platforms change
  • Attention to detail on administrative tasks, from application processing to follow-up tracking
  • Genuine ease with people across a wide range of personalities and situations

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, personal development plans, a 25% rent discount, and a solid benefits package. Those details are worth noting because the rent discount in a market like Hackensack carries real dollar value.

One honest observation from fifteen years of watching leasing teams: the consultants who advance quickly are the ones who treat the CRM like a tool rather than a chore and who actually read the T-3 occupancy and traffic reports. Understanding why closing ratios dip in a given week, and being able to speak to it, is what separates a good leasing consultant from someone who's ready to move into an assistant manager role. Berkshire promotes from within, and this position is a legitimate starting point for that path.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 186
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position draws on a broad technical base. You'll work across plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems on any given day. The work isn't specialized in one trade. It's generalist maintenance done consistently well, which means your ability to diagnose quickly and execute without a lot of hand-holding matters more than depth in any single area.

Resident interaction is part of the job too. You're not just fixing things in empty units. You're communicating with people who live there, which means your customer service instincts get used as often as your tools.

What You'll Handle Day to Day

Walton Lofts is a Berkshire-owned and managed property, so standards get set in-house rather than filtered through a third-party management layer. That means accountability is direct and expectations are consistent.

  • Complete service requests across all trade categories: plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry
  • Support unit turns and make-readies, including punch list completion
  • Maintain curb appeal through regular inspections and follow-through
  • Manage shop organization, equipment upkeep, and inventory control
  • Enforce safety protocols and maintain key security procedures
  • Back up the management team in upholding property and company standards

You'll need at least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or commercial setting. Computer proficiency is required for work order systems and documentation.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Technicians who do well in this kind of role stay ahead of the work order queue instead of just reacting to it. They notice things on property walks before residents call them in. They treat make-readies with the same attention they'd give an occupied unit repair. Berkshire operates its own portfolio, so the care you put into the physical asset has a direct connection to how the property performs. That context tends to matter to people who take their craft seriously.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans. They're explicit about building careers, not just filling positions.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 7 a.m. for a heating issue. By the time the leasing office opens, it's already resolved and closed out. That's the standard this role operates at.

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for their Mountlake Terrace, WA community. The position sits between hands-on technician work and team leadership, which makes it a genuinely useful career step. You're still diagnosing HVAC systems, troubleshooting plumbing, and handling appliance repairs yourself, but you're also modeling the work ethic and attention to detail that shapes how the rest of the maintenance team performs.

What the Role Covers

Day-to-day responsibilities run across the full maintenance spectrum. Service tickets need timely follow-up and thorough completion. The make-ready and turn process requires coordination and precision so units get back into leasable condition without delay. Preventative maintenance programs keep the asset performing well over time rather than lurching from one emergency to the next. You'll also handle grounds upkeep, safety compliance, snow removal, and the general cleanliness standards that affect how both residents and prospective renters experience the property. Weekend availability and participation in an on-call emergency rotation are part of the role. The salary range is $62,400 to $66,560, with additional bonus opportunities.

What You Bring

  • Five or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Familiarity with complex mechanical systems such as boilers, chillers, split systems, or central plant equipment is a plus
  • Understanding of OSHA standards, risk management, and MSDS protocols
  • Supervisory or leadership experience, even informal mentoring, is preferred
  • Comfort with technology platforms and the Microsoft Office suite
  • Physical capability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in variable outdoor conditions

What separates a strong candidate here from a capable technician who's ready to move on: the ability to hold a standard without micromanaging. Bozzuto properties carry a clear brand expectation around resident experience, and the maintenance team is central to delivering it. An assistant manager who can communicate crisply with residents, close work orders completely, and train up junior staff compounds value fast. That combination, trade depth plus people competency, is what opens the door to a full Maintenance Manager role, and from there, Regional Facilities Director tracks become realistic at larger operators.

Bozzuto offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for ongoing development.

job.title: Bilingual Leasing Hub Associate - Sandy Springs, GA
job.description:
Centralized leasing hubs exist because scattered, community-by-community lead handling bleeds traffic and kills conversion. Cortland built this model to consolidate inbound volume, respond faster, and push qualified appointments to their onsite teams at scale. This role sits at the top of that funnel, and the throughput is real: you're working 40 to 50 leads per day across multiple communities.

This is not a traditional leasing consultant position. There's no model unit tour, no lease signing at your desk. The job is phone, email, and text, working RealPage leads and converting cold inquiries into booked appointments for Cortland properties across their portfolio. Think of it as inside sales for a top-10 multifamily operator.

What This Role Actually Requires

The volume is the first thing to internalize. Forty to fifty leads daily means you're building a rhythm fast. Slow typists, people who lose energy on repetitive outbound, or candidates who need face-to-face interaction to close won't last long here. What works is someone who treats each lead like a fresh conversion opportunity, stays organized across a high-contact queue, and communicates clearly in writing as often as by voice.

Bilingual fluency is listed as a qualification, and in the Sandy Springs and broader Atlanta metro market, that typically means English and Spanish. Spanish-speaking prospective residents are a meaningful share of the renter pool in this corridor, and the ability to build rapport in a prospect's preferred language directly affects appointment conversion rates. If that's your edge, it matters here more than in most leasing roles.

OneSite proficiency is required. L2L (Lead to Lease) experience is preferred. If you've worked in RealPage's ecosystem before, the learning curve on this platform is short.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • At least two years of customer-facing experience, with a preference for sales backgrounds
  • Bilingual fluency (English required; second language a strong differentiator)
  • Strong written and verbal communication across multiple channels simultaneously
  • Solid computer and typing skills, given the volume of text and email outreach
  • Working knowledge of OneSite; L2L experience is a plus

What separates strong candidates here is not charm alone. It's the ability to manage lead cadence without dropping threads, adjust your pitch based on a prospect's stated needs and budget, and hand off warm appointments to onsite teams with enough context that the tour actually converts. You're not closing the lease. You're closing the visit, and that's a specific skill.

Cortland is a vertically integrated firm founded in 2005, now operating as one of the largest multifamily owners in the country. The hub model reflects how operators at their scale are rethinking leasing infrastructure: centralize the top-of-funnel work, free up onsite teams to focus on the in-person experience, and use data to track conversion at every stage. For someone building a career in multifamily, that kind of exposure to portfolio-level leasing operations, metrics, and systems is genuinely useful and not common in entry-level roles.

job.title: Property Administrator
job.description:
Commercial property administration runs on details. Purchase orders that don't get coded correctly throw off your NOI reporting. Delinquency letters that go out late push aged receivables into the 60-day column. Vendor COIs that lapse put the property at risk. This role at Lincoln Property Company in Savannah keeps all of that moving, and it demands someone who treats administrative accuracy as a genuine discipline, not a background task.

The Skills This Role Uses Every Day

Real estate accounting fluency sits at the center of this position. You'll apply tenant rents, reconcile open credits, organize and code invoices in Workspace, and compile tenant billings and miscellaneous charges. If you've worked through a monthly accounting cycle before, including A/P, A/R, and lease charge structures in a commercial context, you already understand the rhythm. MRI, Workspace, and Yardi experience will let you move faster from day one. Beyond the numbers, you'll need strong vendor coordination skills: monitoring contractor compliance, tracking certificates of insurance, and helping prepare and administer service agreements. These aren't one-time tasks. They recur every month, every quarter, every lease cycle.

Communication ties everything together. You're fielding calls from tenants, routing messages to the right people, and keeping the property management team informed with aged delinquency reports and purchase order status updates. Clarity and professionalism in every interaction matters because this role touches both the tenant-facing side and the owner-reporting side of the operation.

Responsibilities in Practice

  • Manage the full purchase order workflow: issuance, tracking, and matching POs to invoices as they process for payment
  • Run monthly reports and flag unresolved purchase orders before they create bottlenecks
  • Assist the Chief Engineer with the electrical analysis worksheet as utility invoices arrive (relevant if the property uses RUBS or direct billing structures)
  • Maintain tenant files, filing systems, and the property staff directory
  • Coordinate tenant events, including seasonal programming and community initiatives
  • Provide aged delinquency reports to the management team and send late letters on schedule
  • Support accounts payable and accounts receivable functions and assist with reporting

This is a 100% in-office position in Savannah working standard business hours. No remote or hybrid option.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Lincoln manages more than 680 million square feet of commercial space across institutional clients. At the property level, that scale means the administrative systems and reporting standards are real and enforced. Candidates who thrive in this environment already respect the monthly accounting close. They know that an uncoded invoice or a missed delinquency report doesn't just create internal noise. It affects what an owner sees on their statement. The strongest applicants will bring at least two years of commercial property management experience, genuine comfort with Yardi or MRI, and the kind of organized independence that doesn't need daily direction to stay on top of recurring deadlines. An associate's or bachelor's degree is preferred alongside the high school minimum.

If you've been in a commercial PM admin role and want to deepen your accounting and operations exposure within a well-structured platform, this position gives you direct access to the full property finance cycle.

job.title: Operations Specialist
job.description:
Asset Living runs a large third-party management portfolio across multifamily, single-family rentals, student housing, build-to-rent, and affordable housing. This Operations Specialist role sits at the corporate level, supporting senior managers who oversee that portfolio. The position can be based in Atlanta, Charlotte, or Jacksonville.

Day to day, the work splits across a few different lanes. You'll pull and review financial data on properties, including historical income and expense detail, and help prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly reporting packages. You'll gather rent comps and market trend data from internal tools and third-party sources. You'll also handle client-facing communication, helping stakeholders understand how specific assets are performing. On top of that, there's a real administrative component: coordinating travel, fielding resident calls that come in at the corporate level, and supporting internal projects from start to finish.

The analytical side of this role is real. You're not just formatting reports. You're reviewing T-12 data, identifying trends, and presenting information in a way that helps senior leadership make decisions. Strong Excel skills matter here, and familiarity with property management platforms like MRI or One-Site will help you move faster. A background in finance, real estate, or economics is a plus, but the emphasis is on how you think and how you handle competing deadlines.

What separates a strong candidate from an average one in a role like this is the combination of financial literacy and organizational discipline. Plenty of people can run a spreadsheet. Fewer can manage a full reporting cycle across a large portfolio, stay on top of multiple projects simultaneously, and communicate clearly with both internal teams and external clients. If you've supported a regional or area manager in property management before, you already know how fast priorities shift. That experience translates directly here.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, ideally in finance, real estate, or economics
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel and PowerPoint
  • Experience with MRI, One-Site, or similar property management software is a plus
  • Solid analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines without losing accuracy or attention to detail
  • Comfortable with approximately 10% travel for property visits or internal meetings

This is a corporate support role with real exposure to portfolio-level operations across multiple asset classes. For someone early in their property management career, the visibility here into financials, client relationships, and cross-functional projects builds a foundation that can move toward asset management, regional operations, or portfolio analysis over time.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Bexley Village at Concord Mills
job.description:
Leading Maintenance at Scale

A 624-unit community with a nine-person maintenance team is a real operation. At this size, the Maintenance Supervisor role isn't just a technical job with a title attached. It's a coordination role, a quality control role, and a customer service role, all wrapped into one. Weinstein Properties has owned and operated apartment communities for over 70 years, and that kind of tenure tends to produce clear systems and genuine promotion paths for people who perform.

Bexley Village at Concord Mills sits in the Concord submarket northeast of Charlotte, a corridor that's seen consistent residential demand tied to employment and retail growth around Concord Mills. Keeping a 624-unit garden-style community performing well in that market means occupancy and NOI both depend, in part, on how fast and how cleanly your team executes turns and handles service requests.

What the Role Actually Requires

This is a hands-on supervisory position. Weinstein is specific about that. You'll work alongside your team, not just direct them. The technical baseline is real: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, appliances, pool maintenance, and exterior structural work. EPA/CFC Universal or Type I and II certification is required before you start, not something you'll earn on the job here.

On the supervisory side, you'll coordinate daily workflows, manage vendor scheduling, oversee make-ready turns, and handle work order assignment through business software. With nine people reporting to you, your ability to triage competing priorities across a large property will matter as much as your trade skills. You'll also share on-call rotation with your teammates, and Weinstein pays a bonus for those weeks.

  • Minimum 4 years of trade experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and related disciplines
  • At least 1 year in a lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisor role in apartment maintenance
  • EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal) required
  • Computer proficiency for work orders, supply ordering, and communication
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and your own tools

What This Role Builds

Strong candidates already know their trades cold. What separates the best applicants is the ability to run a team without micromanaging it. At 624 units, you can't be at every work order. You need to trust your team, set quality standards, and inspect results. The supervisors who grow fastest in roles like this are the ones who treat every turn and every service call as a data point: how long did it take, what did it cost, and did the resident notice the difference.

Weinstein promotes from within and backs that up with training investment. A Maintenance Supervisor who performs well here builds a clear path toward Regional Maintenance Director or multi-site oversight. The company owns and manages its entire portfolio, which means the institutional knowledge you develop at Bexley Village translates directly to other Weinstein communities rather than getting lost in a third-party management structure.

A $3,000 sign-on bonus is available. Details are covered during the interview process.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Domain San Diego
job.description:
MG Properties has spent over three decades acquiring, rehabilitating, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S., and the culture they've built reflects that longevity. This isn't a company that treats maintenance as a cost center. The Maintenance Technician role at Domain San Diego sits at the center of daily operations, and how well it's performed shows up directly in resident satisfaction, NOI protection, and the long-term condition of the asset.

The work spans the full range of what apartment maintenance actually looks like: service requests, appliance repairs, painting, make-ready turns, grounds upkeep, and rotating emergency on-call coverage. You'll operate within Yardi's maintenance system, processing requests through mobile tools and keeping records on preventive maintenance, work-in-progress, and make-ready status. HVAC Universal certification and CPO are either required or expected, and you'll need a working knowledge of HAZCOM standards and EPA/OSHA regulations around hazardous materials storage.

At least two years of apartment maintenance experience is the baseline, ideally on a property of 200 units or more. Multi-trade fluency matters here. Plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair: these aren't nice-to-haves. The candidate who thrives in this role moves fluidly between trades without needing to escalate routine issues, which keeps turns tight and service request queues manageable.

What separates strong candidates here

  • Demonstrated ability to complete make-readies on schedule without cutting corners on punch list items
  • Comfort with mobile maintenance platforms, specifically Yardi on an iPhone
  • HVAC Universal and CPO certifications already in hand
  • A track record of resident-facing professionalism, not just technical skill
  • Valid driver's license with current liability insurance

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds the exact foundation that leads to Maintenance Supervisor and eventually Maintenance Director positions. Technicians who develop strong preventive maintenance habits, learn to manage parts inventory efficiently, and build credibility with on-site leadership tend to move up faster than those who focus only on reactive repairs. The administrative side of this job, tracking expenditures, managing work orders, coordinating schedules, translates directly into the supervisory skills that larger portfolios demand. San Diego's Class A and B apartment market is competitive, and properties that run tight operations retain good maintenance staff. This is a role worth taking seriously as a long-term career move, not just a paycheck.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. At Redpoint Columbia, you're supporting the General Manager across every major function: leasing and revenue performance, resident accounts, facilities coordination, staff development, and the annual turn. That last one deserves a direct look. Student properties don't do rolling turns. They do one massive turn in a compressed window every summer, where hundreds of units need to be inspected, punched, cleaned, and ready before move-in day. You'll be in the middle of that physically. Moving furniture, helping the facilities team knock out punch list items, sorting resident trash at volume. It's not glamorous, and it's not optional.

Outside of turn season, your week involves monitoring delinquency and keeping it below 2% by month-end, auditing resident accounts and utility billing, handling escalated resident concerns, and standing in for the GM when they're out. You'll track leasing KPIs through Entrata, including concessions, market rates, and leasing velocity, and use that data to flag issues before they become problems. You'll also manage the on-call rotation schedule alongside the Customer and Sales Experience Manager, which means after-hours emergencies are part of the job description, not an exception to it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year in property management or a residential living environment
  • Comfort with Entrata or a comparable property management system
  • Strong written communication skills, because you'll be drafting resident notices, responding to Google and Yelp reviews, and handling escalated account matters in writing
  • Solid grasp of accounts receivable, damage billing, and collections processes
  • The ability to hold a professional standard under pressure, especially during peak periods when the workload compounds fast

Scion also uses Greenhouse for recruiting, Lattice for performance management, Turnable for the electronic turn board, Qualtrics for resident and employee feedback, and ClickUp for project tracking. You don't need to know all of these on day one, but you should be someone who picks up new platforms without friction.

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing is a distinct niche. Lease terms are fixed, renewal cycles are compressed, and your residents are often signing their first-ever lease. That creates a specific kind of customer service demand. Concerns escalate quickly, parents get involved, and reputation platforms matter more than they do at conventional properties. If you've worked conventional multifamily and are considering a move into student housing, the operational pace during turn and lease-up is genuinely different. The upside is that this role builds a wide skill set fast. An Assistant Community Manager who handles turn execution, financial reporting, team supervision, and leasing performance simultaneously is well-positioned to step into a General Manager role. Scion operates at scale across student markets, which means that path is a real one here, not just a recruiting line.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (550 Moreland)
job.description:
Prometheus Real Estate Group has been quietly building one of the Bay Area's most respected apartment portfolios since 1965, and the Leasing Consultant role at their 550 Moreland property in Santa Clara sits right at the center of what makes their operation work: connecting people to a place they'll genuinely call home.

What This Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

Prometheus calls this position a "Neighbor Ambassador," and that framing tells you something real about the job. It's not a pure sales role. It's not purely administrative. On any given day, you might be walking a prospective resident through an apartment, following up on a rental application, drafting advertising copy, running a market survey, or simply checking in with a current resident who had a maintenance concern. The throughline is people, and your ability to make them feel genuinely taken care of.

The leasing side means guiding future residents through the full process, from that first inquiry call or walk-in visit through signing the rental agreement. The customer service side means existing residents expect to recognize your face and trust your follow-through. The administrative side means you're learning the operational backbone of property management: reports, market comps, lease documentation, and occupancy tracking. It's a lot, and the pace reflects that Santa Clara is a competitive submarket with consistent traffic from the tech sector.

One honest note: weekends are your busiest days, and your schedule reflects that. Your regular days off will fall on weekdays. For some people that's a dealbreaker; for others it's a genuine perk. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing role that runs on a similar schedule, you already know the rhythm.

What Prometheus Is Looking For

  • A background in customer service, sales, or marketing (industry doesn't matter as much as the mindset)
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, since you're representing the community in every interaction
  • Self-direction and creativity when solving problems, without waiting to be told what to do
  • Comfort working weekends as part of your regular schedule
  • Alignment with a team-oriented culture where people are expected to support each other across the property

Compensation and Growth

The pay range runs from $25.00 to $28.75 per hour, with a $200 incentive per lease signed and a discretionary semi-annual bonus on top. Weekend shifts carry premium pay, and there are additional bonus structures tied to referrals, training, renovations, and lease-up performance. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage for eligible employees and dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts.

From a career standpoint, this role is one of the clearest on-ramps into property management. Leasing Consultants who build strong occupancy track records and develop operational fluency often move into Assistant Manager or Community Manager roles over time. Prometheus operates a vertically integrated platform, which means internal mobility is real. The skills you build here, reading traffic patterns, understanding prospect behavior, managing lease documentation, translate directly into more senior operations roles if that's the direction you want to go.

Prometheus is a Certified B Corporation and a recognized Best Place to Work in the Bay Area. That context matters here because it shapes how the team operates internally, not just how the company presents itself externally.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Role and Why It Exists

An Assistant Community Manager sits at the intersection of leasing performance, resident experience, and daily financial operations. At most apartment communities, this role exists because a single manager can't own every moving piece at once. The ACM keeps collections current, delinquency in check, and the leasing pipeline warm while the Community Manager focuses on the bigger picture. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a top-50 multifamily management company based in the Southeast, that partnership is the engine behind how their communities run.

This opening is in Wake Forest, NC, a fast-growing market north of Raleigh where resident expectations skew high and occupancy pressure is real. You'll need to perform on both sides of the desk: closing leases and managing ledgers.

What the Job Actually Looks Like

On the leasing side, you conduct tours, work incoming leads, and shepherd prospects through to a signed lease. You manage renewals, make sure documents are complete and accurate, and help hit occupancy targets through a combination of new leases and retention. You'll also handle the community's social media presence, which means posting content around resident events and keeping the property visible online.

On the financial and administrative side, you own rent collection: posting payments, scanning checks, and monitoring delinquency on a weekly basis. When accounts go sideways, you make the follow-up calls and coordinate eviction procedures when it comes to that. You review ledgers regularly to catch billing errors and misapplied payments before they compound. You'll also assist with financial reporting up to the Community Manager and regional leadership.

When the Community Manager is out, you step into that seat. That means maintaining team direction, keeping operations steady, and handling whatever comes through the door.

Office hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You get one weekday off per week to stay at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come with the territory depending on resident events or community needs.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months of prior assistant community manager experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and telehealth access.

Hawthorne also runs a formal Career Path Program. The ACM role is a direct pipeline to Community Manager. If you're putting in the work on ledger accuracy, delinquency management, and leasing performance, that track record is exactly what gets you there. The skills you build here, reading financial reports, managing conflict, running a leasing office solo, carry directly into any CM role in the industry.

job.title: Recertification Specialist
job.description:
Affordable housing compliance runs on paperwork, deadlines, and precision. Recertification is one of the most time-sensitive and regulation-heavy processes a property team handles, and when it falls behind, the consequences reach residents directly. This role exists to own that process at Pelham Apartments, a property managed by John M. Corcoran and Company, one of New England's more established real estate firms with roots going back to 1951.

What This Role Actually Involves

The core of the job is managing the annual recertification cycle for affordable housing residents. That means scheduling and conducting intake interviews, collecting documentation, and keeping resident files current and audit-ready. You'll coordinate apartment inspections tied to recertifications, assist with waitlist management, and process applicant information in compliance with regulatory agency requirements.

Beyond recertification, you'll support the broader office operation. That includes rent collection, answering phones, logging maintenance requests, and helping coordinate resident programs. The property managers and assistant managers lean on this role to keep compliance tasks moving without pulling their attention away from day-to-day operations.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5. Pay runs between $25.75 and $31.00 per hour, and there's a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) with a company match.

What Makes a Strong Candidate

  • At least two years in an administrative role, ideally one with regulatory or compliance components
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You'll interact directly with residents and coordinate across departments.
  • High attention to detail and the organizational discipline to maintain complete files under agency standards
  • Solid computer skills across standard office platforms
  • Familiarity with affordable housing regulations (HUD, LIHTC, or Section 8 frameworks) is a real advantage, though not a hard requirement

The candidates who stand out here aren't just organized. They understand that a missed deadline or incomplete file can trigger a compliance finding that affects residents' housing status. This role requires someone who treats documentation as a responsibility, not just a task. If you've worked in a regulated housing environment before, that experience will carry real weight.

Recertification work also builds transferable skills in affordable housing compliance that open doors to program coordinator or compliance officer roles at larger housing authorities, nonprofits, or multi-site management companies. It's a specialty that's increasingly in demand as affordable housing inventory grows and regulatory oversight tightens.

job.title: Regional Leasing Floater
job.description:
The Regional Leasing Floater role at John M. Corcoran and Company sits at an interesting intersection: you're not tied to a single property, which means you'll see how different communities operate, how traffic patterns shift by location, and how leasing strategy adapts to each asset's position in the market. For someone early in a property management career, that exposure compounds fast.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you'll tour apartments with prospective residents, walk them through pricing and lease terms, and move applications through to approval. But the role goes further than showings. You'll build lease packages, coordinate move-ins, and own the experience that turns a signed lease into a resident who actually wants to stay. That last part matters more than most leasing postings let on: the resident relationship you establish at move-in shapes renewal conversations twelve months later.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll set your own occupancy goals and work toward them through social media, online advertising, and community networking. You'll also do property inspections to keep curb appeal sharp, which is one of those responsibilities that quietly trains your eye for what makes a community feel well-run versus just occupied.

The floater structure means JMC will place you across their South of Boston portfolio as coverage needs arise. That's a genuine advantage early in your career: you'll build fluency in how multiple properties handle traffic, concessions, and make-ready timelines, rather than seeing just one playbook.

What You Bring

  • A high school diploma or equivalent experience
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with computers and digital marketing tools
  • Solid organizational habits and time management you can demonstrate, not just describe
  • The kind of energy that makes a leasing office feel like a place people want to do business

Where This Role Leads

Leasing consultant experience, especially in a float capacity, is one of the cleaner on-ramps into property management. You build sales instincts, lease administration knowledge, and resident communication skills simultaneously. From here, the natural next step is a Senior Leasing Consultant or Leasing Manager title, and from there, Assistant Property Manager roles become accessible. Companies like JMC, with a portfolio spanning multiple properties, tend to promote from within when they can, and floaters who've worked across several assets often move up faster because they're already known quantities in more than one building.

JMC has operated since 1951 and is considered one of the more established multifamily names in New England. The Monday through Friday schedule (9 to 5 or 10 to 6) is a real differentiator in leasing, where weekend hours are common. Compensation runs $24 to $27.50 per hour, with a $2,500 sign-on bonus, plus medical, dental, vision, life insurance, paid time off, holidays, and a 401k with company match.

job.title: Asset Management
job.description:
This role lives at the intersection of field maintenance and operational coordination. If you're someone who reads a Smartsheet work order list the same way others read a morning newspaper, and you can walk a unit, punch a list, verify deadbolt codes, swap HVAC filters, and document everything in OneDrive before lunch, this position was written for you.

What This Role Actually Requires

Hillpointe operates as a fully integrated developer and investment manager building market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt. They control everything in-house: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management. That vertical integration matters here because this role sits inside that chain directly. You're not a third-party vendor. You're part of the machine that opens and maintains Hillpointe's own assets.

The day-to-day work is field-heavy. You'll be moving between properties across North Carolina, Tennessee, Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, and Colorado, which means roughly 75% travel. On any given day, that might look like pulling the Smartsheet work order queue in the morning, driving to a property, completing make-ready repairs, verifying hide-a-key placements and electronic deadbolt codes, checking HVAC filters, photographing and uploading unit status documentation, and reporting anything beyond your scope to the Asset Management Lead before end of shift. Rinse, repeat, across multiple sites.

Administrative accuracy matters as much as the physical work. Photos get uploaded to the correct OneDrive folders. Reports go out in the correct format. Checklists get completed on time. If that sounds like a lot of documentation for a field role, it is. Hillpointe's in-house model depends on tight feedback loops between field staff and the support team.

Skills This Role Draws On Most

  • Hands-on maintenance ability: basic repairs, HVAC filter changes, unit inspections, and punch list completion
  • Self-management on the road: stocking a work vehicle, managing your own schedule across sites, hitting timelines without someone standing over you
  • Documentation discipline: photos, work order updates, unit status reports, all in the correct format and folder structure
  • Communication upward: knowing when something is beyond your scope and escalating it clearly to the Asset Management Lead or CLS Director
  • Physical stamina: this role involves significant standing, walking, lifting, and driving. The 150 lb lift requirement is real.

What Makes Someone Good at This

The candidates who struggle here are the ones who treat documentation as an afterthought. The field work is straightforward for anyone with maintenance experience. What separates strong performers is the combination: completing the physical work and closing the loop on every unit in the system before moving to the next stop. Hillpointe's model depends on accurate unit-level data flowing back to the support team, so a missed photo or an unreported warranty item creates downstream problems at the asset level.

A high school diploma or equivalent is preferred, and prior maintenance experience is a plus rather than a requirement. Basic Microsoft Office proficiency and comfort with digital platforms like Smartsheets and OneDrive matter more than a specific credential here. If you've done maintenance coordination in a lease-up context or worked across multiple scattered-site properties before, that experience translates directly.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front line of Waypoint Management Services' leasing operation in Jacksonville. Your day runs from first contact to signed lease: answering inbound inquiries, booking and conducting tours, walking prospects through floorplans and amenities, and then doing the follow-up work that actually converts traffic into new residents. You'll handle applicant qualification, prepare lease files for manager review, calculate prorations, and manage move-in paperwork. When occupancy softens, you'll work the waitlist and renewals alongside new leases to keep the community's numbers moving in the right direction.

Beyond the one-on-one work with prospects, you're responsible for keeping the leasing office and model units tour-ready, maintaining accurate records in the property's leasing system (Yardi experience is a plus here), and supporting outreach and networking efforts to generate referral traffic. Weekend availability is part of the rotation, which is standard for any leasing role worth taking seriously.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in leasing, sales, or hospitality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to handle objections without losing the relationship
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations
  • Comfort with leasing software and CRM tools; Yardi familiarity is a genuine advantage
  • Bilingual English/Spanish ability is preferred and will stand out in Jacksonville's growing market
  • A valid driver's license and a high school diploma or equivalent

Waypoint offers a monthly leasing and renewal bonus structure, a leaser-of-the-month monetary award, an employee housing discount, 120 hours of PTO in year one (with progressive increases), two floating days, medical/dental/vision coverage starting day one, a 401k with company match, commuter benefits, and an employee referral program.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Jacksonville's multifamily market has seen significant inventory growth over the past few years, which means prospects have real options and leasing consultants who can articulate genuine community value, not just quote square footage and price, close at a noticeably higher rate. The consultants who thrive in this kind of environment treat follow-up as a system, not an afterthought. They track every prospect interaction, know their competition's concessions and availability, and can speak to why their community fits a prospect's specific situation. If you've worked a lease-up or managed a high-traffic leasing office before, that experience translates directly here. If your background is hospitality or retail sales, the service instincts carry over well as long as you're ready to learn the leasing process in detail.

For someone early in a property management career, this role builds the core skills that lead toward Assistant Manager and then Community Manager positions. The financial side of leasing, understanding prorations, qualifying applicants, and working toward NOI targets, is the foundation for everything that comes next on that track.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
A resident submits an emergency work order at 11 PM: the AC is out and it's July in Palm Bay. You're the one who coordinates the response, confirms the technician is on-site, and follows up to make sure the unit is cooling before the night ends. That's the job, in one moment.

The Role

Waypoint Management Services is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for a high-end luxury community in Palm Bay, FL. This is a hands-on leadership position responsible for all maintenance operations across the property, from managing the day-to-day work order queue to overseeing make-readies, preventive maintenance, and vendor coordination. You'll carry budget responsibility for the maintenance department and be expected to operate with an ownership mindset, identifying inefficiencies before they become problems.

Day-to-day, the scope covers a lot of ground. You'll perform and supervise plumbing repairs, HVAC preventive maintenance, carpentry, grounds upkeep, and general equipment servicing. Make-ready condition reviews with contractors are a regular rhythm. Pool chemical readings, trash compactor maintenance, and security gate functionality all fall within your oversight. Work orders carry a 24-hour completion standard, and service emergencies require immediate coordinated response. You'll work closely with the Community Manager and are expected to communicate proactively, not reactively.

Palm Bay sits in a market where the summer heat puts real pressure on HVAC systems and pool equipment. Residents in luxury communities expect fast, professional service, and deferred maintenance in this climate compounds quickly. The Maintenance Supervisor here isn't just fixing things; they're protecting asset quality and resident retention at the same time.

What You'll Need

  • EPA Section 608 certification, Types I and II (required at hire)
  • CPO certification, or the ability to complete it within 90 days of your start date
  • CAMT certification (preferred)
  • At least two years of general maintenance experience, with prior supervisory responsibility over employees and contractors
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and safe maintenance practices
  • High school diploma or GED
  • Bilingual in Spanish and English (strongly preferred given the local resident base)
  • Availability for on-call rotation

Strong candidates in this role tend to distinguish themselves through vendor management skills. Anyone can fix a leaky faucet. What separates a good Maintenance Supervisor from a great one is the ability to hold contractors accountable to make-ready timelines, document punch list items clearly, and keep the Community Manager informed without being asked. If you've run a make-ready process that consistently hit turn deadlines, that experience will matter here.

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one, a 401(k) with matching, an employee referral program, recognition and incentive opportunities, and an onsite housing discount for qualified employees.

job.title: Full-Time Exterior Porter (Wed-Sun, 3PM-10PM)
job.description:
Exterior porter roles at mixed-use and transit-oriented properties carry more responsibility than the title suggests. When the asset is high-visibility and the operator is managing a branded parking and property experience like ParkX, the person maintaining those common areas is often the first impression a resident, tenant, or visitor gets. Comstock's Reston portfolio fits that description, and this Wednesday through Sunday, 3PM to 10PM shift covers the hours when that impression matters most.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this role is maintaining exterior and interior common areas across assigned sites. That means pressure washing, trash removal, window cleaning, restroom upkeep, and keeping lobbies and public spaces presentable through the evening. You'll work from cleaning schedules and checklists, track supply inventory, handle end-of-shift documentation, and flag any maintenance issues or safety hazards to management. When events or public gatherings happen on property, you'll assist with setup and breakdown. The shift runs into the evening, so expect some variability around event schedules and peak periods.

A good portion of the role is also about communication. You're interacting with property staff, tenants, and visitors throughout your shift, and how you handle those moments reflects directly on the property experience Comstock and ParkX are trying to deliver. Professionalism and a calm, courteous presence matter here as much as the physical work.

What Qualifications You'll Need

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and sustain physical activity across a full shift (standing, bending, climbing stairs, working in variable weather conditions)
  • Flexibility for weekend work and occasional after-hours coverage during events
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to self-direct without constant supervision
  • Comfort working with cleaning chemicals and equipment, following safety protocols

Where This Role Can Lead

Porter and groundskeeping roles are an underestimated entry point into property operations. The skills you build here, specifically physical site standards, equipment maintenance, safety compliance, and shift handoff documentation, transfer directly into maintenance technician tracks. People who treat this role as a craft rather than just a job tend to move into lead porter positions, facilities coordinator roles, or maintenance apprenticeships within a few years. Comstock's note about advancement within their expanding portfolio and annual professional development funds signals that they're thinking about retention, not just filling a shift. If you're early in a property management career and want to understand how a well-run asset actually functions from the ground level up, this is a legitimate starting point.

job.title: Full-Time Overnight Cleaner (Sat-Wed, 11PM-6AM)
job.description:
Overnight porter work isn't for everyone. The shift runs 11PM to 6AM, Saturday through Wednesday, and the job is exactly what it sounds like: keeping common areas clean, presentable, and safe while most people are asleep. If that schedule suits your life, this role with Comstock's ParkX team in Reston, VA is worth a serious look.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your shift covers the common areas: lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces. You'll run through daily cleaning checklists, handle trash removal, pressure wash assigned areas, and keep janitorial closets organized and hazard-free. When events happen on-site, you'll help with setup and breakdown, which can shift the pace of your night considerably. You're also the eyes on the property during off-hours. If you spot a maintenance issue, a safety hazard, or something that needs management's attention, you document it and pass it along. End-of-shift handoff paperwork is part of the job, not an afterthought.

You'll work with cleaning chemicals regularly, so understanding safe handling and proper storage matters. Equipment care is part of the role too. You're expected to flag damage early rather than push a failing machine through another shift.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with a clean record
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods
  • Comfort working outdoors in variable weather conditions
  • Reliability. Overnight shifts depend on people showing up.
  • A professional, courteous manner with staff, tenants, and visitors at any hour
  • Ability to work independently without close supervision

A Realistic Look at the Role

The overnight schedule is the biggest factor here. It's a fixed shift, not rotating, so if you're someone who functions well at night, that consistency is actually an asset. The physical demands are real: stairs, crouching, repetitive motion, outdoor exposure. Some nights are routine. Others involve event cleanup or stepping in for an absent coworker, which means flexibility isn't optional.

What separates a strong porter from an average one in a property like this isn't just cleaning ability. It's noticing things. A lobby that's technically clean but has a burned-out light, a spill forming near a drain, or a supply closet running low on a key chemical. Those details affect how residents and visitors experience the property, and the overnight shift is often the only chance to catch and correct them before the next day begins. Comstock offers medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, and annual professional development funds, along with free parking and EV charging on-site.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Nantucket Cove)
job.description:
Leasing is a sales job with a customer service wrapper, and it helps to know that going in. At Nantucket Cove in Champaign, BAM Companies is hiring a Leasing Consultant who will be the first person prospective residents talk to, tour with, and ultimately trust enough to sign a lease. That's a real responsibility, and it's also a real opportunity if you're the kind of person who genuinely enjoys helping people make decisions.

The day-to-day is a mix of traffic management, follow-up, and relationship-building. You'll greet walk-ins, take prospects on tours, explain pricing and unit features, and then do the less glamorous but equally important work: returning calls promptly, following up on leads that went quiet, keeping the leasing office and show units presentation-ready, and entering data accurately into the CRM. Some days the office is busy and you're juggling three conversations at once. Other days you're doing outreach, helping with community events, or catching up on paperwork. The rhythm shifts week to week.

Weekend availability is required. That's worth saying plainly because it matters. Prospects shop for apartments on Saturdays. If that schedule doesn't work for you, this role probably isn't the right fit. If it does, you'll find that the commission structure adds up meaningfully over time. Every signed lease puts additional money in your pocket on top of the hourly base, which falls between $16.50 and $18.50 depending on experience.

What separates a strong leasing consultant from an average one usually isn't charm. It's follow-through. Plenty of people can give a good tour. Fewer consistently follow up with every lead, track where prospects are in the decision process, and close without being pushy. If you've done that kind of work in retail, hospitality, or any sales-adjacent role, the leasing side of it will come naturally.

BAM offers a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and pet insurance, along with PTO that starts building after 90 days and a notable number of paid holidays from day one. Housing discounts at BAM properties are also part of the package.

What you'll bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent; some college is a plus
  • Background in leasing, retail, hospitality, or sales
  • Strong communication skills and a reliable follow-up habit
  • Comfort with basic tech and CRM tools
  • A valid driver's license and reliable vehicle
  • Availability to work weekends
  • NALP credentials or bilingual skills are a bonus, not a requirement

For someone who wants a foothold in property management or real estate, a leasing consultant role is one of the most direct paths in. You learn the product, the prospect pipeline, and the resident experience from the ground up. Many property managers started exactly here.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Commercial property management in the Greater Los Angeles market sits at the intersection of tenant relations, financial oversight, and physical asset stewardship. This role at Property Management Associates puts you squarely in the middle of all three, managing a mixed portfolio of office buildings and retail space across the LA area for a firm that's been operating in Southern California for over 30 years.

What You'll Actually Do

Day to day, you're the operational anchor for a set of commercial assets. That means conducting regular property and tenant space inspections, staying on top of lease compliance, and making sure the physical condition of each building reflects ownership's standards. When something needs attention, you're sourcing bids, issuing service orders, and coordinating contractors through to completion. Tenant requests don't sit in a queue here. You respond, generate work orders, and follow up until the issue is closed.

On the financial side, you own the annual income and expense budget, handle accounts receivable, produce monthly variance reports, and reforecast quarterly. You'll also verify invoices against approved service orders and contracts, and field questions from corporate accounting when issues surface. Yardi Voyager is your primary tool, so comfort with that platform matters. The reporting cadence here is real and regular, not occasional.

Beyond operations and finance, there's a relationship-management dimension to this role that's easy to underestimate. You'll work across internal departments including leasing, tenant improvement, development, and construction, and you'll interface with city officials and community stakeholders. Strong written and verbal communication isn't a soft requirement here. It's core to the job.

What You Bring

  • At least five years of commercial property management experience, with direct experience in the Property Manager seat
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage annual budgets, explain variances, and reforecast with accuracy
  • Experience managing office and/or retail tenants through the full lifecycle of lease compliance and service resolution
  • Intermediate to strong proficiency in Yardi Voyager and the MS Office Suite, particularly Excel
  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience
  • Organizational discipline and the ability to manage multiple properties and competing priorities without dropping threads

Where This Role Leads

Commercial PM experience compounds differently than residential. The budget ownership, vendor contract management, and cross-departmental coordination you build here translate directly into Senior Property Manager or Portfolio Manager roles, and eventually into asset management or director-level positions. The financial literacy this job demands, specifically variance reporting, reforecasting, and invoice verification against contracts, is exactly what separates mid-level PM candidates from those who move into more strategic roles. At a firm like PMA that manages both commercial and residential assets at scale, there's also lateral mobility if your interests shift. One honest note: commercial portfolios in LA come with real complexity, from tenant improvement coordination to city compliance touchpoints. Candidates who thrive here tend to be self-directed and comfortable holding ambiguity without waiting for someone to hand them a checklist.

job.title: Property Manager - Up to 299 Units - 171
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you in charge of a property in Redmond, Washington, capped at 299 units, which means you're close enough to the day-to-day to know your residents and staff by name while still carrying real financial accountability. Mornings might mean sitting with your regional manager to review monthly actuals, flag delinquency trends, or sharpen a quarterly forecast. Afternoons can look entirely different. Team development, resident communications, a leasing push, a walk of the property. The variety is real, and so is the expectation that you keep both the people side and the numbers side moving in the same direction.

You'll own the full budget cycle: annual budgets, capex planning, monthly and quarterly forecasts, and the staffing and marketing plans that sit underneath all of it. Berkshire manages and owns its own assets, so you're not operating under third-party fee management constraints. The decisions you make about occupancy strategy, concessions, and operational spend connect directly to NOI, and you'll be expected to understand that connection clearly, not just report on it.

On the team side, you'll hire, train, and develop your on-site staff, which at a sub-300-unit property typically means a leasing team, maintenance, and possibly an assistant manager. Building people up is as much a part of this job as reading a T-12.

What You Bring

  • At least five years of multifamily experience, with demonstrated time in a leadership role
  • Comfort reading and explaining financial statements, budgets, and variance reports
  • Proficiency with property management software for both operational and financial analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for resident-facing work and internal reporting
