  • A track record of building and motivating on-site teams
  • The ability to work effectively with residents and staff from a wide range of backgrounds

Context Worth Knowing

Redmond sits in one of the tighter multifamily submarkets in the greater Seattle area. Proximity to major tech employers keeps renter demand relatively stable, but it also means residents have high expectations and plenty of options. Strong operators here tend to win on service consistency and community feel, not just price. If you've managed in the Eastside market before, you already know how much resident experience matters to retention in this corridor.

The salary range for this Washington-based position runs from $84,500 to $90,000, with actual compensation depending on experience. The role includes health care benefits, retirement benefits, paid time off across multiple categories, and performance bonuses. Berkshire also offers a 25% rent discount for salaried employees and an unlimited vacation policy with manager approval.

Candidates who stand out for this type of role tend to be the ones who connect financial outcomes to operational decisions without being prompted. Knowing your T-3 trends, anticipating a soft month before it shows up in the report, and coaching your leasing team accordingly: that's the difference between a competent manager and one who actually moves the needle on NOI.

job.title: Assistant General Manager
job.description:
Skills That Define This Role

The Assistant General Manager position at Bozzuto's Atlanta community draws on three skill sets simultaneously: sales instincts, financial discipline, and people leadership. You'll be conducting tours that convert traffic into signed leases, managing delinquency and posting rental receipts with precision, and stepping into a GM-level leadership posture whenever the General Manager is off-site. Those three things rarely sit in the same job description at a junior level, which is what makes this role genuinely developmental for someone who wants to run a property within the next few years.

Atlanta's multifamily market around the 30308 zip code (Midtown and Old Fourth Ward) is competitive, with strong lease-up activity from newer Class A product putting pressure on retention across the board. That context matters here. Resident retention isn't a soft metric at a property like this. Every conversation at the front desk, every maintenance follow-up call, every community event is a retention touchpoint. Bozzuto emphasizes that connection explicitly, and the AGM is the person most responsible for making it feel genuine rather than scripted.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day to day, this role blends leasing floor work with back-office accountability. On the leasing side, you're conducting personalized tours, building rapport with prospects, and working weekends (roughly one to two per month, with compensating days off mid-week) when foot traffic is at its peak. On the operations side, you're tracking delinquency, managing rent collections, and keeping a close eye on the community's physical presentation, both interior and exterior.

When the GM is out, the job shifts. You're the decision-maker, the coach, and the escalation point. That means handling resident issues with real ownership rather than deferring upward. Bozzuto looks for people who treat that responsibility as an opportunity, not a burden.

Social media fluency matters here too. Creating and posting content on platforms like Instagram and Facebook is part of the role, not an afterthought. If you understand how to build community identity online and connect it to what's actually happening at the property, that's a genuine differentiator.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • At least two years working in a customer-facing environment with exposure to rent collection, budgets, or accounts receivable
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • An active real estate license, or the ability to obtain one within 90 days of hire (where required)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, and a professional presentation that represents the brand on-site

What separates a strong AGM candidate from an average one at a Bozzuto property is the ability to hold both the leasing and the administrative sides of the job at the same time without letting either slip. A lot of people can sell. Fewer can sell, run collections, mentor a team member through a tough interaction, and still close out the day with clean records in Yardi. The salary range for this position is $62,000 to $65,000, with additional bonus opportunities, along with health coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position sits at the intersection of technical trades work and people leadership, and both sides carry equal weight. You'll spend real time with a wrench in hand, working through HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repairs. But you'll also spend real time coaching and setting the standard for how the maintenance team operates day to day. Neither half of that equation is optional.

The make-ready process is where a lot of your organizational skills will show. Coordinating turns efficiently, walking punch lists with precision, and getting units rent-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy and new resident move-ins. If you've managed apartment turnovers before, you already know that small delays compound fast. Bozzuto places a real premium on that detail-oriented, keep-it-moving mindset.

Preventative maintenance is the other skill set this role demands. Sustaining peak efficiency across building systems, from complex mechanical equipment like boilers and chillers to everyday upkeep, requires someone who thinks ahead rather than just reacts. A "know it like you built it" mentality, as Bozzuto puts it, means you treat the property's systems as your personal responsibility, not just a work order queue.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A typical day might open with a walk of the property before the morning gets busy, checking common areas, grounds, and any open service tickets from the prior evening. From there, the day branches out: resident service requests to assign or handle yourself, vendor coordination, a unit turn to inspect, and some version of a facilities check on mechanical systems. You'll also be the person residents and team members look to when something's urgent and the answer needs to come quickly.

The on-call rotation and weekend availability are real parts of this role. That's worth naming plainly. Emergency situations at a residential property don't follow business hours, and Bozzuto expects the Assistant Maintenance Manager to be reachable and responsive. If that kind of availability is manageable for you, it's also where you build the trust that tends to define your reputation on a property team.

South Florida's climate adds its own layer. Boca Raton's heat and humidity put consistent pressure on HVAC systems, and experience managing that kind of demand matters. Grounds and exterior upkeep also carry more weight in a market where curb appeal directly supports leasing traffic.

What Makes This a Good Fit

Strong candidates for this role bring at least five years in the trades or residential facilities maintenance, along with EPA and/or HVAC certification. Supervisory experience isn't strictly required, but if you've never led a team before, you'll want to come in with a clear sense of how you motivate people and hold standards without micromanaging.

  • 5+ years of trades or residential maintenance experience
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Comfort with complex mechanical systems (central plant, split systems, boilers, chillers)
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and willingness to use tech platforms and maintenance software
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in outdoor conditions

Bozzuto is a company with a defined culture and a recognizable name in residential property management. That means residents tend to have real expectations, and the internal team holds itself to a clear standard. If you're someone who finds that motivating rather than pressuring, this is a place where that energy gets reciprocated. The company offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for those who want to keep building credentials alongside their career.

job.title: COE Career Fair 5/21/2026
job.description:
Cortland is holding an open house career fair at its Center of Excellence in Sandy Springs on May 21, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. If you're looking to get into multifamily operations or move up within it, this is a direct line to hiring managers at one of the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the country.

Three roles are actively being filled. The Leasing Hub Associate sits at the front of the leasing funnel, the point where traffic converts to signed leases. The Resident Services Specialist handles the resident-facing work that keeps retention numbers healthy and renewals on track. The Screening and Applications Specialist works the back end of the leasing process, where application review and decisioning keep move-ins moving. Cortland is hiring both monolingual and bilingual candidates across all three positions, so Spanish fluency is a genuine differentiator if you have it.

What makes this event worth showing up to in person: you can interview on the spot. No waiting for a callback, no second application round. Come with a current resume, be ready to talk through your experience, and you could leave with a next step in hand. Cortland's vertically integrated model means these aren't siloed jobs at a third-party shop. Leasing Hub and Resident Services roles here sit inside an operation that controls its own design, construction, and management functions, which means there's actual room to grow into asset management, training, or regional operations over time.

The leasing and resident services side of multifamily has real performance stakes. Leasing associates own traffic-to-lease conversion. Resident services touches delinquency, MTM exposure, and renewal rates. Screening specialists directly affect move-in velocity and lease quality. These aren't background roles. They show up in the NOI.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • Experience in leasing, customer service, or resident relations (multifamily preferred but not always required)
  • Bilingual Spanish/English fluency for designated bilingual openings
  • Comfort working in a metrics-driven, high-accountability environment
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Ability to work on-site in a full-time, in-person capacity

Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with matching, paid time off, and an employee discount. The career fair location is 5775 Glenridge Drive, Building D, Suite 500, Atlanta, GA 30328. Apply before the event so Cortland can schedule your interview slot in advance.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - The Griff
job.description:
Nashville's rental market doesn't slow down, and neither does the maintenance operation at a well-run apartment community. Olympus Property is hiring a Lead Maintenance Technician at The Griff, and this is a genuine supervisory role, not a senior tech position with a fancier title. You're running the shop.

Day to day, that means scheduling your team's workload across turns, service requests, and preventative maintenance, while also staying hands-on enough to coordinate HVAC repairs, manage contractors, and keep the grounds, pool, and building systems in working order. Make-ready quality directly affects lease-up velocity and resident retention, so the pressure to keep vacant units show-ready and move-in ready is real. You'll work closely with the property's Business Manager and office staff, which means communication matters as much as technical skill. A lead who can't translate maintenance priorities into language the leasing team understands tends to create friction that shows up in delinquency excuses and renewal pushback.

Olympus has pulled three consecutive years on the NAA's Top Employer list, which in our industry is not nothing. The benefits package reflects that. Pay comes in at $35 to $37 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top. They also offer an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and a sabbatical program, which you don't see often at the property level.

What separates the strong candidates here from the average ones isn't just the EPA/HVAC cert or the three years of supervisor experience, though both are required. It's the ability to run an organized shop. Inventory control, scheduled inspections, a clean maintenance room, and consistent documentation in the property management software are the unsexy stuff that keeps a community from bleeding capex dollars on reactive repairs. Leads who treat the shop like a priority tend to have fewer emergency calls, lower vendor costs, and crews that actually stay.

What You'll Need

  • Minimum 3 years in an apartment maintenance supervisor role
  • EPA/HVAC certification
  • Experience coordinating third-party contractors and managing a service team
  • Comfort with property management software for tracking work orders, inventory, and inspections
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, plus on-call rotation

On-call is part of this role. That's the honest acknowledgment every lead maintenance posting should include but often buries. If that's a dealbreaker, this probably isn't the right fit. If you've been doing this long enough that on-call is just Tuesday, then The Griff is worth a closer look.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Groundskeeping at a stabilized apartment community is one of those roles that directly shapes first impressions before a prospect ever walks into the leasing office. At a property like Bexley 3Five in South Austin, the curb appeal you maintain on a Tuesday morning is doing real marketing work. Weinstein Properties has been in this business for over 70 years, still family-owned, and they run a hands-on operation across more than 60 communities in five states. That matters here because you're not an afterthought on the org chart.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a Monday through Friday, 8 to 5 position, which is a better schedule than a lot of grounds roles in this industry. That said, Weinstein is upfront that the work is physical and sometimes unpleasant. Daily trash pickup, pet waste station cleaning, trashing out units between turns, operating backpack blowers and power washers, light painting, weeding, and general upkeep of outdoor spaces. You'll work in Austin heat. That part's not negotiable.

The role also calls for some versatility. On any given day you might be supporting the maintenance team on a punch list item, helping make a unit show-ready, or handling housekeeping tasks in common areas. A golf cart and trailer are part of the toolkit. So is a willingness to do the same recurring tasks without letting the repetition affect your standards.

  • Daily litter and pet waste collection across the community
  • Operation of blowers, power washers, and light hand tools
  • Trash-outs and make-ready support between turns
  • Outdoor maintenance including planting, weeding, and general landscaping upkeep
  • Light painting and interior housekeeping tasks as needed
  • Coordination with maintenance and leasing staff

Who Tends to Succeed Here

The candidates who wash out in grounds roles are usually the ones who underestimate the repetition or overestimate how much variety there is day to day. The ones who stick around and move up are reliable, self-directed, and genuinely notice when something looks off without being told. Attention to detail on a grounds team means catching the overflowing trash before a prospect tour, not after.

Starting pay is $18 per hour with quarterly bonuses on top of that. There's also a stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing, worth $1,000. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, and a rent discount.

Where This Role Can Go

Weinstein explicitly invests in growing people from the ground up, and groundskeeping is a real entry point into maintenance tech work. We've seen plenty of people start on a grounds team and move into HVAC-certified maintenance roles within a few years. If you want to build a career in residential property management maintenance, starting here gives you exposure to the full operation of a community. That's worth something.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - The Rylan
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do at The Rylan

The Rylan Apartments in Vista, CA needs a Maintenance Supervisor who can run a full maintenance operation, not just respond to tickets. Day to day, that means diagnosing issues across all trades, delegating work orders to your team, and following up to make sure completed work actually holds up. You'll manage the service request system, keep preventive maintenance on schedule, and maintain accurate records of expenditures and work performed. Safety meetings fall on you to organize and lead. When vendors or outside contractors come on site, you'll be the one coordinating their work and holding them accountable to quality.

Vista sits in North San Diego County, where the rental market draws a mix of long-term residents and military-adjacent households. Properties here tend to run high occupancy, which means turns need to move efficiently and deferred maintenance can compound quickly in a climate that's mild but still hard on HVAC and exterior surfaces. A Supervisor who understands make-ready timelines and can keep a punch list tight will make a real difference to this community's performance.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor role, ideally at a community of 150 units or more
  • Hands-on competency across all trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and general carpentry
  • Experience managing and scheduling a maintenance team, not just working alongside one
  • A service-first attitude when interacting with residents, without letting that slow down the work
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Comfort with record-keeping and administrative side of maintenance operations

The Role in Context

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They're not a startup figuring out operations on the fly. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that means working within established systems while still having real ownership over how your team performs at the property level. The compensation range is $35 to $37 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses, profit sharing, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, paid holidays, and rental discounts.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones is the ability to manage people, not just fix things. A technician who's great with tools but struggles to delegate, schedule, or hold team members accountable tends to become a bottleneck at this level. If you've built a maintenance team's habits around documentation, follow-through, and preventive care, that experience will translate directly into what MG Properties expects from this seat.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Student housing runs on an academic calendar, and that shapes everything about this role. As Assistant Community Manager at The Flats on University in Fairfax, Virginia, you'll work alongside the General Manager on the full scope of community operations: resident accounts, delinquency control, facilities coordination, staff scheduling, and the resident experience from move-in through move-out. When the General Manager is unavailable, you step into that seat completely. That's not a formality. It requires genuine readiness.

Much of the year follows a rhythm, but the annual turn is where this role earns its complexity. Student housing turns at scale, typically over a compressed window between lease terms. You'll help plan and execute that process using Turnable to track unit progress against deadlines, conduct move-out inspections, assess and document damage charges, manage disputes, and provide hands-on support including moving furniture, completing punch list items alongside the facilities team, and organizing high volumes of resident trash. If you've never worked a student housing turn before, understand that it's a different animal than conventional multifamily. Speed, coordination, and physical effort all matter equally.

Outside of turn season, the role stays active. You'll monitor delinquency and keep it below 2% at month-end, post damage charges from quarterly inspections, help reconcile month-end accounts receivable, and coordinate utility billing. On the customer side, you'll use KPIs to track leasing velocity, concessions, and occupancy trends, manage escalated resident concerns, and respond to Google and Yelp reviews through Entrata. You'll also support staff development by helping recruit, train, and retain team members, and coordinating the on-call schedule including after-hours shifts.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of experience in property management or a residential living community
  • Proficiency in a property management system, with Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft resident-facing notices and legal correspondence accurately
  • Comfort working across platforms: Entrata, ClickUp, Microsoft Office, Qualtrics, Greenhouse, Lattice, and Turnable
  • A detail-oriented, confidentiality-conscious approach to resident accounts and financial records
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Where This Role Fits in Your Career

The skills this position builds are directly transferable to a General Manager role in student housing or conventional multifamily. You'll develop fluency in financial reporting, delinquency management, turn execution, and staff leadership simultaneously. What separates strong candidates from average ones here isn't just organizational skill. It's the ability to shift between strategic thinking (reading KPIs, identifying leasing trends, building action plans) and physical, high-effort work (turn support, inspections, facilities coordination) without losing pace on either. Student housing at this level rewards people who don't treat either mode as beneath them.

Scion offers a benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, paid time off, floating holidays, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. This is an exempt, salaried position based on-site at The Flats on University in Fairfax, with additional hours expected during peak periods and emergencies.

job.title: Associate Asset Manager (Foster City)
job.description:
MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970. Their portfolio spans more than 130 properties and houses roughly 20,000 residents, including working families, seniors, and people with special needs. The Associate Asset Manager, Real Estate Transactions sits inside that operation at the corporate level in Foster City, focused specifically on capital transactions within the stabilized portfolio.

What You'll Actually Do

This role lives at the intersection of finance, project coordination, and compliance. On a given week, you might be tracking a loan modification through internal approvals, pulling together a funding application in response to a NOFA, and monitoring draw schedules on an active rehab. The work isn't glamorous. It's detailed, document-heavy, and requires you to stay organized across multiple projects that each move at their own pace.

Property rehab work means managing budgets and schedules, coordinating scope decisions with internal teams, and tracking warranties and O&M materials after construction wraps. On the financing side, you'll support refinancings and loan modifications from research through close, assist with due diligence on 15-year investor limited partner buyouts, and make sure grant and loan draws go out on time. You'll also monitor RFPs and NOFAs to spot funding opportunities that could support capital needs across the portfolio.

Communication is a bigger part of the job than it might look on paper. You'll coordinate with lenders, investors, internal departments, and residents or staff when a project affects occupied properties. Keeping everyone informed without letting things slip through requires real follow-through.

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Urban Planning, Community Development, or a related field, plus at least two years in affordable housing development or asset management (or an equivalent combination)
  • Solid Excel skills and comfort building or working through financial feasibility analyses
  • Experience preparing narrative reports and strategic documents for internal or external audiences
  • Strong project management habits: you track your own deadlines, flag issues early, and don't need to be reminded twice
  • Valid California driver's license with reliable transportation and current auto insurance
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission around affordable housing and community stability

A Few Things Worth Knowing

This is a hybrid role. You're expected in the Foster City office Tuesdays through Thursdays. The pay range is $85,000 to $95,000 annually, depending on experience, and MidPen's benefits package includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, employee education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, and pet insurance.

What separates strong candidates here is less about credentials and more about working style. Affordable housing transactions involve a lot of moving parts across agencies, investors, lenders, and internal teams, often with tight timelines tied to funding cycles. People who do well in this kind of role tend to be genuinely comfortable in ambiguity, good at tracking details across long project timelines, and willing to do the unglamorous documentation work that keeps transactions from falling apart at the finish line. If you've worked in LIHTC development, affordable housing asset management, or community development finance, that experience will translate directly.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Two skills define whether an Assistant Community Manager thrives or just survives: the ability to read a ledger and the ability to read a room. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, you'll use both on the same day, often within the same hour.

The Operational Core

Hawthorne is a top-50 multifamily operator rooted in the Southeast, and this role sits at the center of day-to-day community performance at Hawthorne at Holly Ridge in Holly Ridge, NC. Financially, the work is real: rent collection, payment posting, delinquency tracking with weekly follow-up calls, ledger audits to catch billing errors before they compound, and eviction coordination when softer efforts don't move the needle. You'll pull reports and flag issues for the Community Manager and regional leadership. That means understanding what you're looking at, not just running the numbers.

On the leasing side, you're working traffic: conducting tours, responding to leads, converting prospects, and supporting renewals. Occupancy is a shared responsibility here, not a metric that belongs only to the Community Manager. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, promoting resident events and keeping the property visible and appealing to prospective residents.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the show. That means maintaining team momentum, prioritizing the punch list for the day, and handling resident concerns with both professionalism and follow-through. The office is open Monday through Friday 9 AM to 6 PM and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 AM, with one weekday off per week to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends come with the territory for resident events.

Skills That Get Used Daily

  • Financial literacy: reading ledgers, identifying discrepancies, understanding delinquency trends
  • Leasing fundamentals: qualifying prospects, managing the pipeline, closing renewals
  • Conflict de-escalation: handling resident disputes calmly and consistently
  • Administrative accuracy: lease documents, applications, and renewals processed correctly and on time
  • Digital communication: social media content creation tied to resident engagement

Two years of property management experience is preferred, and prior time in an assistant manager seat is a plus. A valid driver's license is required. A CALP designation strengthens your candidacy but isn't mandatory.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The candidates who stand out aren't just organized. They're the ones who catch a ledger discrepancy before it becomes a collections problem, who can turn a frustrated resident into a renewal, and who step into the manager's chair on a busy Saturday without needing a script. Financial understanding matters as much as people skills in this seat. Both have to be sharp.

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real mechanism here, not a tagline. Assistant Community Manager to Community Manager is the standard trajectory, backed by active investment from their Learning and Development team. Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Floating Leasing Specialist
job.description:
Lease-up velocity matters more than almost any other metric during a new community launch, and coverage gaps during high-traffic periods cost deals. Hillpointe built this floating role specifically to solve that problem across its Sun Belt workforce housing portfolio.

Hillpointe is a vertically integrated developer and builder focused on market-rate workforce housing. They control everything from land acquisition through construction and asset management, which means properties in their portfolio move fast and expect their on-site teams to match that pace. This role puts you at the center of that activity.

What the Job Actually Involves

You move between communities as needed. That might mean covering a lease-up where traffic is heavy and the team is stretched, filling in during a staff transition, or supporting a new community launch from the front lines. You're the person who walks in, gets up to speed quickly, and keeps the leasing process moving without disruption.

Day to day, you'll greet prospects, conduct tours, and tailor your pitch to what each person actually needs. You follow up by phone, text, and email. You keep tour paths and model units presentation-ready. You answer questions, handle objections, and help prospects move toward a decision.

One practical note: Hillpointe offers free rent at an assigned community as part of this role, subject to their internal policies. That's a real benefit worth factoring in, especially given the travel expectations.

Who Fits This Role

  • Comfortable walking into a new property and being productive immediately
  • Background in leasing, sales, hospitality, or customer-facing service
  • Flexible schedule, including weekends and evenings
  • Willing to travel frequently and potentially relocate temporarily or permanently
  • High school diploma or equivalent; valid driver's license required
  • Physically able to tour indoor and outdoor spaces, walk stairs, and stay on your feet for extended periods

Strong candidates in floating roles tend to share one quality: they read new environments quickly. Every community has a different resident profile, different objection patterns, and a different competitive position in the local market. The leasing consultants who perform best here aren't just personable. They adapt their pitch fast and don't need hand-holding to figure out what a property's strongest selling points are.

From a career standpoint, floating roles tend to accelerate development faster than a single-site position. You build exposure across multiple properties, multiple lease-up scenarios, and different team dynamics. That breadth maps well to a future leasing manager or property manager role, particularly within a portfolio that's actively expanding.

job.title: MSG Centralized Agent
job.description:
It's 8 a.m. and you've got three properties in your POD with make-readies stacking up, a vendor who hasn't confirmed the flooring schedule, and the call center queue already showing missed contacts from overnight. That's a typical Tuesday in centralized operations.

The Role

Hillpointe is a vertically integrated developer and investment firm building market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt. They control the full stack: land acquisition, construction, procurement, asset management. Their centralization model means a remote agent can support multiple properties simultaneously, and this position sits at the center of that coordination layer.

As an MSG Centralized Agent, you'll support day-to-day operations across a designated POD of Hillpointe properties or a set of traditional centralized sites. The work splits between general administrative coordination and field-side scheduling. On the admin side, that means fielding resident calls through the call center, routing them correctly to the right regional contacts, monitoring availability reports for accuracy, and flagging discrepancies with onsite staff. Warranty items get reported through established internal channels. You'll keep close communication with the Director of Centralization, the MFM, and centralized field agents to make sure nothing falls through the cracks on quality or timing.

The field coordination piece is equally active. You'll work with the MFM to build schedules around make-readies and work orders based on property need, confirm move-in and move-out accuracy with the CM, and schedule vendors for turns: paint, cleaning, flooring. Attendance at POD and centralized director meetings keeps you current on shifting priorities across your assigned properties.

What They're Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred
  • Prior onsite maintenance experience is a genuine plus, not just a formality
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office suite, Word and Excel in particular
  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through, especially on scheduling
  • Ability to work independently and manage your own time across multiple properties simultaneously
  • Flexibility with hours and the ability to shift priorities when the schedule changes
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and drive longer distances if the role requires it

The physical requirements listed reflect the reality that centralization doesn't mean purely desk work. Exposure to cleaning chemicals is part of the environment on the field side, and PPE is provided.

Where strong candidates separate themselves in a role like this: it's not the scheduling software or the vendor calls. It's the ability to hold multiple properties' turn timelines in your head at once, notice when the availability report doesn't match what the onsite team is reporting, and escalate quickly without waiting to be asked. Centralized operations only work when the agent in the middle is proactive. Reactive gets expensive fast.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
It's 8:05 AM and you're already moving. First stop is a parking lot in Tonawanda where last night's wind scattered trash across the lot. You clear it, check the dog waste station, then drive to Hamburg before lunch. That's the rhythm of this role.

What the Work Looks Like

Birgo manages apartment communities across Buffalo, Tonawanda, North Tonawanda, and Hamburg. This groundskeeper position covers those sites, so you'll drive between properties throughout the day rather than staying in one place. Mileage is reimbursed.

Day-to-day, you're keeping the exterior and common areas in shape: parking lots, trash areas, dog waste stations, and landscaped grounds. That means grass cutting, weeding, mulching, and pruning when the season calls for it. When winter hits Buffalo, snow removal and salting walkways becomes a regular part of the schedule. Inside, you'll clean hallways, stairwells, offices, and shared amenity spaces. You'll also assist with basic maintenance and repairs as needs come up.

Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. This is a full-time, year-round position at $20/hour. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with employer contribution, paid time off, paid holidays, 401(k) match, professional development reimbursement, and discounted rent at Birgo properties.

What You Need

  • Authorization to work in the United States
  • Valid driver's license and reliable personal transportation with insurance
  • Ability to lift and carry 50 pounds without assistance
  • Comfort using power tools safely
  • Physical ability to work in confined spaces, climb ladders and stairs, and move across uneven terrain

Birgo describes the ideal candidate as servant-hearted. That's not filler. Curb appeal at a residential property directly shapes how residents feel about where they live, and the groundskeeper is often the most visible person on site. The people who do this job well take pride in the details that most residents only notice when something's wrong. If you're the type who fixes something without being asked, that matters here.

Buffalo winters are real. Snow removal isn't a footnote; it's a core part of the job from November through March. Candidates who've worked outdoor maintenance in Western New York already know what that means.

job.title: $1,500 Sign-On Bonus Multisite Maintenance Supervisor (The Bristol and Aberdeen)
job.description:
Leading Maintenance Across Two Communities

A multisite Maintenance Supervisor role asks more of you than a single-property position. You're splitting your time between two communities, The Bristol and Aberdeen in Camby, IN, coordinating two teams, and keeping both properties running well enough that residents barely notice the work happening behind the scenes. BAM Companies has been doing third-party and in-house property management since 2010, and this role sits at the operational center of two of their Indiana communities.

The compensation package here includes a $1,500 sign-on bonus and a rent discount if you want to live on-site at a BAM property. Pay lands between $25 and $30 per hour depending on your experience and background.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're overseeing HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general upkeep across both properties. That means building a preventative maintenance schedule that actually gets followed, not just written down. You'll train and coach your maintenance staff, which means you're responsible for the quality of their work, not just your own. When a make-ready is behind or a punch list keeps growing, that lands on you to diagnose whether it's a staffing issue, a process issue, or both.

Budget awareness matters here too. You'll manage supply purchasing and help keep operations cost-efficient, so some comfort with tracking spend and making smart procurement calls is genuinely useful, not just a box on the job description.

  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification (required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable vehicle (you're moving between two sites regularly)
  • 2 to 3 years of property maintenance experience, with supervisory experience preferred
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, for coordinating with staff, vendors, and residents

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The candidates who thrive in multisite supervisor roles aren't just technically sharp. They're organized communicators who can prioritize quickly when two properties have competing urgent needs. If you've ever had to decide which property gets your attention on a day when both feel like emergencies, you already understand the core challenge of this job. Strong candidates also tend to be honest coaches. Maintenance teams respond to supervisors who'll get their hands dirty alongside them, not just assign work from a distance.

BAM describes their culture as team-oriented and growth-focused, and they back that up with paid holidays, PTO, and benefits including medical, dental, and vision. If you're looking to move toward a Regional Maintenance Director or Director of Facilities role down the road, building multisite supervisory experience at a company that invests in development is a reasonable way to get there.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 178
job.description:
Maintenance Technicians at vertically integrated ownership groups like Berkshire Residential carry a broader scope than those working for third-party fee management shops. Because Berkshire owns what it manages, there's real investment in the physical condition of each asset, and the maintenance team plays a direct role in protecting that value long-term.

What the Role Covers Day to Day

At Red Hawk Ranch, you'll be the person keeping the community running. That means handling service requests across the standard trades: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You'll also support make-ready turns between residents, which requires moving efficiently through a punch list while keeping quality consistent. Curb appeal is taken seriously here, so expect to contribute to the overall condition of the property, not just the items on your work order queue.

You'll work alongside management to enforce safety standards, maintain shop organization, manage inventory, and keep key security protocols in place. Resident interaction is part of the job, and how you handle those moments matters. A technician who communicates clearly and follows through builds the kind of trust that reduces friction across the entire community.

What Berkshire Is Looking For

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfort with computers and related maintenance or work order applications
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills in English
  • A detail-oriented approach to both technical work and resident-facing service

The posted salary range for this Colorado position runs from $24.00 to $28.00 per hour, with the actual offer depending on experience and other lawful factors. This position also includes a $2,000 sign-on bonus. Benefits include health care coverage, retirement benefits, paid sick leave, parental leave, vacation, and PTO. Berkshire also offers a 25% rent discount for employees living on-site or at a Berkshire community.

Where This Role Can Take You

Strong maintenance technicians at ownership groups like this tend to develop into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as they accumulate experience across multiple systems and learn to manage a shop independently. The exposure you get working directly under a property management team, rather than through a contracted vendor, gives you broader visibility into how physical asset performance connects to occupancy and NOI. Technicians who understand that connection and can communicate it to management tend to move up faster than those who treat the role as purely reactive repair work.

Berkshire describes its culture as entrepreneurial and performance-oriented, and the team structure reflects that. If you work well with autonomy, take ownership of your area, and genuinely care about the condition of the property you're responsible for, this is the kind of environment where that gets recognized.

job.title: Evening Concierge
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is the Monday through Friday, 3PM to 11PM shift, which means you're covering the hours when the building truly comes alive. Residents are returning from work, packages are stacking up at the front desk, guests are arriving, and the common spaces are in active use. You're the consistent face during all of it. You handle front desk operations, manage package room organization, coordinate club room and freight elevator reservations, and field whatever residents need as the evening unfolds. You also plan and execute resident events that build genuine community, not just a sign-in sheet and some appetizers.

Bozzuto puts real weight on the concierge role as a driver of resident satisfaction and retention. That means you're expected to know residents by name, learn their preferences, and personalize every interaction. You'll also help generate positive online visibility by encouraging happy residents to share their experiences on social platforms, and you'll contribute to the community's social media presence yourself.

What You Bring

  • At least two years working in hospitality, retail, hotel, or a similar customer-facing environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to handle sensitive situations with composure
  • Comfort with software, apps, and property management tools used at the front desk
  • A sharp, professional presentation that reflects the quality of the community
  • Physical ability to lift up to 25 pounds, which becomes relevant quickly during peak delivery seasons
  • Genuine attentiveness to detail, especially in keeping logs, reservations, and front desk records accurate

Context Worth Knowing

Falls Church sits in one of the more competitive Class A rental submarkets in Northern Virginia. Properties in this corridor compete hard on resident experience, and concierge quality is a real differentiator. Bozzuto manages a significant share of upscale multifamily in the DC metro region, and their communities tend to attract residents with high service expectations. The evening shift in particular requires someone who can handle the pace of post-5PM traffic without losing the warmth and attentiveness that defines the role.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones isn't just friendliness. It's anticipation. The best concierges in this type of environment notice what a resident needs before being asked, remember small details from previous conversations, and treat every interaction as an opportunity to reinforce why someone chose to live there. That instinct, more than any specific credential, is what Bozzuto is hiring for in this role.

The salary range for this position is $48,000 to $51,500, with eligibility for additional bonus opportunities. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Bozzuto operates a portfolio that spans design, construction, and third-party management, and the maintenance technician role sits right at the intersection of resident satisfaction and asset preservation. At a Bozzuto-managed property in Fairfax, that means your work shows up directly in renewal rates, online ratings, and ultimately NOI. A slow turn or a recurring HVAC ticket left unresolved doesn't just frustrate a resident. It costs the property.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of building maintenance: service ticket resolution across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair; make-ready work to get vacant units back on the market; and general upkeep that keeps the community presentable and safe. Snow removal and grounds work come with the territory. So does an on-call rotation, which means some evenings and weekends are part of the deal. That's the honest reality of maintenance work at any residential property, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Bozzuto is looking for someone with beginner to intermediate skills across the core trades. You don't need to be an expert in every system, but you should be comfortable diagnosing a problem and knowing when to escalate. Strong candidates in this role tend to close tickets fast and clean, communicate clearly with residents during the process, and show up to on-call situations without needing to be tracked down. The technicians who advance here treat a punch list like a scorecard.

One concrete perk worth noting: after your first 12 months, Bozzuto covers the cost of your EPA 608 Universal Refrigerant Certification. For anyone building a career in HVAC and property maintenance, that certification opens doors. It's a real investment, not a line item buried in the benefits summary.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience or formal trade education in building maintenance
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance systems
  • Reliable personal transportation for commuting and on-call response
  • Physical ability to handle frequent lifting in the 25 to 50 pound range
  • Comfort with software and property management apps used for work orders
  • Clear communication skills and a professional presentation
  • Availability for on-call emergency coverage as part of a rotation

The salary range for this position runs from $50,000 to approximately $53,000 annually, with bonus eligibility on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement for ongoing education.

job.title: Centralized Painter - Colorado Springs, CO
job.description:
It's 8 a.m. and you're already loading your van with paint, primer, and patching compound before heading to the first property on your route. By noon, you've finished a full unit repaint and you're halfway through a touch-up on a second. This is centralized painter work: less standing around waiting for direction, more moving efficiently through a portfolio of properties with clear daily output expectations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cortland is hiring a centralized painter to support unit turns and ongoing upkeep across their Colorado Springs portfolio. The role is travel-based by design. You'll drive between assigned properties rather than staying planted at one community, which suits painters who like variety and work well without someone looking over their shoulder all day.

Day-to-day, the workload typically runs to one full unit repaint or two touch-ups per shift, depending on what the turn schedule demands. Beyond paint application itself, the role includes drywall repairs: patching, sanding, and texture matching. Exterior work comes up too, so you'll need comfort with ladders, lifts, and scaffolding and a working knowledge of elevated-work safety procedures and OSHA requirements.

Spray equipment is a real part of this job, not an occasional add-on. You'll be expected to mix and match coatings, maintain your sprayer, and follow proper maintenance protocols. The paint shop at each location needs to stay clean, stocked, and organized. That's on you too.

You'll log completed work, materials used, and any follow-up items in a CMMS platform. If you haven't used maintenance management software before, there's room to learn, but you should be comfortable picking up new tools quickly.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least two years of interior residential painting experience; custom home background is a plus
  • Solid brush, roller, and spray application skills with strong spray-prep technique
  • Ability to perform small drywall repairs and match texture (larger repairs are a bonus)
  • Valid driver's license, required vehicle insurance, and comfort with regular travel between sites
  • Familiarity with OSHA regulations and MSDS requirements
  • Ability to work at heights and on weekends when the turn schedule calls for it
  • Clear written and verbal communication in English

The pay range for this role is $24 to $26 per hour.

One honest note about this kind of role: the daily output expectations are real. One full repaint per day is a solid pace, and staying on schedule matters because maintenance teams and leasing staff are counting on clean, ready units. Painters who thrive here tend to be the ones who take personal ownership of their work quality and don't need a supervisor to tell them when something isn't finished right. If you've built a reputation for consistent, clean work in residential settings, this kind of centralized structure tends to reward that.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician, Part Time - Cortland Luxe Shadow Creek
job.description:
It's 8 p.m. on a Tuesday, and residents along your assigned route have set their bags outside. You move efficiently from door to door, hamper in tow, keeping the hallways clear and the property looking exactly the way a Cortland community is supposed to look.

This part-time Front Door Waste Technician role at Cortland Luxe Shadow Creek in Houston supports the daily valet trash program for a multifamily apartment community. It's physical, outdoor, route-based work that runs on a consistent schedule. You'll collect resident waste bags, transport them to onsite compactors or containers, and keep common areas clean throughout the property, including pool areas, dog waste stations, mail kiosks, parking lots, and stairwells.

What the Work Actually Involves

Beyond the route itself, you'll monitor for improperly disposed or prohibited waste and take appropriate action when you find it. Spills around doorsteps, sidewalks, and compactor areas get cleaned up as part of your standard responsibilities. You'll operate compactors safely when needed and keep the surrounding areas clear of debris and obstructions.

Every shift, you'll log start and end times and complete required reporting through a mobile app, including photos. This documentation matters. It creates accountability and helps the onsite team stay informed. You'll interact with residents, staff, and management along the way, so your manner in those moments reflects directly on the community's reputation. Cortland communities are positioned as premium living environments, and the cleanliness of common areas is part of what residents are paying for.

What You Bring

  • A high school diploma or equivalent (preferred)
  • At least one year in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations related to waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs
  • Comfort working outdoors in Houston's heat, humidity, and occasional rain
  • A valid Class E driver's license for local driving as needed
  • A personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with data and active email for shift documentation

One thing that separates reliable candidates in this role: consistency. Routes don't get done halfway. Residents notice immediately when a bag gets missed or an area looks neglected. The people who thrive here take the work seriously even when no one is watching, show up on time, and communicate clearly if something is off on the property. That dependability is genuinely valued on a multifamily operations team.

Cortland is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. The company participates in E-Verify and maintains a drug-free workplace policy.

job.title: Compliance Specialist
job.description:
Affordable Housing compliance work sits at the intersection of regulatory precision and resident impact. Every file you review carries real consequences: a missed eligibility issue can jeopardize a property's tax credit status, while an unnecessary denial can block a household from housing they qualify for. This role at Asset Living demands both kinds of accuracy.

The Skills This Role Draws On Immediately

You'll use file review and regulatory interpretation from day one. The core of the position is evaluating Affordable Housing resident applications against current LIHTC requirements, confirming eligibility, and completing that review within a 24-hour window. That turnaround standard requires you to work with speed and accuracy simultaneously, not sequentially. Proficiency with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit is specifically relevant here, so familiarity with that platform shortens your ramp time considerably.

Strong written communication matters more in this role than people often expect. Your file reviews create a documented record that outside entities examine during tax credit audits. Vague notes or incomplete documentation can create compliance exposure even when the underlying decision was correct. Clear, precise written work protects the property and the portfolio.

What This Role Builds Over Time

The requirement to earn the Housing Credit Certified Professional (HCCP) designation within your first two years is a built-in investment in your professional standing. HCCP is a nationally recognized credential, and holding it opens doors to senior compliance roles, portfolio-level oversight positions, and consulting work within the affordable housing sector. You'll also attend TDHCA trainings annually and participate in third-party tax credit reviews, which means you build direct familiarity with how regulatory agencies and outside auditors evaluate compliance programs. That exposure is hard to replicate outside of a role like this one.

Monitoring shifts in LIHTC regulations and translating those changes into updated procedures is another skill this role develops deliberately. Tax credit rules do change, and the compliance specialist who can track those changes, interpret their practical effect, and implement modifications at the property level becomes genuinely valuable to a third-party management firm operating across a large affordable housing portfolio.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

  • Comfort with a 50% travel requirement, including property visits, trainings, and conferences
  • A working knowledge of HUD programs, even if LIHTC is your primary focus
  • The organizational discipline to manage multiple file reviews under tight turnaround windows without cutting corners on documentation
  • Genuine interest in earning and maintaining the HCCP credential, not just completing it as a checkbox

Asset Living operates as a fee management firm across multifamily, single-family rental, build-to-rent, student housing, and affordable housing divisions. That breadth means a compliance specialist here works within a large, structured operation with real infrastructure behind it, including training resources, established procedures, and a compliance team with institutional knowledge. If you're building a career in affordable housing compliance, that organizational depth matters.

job.title: Operations Specialist
job.description:
Operations roles at third-party management firms tend to sit at the intersection of everything: financial reporting, client communication, internal coordination, and the occasional moment where you're fielding a frustrated resident call while simultaneously pulling rent comps for a regional VP. That's the honest picture of what this role looks like at Asset Living, one of the larger fee management operators in multifamily, single-family rental, and student housing.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Operations Specialist supports senior-level portfolio managers across a range of tasks that don't fit neatly into one department. On any given week, you might be reviewing historical income and expense data for a Class B garden-style property, preparing a quarterly performance report for an owner, gathering rent comparable data from third-party sources, and coordinating travel logistics for a regional manager heading out for property visits. You'll also field resident calls that come in at the corporate level, which means you need to be calm, clear, and professional even when the person on the other end isn't.

The financial side of this role carries real weight. Collecting and reviewing T-12 data, understanding what drives NOI movement across a portfolio, and presenting that information clearly to clients requires both accuracy and the ability to translate numbers into plain language. Errors here don't just get flagged internally; they affect owner relationships.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • Strong Excel skills, not just functional ones. You should be comfortable building and auditing reports, not just filling in templates.
  • Familiarity with property management software like MRI or One-Site is a genuine advantage, though not required.
  • A background or coursework in finance, real estate, or economics helps you interpret what the numbers are actually saying.
  • You manage competing deadlines without losing track of details. Multiple senior managers may be pulling your time simultaneously.
  • You communicate professionally with clients and residents alike, adjusting your tone and level of detail for the audience.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this kind of support role is the ability to work ahead of requests. Senior managers shouldn't have to follow up twice. If you read a report and notice something looks off before sending it, if you confirm travel details proactively rather than waiting to be asked, that instinct is what makes this role genuinely valuable rather than just functional.

Context and Growth

Asset Living operates across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and active adult communities, which means the portfolio you're supporting isn't uniform. You'll develop fluency across asset types and management structures that most property management roles don't offer this early. Operations Specialists who perform well here often move into analyst, regional coordinator, or asset management support roles as the company grows. This role is a real on-ramp to the analytical and operational side of third-party management, not just an administrative holding pattern.

The position is based in Bentonville, AR, with travel estimated at roughly 10% annually for property visits and internal meetings.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Avion
job.description:
Three years of hands-on residential maintenance experience, EPA/HVAC certification, and the organizational discipline to keep a team on schedule. Those are the core skills this role runs on. If you've got all three and you're comfortable owning the maintenance operation at a multifamily community, this is worth a closer look.

What This Role Actually Requires

The Lead Maintenance Technician at Avion in Bozeman is effectively a working supervisor. You're not just fixing things. You're scheduling your team's daily workloads, managing turns, coordinating contractors, and keeping inventory stocked and organized. You'll run regular property inspections, track service requests through software, and handle preventative maintenance across HVAC systems, irrigation, appliances, pools, and building structures. The job is Monday through Friday, 9 to 5, with on-call rotation. Full-time, not seasonal.

You'll work closely with the Business Manager and leasing office to make sure make-ready units are show-ready and vacant homes are genuinely move-in ready. That coordination piece matters more than people expect. A unit that's technically fixed but not punch-listed properly creates friction with the leasing side fast.

You're also responsible for hiring and developing the service team beneath you, which means you need some comfort with people management, not just wrenches. Compliance with state, federal, and local regulations is part of the job too. That's not a footnote.

Skills This Role Sharpens

The supervisory layer here is real. Technicians who step into lead roles often underestimate how much of the job shifts from doing to planning and directing. Scheduling forecasted workloads, managing contractor relationships, and keeping the shop organized while also staying current on service requests builds a skill set that transfers directly into Maintenance Director or Service Manager roles. Bozeman's growth as a market means multifamily here isn't slowing down, and experienced leads who know how to run a tight operation are genuinely hard to find in mountain-west markets.

What Olympus Brings to the Role

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer from the National Apartment Association three consecutive years. That's not nothing. Their benefits package is comprehensive: medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, sabbatical, and both short and long-term disability coverage. The pay range comes in at $30 to $35 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly and quarterly bonuses available.

Strong candidates here will be the ones who already think in systems. They track work orders without being reminded. They know when to call a contractor and when to handle it in-house. They leave the shop cleaner than they found it. That's the profile that tends to succeed in a lead role at a company that's clearly paying attention to culture and accountability.

  • Minimum 3 years residential, commercial, or apartment maintenance experience
  • EPA/HVAC certification required
  • Experience in a supervisory or lead maintenance capacity preferred
  • Comfort with property management software for tracking and reporting
  • On-call availability required

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Olympus Grand Crossing
job.description:
Most apartment maintenance requests don't arrive at convenient times, and most properties can't afford a technician who only handles one trade. Olympus Property staffs for versatility. At Olympus Grand Crossing in Katy, TX, they're adding a Maintenance Technician who can move across work orders without needing hand-holding on the basics.

What the Work Looks Like

You'll work under the Lead Maintenance Technician, handling the full mix of resident service requests: plumbing repairs and fixture replacements, electrical switches and fixtures, appliance repair and replacement (refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers, microwaves), lock changes, door repairs, and paint and carpentry as needed. HVAC is a core part of the job. Preventative maintenance on units, filter changes, coil cleaning, and diagnosis are regular tasks, not occasional ones.

Beyond the unit-level work, you'll help maintain grounds, common areas, and pool upkeep, and you'll track all work through the property's software system. Inventory and shop organization are part of the role too. Standard schedule is Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability required outside those hours.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years of maintenance experience in a commercial, residential, or apartment setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems. An EPA/HVAC certification is a plus
  • Hands-on competence across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry
  • Ability to lift 50+ pounds, work on ladders, handle confined spaces, and work indoors and outdoors
  • Comfortable with software tools for tracking work orders

Starting pay is $23 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses available. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and paid time off. Olympus has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025).

The technicians who stand out in roles like this one aren't just fast on work orders. They communicate clearly with residents, keep the shop organized so turns don't stall, and flag recurring issues before they become capital problems. If you've worked through a lease-up or a busy summer season and know how to prioritize when the board is full, that experience translates directly here.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's 9:15 on a Saturday morning. A prospective resident just walked in without an appointment, a current resident is waiting at the desk about a billing question, and you have two leasing applications to process before noon. That's a normal morning at Bexley at Anderson Mill.

Weinstein Properties is a family-owned company that has operated apartment communities for over 70 years, with a portfolio of more than 60 properties across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. The Cedar Park location is looking for an Assistant Property Manager who can hold their own in a full-contact leasing office environment. Starting pay is $23 per hour, with increases based on experience and quarterly bonuses built into the compensation structure. Rotating Saturdays are part of the schedule.

The Day-to-Day Work

This role covers a wide range of operational tasks, and that range is real, not just recruiting language. On any given day you might be responding to internet leads, scheduling tours, walking a made-ready apartment to confirm it's punch-list clean, posting rent payments, and following up on delinquent balances. You'll process leasing applications, prepare lease paperwork, collect security deposits, and get signatures. When residents have questions about renewals, notices to vacate, transfers, or pet addendums, you're one of the first points of contact. You'll coordinate with maintenance on work orders, follow up with residents on open requests, and help process move-out security deposit dispositions. Resident events are also part of the job, including planning and hosting. You'll support the Property Manager and, at times, help train and guide others on the team.

Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein will train the right person who comes from a customer service, sales, or hospitality background. The expectation is that you learn fast and stay organized while the work keeps moving around you.

What This Role Actually Requires

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to handle difficult conversations calmly
  • Comfort working in a physically active role: expect time on your feet, walking the property, and inspecting units
  • Attention to detail when handling lease documents, applications, and financial transactions
  • Ability to shift priorities mid-task without losing accuracy
  • Availability for rotating Saturdays and occasional extended hours for resident events or weather-related situations
  • Goal-oriented approach and willingness to pitch in outside your formal job description when the team needs it

One honest note on this role: the combination of leasing, resident services, administrative work, and maintenance coordination means the job rarely lets you settle into one task for long. If you thrive when the day goes sideways, that's a genuine advantage here. If you need a predictable routine to do your best work, this probably isn't the right fit.

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many people in leadership roles at the company started in leasing or assistant manager positions. The skills you build here, including delinquency follow-up, make-ready coordination, and lease administration, transfer directly to a Property Manager role or broader multi-site responsibilities down the road.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and three internet leads came in overnight. You've got a tour at 10 a.m., a resident stopping by to ask about adding a pet, and maintenance just flagged an apartment they finished turning. You need to walk it before the afternoon showing. That's a normal Tuesday at Bexley Spring Hill.

What This Role Actually Covers

Weinstein Properties owns and manages over 21,000 apartments across five states, and this position sits at the front desk of one of their Tennessee communities. The schedule runs weekdays 9 to 6, with Saturdays 9 to 5 worked on rotation with the team. Sundays are closed. Pay is $21 per hour plus quarterly bonuses. Weinstein structures bonuses on a non-commission basis, which matters: your paycheck doesn't hinge on closing a lease that week.

The core of the job breaks into three tracks. First, leasing: answering internet leads and phone calls, scheduling and conducting tours, processing applications, preparing lease paperwork, collecting security deposits, and getting signatures. Second, resident services: helping current residents with renewals, notices to vacate, early terminations, pet addendums, transfers, account questions, and move-out processing including security deposit dispositions. Third, property operations: walking make-ready apartments to confirm they're punch-list complete, posting rent payments, following up on outstanding balances, and coordinating with maintenance on work orders and resident follow-up. Resident events fall in here too, from planning through execution.

The honest version of this job includes some friction. Difficult conversations happen regularly, whether that's a resident disputing a charge, a prospect who didn't qualify, or a move-out that gets tense. Balances need to be chased. Paperwork has to be accurate. The pace is real and it doesn't slow down much mid-week.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

Previous property management experience is welcome but not required. Backgrounds in customer service, sales, or hospitality translate well here. What the team needs more than a specific resume is someone who stays organized under a shifting to-do list, communicates clearly in both easy and difficult situations, and takes genuine ownership of their property's condition and reputation.

  • Strong administrative skills and attention to detail
  • High sense of urgency and solid time management
  • Warm, professional communication style, written and verbal
  • Self-motivated and comfortable staying busy throughout the day
  • Confidence to learn new systems and processes quickly

Weinstein offers structured training and coaching, so candidates earlier in their property management career can build the technical skills on the job. What they can't train is follow-through and a genuine interest in doing the work well.

For someone building a career in property management, the leasing consultant role is typically the clearest path toward an assistant manager position. The skills you build here, including delinquency follow-up, lease file management, move-out processing, and resident communication, are exactly what the next step requires. Starting in leasing at a company with a portfolio this size also means internal transfer and promotion opportunities exist at scale.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Pulse Millenia
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Pulse Millenia is an MG Properties community in Chula Vista, and this Maintenance Supervisor role puts you at the center of keeping it running. Your day spans diagnostics and delegation: triaging incoming service requests, inspecting completed work, scheduling your crew efficiently, and turning units so they're ready when leasing needs them. You're not just a wrench-turner at this level. You're managing workflow, tracking preventive maintenance schedules, keeping expenditure records accurate, and running safety meetings that actually stick.

At 150+ units, the volume is real. A backlog of open work orders affects resident satisfaction scores, and resident satisfaction affects renewals. Strong supervisors in this role keep their punch list tight, know which repairs to handle personally and which to delegate, and coordinate outside vendors without letting timelines slip. MG Properties has been acquiring and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, so there are systems and resources behind you, but the day-to-day execution is yours to own.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor role, with hands-on responsibility for a community of 150 units or more
  • Working knowledge across all trades: electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliance repair, general carpentry
  • Experience managing a team, not just doing the work yourself
  • A valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Strong customer service instincts. Residents notice how maintenance communicates, not just how fast the work gets done

The Role in Context

Compensation comes in at $36 to $37 per hour depending on experience, plus monthly bonuses and company profit sharing. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with employer match, paid holidays, sick time, and rental discounts. That last one matters in a market like Chula Vista, where housing costs are a real consideration for any employee weighing total comp.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is the ability to manage the full maintenance operation, not just respond to it. Supervisors who build a tight preventive maintenance calendar reduce emergency work orders. Fewer emergency calls means less overtime, lower repair costs, and better NOI contribution from the maintenance side of the ledger. If you've already figured that out at your current property, this role is a natural next step.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Artesia Apartments
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. and your work order queue already has six tickets. One resident has a leaking shutoff valve, another needs a dishwasher swap, and unit 214 just turned yesterday and still needs a final punch list walk. That's a normal Tuesday at Artesia Apartments.

MG Properties, a regional operator with over 30 years of acquisition, development, and management experience across the Western U.S., is adding a Maintenance Technician to the team at Artesia Apartments in Everett, WA. This is a hands-on, multi-trade role on a property that runs at scale. You'll work through service requests, support turns and make-readies, handle grounds and common area upkeep, and carry a share of the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies.

What the Work Actually Covers

Day-to-day, you're moving across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, and painting. Turns require speed and quality in the same breath: a unit sitting vacant is drag on occupancy, and a sloppy make-ready shows up in renewals. You'll also field emergency calls on rotation, so the ability to triage and respond under pressure is part of the job description whether it's written down or not.

  • At least 2 years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally on a 200-unit-or-larger property
  • Competency across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general repairs
  • Reliable transportation (non-negotiable for on-call coverage)
  • Availability for on-call rotation
