  • A customer-facing attitude: residents notice how you communicate as much as how fast you fix things

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range is $25 to $27 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base. Time off includes 10 days of PTO per year, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 52 hours of paid sick time. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance, FSA, dependent care spending account, 401(k) with employer match, and a rental discount. MG Properties also invests in employee development, which matters for technicians who want a path toward lead maintenance or facilities management roles over time.

One thing worth knowing: technicians who build true multi-trade depth on a property like this, especially HVAC and electrical, tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles faster than those who specialize narrowly. If you're looking to grow beyond the wrench, the experience here transfers directly to higher-responsibility positions in residential operations.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space, and this technician role reflects exactly how that model works in practice: you're covering a portfolio of individual homes rather than walking a single apartment community. Based in the Sandy Springs corridor north of Atlanta, you'll move between properties across a defined geographic zone, handling the full range of field maintenance that keeps scattered-site homes rent-ready and residents satisfied.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day centers on skilled trade work across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems. You'll handle both routine service calls and more involved repairs, and you'll own make-readies from start to finish: inspecting vacant homes, building a punch list, completing the work, and getting units back online for incoming residents. Move-in and move-out inspections are part of the rotation as well, along with onboarding audits when new properties come into the portfolio.

A meaningful part of the role involves quality control. When outside vendors complete work, you'll audit it in the field and flag anything that doesn't meet standard. All of this gets managed through mobile apps, so comfort with digital work order systems matters. You'll also post legal notices at properties when required.

The schedule is worth noting: full-time hours, no on-call rotation, no weekends. For experienced techs who've spent years in apartment maintenance with rotating emergency coverage, that structure is genuinely different.

What You Bring

  • HVAC Type II Certification (required); Universal Certification preferred
  • Valid driver's license and comfort driving between sites daily
  • Hands-on experience with HVAC, plumbing, and basic electrical repairs
  • Ability to self-manage in the field without a supervisor on-site
  • Ease with mobile apps for work orders, communication, and documentation
  • Physical capability for the role: lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing, bending, outdoor work in varying conditions
  • High school diploma or GED; must be authorized to work in the U.S.

Context Worth Knowing

Single-family rental portfolios present a different set of challenges than traditional multifamily. There's no leasing office, no on-site team, and no centralized maintenance shop to return to between calls. You need strong troubleshooting instincts because each home is its own situation, and you're often diagnosing problems without another technician nearby to consult. The tech who thrives here is organized, comfortable making judgment calls in the field, and consistent with documentation. Those same skills translate well to regional maintenance roles or field supervisor positions as single-family rental portfolios continue to scale.

Pay runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience and certification level. A company vehicle and gas card are provided. The role is based in the Sandy Springs area north of Atlanta.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates differently than conventional multifamily, and if you haven't worked it before, the learning curve is real. Scion knows this, and the Assistant Community Manager role at Lark Chapel Hill is built for someone ready to get into the weeds of a collegiate property while developing the skills to eventually run one.

This position supports the General Manager across the full range of community operations. That means financial administration, resident account management, delinquency control (Scion targets sub-2% by month-end), facilities coordination, and staff development. You'll also work closely with the Customer and Sales Experience Manager on leasing performance, tracking KPIs like concessions, gain to lease, and leasing velocity. The expectation is clear: when the GM is out, you run the property.

The role carries real weight during annual turn. Student housing turn is compressed, high-volume, and unforgiving. You'll use Turnable to manage the electronic turn board, conduct move-out inspections, assess damage charges, handle dispute processing, and physically pitch in on make-ready tasks including moving furniture, assisting with punch list items, and cleaning units. Anyone who thinks this is a desk job hasn't worked a student turn season.

Day-to-day, you're balancing resident escalations, utility billing, accounts receivable reconciliation, Google and Yelp review responses via Entrata, and monthly property walks to keep the asset up to Scion's standards. The tech stack is heavier than most: Entrata, Greenhouse, Lattice, Turnable, Qualtrics, and ClickUp are all in regular rotation. Comfort with property management systems isn't optional here.

What they're looking for

  • At least one year of experience in property management or residential communities
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proficiency in Entrata or a comparable PMS
  • Solid detail orientation and comfort managing competing priorities
  • A customer-focused mindset and the ability to handle escalated resident situations without losing composure
  • Discretion with confidential information

What separates candidates who thrive here from those who struggle is usually the same thing: the ability to shift from a leasing conversation to a facilities issue to a delinquency report without dropping the ball on any of them. Student housing peaks hard and moves fast. Chapel Hill adds the layer of a university-driven demand cycle that dictates the rhythm of the entire operation.

For someone with conventional multifamily experience, this role builds skills that transfer broadly: Entrata fluency, financial reporting, staff supervision, and turn management all carry weight across Class A, B, and C assets. And for someone already in student housing, this is a clear path toward a General Manager seat.

The position is exempt, includes a discretionary annual bonus, standard health and dental and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. Work is based at the Lark Chapel Hill property with some travel expected. Non-traditional hours during peak periods and on-call coverage are part of the job.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This position lives at the intersection of sales, customer service, and light property administration. You'll use interpersonal skills constantly: giving tours, handling objections, engaging residents on social media, and representing the community at events. You'll also use organizational skills daily, managing packages, maintaining the office, tracking maintenance requests, and keeping common areas presentable. Neither side of the job is optional. Both matter equally here.

Strong communicators who can shift tone quickly do well in this role. One conversation might be with a prospective student weighing housing options. The next might be a frustrated resident waiting on a maintenance follow-up. The ability to read those situations and respond appropriately is what separates consultants who hit their numbers from those who don't.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

University House Midtown is a student housing community in Atlanta, and the pace reflects that. Leasing cycles in student housing compress fast. Most of the year's occupancy gets decided well before summer, which means your sales activity needs to be consistent, not reactive. You'll execute leasing and engagement initiatives set by management, contribute feedback on what objections prospects are raising, and assist with local marketing recommendations.

On the administrative side, the work is straightforward but requires follow-through: package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage on rotation. None of it is glamorous, but it keeps the community running and directly affects how residents feel about living there.

Turn periods deserve a specific mention. Student housing turns over heavily in the summer, and availability during that window is a real requirement. If your schedule can't flex during turn, this role isn't the right fit.

What Makes This Role at Scion Different

Scion operates student housing at scale across the country, which means their systems and expectations are more structured than you'd find at a smaller operator. There's a playbook for sales initiatives, community engagement, and marketing. That's an advantage if you're early in your property management career: you'll build habits and skills within a framework that transfers directly to any leasing or assistant manager role down the road.

  • Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship
  • Available for summer, holidays, and turn periods
  • Comfortable with an on-call rotation for after-hours needs
  • Strong communication skills across a diverse resident population
  • Self-directed and reliable without constant supervision

If you want a leasing role with a clear operator behind it and real exposure to student housing operations, this is a solid place to build that foundation.

job.title: Administrative Clerk (Homestead Park, Moulton Plaza)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the front line of two affordable housing communities in Sunnyvale: Homestead Park and Moulton Plaza. You're the first contact point for residents, guests, and vendors walking through the door. That means monitoring who comes and goes, keeping the visitor log current, answering phones, routing messages, and making sure the lobby and entrance stay clean and orderly. You'll also post and distribute tenant notices, complete incident reports, and help enforce community policies and house rules consistently.

It's administrative work, but it's not back-office work. You're visible, you're interacting with residents daily, and the information you capture (logs, reports, correspondence) feeds directly into how the Community Manager tracks what's happening on the property. If something goes sideways, your incident documentation is part of the record.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least one year of receptionist or administrative experience
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills. You're writing correspondence and talking to residents with a range of needs and backgrounds.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Reliable transportation to get to the site. A valid California driver's license and current auto insurance are required if you're driving.
  • Flexibility to handle varied tasks as they come up, because no two shifts look exactly the same
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission to provide stable, dignified housing for working families, seniors, and people with special needs

Context Worth Knowing

MidPen has operated in Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 130 affordable properties across 12 counties, housing roughly 20,000 residents. They've held Great Place to Work certification in 2025, which in property management circles tends to reflect actual investment in staff rather than just marketing copy. This role supports in-house management, not a third-party fee structure, so the community focus is real and the collaboration with onsite Resident Services teams is a practical part of the job, not an afterthought.

Pay runs $20.77 to $23.37 per hour depending on experience, and the benefits package includes health, dental, vision, 403(b) retirement, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, and an EAP, among others.

One honest note: front desk roles at affordable housing communities carry a different weight than a typical office receptionist job. Residents may be dealing with housing instability, language barriers, or difficult personal circumstances. The candidates who do well here aren't just organized. They're calm under pressure, consistent with boundaries, and genuinely interested in the people they serve.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Homestead Park)
job.description:
It's 11 PM on a Tuesday and a resident at Homestead Park calls in a plumbing emergency. You're on the rotating on-call schedule, so you're the one who shows up, assesses the situation, and makes it right before the night is over. That's the reality of this role, and for the right person, it's also the point.

The Work Itself

MidPen Housing has operated affordable communities across Northern California since 1970, and Homestead Park in Sunnyvale is part of a portfolio that houses working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. The Maintenance Technician here reports to the Community Manager and carries real technical responsibility across electrical, plumbing, and carpentry systems, not just basic repairs but the kind of work that keeps units habitable and safe.

Day-to-day tasks span a wide range:

  • Electrical repairs to appliances, fixtures, switches, and circuits
  • Plumbing repairs to water and sewage systems
  • Rough and finish carpentry, including structural framing and cosmetic work
  • Unit turns: painting, flooring, fixture installation, and appliance replacement within established timeframes
  • Landscaping and irrigation system maintenance to MidPen standards
  • Preventive maintenance scheduling and work order documentation
  • Contractor coordination, including assisting with bids, scheduling, and monitoring completion
  • Support for move-ins, move-outs, and annual inspections alongside the Community Manager

The on-call rotation here is a seven-consecutive-day commitment, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. That's a real ask, and candidates who thrive in this role tend to be people who plan around it rather than resist it.

What MidPen Is Looking For

The baseline is a high school diploma or GED with at least three years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in property management. Extensive plumbing knowledge is specifically called out, as is experience with electrical repairs. Carpentry ability at both the rough and finish level matters here given the mix of structural and cosmetic work that comes up in an affordable housing portfolio.

This role also carries a mentorship component. You'll coach and oversee Maintenance Groundskeeper staff, which means communication skills and a willingness to bring others along are part of the job description in a meaningful way, not just a line item. Candidates who've informally trained a junior tech or walked a newer employee through a repair process will feel comfortable here faster than those who've only worked solo.

Basic OSHA knowledge, physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly, and comfort working across all weather conditions and confined spaces are all required. Computer skills for work order management round out the practical requirements.

Pay runs from $25.00 to $28.13 per hour based on experience, with a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, FSA options, an employee education reimbursement program, and paid time off including company holidays and wellness days.

One thing worth noting about this market: Sunnyvale sits in the heart of Silicon Valley, where the gap between market-rate and affordable housing has widened steadily. The residents MidPen serves here often have very few alternatives if something goes wrong with their unit. The maintenance team's consistency and responsiveness directly supports housing stability in a way that's harder to quantify at a luxury property but very easy to see on the ground.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners sits among the top 50 multifamily management companies in the country, with roots planted firmly in the Southeast. Their Assistant Community Manager position at Hawthorne at the Forest in Wake Forest, NC puts you at the operational center of a community where leasing performance, resident relations, and financial accountability all converge in a single role.

This is a position that requires real financial literacy from day one. You'll handle rent collection, payment posting, ledger reviews, and delinquency follow-up on a weekly basis. Monitoring delinquency isn't just about making calls. It's about reading patterns, understanding account histories, and knowing when to escalate to eviction procedures. That kind of financial discipline, applied consistently, is what keeps a community's NOI healthy. At the same time, you're supporting leasing activity: conducting tours, working leads, completing lease applications and renewals accurately, and contributing to occupancy goals. The dual nature of this role is what makes it demanding and genuinely instructive.

What this role builds is equally important. Stepping in for the Community Manager during absences means you'll practice real decision-making under pressure, not just task execution. You'll develop the communication habits that regional leadership notices: clear updates, clean documentation, and the ability to de-escalate a difficult resident situation without letting it affect the rest of the team's momentum. Those are the skills that move people from assistant to Community Manager, and Hawthorne explicitly supports that path through a structured Career Path Program with dedicated learning and development resources.

What separates strong candidates here isn't just leasing experience. It's the combination of leasing instinct and financial follow-through. Many candidates can show a prospect a home. Fewer can also sit down with a delinquency report, identify which accounts need immediate action, and handle that conversation with a resident the same afternoon. If you've done both in a previous role, you'll find this position moves at a pace that fits you well.

What You'll Bring

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Two years of property management experience (preferred)
  • At least six months in an assistant community manager capacity (preferred)
  • Valid driver's license
  • CALP accreditation is a plus

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off each week keeps the total at 40 hours. Resident events or specific community needs may occasionally require evening availability. Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

The Assistant Community Manager position at Hawthorne at the Forest pulls on two distinct skill sets that don't always coexist naturally: financial fluency and people instincts. On any given day, you might spend the morning posting rent payments, reviewing ledgers for billing discrepancies, and following up on delinquent accounts, then pivot to walking a prospect through a tour or talking a frustrated resident down from a tense situation. The ability to shift between those modes without losing composure is genuinely what separates good candidates from great ones in this role.

Financial comfort matters here more than the title might suggest. You'll be involved in rent collection, payment posting, ledger audits, and delinquency follow-up on a regular basis. You don't need to be an accountant, but you do need to read a report, spot an error, and understand what it means for the community's numbers. That financial awareness, combined with strong leasing instincts, is what makes this role a real stepping stone toward Community Manager.

What You'll Be Working On

Leasing is a core part of the job. You'll handle incoming leads, conduct tours, guide prospects through applications, and work to hit occupancy targets through both new leases and renewals. Hawthorne also expects this person to manage the community's social media presence, which means you'll need some comfort creating content that feels authentic rather than templated.

On the administrative side, your responsibilities include:

  • Overseeing rent collection and payment processing accurately and on schedule
  • Monitoring delinquency, making follow-up calls weekly, and coordinating eviction procedures when necessary
  • Conducting ledger reviews to catch billing and payment errors before they compound
  • Assisting the Community Manager with financial reporting for regional leadership
  • Keeping the office, amenities, and common areas in clean, presentable condition

You'll also step into a team leadership capacity when the Community Manager is out. That means maintaining daily operations, keeping the team focused, and handling resident concerns with the kind of follow-through that builds actual trust over time.

What This Role Looks Like at Hawthorne

Hawthorne Residential Partners ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally and has a strong presence across the Southeast. Their internal career path program is a real differentiator: Assistant Community Manager is treated as a development position, not a holding pattern. If you're aiming for a Community Manager seat, this company appears to promote from within and invest in getting you there.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday with Saturday hours (10 AM to 4 PM), and one weekday off per week keeps the total at 40 hours. Evening availability may come up for resident events. Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses, which means your income has real upside tied to results you directly influence.

Two years of property management experience is preferred, and prior assistant manager experience is a plus. A CALP credential helps, but it isn't required to apply. A valid driver's license is expected. What Hawthorne seems to value most is someone who genuinely connects with people while staying organized enough to manage the financial side without dropping the ball.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a sales job, a customer service job, and an administrative job rolled into one. At Waypoint Management Services in Jacksonville, the Leasing Consultant role leans on all three of those skill sets daily, sometimes within the same hour. If you're comfortable shifting from a warm phone follow-up to a lease file audit to a community tour without losing your footing, this position is built for that kind of range.

The Skills This Role Runs On

The core of the job is converting traffic into signed leases. That means handling inbound inquiries quickly, running confident tours, knowing your floor plans and pricing cold, and following up persistently without coming across as pushy. You'll need to understand how your community stacks up against local competitors, because prospects absolutely will ask, and a vague answer loses the lease.

On the administrative side, you'll manage the full leasing cycle: qualifying applicants, preparing lease documents, calculating prorations, and keeping files organized for manager review. Familiarity with Yardi helps. If you've used a CRM for tracking prospect traffic and follow-up activity, that transfers directly here. Waypoint lists bilingual (English/Spanish) as a preference, and in Jacksonville's market, that's a genuine differentiator when competing for residents.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A realistic picture: mornings often involve reviewing your prospect pipeline and returning inquiries from the night before. Midday might be back-to-back tours. Afternoons can shift to application processing, lease prep, or renewal outreach. Weekend rotation is part of the schedule, which is standard in leasing. The model unit and leasing office need to stay tour-ready regardless of how busy it gets, and that discipline matters more than it sounds.

Fair Housing compliance runs underneath everything. It's not a box to check once during onboarding. It's built into how you qualify applicants, how you present availability, and how you handle objections. Waypoint expects you to apply it correctly without being reminded.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The applicants who tend to do well in leasing consultant roles aren't just personable. They close. They follow up when it's inconvenient. They catch the file error before the manager does. They hit occupancy goals because they treat the waitlist and renewal pipeline with the same energy as new leads. Two years of leasing, sales, or hospitality experience is the baseline Waypoint is looking for, and that background matters because the ramp-up time is real.

  • Minimum 2 years in leasing, sales, or hospitality
  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Yardi and CRM experience preferred
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Weekend availability required

Compensation runs $18 to $20 per hour, with monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, a leaser-of-the-month monetary reward, and an employee housing discount. Benefits including medical, dental, and vision are subsidized and start on day one. PTO begins at 120 hours in the first year and grows with tenure. There's also a 401k with company match, commuter benefits, and an employee referral program.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Luxury apartment maintenance is a different animal from conventional Class B/C work. Residents paying premium rents expect premium responsiveness, and when something breaks, they notice fast. The Lead Maintenance Technician at Comstock's Rockville community sits at the center of that expectation: technically skilled enough to handle complex repairs, and people-smart enough to represent the property well every single time.

What This Role Actually Looks Like Day to Day

Your morning might start with a punch list from overnight calls, a scheduled PM on HVAC equipment, and a make-ready unit that needs to be turned before a new resident arrives Friday. By afternoon, you're troubleshooting an electrical issue in a common area, coordinating with a vendor on a plumbing repair, and doing a quick walk of the grounds to keep the exterior looking sharp. The variety is real, and so is the pace.

Comstock is looking for someone with at least a year of hands-on maintenance experience and working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, and plumbing systems. CFC Universal Certification is preferred, and Class A property experience will help you hit the ground running. Yardi and building automation systems experience are a plus, not a hard requirement, but they matter at a property like this. You'll also need a valid driver's license and the ability to reach the property within 45 minutes during on-call emergencies.

The on-call rotation is worth naming directly: this role includes after-hours and weekend availability. That's a real commitment, and the right candidate knows that going in rather than being surprised by it later.

The Human Side of the Job

Technical skills get you the interview. How you interact with residents, coworkers, and ownership determines how far you go. Comstock specifically calls out the ability to build rapport with a diverse group of people and communicate clearly under pressure. That means when a resident is frustrated at 7pm about a leaking sink, your tone and follow-through matter as much as your wrench work.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is accountability without being asked. The best lead techs don't wait to be told a unit needs attention or a piece of equipment is overdue for PM. They track it, flag it, and own the outcome.

  • HVAC, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, masonry, and painting skills required
  • Make-ready and unit turn experience expected
  • CFC Universal Certification preferred
  • Yardi and building automation systems experience a plus
  • Valid driver's license, no major violations
  • Must be available for on-call rotation including evenings and weekends
  • Must be able to respond to emergencies within 45 minutes
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work in variable conditions

Comstock offers a competitive salary in the $26 to $29 per hour range (Maryland), medical, dental, vision, 401K match, life insurance, annual professional development funds, and advancement opportunities within their growing portfolio.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Comstock has built a reputation in the DMV as one of the more serious mixed-use developers working the transit-oriented corridor, and their Reston presence reflects that. This leasing consultant position sits at a luxury high-rise community where the product sells itself to a point, but converting traffic into signed leases still takes real skill. Reston's rental market draws a tech-forward, commuter-conscious renter base, many of them relocating for work near the Dulles corridor or Silver Line stations. That buyer profile rewards consultants who can speak to lifestyle and convenience with specificity, not just show a unit and hand over a brochure.

The core of this role is owning the full leasing cycle. That means following up on leads before they go cold, walking prospects through the community with enough product knowledge to handle objections on the spot, preparing accurate lease paperwork, and tracking your own activity through weekly and monthly reporting. Yardi experience will help you hit the ground running, though it's listed as a plus rather than a requirement. You'll also carry some responsibility for the community's online presence, including social media, which at a high-rise property often means showcasing amenities, views, and local neighborhood context to prospects who are shopping remotely before they ever schedule a tour.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones is the ability to build genuine rapport quickly without losing the thread of the sales process. High-rise leasing at a community like this tends to attract prospects who've done their research. They're comparing you against other Class A options in Reston and Tysons. The consultants who perform well in that environment listen more than they pitch, know how to read where a prospect is in their decision timeline, and follow up in a way that feels helpful rather than pressured.

What Comstock is looking for

  • At least one year of leasing experience in a multi-family setting, preferred
  • A track record of moving prospects from inquiry to lease signing
  • Comfort with Yardi or a comparable property management platform
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, especially Outlook and Excel for reporting
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A high school diploma at minimum; a bachelor's degree in business or a related field is preferred
  • The ability to manage multiple leads and tasks without dropping details

This kind of role is a real entry point into property management as a career. Leasing consultants who develop both their sales instincts and their administrative discipline often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions within a few years. At a company with Comstock's portfolio depth, internal mobility is worth factoring into how you think about this opportunity.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Running four properties across three San Fernando Valley submarkets takes a specific kind of mental organization. You're not sitting in one leasing office waiting for traffic to walk in. You're moving between Northridge, North Hollywood, and Van Nuys, tracking 141 units across different buildings, each with its own maintenance rhythm, occupancy picture, and resident base. The skills this role tests most are prioritization, vendor coordination, and the ability to context-switch without dropping anything.

What This Role Actually Requires

The core work is property management in the conventional multifamily sense: leasing, inspections, make-ready oversight, delinquency follow-up, and day-to-day resident communication. But the multi-site setup adds a layer most single-property roles don't. You'll need to run competitive market rent analysis across submarkets that don't always move in sync. Van Nuys and North Hollywood can price differently than Northridge even when they're a few miles apart, so your comp analysis work has real operational weight here.

Yardi proficiency matters. So does comfort with property accounting basics, because you're expected to understand what's happening financially at each asset, not just operationally. Scheduling maintenance staff and vendors across multiple locations means you'll spend real time coordinating rather than just supervising from one spot.

The weekend rotation and on-call availability are part of the deal. That's worth stating plainly. After-hours calls come with any onsite role, and this one spans 141 units. If you've managed that volume before, you know what a slow weekend looks like and what a bad one looks like.

The Skills That Travel

Multi-site management builds something that single-property roles often don't: the ability to triage. When you're responsible for more than one address, you develop a faster instinct for what actually needs your attention now versus what can wait until your next scheduled walk. That skill transfers directly to regional manager roles and positions with larger portfolios. Candidates who've held multi-site property manager jobs tend to move into area or regional roles more quickly than those who've only run one building.

  • 3 or more years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Yardi experience and solid working knowledge of Microsoft Office
  • Proven leasing ability and comfort conducting rent comp analysis
  • Experience supervising maintenance staff and managing vendor relationships
  • Valid driver's license with current auto insurance (a monthly auto allowance is included)
  • Must live onsite. A free two-bedroom apartment is provided as part of the compensation package.

Working at PMA

Property Management Associates has operated in the greater LA market for over 30 years and manages both residential and commercial assets across the region. The company describes itself as family-oriented with an emphasis on staff development, which tends to mean more direct access to decision-makers than you'd get at a large institutional operator. For someone who wants to grow without getting lost in a corporate structure, that matters.

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour, plus the onsite apartment, $300 monthly auto allowance, and $25 monthly cell allowance. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance with employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, disability coverage, and paid time off. A background check, DMV review, and pre-employment physical are part of the hiring process.

job.title: Manager of Resident Retention - 177
job.description:
Retention-focused roles like this one sit at an interesting intersection in multifamily operations. You're not purely a leasing consultant chasing traffic, and you're not an assistant property manager buried in administrative work. You're the person whose job is to keep residents who already chose the community from quietly choosing to leave. At a company like Berkshire Residential Investments, where a portfolio of properties runs under centralized support structures, that function carries real weight on NOI.

What This Role Actually Involves

The Manager of Resident Retention at Tinsley on the Park covers five or more communities, so the scope is wider than a single-property leasing role. Your primary focus is the renewal pipeline: identifying residents with upcoming lease expirations, executing weekly outreach, and negotiating renewals that hold occupancy targets. That means you'll need to understand how YieldStar pricing decisions affect what you can offer, and you'll be working alongside the revenue management team rather than just executing whatever rate shows up in the system.

Beyond renewals, the role pulls in resident communications, social media content for each assigned property, reputation management across platforms like Google and Apartment Ratings, and coordination of resident events. You'll be drafting communications through Yardi, running email campaigns, and monitoring review trends to surface patterns for property managers and regional leadership. The reporting side is real: you'll be managing renewal metrics and resident feedback data, not just responding to individual concerns.

  • Proactively contact residents approaching lease expiration and negotiate renewals
  • Draft, review, and execute lease renewal documents, verifying pet records, parking charges, and renter's insurance requirements
  • Develop and manage social media content for assigned communities as a brand ambassador
  • Track and summarize resident reviews and ratings; communicate themes to property leadership
  • Coordinate resident appreciation events and retention programs with onsite teams
  • Support customer satisfaction score goals and maintain competitive market awareness
  • Collaborate with sustainability team to incorporate Berkshire's ESG initiatives into retention efforts
  • Assist property managers with reports, market surveys, and resident communications as needed

Where This Role Leads

Retention specialist experience compounds well. The skills you build here, specifically renewal negotiation, reputation management, resident communication strategy, and cross-functional collaboration with marketing and revenue management, map directly onto leasing director and assistant property manager tracks. If you're aiming toward a property manager role, the exposure you get here to YieldStar, occupancy metrics, and budget awareness gives you a meaningful head start. You're touching the performance matrix, understanding what drives NOI, and working alongside regional leadership regularly. That visibility matters.

Strong candidates in this role tend to be people who can hold a warm, service-oriented tone while also being persistent and organized enough to work a renewal pipeline systematically. The social media and writing components aren't window dressing: Berkshire holds communications to brand standards, and your drafts need to be clean and on-message. If you're someone who treats a lease renewal outreach email with the same care as a resident complaint response, you'll fit this role well.

job.title: Sales & Resident Experience Consultant - 179
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Leasing is a sales discipline, and the best consultants treat it that way. This role at Estancia Townhomes calls for someone who can read a prospect quickly, match them to the right unit, and guide them through a decision without pressure tactics. Berkshire sets a closing ratio floor of 20%, which means you need more than a warm personality. You need follow-through, pipeline awareness, and enough product knowledge to make the case for your property on every tour.

The administrative side matters just as much as the sales side here. Accurate lease files, timely resident communications, and a leasing office that looks polished when a prospect walks in, these aren't background tasks. They're part of what creates the experience Berkshire is known for. Consultants who underestimate the paperwork side of this job tend to struggle once occupancy climbs and traffic picks up simultaneously.

What You'll Actually Be Doing Day to Day

Your mornings often start with a walk of the tour route and models. If a punch list item from the day before wasn't addressed, you catch it before the first prospect arrives. From there, the day shifts between responding to leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and staying current on what competing properties are doing in the market. Berkshire expects its leasing staff to know local market conditions well enough to contribute ideas to the property manager, not just execute them.

Resident communication runs through this role constantly. Whether it's a renewal conversation, a maintenance concern passed along professionally, or a simple check-in, the way you handle existing residents affects both retention and reputation. In a townhome community especially, where residents tend to stay longer and develop stronger ties to the property, that relationship-building work compounds over time.

  • At least two years of customer service experience that translates into a sales context
  • Comfort adapting to new leasing software and digital tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to maintain professionalism across a wide range of resident and prospect interactions
  • Genuine attention to detail in both administrative work and physical presentation of the property

What Makes Berkshire a Different Place to Do This Work

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which matters more than it might seem at first. There's no third-party management layer creating friction between the leasing team and decision-makers. When you bring an idea to the property manager about a marketing angle or a resident satisfaction initiative, it has a shorter path to actually happening. That structure rewards consultants who think beyond their immediate task list.

The consultants who stand out here aren't just closers. They're the ones who combine sales instincts with genuine curiosity about what residents actually need, and who can hold both the high-energy, front-facing side of the role and the detail-oriented administrative side without letting one slip while the other shines. If your career goal is to move toward an assistant manager or property manager role, this position builds the exact mix of skills that transition requires: leasing performance, market awareness, resident relations, and operational discipline.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a people skill first. The ability to read a prospect's hesitation, pivot your pitch without making it feel like a pitch, and turn a casual tour into a signed lease, that's the core of what this role demands. Bozzuto is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Clermont, FL community, and the skills that will carry you here are relational, communicative, and genuinely sales-minded in equal measure.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

You'll spend a meaningful portion of your time converting inbound and outbound leads into scheduled tours, which means your written and verbal communication has to be sharp, warm, and persuasive without feeling scripted. Follow-up is where most leasing consultants either win or lose deals. Bozzuto expects you to stay on top of prospects with helpful, specific information about the community and the surrounding area, not just generic replies.

Touring skills matter just as much. A good tour isn't a walkthrough; it's a conversation where you listen for what the prospect actually values and connect it back to what the community offers. That takes curiosity and presence, not just a memorized script about square footage.

Social media is a genuine part of this job, not an afterthought. You'll create and post content on platforms like Facebook and Instagram to build community awareness and keep interest alive. Candidates who treat this as a creative outlet, rather than a chore, tend to do better here.

One honest note on schedule: this role requires working three weekends per month, with two weekday days off in exchange. Weekends are when most prospects are out looking, so it's where leasing happens. If your lifestyle can accommodate that rhythm, it works. If weekends are a hard limit, this role probably isn't the right fit.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

A typical day might start with reviewing new leads from overnight inquiries, sending personalized follow-ups, and confirming afternoon tours. Midday, you're walking prospects through the community, answering questions about lease terms, amenities, and the neighborhood. Clermont sits in Lake County, west of Orlando, with a growing residential base and strong demand from families and remote workers relocating from larger metros. Knowing the local area, nearby shopping, commute patterns, proximity to I-4 and the Turnpike, is a real advantage when talking to prospects who are still figuring out if Clermont is the right fit for them.

Between tours, you might be posting an Instagram story, updating your CRM notes, or following up with someone who toured last week and hasn't decided yet.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Bozzuto operates at a level where culture and resident experience are central to the brand, not just talking points. The consultants who thrive tend to genuinely care about the people moving in, not just closing the lease. That care shows up in the little things: remembering a prospect's dog's name, knowing which floor plan works for a home office, flagging a maintenance issue before a new resident notices it.

  • Customer-focused mindset with real follow-through
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with social media content creation
  • Sales instincts paired with genuine warmth
  • Proficiency with software, apps, and property management platforms
  • Professional presentation and attention to detail

Compensation sits between $47,000 and $50,000 annually, with bonus opportunities on top of that. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401(k) with company match, and tuition reimbursement. For someone early in a property management career, this role builds a strong foundation. Leasing consultants who develop both their sales numbers and their resident relationship skills often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions within a few years.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Weinstein Properties runs a straightforward operation: they own and manage their communities directly, which means the person giving you direction is the same person accountable for the property's condition. There's no third-party management layer, no conflicting priorities from an outside owner. Standards stay consistent, and when leadership says they support the team, it actually shows up in how the day-to-day works.

What You'll Actually Do

The bulk of your time goes to work orders in occupied units. Residents call in issues, you troubleshoot them, you fix them. HVAC is a big part of that, which is why the EPA certification matters here, not as a checkbox but as something you'll use regularly. Plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry: all of it comes through the queue. You'll also help with turns and make-readies when units come vacant, which means punch lists, coordinating with the team, and getting units rent-ready on schedule. Pool areas, grounds, and amenities are part of the picture too.

The on-call rotation is real. You'll share it with the team, but you should go in knowing that after-hours calls happen. The $150 weekly on-call pay applies whether your phone rings or not, and there's an additional $150 for holiday on-call coverage. That's a straightforward acknowledgment from the company that being available has a cost, and they're compensating for it.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of hands-on apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required, not preferred)
  • Demonstrated HVAC troubleshooting and repair ability
  • Comfort working independently and coordinating within a team
  • Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work both indoors and outdoors year-round
  • Proficiency with basic computer tools: work order systems, Outlook, mobile devices
  • Ability to climb ladders and stairs, and operate a golf cart on property

Strong candidates here aren't just technically capable. They communicate well with residents, they close their work orders with care, and they treat occupied units with respect. A tech who can fix the HVAC but leaves a mess or keeps residents in the dark doesn't last long in a community that cares about its reputation.

The Role in Context

Fort Worth's residential market has stayed active, and well-maintained communities in the north corridor hold their occupancy because residents notice when maintenance is sharp. This position pays $20 per hour to start, with room to move up based on experience. There's a quarterly bonus of up to $980 tied to property and team performance, a rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus a 401(k) with company match.

For a tech with solid HVAC skills and a few years of apartment experience, this kind of in-house ownership structure tends to offer more stability and clearer advancement than a scattered portfolio managed by a third party. Weinstein notes that internal growth is real here, and for someone who eventually wants to move into a lead tech or maintenance supervisor role, that path is easier to walk when the company already knows your work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - The Herald
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles often get undersold. On paper, they look like a front-desk sales job. In practice, they're where you build the skills that make a property management career: reading traffic patterns, closing under pressure, keeping occupancy where it needs to be, and learning how every other department depends on what you do. At MG Properties' The Herald Apartments in Placentia, CA, this role is a genuine on-ramp for someone who wants to grow in the industry.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day centers on converting prospects into residents and making sure those residents stay. You'll greet and qualify applicants, prepare leases, and coordinate with the maintenance team to make sure move-ins go smoothly. You'll also manage the administrative side: keeping rental files current, entering data accurately, and handling monthly paperwork. When residents have complaints, maintenance requests, or rent questions, you're one of the first people they talk to. That mix of sales, service, and admin is intentional. It means you're touching almost every part of the resident lifecycle.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They have a stated track record of promoting from within, which matters here. Leasing Consultants who perform well and absorb the operational side of the role are natural candidates for Assistant Manager and Property Manager positions down the line.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management experience (preferred, not required)
  • Strong sales instincts and genuine customer service ability
  • Comfort with data entry and keeping leasing files organized and accurate
  • Professional communication skills, both with prospects and current residents
  • A team-oriented mindset and the ability to coordinate across departments

Why This Role Builds Something

Here's what separates strong leasing consultants from average ones: the best don't just close applications. They track why traffic converts or doesn't, they notice when concessions are eating into NOI, and they start asking questions that sound like management thinking. If you're someone who wants to understand how occupancy connects to a property's financial performance, a Leasing Consultant role at a company this size gives you real exposure to those mechanics early. The compensation runs $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly and quarterly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, and a standard benefits package including medical, dental, and vision. Rental discounts are also part of the package.

This is a solid position for someone early in their property management career who wants structured exposure to leasing operations and a company that has the track record and size to actually promote from within.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
The Experience Team Member (ETM) role at Scion's 257 Thayer property in Providence puts you at the front line of student housing leasing and resident engagement. This isn't a pure desk job. You'll split time between showing units, working social platforms, handling package logistics, supporting maintenance follow-up, and covering after-hours lockout rotation. The role sits at the intersection of sales and community management, and the pace follows the academic calendar closely.

What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you're the face of the community. That means giving tours, fielding objections, and feeding honest intel back to management about what's stalling lease conversions. You'll help execute leasing and marketing initiatives, contribute to social media content, and assist in planning resident engagement events. On the admin side, you handle package retrieval, office upkeep, and coordination with the maintenance team on open work orders. You're also part of an on-call rotation for after-hours lockouts, so availability matters here.

Turn periods at student properties are intense. Move-out and move-in happen in a compressed window, and the ETM role is expected to be present and reliable during those stretches, along with summers and holidays when most people want time off.

What You Bring

  • Strong interpersonal skills across a genuinely diverse resident population
  • Comfort with shifting priorities and a schedule that doesn't always follow a script
  • Self-discipline and reliability, especially for on-call coverage
  • Basic proficiency with social media platforms used for community marketing
  • A customer-first approach to every interaction, including the difficult ones
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (no visa sponsorship available)

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates differently from conventional multifamily. Traffic spikes are tied to academic cycles, not the broader rental market. Prospects often tour in groups, parents are frequently part of the decision, and lease terms are structured around the school year. Strong ETMs learn to read that dynamic quickly. Providence's proximity to Brown University and RISD creates a competitive student housing market, and residents at a property like 257 Thayer tend to have high expectations for both amenities and responsiveness.

For someone early in a property management career, this role builds a solid foundation. The combination of leasing, resident relations, and light operations exposure translates well into an Assistant Manager or Leasing Manager track down the road. Pay for this position ranges from $19 to $20 per hour, plus bonus and benefits.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor (Oak & Umber)
job.description:
The Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance supervision at scale demands a specific combination of technical depth, crew leadership, and budget discipline. At Prometheus Real Estate Group's Oak and Umber community in Sunnyvale, those three skill sets run together daily. This isn't a role where you hand off work orders and check boxes. You're running physical operations for a property that's part of a 13,000-unit privately held portfolio, one that Prometheus has built and managed in-house since 1965. That vertical integration matters: acquisitions, development, value-add renovations, and operations all sit under one roof, which means the maintenance team is close to capex decisions and renovation scopes in ways that don't happen at third-party management shops.

The technical baseline here is real. Five or more years in apartment maintenance, at least two in a supervisory seat, and a minimum of three certifications from programs like BOMA, IREM, or vocational trades. You'll need working fluency in federal, state, and local safety regulations, because compliance in California's regulatory environment is not an area where approximation works. The ability to read operating manuals, interpret safety rules, and translate both into team behavior is a daily requirement, not an occasional one.

What Running This Neighborhood Actually Looks Like

Your day moves between the budget and the building. On the cost side, you're managing vendor and contractor relationships with an eye on spend, keeping maintenance functions cost-effective without deferring work that creates larger problems downstream. On the physical side, you're overseeing ongoing safety training, capital projects, and inventory management while also being the person your team calls when something goes sideways after hours. On-call isn't a footnote here. It's a real part of the job, and Prometheus pays standby and on-call premium pay to reflect that.

The leadership piece is equally concrete. You'll hire and train your maintenance staff, mentor them through technical challenges, and resolve the interpersonal friction that comes with any crew operating under pressure. The community's residents (Prometheus calls them Neighbors) expect fast, quality responses. Your team's consistency is what makes that possible.

  • Minimum 5 years apartment maintenance experience, 2 years supervisory
  • At least 3 certifications from recognized maintenance or trades programs (BOMA, IREM, vocational)
  • Solid knowledge of California safety regulations and the ability to apply them operationally
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. occasionally; role is physically active
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Available for on-call response as needed

What Makes Prometheus a Different Operator

Prometheus holds its properties long-term and reinvests in them. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that distinction has real operational consequences: capital projects get funded, standards don't erode to protect short-term NOI, and the team you build is meant to stay. The compensation range of $38.75 to $45.00 per hour reflects the Bay Area market and the scope of the role, and the bonus structure includes semi-annual discretionary bonuses, renovation bonuses, and lease-up bonuses where applicable. Benefits include fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision for eligible employees and dependents, 401(k) with employer matching, and tenure-based housing discounts.

Strong candidates for this role aren't just technically sharp. They think about maintenance as an asset preservation function. They know that deferred work has a cost that shows up in capex eventually, and they manage their budgets and vendor relationships accordingly. If you've supervised a team through a renovation cycle or a lease-up and kept physical operations steady while the property was in flux, that experience translates directly here.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Yester Oaks is a residential community where the maintenance supervisor sets the tone for how residents experience their home every single day. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring for that role now, and it's worth understanding what the position actually demands before you apply.

This isn't a solo technician role. You'll lead a maintenance team, coordinate vendor work, manage the unit turn process, and keep a preventative maintenance calendar running across the full property. Budget awareness matters here too: you'll monitor spending, track inventory, and pull in bids when capital work comes up. The make-ready side of the job is yours to own, from scheduling turns to walking vacant units yourself before a new resident gets their keys. If a punch list item slips through, it's on your watch.

On any given weekday, you might start the morning reviewing open work orders and assigning them across your team, check in with a vendor finishing up a scope from last week, walk a turned unit to confirm it's truly move-in ready, and spend part of the afternoon troubleshooting an HVAC issue that came in overnight. The afternoon might end with a quick team huddle or a call with the office about an upcoming lease-up push. The hours are Monday through Friday, 8 to 5, but there's an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That part is real, and it's worth factoring into your decision.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the combination of hands-on technical skill and genuine patience with people. Supervisors who only fix things well but struggle to mentor or communicate tend to create friction on the team and with residents. Hawthorne's culture leans into connection and accountability together, so someone who leads by example and doesn't disappear when things get hard will thrive here. Prior lead technician or supervisory experience is a real differentiator, not just a checkbox.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least 3 years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience (HVAC, plumbing, or electrical)
  • Prior supervisory or lead technician experience, strongly preferred
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA certification (required)
  • CPO certification (preferred, and required in some states)

Compensation includes hourly pay plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also offers an internal career path program and education reimbursement specifically for maintenance skills development, which is a meaningful perk for someone who wants to keep growing in the trade.

If you're the kind of person who takes quiet pride in a well-run property and wants a team that will actually invest in your career, this role at Yester Oaks is worth a close look.

job.title: Limpiador Residencial
job.description:
Comstock's residential porter role at their Ashburn, VA property is the kind of position where your presence is felt the moment someone walks through the front door. The cleanliness and condition of common areas shape how residents and visitors feel about where they live or work, and that's the direct result of this person's daily effort.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're responsible for keeping lobbies, restrooms, sidewalks, and shared spaces clean and presentable across assigned areas. That means following scheduled checklists, responding to cleaning concerns as they come up, and completing pressure washing assignments in the areas management designates. You'll also support event setup and breakdown when the property hosts gatherings, which adds some variety to the routine but also means weekend and occasional off-hours availability is part of the deal.

You'll maintain your supply closet and storage areas in good order, track cleaning inventory, and handle chemicals according to safety standards. At the end of each shift, you'll complete required documentation and hand off properly to the next person. If a teammate is out, you may be asked to cover. The work is physical: you'll be on your feet for extended stretches, lifting up to 50 pounds, working in varying temperatures indoors and out, and sometimes in conditions that include dust, fumes, or cleaning agents.

One thing that sets this role apart from a standard janitorial position is the guest interaction piece. You're wearing a ParkX Porter uniform, arriving before your shift starts, and greeting residents and visitors as part of the job. That's not incidental. Comstock expects the person in this role to carry themselves with a service mindset, not just a cleaning mindset.

Who Tends to Do Well Here

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Flexibility to work weekends and during events or high-activity periods
  • Strong reliability and personal accountability
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal supervision
  • Able to manage multiple tasks and prioritize in a busy environment
  • A genuine ease with people from different backgrounds

The candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the longest cleaning resume. They're the ones who show up on time every shift, notice things before they become problems, and treat every resident interaction as part of the job rather than an interruption to it. Self-direction matters here because you won't always have someone looking over your shoulder.

Benefits and Growth

Comstock offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, and life insurance. There's annual funding for professional development, a parental leave program, and free parking with EV charging on site. The company also notes that this role sits within a growing portfolio, which means advancement opportunities exist for people who prove themselves.

For someone who wants a foothold in property operations, this kind of role builds real familiarity with how a residential property runs. Porters who develop strong relationships with maintenance and management teams often move into maintenance tech or lead porter positions over time.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager ($1,000 Sign-On Bonus)
job.description:
Property maintenance teams at well-run communities carry two responsibilities at once: keeping current residents comfortable and keeping the asset in shape for the long term. The Assistant Maintenance Manager role at Bozzuto's Issaquah, WA property sits squarely at that intersection, with a $1,000 sign-on bonus attached.

What the Job Actually Involves

Day to day, you're resolving service tickets across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair while also keeping the make-ready process moving. Turns need to be completed on time so units can be leased and new residents can move in without delays. That means your attention to detail on a punch list matters as much as your technical skill with a wrench.

Beyond reactive work, you'll run preventative maintenance programs, handle grounds upkeep, manage snow removal, and keep all property systems operating at peak efficiency. You'll also make sure the team operates within applicable safety codes and OSHA standards, with zero tolerance for shortcuts that create liability. On-call rotation and weekend availability come with the territory.

This is a leadership role, not just a senior technician position. You'll be expected to set the standard for how the team works and how they treat residents. Strong candidates know how to motivate a crew, not just outperform one.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • 5 or more years in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • Supervisory experience, or a clear track record of leading others informally
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of OSHA, risk management, and MSDS standards
  • Hands-on proficiency with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Exposure to complex mechanical systems (boilers, chillers, central plant, split systems) is a plus
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property management technology platforms
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb stairs, use ladders, and work in varying weather

The salary range runs from $60,000 to approximately $66,747, with additional bonus opportunities beyond the sign-on. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of paid time off plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: the ability to think like an owner about asset condition. Technicians fix what's broken. The right person for this role notices what's about to break, flags it, and builds it into the preventative maintenance schedule before it becomes a resident complaint or a capital expense. That instinct is harder to train than any technical skill.

job.title: Community Manager - Cortland at the Nations
job.description:
Community managers at large institutional operators like Cortland carry a different weight than the title might suggest. You're not just running a property. You're running a business with a P&L, a team, a sales floor, and a resident base, all at once, every day. This role at Cortland at the Nations in Nashville puts you at the center of all of it.

What the Job Actually Involves

The Nations is one of Nashville's most actively developing neighborhoods, which means your community sits in a market where prospects have real options and leasing pressure is genuine. Your job is to make sure your occupancy, revenue, and NOI targets don't just get met on paper but hold up month over month. That means coaching a leasing team through traffic peaks and slow stretches alike, managing vendor relationships without letting costs drift, and doing regular property walks that catch problems before they become expenses or complaints.

Financially, you own the budget. Cortland expects community managers to read their numbers, understand variance, and make decisions based on what the T-12 and current KPIs are actually telling them. If delinquency creeps up or concessions are eroding revenue, you're the one who needs to see it early and respond. The corporate infrastructure is there to support you, but the community-level accountability sits with you.

On the people side, you'll handle escalated resident concerns that the team can't resolve. Some of those conversations are straightforward. Some aren't. The job requires genuine composure when a resident is frustrated, a vendor has dropped the ball, or a make-ready is running late and a move-in is scheduled for tomorrow morning.

Who Fits This Role Well

  • 2 or more years leading a sales team in a high-volume, short-cycle environment. Multifamily experience is a plus, but Cortland has also hired strong candidates from hospitality, luxury retail, and premium automotive.
  • A real track record of hitting occupancy and NOI targets, not just participating in the process.
  • Experience with property management software and CRM tools. Comfort using data to make decisions rather than relying on gut feel alone.
  • A high school diploma is required. A bachelor's degree is preferred but not a dealbreaker if the experience is there.
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing regulations and OSHA standards. Compliance isn't optional at any level of this role.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is the ability to hold two things at once: genuine care for the resident experience and disciplined focus on financial performance. Managers who lean too far into one tend to struggle. The ones who last build teams that convert traffic, retain residents, and control costs without those goals feeling like they're in conflict.

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator, which means design, construction, and management all sit under one roof. For a community manager, that structure brings real resources but also real accountability to brand standards and internal partners. If you want autonomy without isolation and a clear line between your work and the portfolio's performance, that setup works. If you prefer a smaller, more informal operation, this probably isn't the right fit.

job.title: Community Manager - Cortland Hickory Hollow
job.description:
Cortland has built a reputation as one of the top ten multifamily owners and operators in the country, and that scale shows up at the property level. As Community Manager at Cortland Hickory Hollow in Antioch, TN, you're not just running a community. You're running a multimillion-dollar asset with full accountability for NOI, occupancy, team performance, and resident experience.

This role covers the full spectrum. On any given day you might be reviewing a T-12 with an eye toward expense variances, coaching a leasing consultant through a stalled pipeline, walking the property for curb appeal and punch list items, and then fielding an escalated resident concern before the afternoon is done. Cortland operates with centralized support teams, which means you have resources that smaller operators can't offer, but it also means you need to be comfortable aligning with corporate partners and navigating competing priorities without losing momentum onsite.

The financial piece carries real weight here. You'll own budget management, forecasting, and expense control while working to hit and exceed NOI targets. That means knowing where your revenue leakage is, understanding your concessions strategy, and keeping delinquency tight. Cortland uses data and KPIs to drive decisions, so comfort with property management software and a willingness to dig into the numbers isn't optional.

On the leasing side, you'll set goals, monitor conversion rates and traffic, and coach your team to close. Cortland's brand sits at the premium end, so the sales culture here leans toward hospitality and lifestyle, not just unit counts. If you've come up through Class A or lease-up environments, that instinct will translate well.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in this role is the ability to hold both sides of the job at once. A lot of managers can run operations or lead a sales team, but doing both well, consistently, while keeping a team aligned and a resident base satisfied, is where most people show their ceiling. Cortland is also a vertically integrated firm with in-house design and construction, which means there's genuine career mobility for managers who perform.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • At least two years of measurable sales leadership in a high-velocity environment, multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or similar
  • Demonstrated track record hitting occupancy and NOI targets, not just familiarity with the concepts
  • Experience coaching and developing onsite teams with real accountability structures
  • Financial acumen across budgeting, forecasting, and expense management
  • Proficiency in property management software and CRM tools; comfort using social platforms for marketing and brand presence
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and OSHA standards

Antioch sits in the southeast Nashville metro, a submarket that has seen consistent multifamily demand tied to the broader Nashville growth story. Residents here expect quality, and Cortland's brand standard reinforces that expectation at every touchpoint. If you've managed premium product and understand what it takes to deliver that experience without letting operations slip, this is a role worth a serious look.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and a tenant on the fourth floor has flagged a billing discrepancy on their CAM reconciliation. Before you've had your second cup of coffee, you're pulling lease abstracts, cross-referencing the recovery methodology with the management agreement, and coordinating with accounting to get a clean answer before end of day. That's the texture of this role at Lincoln Property Company.

The Work Itself

Lincoln is one of the larger third-party commercial management platforms in the country, with a portfolio that spans office, retail, industrial, and more. This Assistant Property Manager position is based in Washington, DC and supports the day-to-day operations of a commercial property or portfolio. The scope is genuinely broad: you'll touch financial reporting, vendor procurement, tenant relations, lease administration, and property inspections, often within the same week.

On the financial side, you'll help prepare monthly reporting packages and budget materials for institutional clients, review vendor invoices against contract terms and authorization limits, and assist with tenant billing accuracy and aging review. CAM reconciliations and operating expense recovery (OpX) are part of the territory, which means you'll need to get comfortable reading lease language and translating it into billing logic.

Operationally, you'll coordinate tenant move-ins and move-outs, keep vacant spaces tour-ready, and assist with vendor bidding and contract documentation. Emergency preparedness planning and drill coordination are also on the list. This is a 100% in-office role with occasional property travel, and the position requires availability for after-hours needs when situations demand it.

Who Fits This Role

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, with 1 to 2 years of commercial property management or related experience
  • Solid working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel for financial calculations and reporting
  • Comfortable reading and interpreting lease documents, vendor contracts, and management agreements
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for tenant-facing and client-facing work
  • Organized, analytically minded, and able to manage competing priorities without losing accuracy
  • Compensation range is $70,000 to $75,000 annually

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is comfort with the financial layer of commercial management. CAM reconciliations and OpEx recovery aren't glamorous, but they're where tenant disputes get triggered and where client trust is built or eroded. Candidates who've handled even basic lease administration or billing review will ramp faster and carry more weight earlier.

From a career trajectory standpoint, this role builds exactly the skill set that feeds into a Property Manager position on a commercial portfolio. The combination of client reporting, lease administration, vendor oversight, and tenant relations is the full foundation. Lincoln's platform is large enough that internal movement is realistic, and the institutional client exposure you get here translates well whether you stay in third-party management or eventually move to an owner-operator or REIT environment.

job.title: Regional Facilities Manager - Seattle
job.description:
Regional facilities work in multifamily is one of those roles where the job description reads like a checklist but the actual work is constant judgment calls. Which site needs a visit this week versus which one can wait? Which capital project is behind because of a vendor problem versus a site team problem? Which maintenance supervisor is quietly struggling and needs coaching versus which one just needs to be left alone to do good work? That's the texture of this role at Asset Living, a third-party management company overseeing a portfolio that spans multifamily, affordable housing, build-to-rent, and student housing across the country.
