The role is based in Mountain View, California.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Running a multifamily community in Mobile takes a specific blend of financial discipline and people instinct. Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Community Manager to bring both to one of their Alabama communities. This is a role where your sharpest skills get used every single day: budget interpretation, delinquency management, leasing strategy, team coaching, and resident retention.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work

On the financial side, you'll own the community's P&L in a real operational sense. That means reading reports, managing collections, overseeing deposit accounting, and tracking delinquency with enough precision to make timely decisions. You'll work in Yardi and Knock, so familiarity with both platforms matters. Understanding how occupancy, concessions, and renewal rates interact to affect NOI is the kind of thinking Hawthorne expects from this seat.

On the people side, you're coaching a team that spans leasing and maintenance. That means hiring, training, running weekly meetings, and holding people accountable while keeping morale intact. You'll also handle escalated resident concerns directly and plan community events that actually build retention rather than just fill a calendar. Managing online reputation is part of the job too, which requires both thick skin and good judgment about when and how to respond publicly.

Leasing isn't delegated away from this role. You'll conduct tours, respond to leads, and guide prospects through the process when the team needs support. Keeping occupancy healthy in a market like Mobile requires attention to pricing strategy and renewal timing, not just foot traffic.

What the Background Should Look Like

  • At least two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • Six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Hands-on experience with Yardi and Knock, preferred
  • CAM, CAPS, a real estate license, or a property management license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED required; valid driver's license required

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The candidates who thrive in this role aren't just competent operators. They read a T-12 and connect what they see to decisions they make that week. They give feedback to their team without waiting for a performance review cycle. And they treat resident concerns as real problems to solve rather than complaints to manage. Hawthorne's internal culture, which they call Live It, puts genuine emphasis on service and connection. Managers who lead with that sincerity rather than performing it tend to build communities with lower turnover and stronger online ratings.

Hawthorne's career path program is worth noting here. Community Manager to Regional Manager is a real trajectory within the company, and the Learning and Development investment they describe reflects that. If you're at the point in your career where you want structured growth toward a regional role, this is the kind of platform that makes that progression concrete rather than theoretical.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off to maintain a 40-hour week. Evening and weekend availability may come up for resident events or community needs. Compensation includes base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses.

job.title: Market Maintenance Manager II
job.description:
John M. Corcoran & Company has been managing residential communities in New England since 1951, and The Halstead in Plymouth, MA is one of the properties where that long history shows up in day-to-day expectations. They want a Maintenance Manager who treats the physical condition of a community as a direct reflection of the people who live and work there. That's the culture here. It's not just about closing work orders.

In this role, you'd be responsible for the full scope of maintenance operations at The Halstead. That means overseeing work orders, conducting inspections, keeping up with preventive maintenance schedules, and making sure unit turns happen on time and to standard. You'd also be supervising a team that includes maintenance techs, janitorial staff, and grounds crew, which means your day involves as much people management as it does hands-on work. Coordinating with vendors, tracking supplies against budget, and keeping accurate records all fall in your court too.

The on-call rotation is real. After-hours emergencies happen, and this role is part of the response. That's worth knowing upfront. The regular schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, but you'll need to be reachable when things come up outside those hours. If that kind of responsibility fits how you already think about the job, it won't feel like a burden.

What they're looking for

  • High school diploma or equivalent; relevant experience counts
  • At least 3 years in trade or general building maintenance
  • Working knowledge of electrical, mechanical, and building systems
  • Demonstrated ability to lead a team and stay organized under pressure
  • Comfort with safety procedures, reporting, and budget adherence

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one isn't just technical range, though that matters. It's the ability to keep a team accountable without micromanaging, and to communicate clearly with both residents and the management office. The Maintenance Manager at a community like this sits in the middle of a lot of relationships: residents who want things fixed fast, a property management team tracking make-ready timelines and capex spend, and vendors who need clear direction. The people who thrive in this seat tend to be organized communicators who also know how to get their hands dirty when needed.

JMC offers competitive pay in the range of $38.25 to $44.25 per hour, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, paid time off and holidays, and a 401(k) with a company match. The company has a notable track record of long-tenured employees, which often signals something real about how people are treated once they're in the door.

job.title: Seasonal Grounds Person
job.description:
Grounds work at a residential property is physical, repetitive, and genuinely important. The residents notice every piece of litter, every overgrown edge, every dead patch of grass. That's the job: keeping the exterior of The Ledges in Weymouth looking the way it should, day after day, without much fanfare.

Skills This Role Draws On Constantly

This isn't a role that asks for a long list of credentials. What it actually requires is the ability to operate landscaping equipment correctly and safely, a good eye for what looks off, and the discipline to work independently without someone checking in every hour. You'll mow, trim, prune, and plant. You'll handle irrigation. You'll do daily trash and pet waste removal, which is unglamorous but non-negotiable on any well-run residential property. Curb appeal is the first thing a prospective resident sees, and it's one of the things current residents notice when something slips.

Beyond the landscaping basics, you'll assist with exterior repairs, painting, fence work, and general installations. The role also includes identifying and flagging safety hazards before they become problems. Snow removal and ice treatment are listed as seasonal needs, which suggests this position may extend into colder months depending on the property's staffing structure.

The Practical Reality of the Work

The schedule is straightforward: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. That's a real advantage compared to maintenance roles that carry on-call or after-hours obligations. You're not getting emergency calls at midnight. The tradeoff is that the work is outdoors and physical regardless of weather conditions, and the summer months in Massachusetts mean heat and humidity during peak grounds season.

This is a temporary, seasonal position. John M. Corcoran and Company has been operating since 1951 and is considered one of the more established residential real estate firms in New England. For someone who wants a foot in the door at a company with genuine longevity and a track record of internal growth, a seasonal grounds role is a legitimate starting point. Property management companies often pull from their own seasonal and hourly workers when porter, maintenance tech, or facilities coordinator openings come up. Showing you're reliable and detail-oriented in this role is the kind of thing that gets noticed.

What Makes Someone Stand Out Here

  • Actual hands-on experience with landscaping equipment, not just a general willingness to learn
  • Comfort working without direct supervision for stretches of the day
  • The habit of noticing things: a hazard, a broken fixture, a section of fence that needs attention
  • Clear, basic communication with supervisors and vendors when something needs to be escalated

Pay runs between $16.00 and $18.75 per hour. If you've done grounds or landscaping work before and want a structured, predictable schedule at a well-established residential community, this is worth a close look.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

This position runs on a specific combination of technical depth and team leadership. HVAC troubleshooting is the core technical skill here. EPA Type II or Universal certification is required, and Cottonwood expects someone who can diagnose a refrigerant issue, a failing capacitor, or a heat exchanger problem without waiting on a vendor. Beyond HVAC, you'll work across electrical, plumbing, and appliance repair, so broad mechanical competency matters more than being a specialist in one trade. A valid driver's license is required.

The leadership side is equally weighted. You'll hire, schedule, and develop maintenance techs and community care associates. That means classroom time, hands-on coaching, and setting the standard for how work gets done. If your team cuts corners on a punch list, that shows up in resident satisfaction scores and re-leasing timelines. The best supervisors in this role treat training as an operational investment, not an interruption.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Fox Point at Old Farm is a residential community in Millcreek, UT, and your operational fingerprints are on everything. Service tickets need timely completion and meticulous follow-through. A resident who waits four days for a plumbing fix is a resident who doesn't renew. The make-ready and turn process is another high-stakes responsibility. Every day a unit sits unready between residents is a day of lost revenue, so your ability to run a tight turn schedule directly affects NOI. You'll also own grounds upkeep, building cleanliness, and compliance with applicable building, county, and safety codes. Emergency coverage is a real part of the job. You'll maintain 24/7 on-call scheduling across your team, which means building a rotation that works and holding people accountable to it.

One thing that separates strong candidates here: the ability to hold quality standards under schedule pressure. Turns are often the friction point where supervisors either build a reputation for reliability or lose it. Coming in with a system for punch lists and a habit of walking completed units before handing them to leasing is a meaningful differentiator.

Working at Cottonwood Residential

Cottonwood has positioned itself as an innovation-minded operator, notably as an early adopter of self-guided tours. That culture of process improvement extends to maintenance. You're not walking into a rigid, unchanging operation. There's expectation that you'll bring ideas and refine how the team works.

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification required
  • Considerable HVAC troubleshooting experience expected
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Benefits including full health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within 30 days
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • Three weeks PTO eligible in the first year, plus 10.5 paid holidays
  • Competitive pay with bonus structure

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Role and What It Demands

An Assistant Community Manager at a multifamily property sits at the intersection of leasing performance, financial accountability, and daily operations. You're not just supporting the Community Manager; you're the person who keeps the gears turning when attention pulls in three directions at once. Waypoint Management Services is hiring for this position at their Daytona Beach community, and the scope here is genuinely broad.

Day to day, you'll work alongside the Community Manager on everything from rent collection and delinquency follow-up to tracking make-ready schedules and occupancy reports. You'll support the leasing team, which means coaching and observing, not just filling in when someone's out. You'll help execute marketing strategies, conduct market surveys, and recommend pricing adjustments based on what you're seeing in occupancy trends and competitor activity. Financial reporting, lease records, renewal tracking, and administrative accuracy round out the operational side. Weekend availability is part of the rotation here, which is standard at the ACM level and worth factoring into your schedule.

Yardi experience is preferred, and strong command of Microsoft Office is expected. Comfort with social media as a leasing tool is part of the picture too. A high school diploma is the baseline education requirement, and the role targets candidates with at least two years in leasing, sales, or a hospitality-adjacent field.

What This Role Builds vs. What It Requires

Here's the distinction worth drawing clearly: this role requires organizational discipline, financial literacy at the property level, and the ability to hold a leasing team accountable to performance. What it builds is the full Community Manager skill set. You'll develop comfort reading a rent roll for risk signals, tightening delinquency processes before they affect NOI, and making pricing recommendations you can defend with data. Those are exactly the competencies that move someone into the CM seat.

Strong ACM candidates tend to show up with one thing average candidates don't: they treat the financial reports as a story, not a checklist. If you can look at a T-12 and ask the right follow-up questions, or spot a pattern in concessions that signals a leasing strategy problem, you'll stand out here. That analytical instinct, paired with genuine relationship-building on the resident side, is what separates candidates who plateau at this level from those who advance.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Monthly leasing and renewal bonuses
  • Employee housing discount program
  • 120 hours PTO in year one, increasing with tenure, plus two floating days
  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage subsidized and effective on day one
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Commuter benefits, employee referral program, and professional development training
  • Employee recognition monetary rewards

Waypoint is an equal opportunity employer. All hiring decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business need.

job.title: Property Manager - 300-500 Units - 175
job.description:
Managing a 300 to 500 unit asset for an owner-operator is a different job than managing for a third-party fee management shop. When the company owns what you're running, the scrutiny on NOI, delinquency, and capex decisions is real and ongoing. Berkshire Residential Investments operates that way, and the Property Manager role at Soho Parkway reflects it.

What the Role Actually Involves

This is a full-scope property management position. You'll own the financial performance of the asset alongside your Regional Manager, which means budgets, monthly and quarterly forecasts, and capital planning aren't things that happen to you. You build them. You need to understand how an operational call (a concession, a staffing decision, a deferred punch list item) shows up in the financials later. If you can read a T-12 and explain variance, you're already ahead of most applicants.

On the people side, you'll recruit, hire, train, and manage your on-site team. That includes performance reviews and the harder conversations that come with them. Berkshire puts real weight on team development, so if your instinct is to hoard knowledge rather than build the people around you, this probably isn't the right fit.

Resident communication and marketing round out the day-to-day. You'll handle communications on service requests, concerns, and community engagement, and you'll stay active on the promotional and content side. Traffic and occupancy don't manage themselves.

What Berkshire Is Looking For

  • Five or more years in multifamily property management
  • Demonstrated experience with budgeting and financial reporting
  • Comfort with property management software and financial analysis tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Proven leadership, with the ability to hire and develop a team
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and staff from diverse backgrounds

The posting mentions a sense of humor explicitly, which is either a cultural signal or a warning. Probably both.

A Note on What Separates Strong Candidates

We've seen a lot of property managers who can hold occupancy in a stable asset. The ones who stand out at owner-operator companies can also explain why a decision they made in Q2 showed up as favorable variance in Q3. At this unit count, you're large enough that small operational inefficiencies compound fast, but not so large that you can hide behind layers of staff. You're close to the work. The best candidates for this role are comfortable being accountable for both the numbers and the culture on the same day, sometimes before lunch.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development planning, and competitive benefits. The company is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion across all employment practices.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
You're standing in a unit, work order on your phone, and you've already spotted two things the previous tech missed. That instinct, the ability to assess a space and think three steps ahead, is exactly what this role asks of you from day one.

The Work Itself

Lessen operates a tech-enabled property services platform that manages work orders at significant scale, completing over 3.5 million annually across a portfolio exceeding one million properties. As a Field Maintenance Technician in Seattle, you're the hands-on execution layer of that system. You'll own your work orders from dispatch to close-out, manage per-job budgets, and deliver maintenance across a mix of residential and commercial properties in the local portfolio.

This isn't a reactive, break-fix-only position. Lessen's model emphasizes quality over volume, which means you're expected to think through a repair rather than just patch it. You'll work a weekday schedule with no on-call rotation, which is a real differentiator compared to most in-house property maintenance roles where after-hours calls are part of the deal.

The company provides a fleet vehicle with a fuel card, a monthly tool and equipment allowance, and a cell phone allowance. OSHA training is provided. A sign-on bonus and quarterly discretionary bonuses up to 5% of quarterly earnings are also part of the compensation structure, with a base pay range starting at $23 to $27 per hour depending on skill level and verifiable experience.

What This Role Requires and What It Builds

The baseline requirement is at least three years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a skilled trade. You need to arrive able to manage general repairs independently, read a work order critically, and handle budgets at the job level without hand-holding. Those are entry requirements, not things you'll develop here.

What the role builds is different. Working across a diverse portfolio through a platform that tracks performance data gives you exposure to how maintenance operations are measured and optimized at scale. That's a skill set that translates directly into lead technician and field maintenance manager roles, which Lessen explicitly supports as growth paths. Techs who advance here tend to be the ones who treat each work order as a diagnostic exercise rather than a task to close out quickly.

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on property maintenance or trade experience, verifiable
  • Comfort working independently across multiple properties in a given day
  • Ability to manage job-level budgets and document work accurately through a tech platform
  • Solution-oriented approach to repairs, not just symptom treatment
  • Valid driver's license required for fleet vehicle use

One honest note on what separates strong candidates here: Lessen's platform-driven model means your work is tracked and visible in ways that traditional in-house roles don't always surface. Techs who are consistent, thorough, and accurate in their documentation stand out quickly. Those who rely on informal workarounds or incomplete close-outs will find the model less forgiving than a single-site job might be.

job.title: Assistant Maintenance Manager ($3,500 Sign on Bonus)
job.description:
It's a Tuesday afternoon and three service tickets just came in while you're overseeing a make-ready on a vacated unit. The HVAC tech needs a decision, a resident is waiting on a plumbing fix, and the grounds crew has a question about the week's schedule. This is the job.

What the Role Actually Involves

Bozzuto is hiring an Assistant Maintenance Manager for their community in Venice, FL. The salary range is $52,000 to $55,000, and there's a $3,500 sign-on bonus attached to this one. The role sits between hands-on trade work and team leadership, which means you're not just fixing things. You're making sure others fix things correctly, on time, and to a standard.

Day-to-day, you're managing apartment turns, running the preventative maintenance program, and keeping service tickets moving so residents aren't waiting. You'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair directly when needed, and you'll be responsible for keeping the building components operating at peak efficiency. General upkeep, grounds maintenance, and safety compliance are all part of the scope. You'll also participate in the emergency on-call rotation, so if evenings and weekends are a dealbreaker, this isn't your role.

What Bozzuto Needs From You

  • At least 5 years of hands-on experience in the trades, facilities, or residential building maintenance
  • HVAC, EPA, and/or NAPE certification
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and appliance repair
  • Familiarity with OSHA, MSDS, and risk management practices
  • Basic carpentry, drywall, and painting skills
  • Experience with complex mechanical systems (central plant, split systems, boilers, chillers) is a plus
  • Some supervisory or leadership experience, even informal
  • Comfort with technology platforms and basic Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Physical ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds frequently, climb ladders, and work in varying outdoor conditions

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 20 days of PTO plus holidays, a 401k with company match, and tuition reimbursement.

What separates the strong candidates here is the combination of trade depth and people skills. We've seen plenty of excellent technicians who struggle when they step into a supervisory role, and we've seen leaders who can't command respect on the shop floor because their technical knowledge is thin. This role requires both. If you can diagnose a split system issue and coach a junior tech through the repair without taking over, you're the profile Bozzuto is looking for.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Monte Viejo
job.description:
A prospect walks in on a Saturday morning without a tour scheduled. You're the first person they meet. What happens next shapes whether they sign a lease or walk out and call your competitor down the street.

That's the core of this role at Monte Viejo, an Olympus Property community in Phoenix. As a Leasing Consultant, you're the first impression and the closing conversation. You handle tours, explain floor plan options, prepare lease paperwork, and get new residents ready for move-in day. You also respond to current resident concerns, keep your traffic data current in the resident database, and help plan community events that keep people engaged after they've already signed.

What the Job Actually Involves

Day-to-day, you're doing a mix of sales, customer service, and light administration. You'll show units, follow up on leads, close leases, and process the paperwork that goes with each new move-in. You'll also visit local businesses and locators to drive traffic to the property. Resident events are part of the job too, including some after-hours availability each month.

The schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday with rotating hours between 9 AM and 6 PM, and both weekend days are required. Hours can shift depending on the property's needs.

What Olympus Is Looking For

  • At least one year of apartment leasing experience
  • Comfort with the full leasing cycle: from greeting a walk-in to getting keys in a resident's hand
  • Strong follow-through on leads and a genuine interest in helping people find the right home
  • Ability to work weekends consistently and attend occasional evening events
  • Familiarity with entering and maintaining data in a resident management system

Pay starts between $19 and $22 per hour depending on experience, and the role comes with monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses. Olympus also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, an apartment rental allowance, and pet insurance, among other benefits.

One thing worth knowing: strong leasing consultants here tend to separate themselves not by being the most talkative, but by being the most prepared. Knowing the product cold, understanding your comp set in the Phoenix market, and following up consistently after tours are what actually move the needle on occupancy. Consultants who treat every Saturday walk-in with the same energy as a scheduled appointment tend to be the ones earning the better commission checks.

Olympus has been named a Top Employer by the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running (2023, 2024, and 2025). They're a third-party management company with a defined career pathing program, so this role can realistically lead to an Assistant Manager position for someone who performs well and wants to move into operations.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - The Residences at Escaya
job.description:
Leasing is often treated as entry-level, but anyone who's worked a busy lease-up or carried a community through a rough occupancy dip knows the role takes real skill. At The Residences at Escaya in Chula Vista, Olympus Property is looking for a Leasing Consultant who can handle the full cycle: generating traffic, converting prospects, executing lease paperwork, and keeping current residents happy enough to renew.

What This Role Actually Involves

You're the first person a prospect meets, and often the last voice they hear before signing. That means your day moves between showing units, fielding phone and email inquiries, entering data into the resident database, and preparing move-in files. It's not a sit-at-the-desk job. You'll also get out into the community, visiting locators and local businesses to keep your property's name in front of referral sources, and you'll help plan and run resident events. Those events aren't optional extras; they're part of how this property holds occupancy and reduces turn.

The schedule is full-time, Monday through Friday with rotating hours in that 9-to-6 window, Saturdays required, and some after-hours availability for resident functions each month. That last part is worth being honest about: if evenings and occasional weekends are a hard no for you, this posting probably isn't your fit.

Base pay runs $18 to $20 per hour depending on experience and location, with monthly leasing commissions and renewal bonuses layered on top. Bilingual candidates are preferred, which makes sense given the Chula Vista market.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

A year of apartment leasing experience is the floor, not the ceiling. What actually moves the needle in a role like this is someone who closes without being pushy, handles objections on pricing or availability without getting rattled, and understands that a resident who renewed quietly in month 12 is just as valuable as a new lease signed this week. Renewal bonuses are part of the comp structure here for exactly that reason.

  • Minimum one year of apartment leasing experience
  • Bilingual (Spanish preferred given the local market)
  • Comfortable with sales goals and tracking your own performance
  • Able to work Saturdays and occasional evenings for resident events
  • Organized enough to manage lease paperwork accurately under busy conditions

Olympus Property has been recognized as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years. The benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Career pathing is listed explicitly, which in our industry is worth paying attention to. Leasing Consultant is a natural on-ramp to Assistant Manager and eventually Property Manager for people who develop their numbers sense alongside their people skills.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Canopy at Citrus Park
job.description:
It's 10 AM on a Tuesday and you've already turned two work orders: a leaking shut-off valve under a kitchen sink and a tripped breaker that had a resident convinced her oven was dead. That's the rhythm at a property like Canopy at Citrus Park, where your technical range matters as much as your speed.

What This Role Actually Covers

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer in the National Apartment Association three years running, and their maintenance teams are a big reason why. At Canopy at Citrus Park in Tampa, you'll work alongside a service team and leasing office to keep apartment homes and common areas running at a high standard. The scope here is genuinely broad.

  • HVAC preventative maintenance and diagnosis, including filter replacements and coil cleaning (EPA/HVAC license required)
  • Plumbing repairs ranging from fixture replacements to minor installations on sinks, showers, and toilets
  • Appliance work on refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers, ovens, and microwaves
  • Electrical fixture and switch repairs or replacements
  • Lock changes, lockouts, and door hardware repairs
  • Grounds upkeep and pool area maintenance alongside interior and exterior common areas
  • Tracking all work through property management software and coordinating daily priorities with the Lead Maintenance Technician

This is a full-time position, Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with availability needed for after-hours emergency calls. The starting rate is $21 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses available for eligible team members.

What You Bring and Where It Takes You

You'll need at least two years of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential, apartment, or commercial setting, plus a current EPA/HVAC certification. Beyond the license, the candidates who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who can diagnose quickly without over-ordering parts and who communicate clearly enough that residents feel heard even when a fix takes a day or two.

Tampa's rental market runs hot, with strong occupancy across garden-style communities keeping maintenance teams busy year-round. Humidity and heat cycles here are hard on HVAC equipment, so your coil-cleaning and filter discipline isn't just routine work. It directly protects NOI by reducing emergency service calls and extending equipment life.

From a career standpoint, a well-rounded technician role like this one is a direct path toward Lead Maintenance and eventually Service Manager. Olympus specifically offers career pathing as part of their structure, which means the progression isn't just theoretical. Technicians who develop strong HVAC skills, get comfortable with software-based work order systems, and build a reputation for consistent make-readies tend to move up faster than those who specialize too narrowly too early.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, and an apartment rental allowance. The sabbatical benefit and team trips are less common perks at this level and worth noting if work-life balance factors into your decision.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, and that tenure shows in how they actually operate. Headquartered in Richmond, Virginia, they own and manage more than 60 apartment communities across five states. This Leasing Consultant opening is at The Bowery at Southside in downtown Fort Worth, a position where you're the face of the community from day one.

What's worth knowing upfront: Weinstein isn't looking for someone who already knows the difference between a T-12 and a T-3. They're looking for someone who connects with people easily, follows through, and brings consistent energy to a role that's genuinely varied. If you have retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing background, that translates here. The training program is hands-on and real, not a binder you flip through once.

A typical day involves greeting prospects, walking units, following up on leads, handling resident concerns, and keeping the office running smoothly. You're not parked at a desk. The role mixes leasing activity with light administrative work and property walk-throughs, so the day moves fast. Saturdays are part of the schedule on a rotating basis with your team. The starting rate is $19 per hour, with quarterly bonuses on top of that.

Downtown Fort Worth has seen real momentum in its multifamily market over the past few years, with renter demand holding strong in urban-core product. The Southside neighborhood sits at an interesting intersection of walkability and value, which gives you a genuine story to tell prospective residents rather than a generic pitch.

What Weinstein is looking for

  • Strong verbal and written communication, warm and confident in both
  • A customer-first instinct, especially when situations get complicated
  • Comfort with shifting priorities without losing focus or composure
  • Team-oriented attitude. You help where it's needed, not just where it's assigned
  • Goal orientation and personal accountability
  • No prior leasing experience required, though a service or sales background is a plus

One thing that separates strong candidates in this kind of role: the ability to hold a real conversation. Leasing software and process can be taught quickly. What can't be taught as easily is the instinct to read a prospect's hesitation, address it honestly, and build enough trust that they want to sign a lease with you specifically. That relational skill matters here more than any credential.

For people who want a career path, not just a paycheck, Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many of their current leaders started exactly where this role begins. Whether that means moving into an Assistant Manager role, taking on a property with more units, or eventually stepping into corporate operations, the infrastructure to grow is there if you put in the work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, and that longevity isn't accidental. The company owns and manages more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, and their Richmond-area portfolio spans communities in Goochland, Henrico, the West End, and Downtown. This Leasing Consultant opening sits within that Abbington West End region, with some flexibility on exact placement depending on fit and availability.

The pay range is $18 to $20 per hour based on experience, plus quarterly bonuses and a $1,500 sign-on bonus (details discussed during the interview). The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9am to 6pm, with rotating Saturdays from 9am to 5pm. There's also an alternative schedule available for candidates who can commit to a fixed five-day week that includes Saturdays, which comes with an additional per-pay-period bonus. If your availability is consistent and you don't mind working Saturdays regularly, that option is worth asking about.

Weinstein is direct about something most apartment companies talk around: prior leasing experience is not required here. What they're actually hiring for is someone who communicates clearly, handles interruptions without losing composure, and genuinely enjoys helping people find a home. The training program is hands-on and structured, not a pile of PDFs and a wish of good luck. That said, expectations are real. This is not a role where you sit at a desk and wait for phone calls. You'll walk units, inspect make-ready homes, work through a punch list with your team, manage administrative tasks in your property management software, and handle resident concerns that don't always arrive at convenient moments.

The honest reality of leasing is that some days you'll show five apartments and convert none, and other days a prospect will sign a lease on the first tour. The rhythm shifts. Resident events, weather-related situations, and last-minute coverage requests are part of the job. The people who thrive here tend to be the ones who don't need every day to be predictable.

From a career standpoint, leasing consultant roles at owner-operated companies like Weinstein often serve as the clearest path into assistant management and eventually property management. You build a real understanding of how a community runs, how to read traffic patterns, and how to talk to residents in ways that reduce delinquency and improve renewals. Those skills carry weight whether you stay on-site or move toward a regional role.

What they're looking for

  • Strong verbal and written communication, especially with prospective and current residents
  • Comfort with sales goals and the ability to follow up without being pushy
  • Willingness to help outside your defined lane when the team needs it
  • Organized and detail-oriented enough to manage leasing paperwork and resident files accurately
  • Availability that includes Saturdays, either on a rotating or fixed basis
  • A stable, professional attitude on difficult days (and there will be some)

Benefits include a rent discount, health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, vacation and sick time, and access to an Employee Assistance Program.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
The Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing is its own category. Residents are signing leases months before they've graduated high school, parents are often the financial decision-makers, and the community turns almost entirely in a compressed summer window. The Community Manager at The Flats on University in Fairfax, Virginia needs a specific combination of skills: financial fluency, people leadership, operational discipline, and the ability to stay steady when three things go wrong at once. If you've managed a conventional apartment community and found the pace comfortable, this role will feel different.

Scion is looking for someone who genuinely understands both sides of property performance. You're reading variances and managing NOI, but you're also walking units during turn, helping move furniture, and handling a punch list alongside your facilities team. The expectation is that you lead from the floor, not from a desk. That's worth knowing before you apply.

What You'll Actually Be Doing Day to Day

The financial responsibilities here are real and broad. You'll prepare annual operating and capital budgets, manage invoice entry and payroll, track concessions and leasing velocity, and report on variances. Entrata is the property management system, and comfort with it matters. Scion also uses Vena for budgeting, Turnable for the electronic turn board, and ClickUp for project management, so you're working across several platforms simultaneously.

The annual turn process deserves its own mention because it's genuinely one of the most demanding stretches in student housing. You'll plan it months in advance, coordinate vendors and staff, manage the financial forecast for the turn, and still be physically present to help punch units and keep things moving. It's organized chaos if you run it well, and actual chaos if you don't.

Outside of turn season, your responsibilities include:

  • Hiring, scheduling, and developing your on-site team, including accountability for after-hours on-call coverage
  • Quarterly apartment inspections and monthly property walks with scorecard documentation
  • Capital expenditure identification and vendor bid management, working with your Regional Manager for approvals above budget thresholds
  • Permit compliance and building code adherence
  • Resident experience oversight through Qualtrics survey data and online reputation management
  • Escalated resident conflict resolution alongside your Assistant General Manager
  • Legal coordination with Scion's internal team for vendor contracts, risk matters, and any court appearances

What Makes the Difference at Scion Specifically

The candidates who do well in this role tend to combine two things that don't always show up together: strong financial ownership and genuine comfort with high-volume resident interaction. Student housing communities see a lot of traffic, a lot of maintenance requests, and a lot of residents who are living independently for the first time. You're managing KPIs and budget performance, but you're also setting the tone for how the team handles a noise complaint at 11pm or a parent calling upset about a charge.

Scion has built a structured career development path, and the General Manager role is intentionally positioned as a leadership development seat. They use Lattice for performance management and invest in learning reimbursement. If you've been in a community manager role that felt like a ceiling, this one is structured to be a step, not a stop.

Three or more years managing a residential community with a team of at least three direct reports is the baseline. Entrata experience is preferred. The role is exempt, includes a discretionary annual bonus, and offers health, dental, vision, 401k matching, and paid parental leave. Work authorization in the U.S. is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Fair Haven Commons)
job.description:
It's 2 a.m. on a Saturday and your week of on-call duty isn't over yet. A resident at Fair Haven Commons has a water leak that can't wait. You handle it, document it, and get back to bed. That's the honest reality of this role, and it's also why the work matters in a way that's hard to replicate in most maintenance jobs.

What This Role Actually Involves

MidPen Housing has been developing and managing affordable housing across Northern California since 1970. Their portfolio covers more than 130 properties serving working families, seniors, and residents with special needs. Fair Haven Commons in Fairfield is one of those communities, and this Maintenance Technician position sits at the center of keeping it functional and livable.

You'll report to the Community Manager and handle a wide range of skilled repairs: electrical work on appliances, fixtures, and circuits; plumbing repairs to water and sewage systems; rough and finish carpentry. You'll also manage unit turns, which means getting vacant units rent-ready within established timeframes through painting, flooring replacement, and fixture installation. Landscaping and irrigation upkeep are part of the job too, along with maintaining clean, well-lit common areas.

Beyond the hands-on work, you'll coordinate with outside contractors, including helping with bid processes and monitoring their work through completion. Preventive maintenance schedules, work order documentation, and supply inventory are all yours to manage. You'll also assist the Community Manager during move-ins, move-outs, and annual inspections.

One aspect that sets this position apart from a standard tech role: you'll provide coaching and oversight to Maintenance Groundskeeper staff. If you've been the person everyone informally turns to on a maintenance team, this role formalizes that.

What MidPen Is Looking for

  • High school diploma or GED with at least three years of maintenance experience, ideally in property management
  • Solid plumbing knowledge and hands-on experience with electrical repairs to appliances, circuits, and fixtures
  • Rough and finish carpentry skills, both structural and cosmetic
  • Basic familiarity with OSHA safety regulations and landscape maintenance practices
  • Comfort with work order software and written documentation
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work in all weather, and handle tasks that involve climbing, bending, and confined spaces
  • Genuine ability to coach and communicate clearly with junior team members

The pay range runs from $27.50 to $30.94 per hour based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP program, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

The candidate who will thrive here isn't just technically capable. They're someone who can hold a full week of on-call responsibility without burning out, who documents their work accurately without being reminded, and who takes the mentorship piece seriously. Affordable housing maintenance carries a layer of accountability that market-rate work sometimes doesn't: the residents you serve often have fewer options if something goes wrong. That context tends to attract people who take the work personally, in the best way.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Essex House & The Merrick)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at two properties in Portland: Essex House and The Merrick. You'll be the first real conversation most prospective residents have with either community, which means your ability to read people quickly and match them to the right apartment matters more than any script. Prometheus calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador, and while that might sound like rebranding, the intent is genuine. You're not just running people through a tour checklist.

On a typical day, you're fielding inquiries, scheduling and conducting tours, following up with prospects, and helping move applications through to signed leases. You're also handling the administrative side: market surveys, rental agreement prep, posting availability, and keeping occupancy data current. Neither side of the job is optional. The leasing numbers matter, and so does the paperwork that supports them.

Weekends are non-negotiable here. Traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, and that's when the properties need coverage most. Your days off will fall during the week. If your personal schedule requires every weekend free, this role isn't the right fit right now.

One honest note about leasing roles in general: you'll encounter prospects who don't qualify, residents who are frustrated about things outside your control, and weeks where traffic is slow and you're still expected to hit your numbers. None of that is unique to Prometheus, but it's worth naming so you're not caught off guard.

What You Bring

  • A background in customer-facing work, whether that's retail, hospitality, sales, or something else entirely. Prometheus hires across industries.
  • Comfort with both the relationship side and the follow-through side. Plenty of people are great with prospects face-to-face but drop the ball on callbacks and paperwork. Strong candidates do both.
  • Self-direction. You'll have support, but you won't be micromanaged through every task.
  • Clear, consistent communication. Written and verbal.
  • Availability to work weekends as part of your regular schedule.

Compensation and Benefits

Base pay runs $21.00 to $23.00 per hour, with a $200 incentive per lease signed. There's also a discretionary semi-annual bonus, weekend shift premium pay, and additional bonus opportunities tied to referrals, lease-ups, and occupancy contests. The benefits package is notably strong for this level of role: Prometheus covers 100% of medical, vision, and dental premiums, including eligible dependents, and offers 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteer time, and tenure-based housing discounts. Your birthday is a paid holiday.

For someone early in a property management career, this role builds real foundational skills. Leasing consultants who develop strong closing habits and learn the operational side of a property, things like reading a market survey or understanding how concessions affect NOI, are well-positioned to move into assistant manager or community manager roles down the road. Prometheus is a vertically integrated company with properties across Portland, Seattle, and the Bay Area, so internal mobility is a realistic path, not just a talking point.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Hawthorne Residential Partners operates one of the larger multifamily portfolios in the Southeast, and this Community Manager opening sits at Hawthorne at the Mill in Myrtle Beach. It's a full-scope role. You own the property's financial performance, occupancy, team, and resident experience. That's not a summary. It's the actual job.

Day to day, you're reading delinquency reports, walking the property, coaching leasing staff, and fielding escalated resident issues before they become bigger problems. You're also the person who makes sure a unit turn gets punched out correctly and that vendors show up when they say they will. The financial side is real: you're managing budgets, reviewing reports in Yardi, tracking renewals, and making pricing decisions that affect NOI. If numbers make you uncomfortable, this role will be a grind.

On the leasing side, you're not just supervising. You'll conduct tours, work leads, and close prospects yourself when the team needs support. Renewals are part of your retention strategy, not an afterthought. You'll also manage the community's social media presence and monitor online reviews, which matters more than most managers expect. A few unaddressed reviews can drag traffic down noticeably.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to keep the hours at 40. Resident events and community needs can push into evenings occasionally. That's the honest version of the schedule.

What Hawthorne is Looking For

  • Two years of property management experience, including time as a Leasing Consultant and Assistant Community Manager
  • At least six months of direct Community Manager experience in multifamily, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and Knock preferred
  • Valid driver's license required; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent required

The candidates who tend to do well in roles like this aren't just organized. They can hold a team accountable without losing the relationship. That balance, between empathy and performance standards, is where a lot of managers struggle. If you've successfully managed a team through a lease-up or a difficult occupancy stretch, that experience translates directly here.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off, paid parental leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance. Hawthorne also has a formal career path program, and the Community Manager to Regional Manager track is a real one within the company, not just a line in a posting.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing Consultants at residential communities like Meridian at Sutton Square sit at the intersection of sales and hospitality. You're often the first person a prospective resident speaks to, and the last one they remember when deciding where to sign. That dual responsibility, converting traffic while keeping current residents happy, shapes everything about this role.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Hawthorne calls this position a Leasing and Live It Specialist, which is a branded title but reflects something real: the expectation is that you bring genuine energy to both sides of the job. On the leasing side, you're conducting personalized tours, following up on phone, email, and web inquiries, processing applications and move-in paperwork, and working toward the community's occupancy and renewal goals. On the resident side, you're coordinating events, fielding concerns with patience, and keeping the office and common areas presentation-ready.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off per week keeps it at 40 hours, though resident events or community needs can occasionally require flexibility beyond the standard hours. That's worth knowing upfront.

You'll also assist with marketing and social media outreach, and you're expected to stay current on competing properties in the area. Raleigh's rental market is competitive, and knowing how Meridian at Sutton Square stacks up against nearby communities helps you have honest, confident conversations with prospects who are comparison shopping.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience is preferred, but it's not a hard requirement. A high school diploma or GED is the minimum education threshold. A CALP certification is a plus if you have it.

What separates strong candidates from average ones in a leasing role isn't just friendliness. It's the ability to read where a prospect is in their decision process and adjust accordingly, whether that's knowing when to push gently on a follow-up call or when to back off and let the apartment sell itself. People who can handle a busy Saturday afternoon, multiple walk-ins, ringing phones, and a renewal question from a current resident, without losing their composure, tend to do well here.

  • Confident communicator across in-person, phone, and digital channels
  • Comfortable with sales follow-up and objection handling without being pushy
  • Genuinely service-oriented, not just professionally polite
  • Coachable and open to learning Hawthorne's specific processes and culture
  • Valid driver's license required

Compensation and Career Path

Beyond hourly pay, Leasing Consultants earn monthly commissions tied to new leases and renewals, plus access to leasing incentive programs. Hawthorne is a top-50 multifamily operator nationally with deep roots in the Southeast, and they maintain a formal career path program. The stated trajectory from this role is toward Assistant Community Manager, which is a meaningful step because it shifts you from leasing-focused work into broader operations including delinquency tracking, reporting, and vendor coordination. If you're looking to build a career in property management rather than just fill a position, that path is real and supported by an internal learning and development team.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with employer match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, and company-paid life insurance, among others.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Some leasing roles are purely transactional. This one isn't. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, the Leasing Consultant position at Hawthorne at Oak Ridge in Greensboro, NC is built around relationship-building and genuine hospitality. The skills this role calls on most are persuasion, empathy, and communication. If those come naturally to you, the rest is learnable.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Conversion is the core skill here. You're taking a prospect who found the community online or walked in off the street and turning that curiosity into a signed lease. That means conducting personalized tours that connect the physical space to what the prospect actually wants in a home, following up consistently, handling objections without pressure, and completing leasing applications and move-in paperwork with accuracy. It's sales, but the kind that works best when it doesn't feel like sales.

Communication across multiple channels matters just as much. You'll field inquiries by phone, email, and web platforms throughout the day, often while managing walk-in traffic at the same time. Clear, prompt responses directly affect occupancy. Greensboro has a competitive rental market with several well-managed communities in the northwest corridor near Oak Ridge Road, so prospects are comparison shopping. The speed and quality of your follow-up often determines whether the lease lands here or somewhere else.

Resident relations is the other half of the job. You'll help coordinate community events, respond to resident concerns, and contribute to renewal efforts. Those two sides of the role, leasing and retention, reinforce each other. A community where current residents feel genuinely connected is easier to lease because the atmosphere shows.

Responsibilities at a Glance

  • Greet and tour prospective residents, matching unit options to their specific needs
  • Respond to inbound inquiries promptly across phone, email, and web
  • Manage the full leasing process from application through move-in paperwork
  • Support occupancy and renewal goals alongside the broader site team
  • Help plan and attend resident events and community engagement activities
  • Assist with social media and local outreach to build community awareness
  • Track competitor properties and stay current on local market conditions

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays 10 AM to 4 PM, with one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Some evenings and weekends may come up for resident events.

What Makes This a Strong Career Starting Point

Hawthorne is a top-50 multifamily management company with deep roots in the Southeast. They offer a defined career path program, and the Leasing Consultant to Assistant Community Manager progression is a real one, not just a line in the posting. The skills you build here, closing leases, managing resident relationships, learning the operational rhythm of a community, translate directly into site management roles down the line.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, along with leasing incentive programs. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), pet insurance, and paid parental leave options. A high school diploma or GED is the baseline requirement. One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience is preferred but not a hard requirement. A valid driver's license is required, and a CALP certification is a bonus if you already have it.

What separates strong candidates here isn't a polished resume. It's genuine enthusiasm for connecting with people and a willingness to be coached on how Hawthorne runs its communities. The technical side of leasing is teachable. The interpersonal instincts are harder to develop from scratch.

job.title: Office Administrative Assistant
job.description:
Corporate property management offices run on information flow. Residents need answers, vendors need coordination, leadership needs reports ready before they ask for them. This Office Administrative Assistant role at Paragon Properties in Bingham Farms sits at the center of that flow, touching nearly every department in the company.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're the first voice a resident hears when they call the office and the first face a visitor sees at the front desk. That's not just customer service. It's brand management. From there, the day branches in a dozen directions: routing maintenance concerns to the right team, pulling together variance reports for leadership, keeping vendor compliance files current, and making sure the conference room is set up before a 9 a.m. meeting anyone forgot to mention until 8:55.

The cross-functional piece is real here. You'll support facilities, HR, accounting, and executive leadership, which means your week will never look exactly the same twice. Some days are heavy on data entry and report compilation in property management software like Yardi. Others are heavy on coordination, onboarding logistics, supply ordering, or drafting notices that go out to residents across Paragon's portfolio.

What Paragon Is Looking For

  • High school diploma required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree preferred
  • At least two years of administrative or office support experience
  • Property management or real estate background is a plus, not a requirement
  • Solid command of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook
  • Yardi experience is preferred but not mandatory
  • Strong written communication skills, because resident notices and internal memos both carry the company's name
  • Comfortable handling confidential information, including employee files and financial documentation
  • This is an on-site role, full-time 40 hours per week

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The difference between a good admin and a great one in property management usually comes down to anticipation. Good admins respond. Great ones notice that the vendor certificate of insurance expired before anyone else does, or that a report is due Thursday and the data isn't pulled yet on Tuesday. If you've worked in an environment where the pace shifts without warning and you've learned to triage without being told, that matters here.

Paragon offers a full benefits package including PTO, nine paid holidays, a performance bonus, 401(k) with employer contribution, health coverage with a short waiting period, and a rent discount. The company's stated focus on people, residents, employees, vendors, and ownership alike, suggests an operator that thinks about retention seriously. For someone looking to build a long-term administrative career in the property management industry, this kind of multi-department exposure is genuinely useful. It's the kind of role that teaches you how a property management company actually works, from the inside out.

job.title: Service Manager (The Piedmont Raleigh)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a working supervisor role at The Piedmont Raleigh, a 382-unit mid-rise community. You're leading a team of three maintenance technicians while staying hands-on yourself. That means you'll be troubleshooting HVAC systems one hour, walking a punch list on a make-ready the next, and meeting with a contractor about building exterior work before the afternoon is out. The daily flow of service requests runs through you, and so does the facility side of the budget.

You'll own the make-ready process from scheduling vendors to coordinating turns so vacant units are rent-ready on time. Preventative maintenance programs, weekly reports to the corporate office, and compliance with state and federal requirements (think OSHA, safety standards, building codes) are all on your plate. When something breaks at 2 a.m., the emergency maintenance schedule you built and manage is what determines how that call gets handled.

A few things worth saying plainly: weekends are required, and the 24-hour emergency rotation is real. This isn't a role where you clock out at 5 and disconnect. That's the job. What makes it workable is having a competent team around you and a property management company that's been doing this since 1955.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of hands-on maintenance experience, with prior supervisory responsibility
  • Universal CFC Certification (required, not preferred)
  • CPO Certification (required)
  • Solid working knowledge of HVAC: maintenance, repair, and replacement
  • Competency across electrical, plumbing, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting
  • Familiarity with OSHA and current building and safety standards
  • Your own basic tools and the skill to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license

The Bigger Picture

Service Managers at mid-rise communities like The Piedmont Raleigh sit at the intersection of resident satisfaction and asset preservation. The condition of the property directly affects occupancy, renewal rates, and NOI. When make-readies slip or service requests pile up, the leasing side feels it fast. Strong candidates in this role aren't just technically sharp. They communicate clearly with residents, hold vendors accountable, and keep their team organized without micromanaging.

Van Metre is a development and management company with deep roots in the mid-Atlantic market, and this role connects to a broader facilities structure that includes a Director of Facilities at the corporate level. That means you have support above you, but you're expected to run your property day-to-day without hand-holding. The pay range is $31 to $35 per hour depending on experience, plus a $5,000 annual bonus paid quarterly, renewal and survey commissions, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, and up to $900 in annual wellness reimbursement.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Property managers at well-run multifamily companies spend their days balancing two very different kinds of work: the operational side (maintenance coordination, vendor relationships, budget tracking) and the people side (resident retention, team development, leasing performance). At Cottonwood Residential's Steepleway Downs community in Houston, you're expected to do both well.

What This Role Actually Involves

You'll carry full accountability for site operations. That means owning the annual operating budget, managing cost control initiatives, and keeping NOI on track. It also means developing and executing the property's sales and marketing strategy, not just reviewing reports someone else builds. On any given week, you might be reviewing delinquency with your team in the morning, walking a make-ready with maintenance in the afternoon, and approving a vendor invoice before you leave.

Your team looks to you for direction. Effective leadership here isn't about issuing instructions. It's about setting the standard for how residents are treated, how quickly work orders get resolved, and how the leasing team presents the community to prospects. Cottonwood has been an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so you'll be working within a leasing model that requires your team to perform without being physically present for every interaction. That takes systems, trust, and consistent training.

What You Need Coming In

  • At least three years of experience as a property manager or in a closely related role
  • Strong background in leasing, sales, or customer service
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing laws
  • Experience with Entrata Core is a plus, though not required
  • REIT experience is preferred. Cottonwood operates within that structure, and familiarity with owner expectations at that level helps
  • NALP designation is a plus for candidates earlier in their management career

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The managers who thrive in this type of role come in already comfortable reading a T-12 and asking the right questions about variances. They don't wait for corporate to flag a budget problem. They also understand that occupancy and resident satisfaction aren't separate goals. High turnover kills NOI just as surely as poor expense management does, and the best property managers treat retention as a financial discipline, not just a hospitality one.

If you're currently a strong assistant manager ready to take the next step, or an experienced PM looking for a company that invests in innovation rather than just maintaining the status quo, this role is worth your attention. The quarterly bonus structure ties your compensation directly to property performance, which means your instincts and effort show up in your paycheck.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-scope Community Manager role at a multifamily property in Gainesville, FL under Waypoint Management Services. You're running daily operations, leading a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff, and owning the financial performance of the asset. That means monitoring delinquency, managing collections proactively, controlling expenses, and keeping occupancy where it needs to be.

You'll handle budget prep, track capex projects, and report on property performance with enough detail to drive real decisions. On the leasing side, you're watching traffic, conducting market surveys, adjusting strategy based on what competitors are doing, and closing. You're also the person vendors, contractors, and residents escalate to when things get complicated.

Team development is a real part of this job, not a line item. You're recruiting, coaching, and setting performance expectations for leasing agents and maintenance techs. Culture on-site reflects how you lead.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years as a property manager and 5 or more years in multifamily, including experience at Class A communities
  • Solid financial background: budgeting, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and capital project oversight
  • Working knowledge of Yardi and CRM tools
  • Demonstrated experience building and developing a site team
  • Strong grasp of Fair Housing law, leasing procedures, and maintenance operations
  • A track record of improving NOI through a combination of rent growth, retention, and expense discipline
  • A bachelor's degree is preferred but not a hard requirement given the right experience

Context Worth Knowing

Gainesville is a college-influenced market, which means you're likely dealing with lease-up cycles tied to the academic calendar, a resident base with higher turnover than typical suburban multifamily, and a competitive landscape where concessions and marketing timing matter more than in steady-state markets. Managers who succeed here know how to run a tight make-ready schedule, keep renewal rates up despite seasonal move-outs, and stay visible in the local market.

What separates strong candidates from average ones here is financial ownership. Plenty of managers can handle resident relations and day-to-day ops. The ones who move up are the ones who treat the P&L like it's theirs, catch expense creep early, and can walk a supervisor through a T-12 without needing to be coached. If that's how you already operate, this role is a fit.

Waypoint offers quarterly manager bonuses, monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, benefits starting day one, 401k with company match, and 120 hours of PTO in year one with progressive increases.

job.title: Limpiador Residencial
job.description:
Residential porter roles at mixed-use and multifamily properties exist because first impressions are constant. Residents and visitors judge a community by what they see the moment they walk through a door. Comstock is hiring a Residential Cleaner (Limpiador Residencial) for their Ashburn, VA portfolio to keep that standard consistent every single day.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're responsible for common areas: lobbies, hallways, restrooms, sidewalks, and public spaces. Daily cleaning checklists guide your shift, but you also respond to issues as they come up. Pressure washing, window cleaning, trash collection, and routine maintenance tasks are all part of the rotation. When events are scheduled, you help with setup and breakdown. You track supply inventory, report equipment damage, and document any safety hazards you spot before they become bigger problems.

You'll be in uniform, on-site before your shift starts, and working with a team that includes property managers, residents, and visitors throughout the day. The Senior Operations Manager sets priorities. You execute them cleanly and on time. End-of-shift documentation and a proper handoff to the next person keep operations running without gaps.

Weekend availability is required, especially during high-traffic periods or events. This isn't a Monday-through-Friday desk job.

What Comstock Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license with no major violations
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and work on your feet for extended periods
  • Comfort working outdoors in variable weather, around cleaning chemicals, and in physically demanding conditions
  • Flexibility to work outside regular hours, including weekends and event days
  • Strong reliability and punctuality. These are non-negotiable in this role.
  • Ability to interact professionally with a wide range of people throughout the day
  • Self-directed work style with the ability to follow checklists and schedules accurately without constant supervision

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) matching, life insurance, free parking and EV charging, parental leave, and annual professional development funds. Benefit availability may vary by position type.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: it's not just cleaning skill, it's consistency. Property management teams notice the porter who flags a maintenance issue before a resident complains, who keeps the supply room organized without being asked, and who handles an unexpected mess during a busy event without losing composure. That kind of reliability is what gets noticed and leads to more responsibility within a growing portfolio like Comstock's.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, slightly skeptical, comparing your community to three others they toured this morning. What happens in the next 20 minutes often determines whether they sign or disappear. That moment is the core skill this role sharpens every single day.

Property Management Associates, one of the larger full-service property management firms in Southern California with over 30 years operating across the greater LA County market, is building a pipeline of strong leasing talent for upcoming openings at their Carson location. This is a full-time, hourly position with a pay range of $19.50 to $23.00 per hour, plus a commission structure that rewards performance directly: $100 per new lease signed and $50 per renewal.

What This Role Involves

Day to day, you're conducting property tours, walking prospects through the community and converting interest into signed leases. You'll manage applicants through the full cycle, from initial inquiry to application review, screening, and lease execution. You'll also contribute to the property's marketing efforts, which at PMA includes both traditional outreach and active use of online platforms and social media to generate traffic and fill vacancies. One weekend day per week is a standard expectation in this role.

PMA is a company that manages both residential and commercial properties, so there's real breadth to the organization you'd be joining. They describe themselves as family-oriented and encourage an entrepreneurial approach among their staff.

What You'll Need Coming In

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, you're representing the property in every interaction
  • Genuine comfort with the leasing and rental application process, including lease signings
  • Sales instincts and the ability to read what a prospect actually needs
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and experience using social media for marketing purposes
  • Familiarity with Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe is a plus, not a requirement

What This Role Builds

Strong leasing consultants who understand how to read traffic patterns, track conversion rates, and adjust their pitch based on what's driving or killing applications develop a skill set that translates cleanly into assistant manager and property manager roles. If you want to grow in residential property management, the leasing desk is where you learn the product, the residents, and the numbers. The commission structure here also trains you to think like an operator, every lease is a real outcome with a real dollar value attached to it.

Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short-term and long-term disability coverage, supplemental insurance options, and a PTO package that includes vacation, holidays, and sick time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a multi-property maintenance role covering residential units in Hawthorne, CA. You're moving between sites, working through work orders, and keeping things running. A typical day includes plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, drywall patches, appliance fixes, and rent-ready unit prep. Make-readies are a real part of this job. You'll inspect properties on a regular cycle, catch problems before residents do, and handle repair requests without someone looking over your shoulder.

You'll also manage parts inventory and order supplies as needed. Saturdays are possible. You need a valid driver's license and your own insured vehicle. PMA covers $300/month toward vehicle use and $25/month toward your cell.

Tools are provided and stored on-site. That's worth noting if you've been burning through your own kit at previous jobs.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of hands-on maintenance experience across plumbing, electrical, drywall, and appliance repair
  • Solid knowledge of repair methods, materials, and the tools that go with them
  • Experience prepping units for move-in, including full punch list completion
  • Ability to lift 25 to 50 pounds and stay on your feet for a full 8-hour shift
  • Strong organizational habits. You track parts, close work orders, and don't let things slip.
  • Valid driver's license and proof of auto insurance
  • Clear English communication skills, both with residents and with management

The Role in Context

PMA is one of the larger third-party property management operations in the greater LA area, with a portfolio spanning thousands of residential units across Southern California. That scale means consistent work and a structured maintenance operation, not the chaos of a small owner-operator setup. You're not reinventing the wheel every week.
